STARTING THE VEHICLE FROM STATIONARY Once the starting procedure is over, the vehicle is running, at a speed V = 0 km/h, gearbox in neutral (N) and selector lever in N. The user can chose to set off in a forward or reverse gear. The instrument panel, in addition to displaying the operating mode (and the SPORT logic if engaged), displays neutral "N". Irrespective of the mode (AUTO/MANUAL) or the operating logic (SPORT/NORMAL) selected: from lever position N: to engage 1st or 2nd gear or Reverse, press the brake pedal: the system enables the coil in the shift-lock and releases the lever. Below a certain speed (10 km/h) the control unit leaves the shift-lock coil released to allow the shift from 1st to R or from R to 1st even without pressing the brake pedal. The engagement takes place in any situation until the vehicle speed is below 5 km/h. This condition ensures that the driver should not press the brake repeatedly to release the lever especially in parking situations. with the brake pressed, therefore: - place the lever in TIP if setting off in 1st - place the lever in TIP and move the lever towards "+" (still pressing the brake pedal) if you decide to set off in 2nd for departures in poor grip conditions. The levers on the steering wheel do not work because the lever is in position N. from the TIP position or R: - it is possible to move the lever in N even if the brake is not pressed: N is engaged. - it is possible to shift from 1st to R or from R to 1st without pressing the brake if the manoeuvre is made quickly (parking manoeuvre); stopping in position N causes the lever to be locked: the gearbox stops operating the shift-lock coil. - to engage 2nd, with 1st gear engaged, push towards "+"with the brake pressed. Starting from AUTO mode: the engagement of 2nd does not involve the return to manual mode. - the levers on the steering wheel work (if the lever is in the TIP position): it is possible to engage 1st and 2nd gear with the brake pressed (the AUTO mode is maintained if it is engaged). ENGINE STARTED The vehicle starts to move (take off) using the accelerator pedal only. Only the following gears can be engaged with the engine started: 1st, 2nd or Reverse. When R is engaged there should NOT be any ACOUSTIC WARNING. Coming from "N" or "R" the TIP position corresponds to 1st gear. Every TIP - request is not considered by the system because it is not a plausible request. Gear change with vehicle moving GEAR CHANGE IN MANUAL MODE Every gear change request for a higher ratio takes place by moving the lever to the UP + position or using the levers on the steering wheel "+". The requests are only accepted if the gear change is over and the engine revs are such that the engine will not stall. If the request is accepted by the system: when the gear change is over, the display will show the new current gear. The system shows the gear actually engaged on the display and not the gear requested by the driver. If the request is not accepted by the system: the gear engaged before the request will remain on the display (there is no acoustic signal). In a similar way, the user can proceed and request lower ratios using the lever, placing it in the DOWN "-" position or via the levers on the steering wheel "-". In this case the system will only accept the request if the engine speed, after the gear change, does not exceed the maximum rotation speed permitted for the engine. The system also automatically selects the lower ratio if the user keeps the current ratio at the engine stall speed limit (AUTODOWN manoeuvre). The lever is in the TIP postion during the manoeuvres described above. There is no AUTOUP. GEAR CHANGE IN AUTOMATIC MODE The letter D appears at the top of the display (on the left) above the indication of the gear engaged. To move the vehicle (fowards or backwards) in spite of being in automatic mode. The driver should request the two possible gears for take off (1st or 2nd) or Reverse with the brake pressed (obviously the system will maintain the automatic mode). the system accepts requests in this mode from the lever or the levers on the steering wheel which keep it in automatic mode. The Kick Down function is also available: following a brisk action on the accelerator towards the end of travel position, the system recognizes the request for maximum torque and changes down by one, two or three gears if conditions allow. SPORT/NORMAL LOGIC In any mode by pressing the SPORT button the display also shows the letter S. Pressing the SPORT button a second time, the logic is deactivated (the letter S is no longer shown on the display (Normal logic)). - Moving the lever or the gear lever never involves deactivating the SPORT mode: it can only be deactivated using the button. - If the system is operating in Automatic Sport mode, placing the lever in M/D engages the Manual Sport mode (and viceversa). REQUEST FOR NEUTRAL OR R/1ST WITH VEHICLE MOVING Reverse gear can only be engaged in the following conditions: - brake pedal pressed - vehicle speed close to 0 km/h (below the engagement speed of 5 km/h). Position: threshold speed greater than speed engaged (the threshold speed coincides with the maximum speed at which the manoeuvre is permitted). If there is a request for N or R/1st with: the vehicle speed less than or equal to the speed engaged, irrespective of the brake status, with the accelerator released: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows neutral N. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows R. The vehicle speed less than or equal to the speed engaged, irrespective of the brake status, with the accelerator pressed: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is accepted by the system; in addition to the operating mode and the logic, the display also shows R. It is possible to make the shift from 1st to R and viceversa without pressing the brake, if the manoeuvre is made quickly (parking manoeuvres). Speed between the speed engaged and the threshold speed (intial threshold speed = 20 km/h), irrespective of the brake with the accelerator released: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; N is shown on the display. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which automatically engages N; N and the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" are shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted. Speed between the speed engaged and the threshold speed (intial threshold speed = 20 km/h), irrespective of the brake with the accelerator pressed: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which automatically engages N; N and the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" are shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted. Vehicle speed above the threshold speed, irrespective of the brake, with the accelerator released: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is accepted by the system; N is shown on the display. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): N is not accepted and the message is "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED". There is also an acoustic signal. When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted. Vehicle speed above the threshold speed, irrespective of the brake, with the accelerator pressed: - manoeuvre from TIP to N (or from R to N): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. - manoeuvre from TIP to R (or from R to TIP): it is not accepted by the system which displays the current gear; the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" is shown on the display. There is also an acoustic signal. When consistency is restored between the lever position and the gear engaged both the message and the acoustic signalling are interrupted. When the lever is placed in any position, if the manoeuver is not accepted bu the lever remains in that status, as soon as the vehicle stationary conditions (vehicle speed = 0 km/h) are verified, there will be an attempt to engage neutral (N). If the vehicle speed is equal to or less than the lock speed: the lever will be locked in N. To release it, press the brake. If the vehicle speed is greater than the lock speed: the lever will not be locked in N. Instructions on request for Reverse/1st with vehicle speed above threshold speed - if within a parameter time T1 (which can be calibrated) the vehicle speed is below the value of the speed engaged, the request is accepted by the system which engages reverse gear. - if within the time T1 mentioned above, the vehicle speed remains below the threshold speed, but above the value of the speed engaged, the request (WITHOUT THE BRAKE PEDAL PRESSED) is refused by the system which engages N and the driver receives the warning message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" and there is an acoustic signal. - if within the time T1 mentioned above the vehicle speed is maintained above the threshold speed, the request is refused by the system and the driver is warned by the message "MANOEUVRE NOT PERMITTED" and the acoustic signal. In any case, if the lever is placed in "R" at any speed, without pressing the brake, with the lever remaining in this position, as soon as the system verifies that the vehicle is stationary (speed = 0 km/h), neutral is engaged. A return from "N" or "R", either with the system either in AUTOMATIC or MANUAL, is produced by placing the lever in the stable TIP position: THE BRAKE PEDAL DOES NOT HAVE TO BE PRESSED. The manoueuvre restores the gearbox to the most suitable gear. SYSTEM SAFETY FEATURES A. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R): Press the brake and/or accelerator pedal, then open the driver's door: the system maintains the current gear. The instrument panel continues to display the mode, the logic and the current gear; no acoustic warning. B. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R): Do not press the brake pedal or the accelerator pedal, then open the driver's door: the system engages N (neutral) after around 3 seconds (which can be calibrated between 1 to 5 seconds). The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N. Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored. (To reinsert 1st (with the lever in TIP) it is also possible to use the levers on the steering wheel, with the brake pressed). The use of the buzzer is planned for all cases where N is engaged automatically. C. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R): Never carry out any action for more than 3 minutes (which can be calibrated) (i.e. do not press either the brake pedal or the accelerator pedal and do not move the lever (e.g. stopped at traffic lights)): the system automatically selects N (neutral). The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N. Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored. D. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, GEAR ENGAGED (usually 1st, 2nd or R): Keeping the brake pedal pressed and not carrying out any action for more than 10 minutes (which can be calibrated): the system automatically selects N (neutral). The instrument panel will continue to display the mode, the logic and N. Since the lever may be in TIP or in R, the shift to N (neutral) controlled by the system involves an inconsistent situation between the position of the lever and the gear engaged in the gearbox, therefore the manouevre is accompanied by an acoustic inconsistency signal. the sound continues until consistency is restored E. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, gearbox in neutral (N): KEY-OFF procedure: Switch off the engine: N flashes in the display accompanied by an acoustic warning that the vehicle has been abandonned with the gearbox in neutral (N): it flashes and sounds for about 4 seconds. F. VEHICLE STATIONARY, ENGINE RUNNING, gear change other than neutral (N): KEY-OFF procedure: Switch off the engine: no information relating to the gearbox is displayed.

CO-AXIAL HYDRAULIC OPERATION (CSC) The (CSC) operating system comprises an actuating cylinder located on the bellhousing which controls the clutch, working co-axially in relation to the main shaft. 1. Air bleed plug 2. Oil pressure inlet 3. Co-axial hydraulic operation assembly F40 GEARBOX The diagrams show the F40 gearbox assembly with three propeller shafts. 1. Gear engagement assembly 2. Layshaft C 3. Main shaft A 4. Main shaft B The configuration of the gearbox is transverse with three shafts: one main shaft (A) and two layshafts (B and C). The main shaft A contains five fixed gears designed to transmit power to the gears for 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th 6th and Reverse speeds on the two layshafts B and C which they mesh with constantly. The two layshafts B and C both have a pinion which meshes constantly with the differential ring gear. The layshaft B contains the 1st and 2nd speed and the 5th and 6th speed gear trains, whilst the layshaft C contains the 3rd and 4th speed and the reverse gear trains. The components inside the gearbox are lubricated dynamically, by means of the oil flowing through the ducts in the casings and the ports in the shafts as well as additional plastic ducts; all of this allows improved torque transmission and better protection against wear. The clutch is hydraulically operated with the C.S.C. system co-axial on the main shaft inside the gearbox. This system produces the following advantages: recovery of the clutch plate wear which allows the load on the clutch pedal to remain constant throughout the life of the vehicle improved acoustic comfort reduction of the engagement force no vibrations / shuddering of the lever Gearbox in neutral position The diagram below shows the position of the gearbox when no gear is engaged. 1. 1st speed gear 2. 1st and 2nd speed synchronizer 3. 2nd speed gear 4. 3rd speed gear 5. 3rd and 4th speed synchronizer 6. 4th speed gear 7. 5th speed gear 8. 5th and 6th speed synchronizer 9. 6th speed gear 10. reverse gear 11. GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS - Type 6-speed automatic transmission - Architecture: 3 clutches, 2 brakes, 1 free wheel, 2 epicyclic trains - Hydraulic: 4 linear solenoids, 2 on/off solenoids - Electronic: Neutral Start Switch and control unit built in, internal wiring and speed sensors NAME AT6 TRANSMISSION RATIO 1 4.148 2 2.370 3 1.556 4 1.155 5 0.859 6 0.686 R 3.394 Idler shaft 0.836 Differential 3.188 BRAKES AND CLUTCHES CLUTCHES C1 1 flange, 6 discs, 6 plates 1 flange, 7 discs, 7 plates C2 1 flange, 3 discs, 3 plates 1 flange, 4 discs, 4 plates C3 1 flange, 4 discs, 4 plates BRAKES B1 Band B2 2 flanges, 6 discs, 5 plates 2 flanges, 6 discs, 5 plates One-Way F1 Roller type SOLENOIDS Shift solenoid n. 2 Linear n. 6 LINE PRESSURE [KPa] MINIMUM D 372 - 414 R 575 - 665 STALL D 1350 - 1460 R 1905 - 2125 FUNCTION Neutral control When the vehicle stops with the lever set to "D", the clutches are automatically released and the transmission changes to neutral. In this way, the torque converter is not put under stress, there are fewer vibrations and fuel consumption is minimal. On rough roads or on hills, the function does not activate. On hills, the transmission remains engaged to assure a hill holder effect. Reversing control When the gear lever is shifted from "N" to "R", reverse is not engaged if vehicle speed exceeds 11 km/h. Adaptivity MODE DESCRIPTION ADAPTIVITY Used during normal driving The sports or economy modes are selected automatically depending on driving conditions SPORT In this mode, the speed passage points and lock-up operation are higher because the rpm is higher WINTER/LOW GRIP In the event of ice, snow and low grip in general, the car sets off in third gear to prevent the front wheels slipping TIP When the lever is moved from “D” to “+/-”, the driver can select the speed passage point sequentially. In any case, the control unit changes the ratio automatically to prevent over-revving or viceversa to prevent juddering because the engine speed is too low. HIGH TEMPERATURE If the transmission fluid temperature is too high, the control unit advances lock-up intervention to prevent the torque converter slipping excessively and thus lowering the temperature. Introduction The transmission used connected to the 3.2 V6 JTS engine type is permanent four wheel drive with a Torsen Twin C type centre differential and front differential built into the Torsen assembly casing. The torque supplied by the engine enters the F40 gearbox, with specific ratios to ensure optimum exploitation of the power and torque to maximize the efficiency of the four wheel drive. At the gearbox output, the torque reaches the centre Torsen differential, by means of a crown wheel and pinion reduction with helical teeth and the drive torque is distributed between the front and rear axles with a ratio of 56/44. The torque distributed to the front axle enters the "open" type front differential incorporated in the Torsen casing and is shared between the two wheels on the front axle. The torque distributed to the rear axis on leaving the Torsen on the other hand enters the rear axle from the torque rear idler (PTU: Power Trasmission Unit). The PTU comprises a crown wheel and pinion reduction with helical teeth and a bevel pinion that transfers the engine torque to the propeller shaft. The propeller shaft, in turn, directs the engine torque to the rear differential (RDA: Rear Differential Axle) where the distribution to the two wheels on the rear axle takes place. The transmission is assembled on the 3.2 V6 engine using new fixing bolts; the PTU, in turn, is secured to the transmission by the centre differential by means of four bolts and centered through two bushes on the gearbox casing; there is an o-ring between the flanges matching the PTU and the gearbox which is replaced at each dismantling. The tightening of the PTU is then completed by two further bolts that join it directly to the engine. Gearbox The gearbox used on this transmission system is the F40 with six speeds, designed to ensure optimum matching with the 3.2 V6 JTS power unit in terms of maximum exploitation of the engine torque and, at the same time, adjusting the ratios to the four wheel drive system. Flange Centre differential The centre differential is the Torsen Twin C type and also contains the transmission front differential in the casing. It comprises two half shells on the outside of which the crown wheel that meshes with the gearbox final gear is tightened; the casing also houses the eight planet gears with helical teeth that rotate with the casing and transmit the drive for the rear axle to an outer ring gear and the drive for the front axle to an inner ring gear connected directly to the front differential by means of ribbing. A. Meshing line between planet gear and rear axle ring gear B. Meshing line between planet gear and front axle ring gear C. Drive entry into centre differential (coming from the gearbox) D. Drive output to rear axle E. Drive output to front axle The sharing of the torque between the two axles takes place by means of a series of metal rings that control the drive for the two axles. When one of the axles "tends to rotate more than necessary" following variations in the grip conditions or critical connections connected to the vehicle dynamics (understeer, oversteer, etc.), the planet gears which, in normal circumstances rotate with the casing, without rotating around their own axis, "tend instantly to rotate around their own axis" producing axial thrusts typical of toothed wheels with helical teeth; these thrusts are discharged to the inner rings of the Torsen which instantly oppose the movement between the outer ring gear (rear axle) and inner ring gear (front axle) thereby transferring the torque from the axle that is rotating faster to the slower axle. Obviously, depending on whether it is the outer ring gear that wants to rotate faster or, alternatively, the inner ring gear that wants to rotate faster, the direction of the axial thrusts changes, involving different rings to discharge the forces involved transferring the torque from one axle to the other depending on requirements The possibility of locking the Torsen, which allows these transfers of torque to be controlled, is not infinite, in effect when the maximum torque transfer percentage from one axle to the other is reached the Torsen "opens" and allows slipping between the two ring gears; in these Torsen opening conditions the planet gears rotate around their own axle and the locking power, once the maximum value is reached, no longer increases. This is, for example, the condition produced for a fairly tight bend where the kinematic trajectories imposed by the steering manoeuvre lead the Torsen to become unlocked. Transmission of drive to rear axle (PTU) The casing is made from aluminium and the assembly weighs 22.2 Kg. The function of the idler unit, PTU, is to direct the engine torque to the rear axle. The PTU is connected to the gearbox by means of four bolts and to the engine by two bolts; as has already been stated, there is an O-ring between the PTU-gearbox flanges that ensures the seal and the insulation between the gearbox-centre differential internal chambers on the one hand and the PTU on the other. The PTU is lubricated internally by its own fluid and not by the same fluid that lubricates the gearbox and differential. There is an assembly inside the PTU that has the task of transferring the power from the axle coming out of the Torsen ot a second shaft with the helical wheel, on the one hand, meshing with the one on the axle coming from the Torsen and, on the other hand, the conical gear meshing on the pinion transferring the drive to the propeller shaft. Final drive ratio 1.520 (38/25) Crown wheel and pinion ratio 2.067 (31/15) Final drive reduction ratio section Idler final drive section Propeller shaft The propeller shaft comes in three parts and is connected to the bodyshell by means of two supports. The shaft has the function of transferring the PTU output power to the rear differential RDA. Rear differential (RDA) The casing is made from aluminium and the assembly weighs 17 Kg. The rear differential (RDA: Rear Differential Axle) is the open type and has the function of directing the input drive, coming from the propeller shaft, to the rear axle wheels. Crown wheel and pinion ratio 3.130 (47/15) Vehicle dynamics Driving in a straight line When driving in a straight line, if the grip conditions are even, the vehicle travels with the torque shared between the axles around the nominal rate; small variations in this nominal distribution are due to variations in the rolling circumference between the tyres on the two axles and the weight distribution between the axles. When the grip conditions between the two axles are no longer the same, as can be seen in the diagram, the torque is moved from the axle with less grip to the one with more grip to counterbalance the slipping of the axle which, from time to time, finds itself in poor grip conditions. Driving round bends Round bends, when the radius is fairly consistent, the front wheels cover kinematic trajectories that make the actual wheels rotate faster than the rear wheels; in these conditions the Torsen removes torque from the front wheels and sends it to the rear wheels. When the maximum internal locking limit is reached, the Torsen opens allowing the vehicle to follow the trajectory imposed by the steering manoeuvre without the wheels slipping. Understeer In the case of understeer the front wheels tend to rotate faster following the slipping typical of this manoeuvre, normally due to the grip limit being exceeded and allowing the engine torque to be "drained" to the ground; this usually happens either through excess torque discharged to the ground or through a decrease in road surface grip conditions. In this situation, as the tyre side road holding margin no longer remains (all the grip is used for the longitudinal part of the tyre) the vehicle tends to extend the trajectory and not follow the bend. In this situation the Torsen removes torque from the front axle and distributes it to the rear axle, returning the "side" grip margin to the front wheels and thereby restoring the stability of the vehicle, obviously within the physical limits of the vehicle dynamics. Oversteer In the case of oversteer the rear wheels tend to rotate faster following the slipping typical fo this manoeuvre normally due to the grip limit that allows the engine torque to be "drained" to the ground having been exceeded. This usually happens either through excess torque drained to the ground or through a decrease in the road surface grip; in this situation as the tyre side road holding margin no longer remains (all the grip is used for the longitudinal part of the tyre) the vehicle tends to pitch at the rear making the vehicle unstable. In this situation the Torsen removes torque from the rear axle and distributes it to the front axle, returning the "side" grip margin to the rear wheels and thereby restoring the stability of the vehicle, obviously within the physical limits of the vehicle dynamics.

SPECIFICATIONS The drive shafts, constant velocity joints and intermediate drive shaft that make up the transmission assembly transmit motion from the gearbox to the drive wheels. The transmission features wheel side constant velocity joints and one gearbox side constant velociy joint known as a "TOULIP". The opposing drive shaft features a constant velocity joint with an intermediate drive shaft. The intermediate drive shaft transmits drive to the right drive shaft, which is the same as the left. This solution allows drive torque to be distributed in perfectly symmetrical manner over both wheels. This prevents the longer drive shaft from curving due to bending induced bythe transmitted drive torque, which could cause changes in the vehicle's dynamic attitude.

SPECIFICATIONS The braking system is the power assisted hydraulic type, comprising two crossover, independent ciruits (each circuit acting on one front wheel and the diagonally opposite rear wheel) to ensure braking and stability even if one of the circuits fails. The system is also equipped with the following assisted braking and steering systems: - ABS: anti-lock brakes; - EBD: electronic brakeforce distribution between the front and rear wheels; - ASR: traction control via management of the brakes and engine control unit; - MSR: engine brake control by means of engine control unit management; - VDC: vehicle electronic stability control; - HBA: automatic increase in braking pressure during emergency braking; - Hill Holder: assisted hill start system that keeps the vehicle braked while parked on slopes and automatically releases the brakes when the driver wishes to set off. The vehicle is equipped with an ABS/EBD brake control system. The ABS is fitted parallel to the hydraulic braking system so that should it not work braking would still be guaranteed. The ABS incorporates the EBD function (Electronic Brake force Distribution) therefore the hydraulic system does not have a rear load proportioning valve. ABS/EBD SYSTEM View of assembly 1. ABS/EBD control unit 2. Left front wheel sensor 3. Right front wheel sensor 4. Right rear wheel sensor 5. Left rear wheel sensor 6. EBD warning light 7. ABS warning light Specifications The ABS control unit implements the ABS and EBD functions. The ABS control unit is connected to the front wiring, the system cable loom is incorporated with the engine compartment cable loom. The pin out of the ABS control unit with EBD is different from control units with ASR and VDC functions. Composition The ABS consists of: - an electronic control unit integral with the hydraulic control unit - an electrohydraulic control unit that modulates braking pressure by means of eight solenoids, two for each wheel - four active sensors that detect the angular rotating speed of the wheels. - wiring with specific connector Operation Introduction The electronic control unit processes signals from the active sensors and brake light control switch. It identifies the wheel or wheels with a tendency to lock (maximum slip between wheel and road surface) by means of the control unit software and modulates the brake fluid pressure selectiely for the front wheels and in tandem for the rear wheels (select-low function). The ABS modulates brake pressure in accordance with three basic stages: - pressure maintenance stage - pressure reduction stage - pressure increase stage If operation is requested, the ABS stays active at speeds greater than 2.7 km/h. After that, it cuts out to allow the car to stop. After each key ON and when a speed of 6 km/h is exceeded, the control unit carries out an operation check on the solenoids and pump engine. The control unit also tests the sensors when a speed of 12 km/h is exceeded. Operating logics PRESSURE INCREASE STAGE WITHOUT ABS OPERATION When the brake pedal is pressed, the electronic control unit (1): - does not supply the load solenoid (N.A.) (2) - does not supply the discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3) The pressure generated by the brake pump (4) therefore reaches the brake calipers (5) without undergoing changes. EXAMPLE OF ABS OPERATION Pressure maintenance stage The electronic control unit (1): - supplies the load solenoid (N.A.) (2) - does not supply the discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3) Therefore the hydaulic connection between the brake pump (4a) and the brake caliper (5) is broken. The pressure in the brake caliper (5) remains constant even when pressure on the brake pedal is increased. Pressure reduction stage The electronic control unit (1): - supplies the load solenoid (N.A.) (2) - does not supply the discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3) The hydraulic connection between the brake pump (4) and the brake caliper (5) is broken and the discharge solenoid (3) opens and brings the brake caliper (5) into communication with the low pressure accumulator (6) and scavenger pump (7). The control unit (1) also supplies the motor (8) controlling the scavenging pump (7) to restore the fuel taken to the brake callipers (5) to the main circuit. The fluid flows through the high pressure accumulator (9) and the restriction (10) that performs a damping function. The system is equipped with a check valve (11) fitted in parallel with the load solenoid (2) that allows fast reduction of pressure in the brake caliper (5) during brake pedal release. Pressure increase stage The control unit (1): - does not supply the load solenoid (N.A.) (2) - does not supply the discharge solenoid (N.C.) (3) The fluid taken into the main circuit is then free to return to the brake caliper (5) and increase the pressure acting on the brake caliper. EBD function (Electronic Brake-Force distribution) The EBD function controls the distribution of brakeforce and therefore replaces the conventional mechanical load proportioning valve to allow: - independent action on the rear brake callipers - improved brakeforce distribution - perform in optimum manner under any load condition (static or dynamic), driving conditions (in a straight line or corner) and when the vehicle is in any state of repair (worn tyres, brakes and suspension) - implementation of a strategy that follows the ideal distribution curve. Fa - Front axle brake force Fp - Rear axle brake force A - Distribution curve implemented by the braking system B - Ideal distribution curve C - Distribution curve implemented by a conventional hydraulic load proportioning valve D - Distribution curve implemented by the EBD function EBD function failure is indicated by the simultaneous activation of: - ABS warning light; - low brake fluid and/or handbrake-on warning light. Under these conditions, the car must be driven with extreme caution to the nearest authorised workshop to check the system. RECOVERY The electronic control unit is equipped with a safety circuit that monitors ABS efficiency. With key on, the safety circuit carries out an initial autotest for 4 seconds to check: - electronic control unit operation; - solenoid operation. Every time the car starts off from a standstill, the safety circuit checks for signals from active sensors. When the car is in motion, the safety circuit works as follows: - continually compares angular wheel speed with the calculated reference speed - checks memory conditions; - checks operation of both relays, the solenoids and the pump motor; - constantly monitors battery voltage; - monitors the efficiency of the brake pedal switch. If the safety circuit detects one or more faults in system components during the check stage, the safety circuit operates as follows: - deactivates the ABS while still guaranteeing operation of the conventional braking system; - indicates the fault status to the driver by turning on a warning light on the control panel. BRAKE VACUUM SYSTEM - For 3.2 JTS version only Due to its operational characteristics, the 3.2 JTS version of the engine, under the following conditions: - after cold starts; - while warming up; - with the climate control system in operation, generates a minimal vacuum in the brake servo caused by the greater throttle opening. Description The brake servo vacuum circuit is eqiupped with a bypass that incorporates two single-acting valves (5) and (7) that operate due to the pressure differences (P1) and (P2) pesent upstream and downstream of the throttle body. At the level of the valve (5), the pipe contains a constriction (6) to take advantage of the Venturi effect. The brake servo (9) is fitted with a brake servo minimum vacuum sensor (8) that indicates the vacuum present in the brake servo to the engine management unit. Operation With the engine cold or with additional loads, the air flows through the bypass and communicates with the brake servo by means of the single-acting valve (5) and the presence of the constriction increase the vacuum that removes air from the brake servo. With the engine warm and without additional loads, the vacuum in the modular intake manifold is greater than or equal to - 600 mb (ideal value) and the air in the brake servo is therefore removed through the valve (7). When the brake pedal is pumped rapidly and in particular if the throttle is open to meet the needs of other appliances in operation, the pressure in the brake servo may drop below the threshold of - 290 mb. At this point, the brake servo minimum vacuum servo (8) cuts in and send an electrical signal to the engine control unit. Once the control unit has received this signal (1.5 - 5 Volts), it processes the signal, converts it to a physical vacuum value and cuts in to deactivate: - the air conditioner, - the stratified engine operating mode, pressure in the brake servo therefore increases to guarantee service for at least three repeated presses of the brake pedal. Fault diagnosis Once it has received the signal, the engine control unit performs an electrical diagnosis. Once it has detected a sporadic error, it cuts in to temporarily deactivate the air conditioner and and the stratified engine operation mode. When it detects a validated error (i.e. that has occurred at least three times) caused by an open circuit or a short circuit to battery/earth, it enters STOP mode, i.e. it finally deactivates the air conditioner and the stratified engine operation mode until the fault is repaired. 1. The VDC system, in particular, thanks to slewing sensors and steering wheel angle sensors, guarantees the monitoring of the dynamics of the entire vehicle thereby improving active safety. ABS warning light Specifications Driving a vehicle in all conditions where the physical limits of grip and, consequently, stability may be reached can be a difficult task for the average driver therefore in order to further improve safe driving conditions an electronic system capable of assisting the driver with this difficult task is available. The systems currently employed to ensure safer driving in particular conditions are mainly the A.B.S. which controls braking and the T.C. and systems which control traction during acceleration through action on the brakes (T.C.) and traction/drive torque during acceleration and release through action on the brakes and on the engine control system motorized throttle (A.S.R./M.S.R.). The VDC system includes all the above listed functions ensuring optimum dynamic control of the vehicle with the addition of specific sensors: - steering angle sensor on the steering wheel; - slewing/lateral acceleration sensor at the centre of gravity under the centre tunnel. μ - Wheel grip S - Slipping A - EBD intervention area B - ABS intervention area C - VDC intervention area 1 - Lateral force curve 2 - Longitudinal force curve As can be seen from the grip/slipping diagram, the area covered by the VDC system is larger than that covered by a conventional ABS/EBD system. The VDC system cannot be switched off as it is a safety system; the A.S.R./M.S.R. function, on the other hand, can be switched off via the button in the centre console. To ensure the drive of the vehicle (drive wheels) with snow chains fitted or in particular road surface conditions (snow, ice, deep mud, sand or gravel) it is advisable to switch the A.S.R. off. The intervention of the VDC system is signalled by a special warning light in the instrument panel node. Composition The VDC system consists of: - an electro-hydraulic/electronic A.B.S. control unit (with an VD logic); - interface with the C-CAN line, resident in the ABS control unit for communication with the engine control unit, steering angle sensor and lateral acceleration sensor; - Magnetic-resistive type wheel speed sensors; - steering angle sensor with C.A.N. interface (steering angle sensor); - slewing/lateral acceleration sensor in one piece integral with the CAN interface; - brake fluid pressure sensor incorporated in the A.B.S. control unit; - ABS-EBD-VDC warning light in the instrument panel controlled via the dedicated serial line; - A.S.R. off switch with a warning light in the button. Operation The VDC continuously recognizes a loss in grip for the wheels, both longitudinal and transverse, in all driving conditions from braking to acceleration in order to ensure the direction and the stability of the vehicle. The management of the VDC system is entrusted to the A.B.S. electronic control unit, integrated with a special electro-hydraulic control unit, that allows action on the braking system independently of the action of the user. The control unit processes the following signals: - steering wheel rotation angle; - lateral acceleration and slewing; - engine operating conditions: - wheel rpm; - hydraulic braking system pressure and uses special algorithms in the electronic control unit software to obtain the figures for the dynamic control of the vehicle: - longitudinal and transverse sliding between the wheels and the road surface; - axle drift. Using these figures the system interprets the effective dynamics of the vehicle; having identified all the critical conditions due to environmental factors (e.g. surface with poor grip) or any errors made by the user (e.g. panic situations) and with subsequent intervention on the brakes and the drive torque, the vehicle is restored to good driving conditions. The system interfaces with: - NCM for drive torque adjustment via the C-CAN line; - control panel via a serial line for warning light control. The system is combined with a power unit with a specific brake pump; in addition, the pipes between the brake pump and the A.B.S. control unit have a Titaflex insert because the diameter of the pipe (6mm) is larger than regular pipes (4 mm); this is designed to prevent adverse effects on the operation of the VDC at low brake fluid temperatures. There is a dedicated line (line K) for the diagnosis of the system: The VDC system switches on automatically when the vehicle is started up and cannot be switched off by the user; the button in the centre console only switches off the A.S.R. function and only when advisable. Operating logics As stated previously, in addition to controlling the slipping of the vehicle in a lengthwise direction, the VDC system also controls slipping in a sideways direction and, as a result, controls the lateral stability of the vehicle. The lateral stability of a vehicle is the result of the reaction of the tyres to lateral forces due to increased centrifugal force. The action of the lateral forces produce a variation in the drift angle of the wheels and, consequently, a variation in the axle drift (drift angle = difference between the desired route and the effective route). The lateral forces do not, however, act equally on all four wheels because they are not all subject to the same load conditions; in effect the load on the wheel differs depending on the situation the wheel is in, namely: - acceleration (lightening of the front axle and loading of the rear axle); - braking (loading of the front axle and lightening of the rear axle); - bend to the right/left (loading or the outer wheels and lightening of the inner wheels); - accelerating/decelerating round a bend (combination of the cases mentioned above). It is obvious that if the lateral forces acting on the individual wheels vary, there will also be a variation in the forces acting on the vehicle axles; consequently the lateral forces acting on the front axle overcome those on the rear axle and viceversa determining a rotation (moment) on the vehicle axis of the vehicle (slewing axis). The yaw moment affects the behaviour of the vehicle, producing either understeer or oversteer. Understeer for a vehicle is when, with increasing lateral acceleration, the drift angle for the front axle increases greatly compared with that of the rear axle. When this happens, the vehicle tends to go straight ahead (taking the curve wide) when cornering. Oversteer for a vehicle is when, with increasing transverse acceleration, the drift angle for the rear axle increases greatly compared with that of the front axle. In this case the vehicle tends to turn around on itself (the rear axle tends to go straight, therefore the vehicle "hugs" the bend). In order to keep the effect of lateral forces under control and limit the slewing moment, the A.B.S. control unit must firstly calculate the behaviour of vehicle set by the driver using: - steering wheel angle sensor; - accelerator pedal position; - brake circuit pressure; after which the control unit should check the actual behaviour of the vehicle through: - the wheel sensors (vehicle speed/wheel speed); - lateral acceleration sensor; - slewing sensor. The control unit is capble of: - detecting actions carried out by the user, in effect, through the position of the steering wheel it checks the number of degrees (wide radius or narrow radius bends) and the speed for rotating the steering wheel (sharp or gentle rotations) and, using the position of the throttle and the brake pressure when accelerating or braking, how the user is taking the bend or deviating from the straight path. - detecting the actual behaviour of the vehicle given the environmental variables, e.g. slippery surface, reaction of the vehicle to incorrect manoeuvres by the user, etc., in order to identify the moment of slewing and the lateral sliding of the axles via the sensors on the four wheels and the slewing/lateral acceleration sensor. These two operations are necessary to superimpose the mathematical model mapped in the control unit on the effective behaviour of the vehicle in order to identify the state in which the vehicle is in (understeer or oversteer) and decide the action for the brakes and the engine UNDERSTEER ON CORNERS The control unit verifies the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the front axle), corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the inner wheels round the bend in order to create an opposing moment which will lead the vehicle towards the centre of the bend and, possibly, reducing the drive torque. OVERSTEER ON CORNERS In the presence of understeer (mainly from the drift of the rear axle) the control unit corrects the behaviour of the vehicle, braking the outer front wheel round the bend in order to create an opposite slewing moment, if necessary increasing the drive torque. The system intervenes before the oversteer and understeer values are too high in order to limit the corrective measures that have to be taken, which could make handling difficult. ABRUPT VARIATIONS FROM A STRAIGHT PATH (SLALOM/OVERTAKING) In the case of sharp variations from the path (e.g. overtaking, slalom), the control unit identifies possible oversteer and understeer conditions and corrects the path of the vehicle, acting as described in the cases mentioned previously. ABRUPT VARIATION FROM A STRAIGHT PATH (DRIVING OVER DIFFERENT SURFACES) The control unit is capable of detecting deviations in the path and the prevalence of axle drift, correcting the path through suitable action on the brakes and the engine. ABRUPT ACCELERATION/DECELERATION The control unit uses the A.S.R./M.S.R. strategy also controlling the lateral acceleration of the vehicle and, as a result, regulating the action on the front and rear brakes and on the engine torque in a more complete way than on vehicles with ASR only. INTERVENTION - INTERVENTION TIMES IN CONDITIONS WHERE ROAD SURFACE GRIP IS GOOD (ASPHALT) For JTS versions: Engine torque reduction by the engine management control unit through the alteration of the ignition advances, 6/100 of a second after the slipping limit is exceeded. In this case there is an increase in drive torque through the intervention of the engine management control unit opening the motorized throttle (petrol versions) or fuel flow (JTD versions) to overcome the natural instability of the vehicle due to the engine braking torque in poor grip conditions. Description of components HYDRAULIC SYSTEM OPERATION The electro-hydraulic unit on the version equipped with VDC has 4 additional solenoid valves. When the (normally closed) intake solenoid valve is activated, the additional quantity of fluid required to increase the pressure and brake the wheel(s) can be received. When the (normally open) solenoid valve is activated, the modulated pressure produced by the supply pump can be maintained in the circuit. When the ESP system is not intervening, the electronic control unit: - does not activate the (N.C.) intake solenoid valve (2). - does not activate the (N.A.) operating solenoid valve (3). In this way the system operates during the following stages: - pressure increase; - pressure maintenance; - pressure reduction; - pressure increase and resupply. During the intervention of the VDC system, the electronic control unit: - activates the hydraulic pump (1); - does not activate the (N.C.) intake solenoid valve (2); - activates the (N.A.) operating solenoid valve (3). Therefore the pressure produced by the pump (1) reaches the brake caliper and is modulated, on the request of the electronic control unit, by the discharge (5) and pressurising (6) solenoid valves. The flywheel is a multipolar ring, an elastomer with a certain quantity of magnetic particles which, by means of a special magnetization technique, are orientated to produce different magnets with alternate North South poles in a circumference arrangement. SPECIFICATIONS The steering control has been designed to guarantee the best performance for the driver during sporty driving together with excellent handling and limited effort during parking manoeuvres. The development of these objectives, in conjunction with the search for excellent driving comfort, has led to the production of a steering system with the following technical specifications: - steering wheel turns: 2.33 in total on all versions - steering ratio: 13.0 steering wheel turns/wheel rotation - steering wheel effort: ~ 4 Nm when steering from stationary - turning circle: 11.1 m Driving comfort has been improved by taking care of the power assisted steering system sound insulation and by adopting a new design steering wheel and steering column featuring high structural strength. In addition, a new type vibrational damper with excellent uncoupling has been fitted on the intermediate steering column shaft. Lastly, great attention has been paid to passive safety both in terms of the layout, with the movement of the electric steering lock to the front area of the steering column, away from the area of the knees, and with the adoption of a controlled energy absorption collapsing device on the steering column. This, in conjunction with the steering wheel and knee air bags and the retaining belts, makes it possible to produce a five star performance in EUNCAP impact tests. Cooling coil The hydraulic circuit has a hydraulic pump rotated by service belts; the pump draws in oil from the reservoir near the actual pump; the pump supply reaches the steering box; the fluid leaving the steering box is sent to the reservoir passing through the cooling coil at the side of the radiator. Electric steering lock 3. Lower cover 4. Mounting bracket on dashboard crossmember Designed in accordance with the telescopic covers, it guarantees: - vertical adjustment with ± 2 degrees travel, - axial adjustment with 45 mm of total travel. The locking lever is located under the upper cover, in the special housing for the lower cover, in accordance with the most up to date EUNCAP safety requirements. The electric steering lock, fitted as standard, is housed on the lower steering column cover, by the mounting bracket on the dashboard crossmember. This means that it is out of the way of the driver's knees in line with current EUNCAP recommendations. In this configuration the shock absorber and the spring are flexible damping elements without structural functions. The rear suspension is the multilink type designed to allow: - recovery of camber during roll to keep the tyre vertical in order to maximize the lateral force that can be transmitted; - the elastokinmeatic retraction of the wheel centre when going over an obstacle to reduce the longitudinal component of the impact force; - control of steering round bends and when braking through a stabilizing effect and prompt response in the various usage conditions. The combination of the two suspensions makes it possible to produce the following strong points: - precise, gradual steering and steering wheel load - good responsiveness - good stability and ease of control even in poor grip conditions - very smooth, balanced movements - very good comfort for a sports vehicle. Front and rear wheel hubs with integrated bearing for A.B.S. active sensors. FRONT SUSPENSION The quadrilateral structure guarantees very good dynamic performance, excellent steering and precise driving. The track rod end-steering knuckle connection has been retracted and moved towards the outside. This has made it possible to improve the stability of the vehicle during braking. Careful attention to the matching of the steering geometry and wheel arch volume has made it possible to produce high steering angles even with larger tyres with notable improvements in the turning circle. INTRODUCTION The climate control system makes it possible to alter the features of the air introduced into the passenger compartment (temperature, humidity) designed to create and maintain a high level of comfort whilst driving. Climate control system components The climate control system components are illustrated in the diagram. 1. Linear pressure switch 2. Condenser 3. Drier filter built into the condenser 4. Low pressure gas pipe 5. Expansion valve 6. Evaporator 7. Duct/distributor assembly 8. Control panel with electronic control unit 9. Compressor 10. High pressure gas pipe 11. High pressure fluid pipe Operating principle The aim of refrigeration equipment is to absorb heat from an environment. In order to do this an air conditioner has recourse to certain fluids (known as refrigerants) capable of cooling down (lowering their temperature) and changing state (from liquid to gas) when they are subject to a large drop in pressure, expanding. They are therefore capable of absorbing heat from the environment. When the temperature increases thereby also increasing the pressure, they change state, another time, from gas to liquid, and condense. The first problem is therefore to liquefy this gas which can be achieved simply by bringing it to a temperature below that of evaporation (or boiling) which, as has already been stated, is -26°C at atmospheric pressure for R134a. In order for this to be achieved at ambient temperature which, in our case, may be rather high (in the engine compartment), it is necessary to increase the evaporation point of the gas so that it remains liquid until the moment it is made to expand to produce the desired refrigerant effect. To raise the boiling point of the gas its pressure must be increased, at the same time, decreasing the temperature. In order for this to take place the system requires a certain amount of power. This power, supplied by the compressor, is subtracted from the power produced by the engine. The operating principle of the refrigerant cycle phases in the air conditioning system for a motor vehicle can be summed up as follows. The gaseous R134a refrigerant is drawn in by the compressor at a pressure of between 0.5 and 2 bar and is compressed at a value of between 10 and 17 bar. The boiling point at these pressures is around 60 °C. This fluid, heated by the compression stage at 80 - 100 °C, always in a gaseous state, in the compressor where, through the effect of the cooling air flow (produced by the vehicle moving forward or through the action of the fan) that passes through, reaches condensation point, changing at high pressure to a liquid state. Later on the refrigerant passes through a filter which has three functions: to trap the impurities, absorb the dampness contained in the circuit and work as a reserve reservoir for the actual refrigerant. The refrigerant reaches the expansion valve, where it is introduced into the evaporator where the pressure is around 1.5 atm. (1.52 bar). At this pressure the liquid/vapour system saturated with the refrigerant fluid is in equilibrium at a temperature of about -7 °C. At the same time, the air that passes through the evaporator (through the action of a fan), being at a considerably higher temperature than the refrigerant fluid it contains, causes it to boil and evaporate completely by imparting heat. On cooling, the air deposits some of the dampness it contains on the evaporator fins in the form of droplets which are collected in a chamber and drained off from the vehicle. The cooled and dehumidified air is sent inside the vehicle. The refrigerant is drawn in by the compressor again at the evaporator outlet, thereby giving rise to a new cycle once again. The route of the refrigerant fluid can be summarized as follows: - In the compressor - the fluid coming from the evaporator is gaseous (temp. -5, -7°C, pressure 0.5 - 2 bars). Compression phase - the gaseous fluid is overheated (temp. 80 -100 °C, pressure 10 -17 bars). - Condenser - Compression phase: the fluid gives off heat to the outside, cools down and returns to a liquid state (temp. 40 -60 °C, pressure 10 -17 bars). - Thermostatic expansion valve - Expansion phase - the fluid loses pressure (0.5 - 2 bar, possibly even 3 bar) becomes a gas + liquid mixture; the temperature is low, typical of air conditioning. - Evaporator - Evaporation phase - the fluid becomes completely gaseous because the hot air driven by the fan finds itself at a higher temperature than the refrigerant fluid and causes it to boil and evaporate completely giving off heat. The temperature is low, typical of air conditioning (pressure 0.5 - 2 bar). Operating strategy The principle on which the temperature control is based is linked to the "EQUIVALENT TEMPERATURE" concept. A control based on the equivalent temperature concept does not try and keep the passenger compartment at a constant temperature, but tries to maintain the user's feeling of heat. The thermal sensation depends on all the thermal energy exchanges with the environment and is estimated by the climate control system control unit on the basis of ambient parameters. In particular, inside a VEHICLE, it depends on the following: - Average temperature in the passenger compartment - Temperature of the air sent to the passenger compartment interior - Temperature of the walls and surfaces exposed to passengers (dashboard, seats, etc.) - Air flow rate in the passenger compartment - Sun's rays There is a sensor to measure the sun's rays, which acquires a bilateral signal (left-right) which contributes towards determining the comfort conditions in terms of air distribution and temperature. The only action that the user has to take is to identify and select an equivalent temperature value that is comfortable for them and, irrespective of outside conditions, the system will work to adjust all the variables under its control to ensure the desired thermal sensation. The system automatically adjusts the following parameters/functions: - air temperature at the vents - air distribution - air flow rate in the passenger compartment - compressor enablement - recirculation All these functions can be modified manually, in other words the user can intervene and select one or more functions at will: in this way the user removes the control of the functions selected manually from the automatic system (with the system unable to intervene unless it is for safety reasons) to guarantee the requested equivalent temperature. Air mixture control The control of the outlet air temperature at the vents is fairly important in the adaptation of the Equivalent Temperature to the value set with reference to comfort conditions. This check is carried out by activating the mixture flap. The movement of the mixture actuator is filtered so that movements that are too quick cannot take place thereby preventing unpleasant fluctuations in temperature. Air flow rate control Another fundamental parameter for reaching and maintaining the Equivalent Temperature at the value set is the control of the outlet air flow rate at the vents. This check is carried out by activating the fan speed control. For this purpose the control algorithm calculates a flow rate figure dependent on the previous flow rate and the difference between the objective equivalent temperature and the one measured. Similarly to the calculation of the Mixture, in this case too the value of the flow rate is filtered so that variations that are too rapid are not produced; a "seasonal" parameter is also taken into consideration to adapt the operation of the fan depending on whether it is summer or winter. Use of the system As described previously, the climate control system control system is based on the equivalent temperature and works to stabilize the thermal sensation inside the passenger compartment (compensating for any variation in the outside climate conditions). The user has to identify and select an equivalent temperature value that they are comfortable with and, irrespective of outside conditions (it does not matter whether it is summer or winter, sunny or raining), the system will work, adjusting all the variables in its power to ensure the desired thermal sensation. - To check that the system control is fully prepared for automatic operation, make sure that the words FULL AUTO are shown on the display. To produce the fully automatic conditions, press the AUTO buttons which enable the automatic adjustment functions: DISTRIBUTION, AIR FLOW RATE, COMPRESSOR ENABLEMENT, RECIRCULATION MANAGEMENT. If the air flow rate or distribution is selected manually, the word FULL will disappear; if the compressor is disabled manually the LED will go out: if the system is capable, depending on the ambient temperature, of keeping the comfort level constant, the word AUTO will remain on, otherwise it will go out. - The compressor button enables the COMPRESSOR ON/OFF function When the compressor is working, the user is guaranteed not only the possibility of cooling the temperature of the passenger compartment (especially in hot weather), but also the chance of dehumidifying the air (preventing the problem of the windows misting up, especially in cold weather). The compressor, however, cannot work when the outside temperature is low. In this case, to prevent problems of misting up, the system forces the dynamic air intake leaving the button enabled (this way the user can set it how they want). In any case, if there visibility problems linked to the windscreen misting up, it is a good idea to check that the recirculation button LED is off. The recirculation button can be managed manually or automatically. Automatic management of the recirculation is also connected (if present) to the air quality sensor (AQS) which, on recognizing the pollutant factors present in the air, closes the recirculation automatically. If there is no AQS, the automatic management of the recirculation is carried out with a view to improving the thermal adjustment transitions. The exchange of air inside the passenger compartment is also guaranteed (every 25 minutes consecutively with the recirculation on, the system moves automatically to outside air for a period of 60 seconds). When the AQS sensor is present, it is disabled automatically at low outside temperatures to prevent the windscreen from misting up. The user, using the rolling recirculation button, can, on exiting from the fully automatic function, re-enable the operation of the AQS sensor. The information transmitted by the AQS is compared by the system with the information from the (optional) DEFOG sensor (which controls the degree of humidity present on the windscreen). If the windscreen is misted up and the compressor is disabled, the system forces the recirculation open for safety reasons (the priority of the system is obviously to ensure good visibility for the driver). To switch the system off, keep the speed rocker switch pressed at the "-" symbol until the word OFF appears on the display. When the system is OFF, the passenger compartment is insulated from the outside (recirculation closed, LED in the button on). The recirculation can, however, be opened (to allow outside air to enter the passenger compartment) by pressing the recirculation button (switching off the LED). The system contains pre-defined functions that determine specific operation in certain conditions. - LO function. When a temperature of less than 16°C is set, the "maximum cooling" condition is produced; in these circumstances the system is in MONO operation, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are activated: temperature regulator in maximum cold position, front air distribution, air flow rate at seasonal maximum, compressor enablement, recirculation as requested by user. - HI function. When a temperature of more than 32°C is set, the "maximum heating" condition is produced; in these circumstances the system is in MONO operation, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are activated: temperature regulator in maximum hot position, air distribution to feet, air flow rate at seasonal maximum, compressor managed according to logic (depending on whether rest is more than 2°C), recirculation as requested by user. - MAX DEF function. When the specific button (7) is pressed, the system switches to MONO, the words FULL and AUTO go out and the following actions are implemented: temperature regulator in maximum hot position, air distribution to the windscreen, increase in the air flow rate (if the temperature of the engine is sufficiently high), compressor function enabled (LED on), recirculation forced open, HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN activated (LED on). Functions Temperature setting control knob Knob for setting passenger compartment temperature (zone by zone). By turning the knob for the desired zone (driver/passengers) the desired passenger compartment temperature can be increased (clockwise direction) or decreased (anti-clockwise direction). The increases/decreases are in steps of 0.5 ºC and one complete revolution of the knob produces 24 steps. The temperature settings are memorized at the key off and then restored at the next key on. The temperature range can be set between 16 and 32 ºC; below 16 ºC the value set becomes «LO» whilst above 32 ºC the value set becomes «HI». If the user sets a temperature below the outside temperature, with the compressor button disabled, the system is not capable of reaching it or maintaining it and this impossibility is signalled by the Temperature setting flashing. Hi condition The HI condition is reached by setting a temperature above 32 ºC. This request by the user switches off the words FULL and AUTO, forces the system to MONO and involves the following actions: - Mixer in fully hot position. - Distribution towards the feet. - Air flow rate increase (if the temperature of the engine is sufficiently high). - Recirculation remains as requested by user. Manual settings are allowed in the HI condition. Exiting the MONO condition using the button determines exiting the HI function and the temperature setting of 32° C for both zones. If the driver turns the temperature setting this moves the passenger setting out of HI to 32° C If the passenger turns the temperature setting this also moves the driver's setting out of HI (to 32ºC), then changing their own settings placing the system in the 2/3 zone mode. Lo condition The LO condition is reached by setting a temperature below 16 ºC. This request by the user switches off the words FULL and AUTO, forces the system to MONO and involves the following actions: - Mixer in max cold position. - Air distribution to the dashboard - Air flow rate increase - Compressor enablement Manual settings are allowed in the LO condition. Exiting the MONO condition using the button determines exiting the LO function and the temperature setting of 16° C for both zones. If the driver turns the temperature setting this moves the passenger setting out of LO to 16° C If the passenger turns the temperature setting this also moves the driver's setting out of LO (to 16ºC), then changing their own settings placing the system in the Dual Zone mode. The flashing logic is valid, if the compressor is disabled after the LO request and the forced recirculation is automatic if it was not already. Auto button Pressing this button restores the automatic operation of the following functions - Air distribution - Fan speed - Compressor - Recirculation The words FULL AUTO lit up indicate that all the above mentioned functions are controlled automatically. The word FULL goes out in the area considered when a Distribution manoeuvre is carried out manually. The word FULL goes out in all the zones when a manual operation is carried out on the flow rate, compressor or recirculation. The word AUTO also goes out if the control system (mainly when the compressor is manually disabled) does not reach or maintain the required temperature. The button that disables the Compressor does not switch off the word AUTO when the system is capable of maintaining the desired comfort. Distribution buttons There are 7 possible positions for the air distribution (VENT, BI-LEVEL, HEAT, FLOOR, DEF, HI-LEVEL, TRI-LEVEL). In Automatic mode the system manages the distribution and does not display its selection. One of the 7 positions can be selected manually by activating the buttons according to the following combination logic: - Main Distributions: DEF VENT FLOOR - Combined Distributions BI-LEVEL HEAT HI-LEVEL TRI-LEVEL With the combined distribution activated, the LED goes out when one of the two buttons is pressed. With the main distribution activated (one LED on), when the same button is pressed the existing distribution is confirmed. Recirculation The recirculation button operates with a ROLLING logic. By pressing the AUTO button, automatic management of the recirculation is selected - Automatic The A in the button lights up This informs the user that the recirculation is managed automatically to improve the thermodynamic comfort; in addition, if an AQS sensor is fitted, it is also dependent on the quality of the air. For safety reasons (e.g. windows misted up, long periods of closure), A is switched off to signal the deactivation of the automatic control. When A is switched off, it is possible to select automatic operation using the recirculation rolling button and exiting from the system fully automatic mode. - Recirculation forced closed With this type of manual operation, the red LED signals the closure of the recirculation flap. - Recirculation forced open (outside air) With this type of manual operation, the red LED off signals the forced opening of the outside air flap. This mode should be selected if the windows are misted up. Air flow rate variation control The air flow rate can be adjusted manually in steps, which are displayed as one bar for every 2 steps up to a maximum of 6 bars when it then goes out. If there have been no manual interventions, the fan speed is controlled continuously by the system and this is shown on the display by the relevant number of bars lighting up according to the flow rate. If the ventilation control is operated manually, the FULL AUTO condition is exited. In particular, to increase or decrease the fan speed, press the rocker switch on the + and - symbols. At the key on, if the control unit is controlling the air flow rate Automatically, this air flow rate corresponds to the 1st bar (minimum flow rate) until the engine is started. If the compressor is disabled, the ventilation control can be operated manually until the display shows 0 bar. If the compressor is enabled and the engine started, the manual ventilation cannot go below 1 bar on the display because with the compressor enabled there must be a minimum air flow rate to prevent ice from forming in the evaporator. Switching off the control unit (off) Operating the air flow rate control (decrease) below 0 bars (fan off) causes the word OFF only to light up on the display. The following actions take place in OFF: - memorizing of the current state - switching off of the display (with the exception of the OFF symbol) - closed recirculation and relevant LED lit up - compressor excluded - fan excluded - mixer in max cold position - distribution in Vent - in the OFF state the Heated Rear Windscreen button is managed normally without activating the climate control system. In the OFF condition the recirculation button is dual control (ON/OFF) opening (red LED off) and closing (red LED on) the flap, without managing the automatic operation (red LED off). Pressing the air flow rate control button at the + symbol or pressing any button (except for the Heated Rear Windscreen and Recirculation) or pressing any of the AUOT buttons, switches the system back on. When exiting from OFF, the recirculation returns to Automatic mode. Compressor enablement With the compressor enablement LED on, pressing the button switches the LED off and disables the compressor Once the button has been pressed, this selection remains memorized indefinitely even after the vehicle has been switched off, the same as for the other manual controls. The button is dual function: pressing it a second time re-enables the compressor and switches the LED on. With the compressor disabled, the system checks whether the outside temperature is higher or lower than/the same as the temperature set: - if the outside temperature is less than the temperature set then the system works normally and is capable of complying with the request even without the compressor being switched on; - of the outside temperature is higher than the temperature set then the system is not capable of complying with the request and signals this by making the temperature settings flash. The control (system with compressor disabled and outside temperature higher than temperature set) is activated at the key on. Mono Pressing the MONO button determines the following action: - the temperature set by the passenger made is made the same as that set by the driver and the LED comes on. From that moment the system behaves like a single zone system. Pressing the MONO button again or altering the temperature set by the passenger causes the following results: - the MONO button LED goes out and there is a shift to dual zone temperature control. Max def The Max-Def function is also managed with the engine switched off. The following operations are activated: - Max-Def LED lit up - memorizing of the function state and previous displays of Max-Def control - words FULL and AUTO switched off and automatic recirculation (if on) - switching on of the DEF distribution, compressor enablement, MONO and HEATED REAR WINDSCREEN LEDs - display of fully hot temperature (HI) - display of the ventilation in the front display - switching off of the rear panel - activation of the following controls - air flow rate increase (with coolant temperature sufficiently hot) - air distribution in Def position (before implementing the mix) - forced air intake open (dynamic) - compressor function enabled - AQS disabled (if present) - rear windscreen defrosting When exiting from Max-Def the mix is implemented first and then the distribution. During the operation of the Max-Def it is possible to: - Alter the air flow rate (up/down) at will - Deactivate the heated rear windscreen It is not possible to - Alter the temperature setting (driver/passengers) - Alter the distribution setting It is possible to interrupt the Max-Def function by activating any one of the climate control buttons (Recirculation, Compressor, AUTO, MONO, Max-Def) implementing the return to the prior to the Max-Def plus the implementation of the control for the button pressed. Heated rear windscreen The defrosting of the rearscreen is activated both through the special button and through the Max-Def procedure. The display of the function status takes place through the LED switching on/off. The function requesting the activation of the heated rear windscreen is only subject to the key-on condition. Intake air quality sensor (aqs) The AQS sensor (available on request for the automatic climate control system) is an electronic device that is designed to supply a signal to the climate control unit when the air pollution index exceeds a preset danger level. The control unit manages the automatic recirculation function to prevent the introduction of polluted air into the passenger compartment. The sensitive element of the sensor is capable of detecting the presence of oxidizing particles (e.g. CO) or reducing particles (e.g. NOx) in the flow or air entering the vehicle. Misting sensor (fog sensor) This sensor (available on request for the automatic climate control system) is housed in the area of the interior rear view mirror with the sensitive element facing the interior surface of the windscreen/ An electronically managed optical system makes it possible to detect the degree of misting of the windscreen and provides a series of signals for the control unit depending on the pre-set intervention levels. The signal is represented by a train of impulses with a Duty Cycle that varies between 10% and 90%. We wish to point out that the misting sensor is enabled at every Key-on and therefore if the windscreen is (even partly) misted up the climate control is automatically activated even if it is turned OFF. When the automatic climate control system control unit is turned on the sensor can be disabled by one of several manual methods. Expansion valve The tasks of this valve are to: - Separate the high pressure circuit from the low pressure circuit; - Expand the refrigerant (change in state from liquid to gas); - Regulate the evaporation process (flow rate); - Regulate the evaporation temperature; - Protect the compressor from refrigerant fluid. The thermostatic expansion valve is fitted on the evaporator inlet and outlet ducts with the task of regulating the flow and expansion (drop in pressure) of the R134a fluid before entry into the evaporator. The automatic regulation of the size of the passage for the gas inside the expansion valve is produced by a sensitive bulb which measures the temperature of the refrigerant fluid and depending on this suitably adjusts the size of the opening that the gas passes through by means of a special spring that moves a shutter determining the extent of the expansion. The increase in temperature at the evaporator outlet, detected by the bulb, ensures that the valve is opened with a consequent increase in the flow rate of the fluid in the evaporator. Conversely, low temperatures involve a reduction in the size of the gas port determining a decrease in the flow of gas. The expansion valve is directly accessible from the engine compartment. Linear pressure switch The linear pressure switch makes sure the system is working properly. By continuously analyzing the pressure of the climate control system circuit, the sensor provides the engine management control unit, in real time, wih the variations in pressure making the management of the activation levels more flexible. For each variation in pressure there is a corresponding voltage signal used by the engine management control unit to activate the fan speed and switch off the compressor if the pressure increases or decreases beyond the permitted limits (safety function). The operating range of the linear sensor goes from 3.018 bar up to 29.508 bar according to the following pressure (bar) / output voltage percentage (%Vcc) curve. The go ahead for the activation of the compressor and the adjustment of the fan speed, depending on the variation in pressure, takes place in this pressure range; the compressor is deactivated above and below these values for safety reasons to prevent damage to the system.
