“BLUE & ME “ BLUE&ME based on Windows Mobile is a personal telematic system which allows the use of applications for communication and entertainment, specially designed for use in vehicles. The BLUE&ME system is available in two versions: - standard version, with hands-free function for Bluetooth mobile phones with voice commands, SMS voice player and media player with USB port - BLUE&ME Nav de-luxe version which, in addition to the previous functions, includes a satellite navigation system which uses the USB port, with map pre-loading and shows the navigation information on the control panel reconfigurable multifunction display. The BLUE&ME Nav de-luxe version is described in See descriptions 5580M ON-BOARD NAVIGATOR "BLUE&ME" HANDS-FREE SYSTEM The "BLUE&ME" system includes hands-free preparation for Bluetooth mobile phones with voice commands and a multimedia MP3 player with a USB port. Thanks to its complete integration with the voice commands, the controls on the steering wheel and the information in the on board multifunction display information, the Blue&Me system allows Customers who have a mobile phone with Bluetooth to use it even if it is in their jacket pocket or handbag without ever having to take their hands off the steering wheel. In order to use the voice commands the voice recognition system does not require any preparation process. The system is capable of recognizing the voice commands given, irrespective of gender, by the tone of voice and intonation of the person giving the instructions. It is possible to listen to music stored on a USB device, selecting the tracks and play modes using either the controls on the steering wheel or voice commands. The C1 v2 version control unit includes the following modules: - Bluetooth receiver - integrated voice recognition module - Text to Speech integrated module - USB interface - SMS message voice reader. The alphanumerical display used for text messages is the one for the control panel. See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS An example of a screen is illustrated. The control unit is then connected to the controls on the steering (in addition to the radio control buttons there are 2 specific buttons for this function). List of controls on the steering wheel functions Key Short press (less than 1 second) Prolonged press (longer than 1 second) 1 - Activation of Blue&Me Main Menu - Confirmation of menu option selected - Accept incoming phone call - Change from one telephone conversation to another in second call mode (call notification) - Selection of message displayed - Refuse incoming phone call - Ending of phonecall in progress 2 - Deactivation of voice recognition - Interruption of voice message - Interruption of SMS message reading - Exit from Blue&Me Main Menu - Exit from a sub menu and return to the previous menu option - Exit from the current selection with memorizing - Deactivation/reactivation of the microphone during a phone conversation - Resetting the volume of the call tone for the incoming phonecall - Activation/Deactivation of multimedia player pause function 3 - Activation of the voice recognition - Interruption of the voice message in order to give a new voice command Repetition of the last voice message given by the system 4 Adjustment of audio volume for Blue&Me functions: hands-free, multimedia player, voice announcements 5 - Scrolling through Blue&Me menu items - Scrolling through SMS messages in the list - Direct access to multimedia player menu during display of information relating to audio track being played 6 - Selection of multimedia player tracks - Selection of message displayed 7 - Confirmation of menu option selected during manual interaction - Transfer of the telephone conversation in progress from the hands-free system to the mobile phone and vice versa - Audio source selection (Radio, CD, CD Changer, Multimedia Player) For both operating modes for the controls on the steering wheel (short or prolonged press), the function is activated when the button is released. Connection with bluetooth telephone The system is connected to a mobile phone with a Bluetooth interface and hands-free profile. The first connection between the mobile phone and the device (pairing procedure) is regulated by a password; the user connects by keying in the password into their own mobile phone in the menu for Bluetooth connections. It is possible to memorize up to 5 users who are connected automatically at subsequent keys on without manual intervention on behalf of the actual user. In each case, only one mobile phone can be connected to the control unit via Bluetooth. The operation of the control unit is linked to the availability of the user's mobile phone for Bluetooth hands-free profiles, in particular: - the Bluetooth system comes on independently at the Key on and starts the search for Bluetooth (mobile) devices to connect with immediately. - the equipment switches off independently at the Key off releasing any Bluetooth connection that may be activated: there is a delay of 30 seconds (provisional figure) to suppress accidental switching off of the engine (in traffic, at traffic lights, etc.). - if a phonecall is in progress, the conversation is kept activated (except for the display in the control panel) even after the car is switched off; the control unit and the radio finally switch off at the end of the conversation. List of compatible mobile phones The current hands-free system with Bluetooth technology is compatible with all mobile phones that support Bluetooth 1.1 and a 1.0 hands-free probile (refer to the Bluetooth connection specifications in the mobile phone user manual). As a result of the different possible software versions available on the market for different models of mobile phone, some additional functions (e.g.: second call management, call transfer from hands-free system to mobile phone and vice versa, etc.) may not correspond exactly to the description in the mobile phone user manual. INTRODUCTION The Cruise Control system automatically maintains a cruising speed set by the driver. It consists of a lever on the steering wheel stalk unit with two rotary wheels and a button. The lever is connected to the engine control unit that manages system operation. Operation is controlled by means of the RES (resume) button besides the lever, vertical operation of the lever (set +/set -) and the on/off wheel: 1 - RES (resume) button recalls a stored speed 2 - wheel switch (Cruise symbol: Cruise attivated; O: Cruise deactivated) 3 - movement of lever to store increase (+) or decrease (-) OPERATION The system governs engine operation - and more specifically the motorised throttle - directly so that a constant engine speed can be maintained independently of changes in driving conditions. The driver performs the following controls: - stores speed achieved, discrete and continuous speed increase (set +); - stores speed achieved, discrete and continuous speed dcrease (set -); - recalls stored speed (resume). A warning light on the dashboard activated by the engine control unit indicates system operation or deactivation status. To activate the system, operate the main switch (On / Off) to On position. Then adjust the vehicle to the required speed and operate the wheel to + or - : the system comes on at the current speed; the accelerator may be released to allow the Cruise Control system to act alone. System adjustment does not cut in under the following circumstances: - neutral, reverse, 1st gear, with manual gearbox; - n, reverse, 1st gear, with robotised gearbox; - N, P, R, 1st gear, with automatic gearbox; The Cruise control can also be activated only at speeds greater than 40 km/h. The system operates throughout the permitted engine rpm range and controls cars with manual or automatic/robotised gearboxes. It is nevertheless advisable to turn it on at speeds greater than equal to IVth gear with manual gearboxes, with road conditions that allow the set speed to be safely maintained. The driver can always temporarily disable the Cruise control system by simply operating the brake or clutch: if the "res" (resume) button is pressed, the vehicle returns to the speed conditions originally set in its memory. Cruise control is not disabled when the accelerator is pressed (e.g. to overtake) and automatically restores the vehicle to the set speed as soon as the accelerator is released. Turning off the main switch turns off the system and clears any speed set previously. Cruise control manual deactivation conditions The Cruise control system can be deactivated by the following driver manoeuvres: - turning off engine or key-off; - main wheel switch in off position; - brake operation: the latest speed is stored and can be recalled by mean of the RES key; - clutch operation: the latest speed is stored and can be recalled by mean of the RES key; - autoamtic transmission lever set to N,P,R: the latest speed is stored and can be recalled by mean of the RES key; - vehicle speed below the set limit (40 km/h): the latest speed is stored and can be recalled by mean of the RES key; - accelerator operation: in this case the system is not effectively turned off but the acceleration request takes priority so that the driver can perform the required manoeuvre; the Cruise control remains active but without the need to press the RES key to return to the previous conditions once the acceleration is concluded. Cruise control automatic deactivation conditions The Cruise control turns off automatically under the following circumstances: - accidental or incorrect operation of the keys on the lever; - acceleration higher than a set limit (in this case, the Cruise control may be reset by operating the set +/- wheel after restoring the vehicle to the required speed). Diagnosis The system turns off automatically when the signals used by the Cruise Control software are incorrect because they are due to component defects: - vehicle speed sensor; - accelerator pedal potentiometer; - brake/brake light switch plausibility; - clutch switch plausibility; - lever position on automatic transmissions; - Cruise control switch plausibility and Resume key; - Cruise control switch plausibility and (+) (-) keys; The Cruise Control system is also deactivated if errors occur in components that impair engine operation, namely: - engine management control unit; - engine rpm sensor; - electronic throttle body sensors/actuators); - Ignition coils (for petrol engines), - injectors; - hgh pressure system components (for diesel engines); In this case, the engine control unit must be tested and repaired using diagnostic instruments during Service (Examiner). CRUISE CONTROL COMMANDS The lever containing the Cruise Control commands is part of the steering wheel stalk unit but connected to a specific connection. PASSIVE SAFETY SYSTEM Introduction The vehicle is equipped with an electronic control system that governs the activation of specific containment devices in the event of frontal or side impact: The frontal protection system includes: - driver and passenger front air bags with two-stage activation; - single-stage driver's knee bag, single-stage passenger's knee bag (option); - front belts with pretensioner and regressive load limiter; - direct mesh rear seat belts (without idler ring) and strap buckle branches - decentralised supplementary front impact detection sensor; - passenger air bag manual disabling switch. The side protection system comprises: - two sidebags under the fabric on the front seats; - two drop-down headbags housed in the under-roof rails (not present on Spider versions); - two impact detection sensors located in the central pillar. The front protection system features new Air Bag Smart 2 activation software that automatically adapts activation parameters according to impact severity. Driver and passenger front airbags feature two-stage activation: - when the impact is of moderate severity, the electronic control unit controls the first airbag activation stage and then, following a significant temperature increase, the second stage so that the energy discharged onto the occupant is not harmful. - for very severe impact, the control unit activates the second stage after a small temperature rise, i.e. almost immediately, so that as much of the occupant's kinetic energy as possible can be absorbed before he or she strikes the steering wheel or dashboard. A supplementary ECS “Early Crash Sensor” on the front beam near the bonnet lock also helps the electronic control unit to operate more quickly than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is completed before the occupant's body begins to move towards the steering wheel or dashboard. The Air Bag system components are designed to work on a specific vehicle. They therefore CANNOT be tampered with, adapted or installed on other types of vehicle. The car must be handed over to the customer with the passenger airbag deactivation switch in the ON position and control panel warning light off. For safety reasons, NO continuity checks can be carried out on the wiring. The electrical connection between the airbag system components is via dedicated wiring integral with the dashboard cable loom and the rear cable loom. The control unit is connected to the system via two connectors, one for the dashboard lead and the other for the rear lead. The control unit is connected to the vehicle CAN, through which it exchanges information with other nodes, turns on warning lights in the dashboard and the front courtesy light and performs diagnostic operations. Because the control unit is a node in the CAN, the airbag system is connected: - to the standard diagnostic socket via the CAN and not the dedicated K line; - to the instrument panel, again via the CAN, to control the airbag system failure warning light; - to the Body Computer for potential end of line customisation (Proxy) with a consequent reduction in the number of spare parts. The control unit also controls the "seat belt unfastened" buzzer and the "seat belt unfastened" and "passenger airbag deactivated" warning lights on the front courtesy light via a direct connection. GRAVE DANGER! The front airbag module MUST be deactivated if a child seat is fitted to the front passenger seat. If the vehicle is equipped with a side bag, deactivation of the front passenger side airbag module does not disable the side modules. This means that any children carried in the car are protected against side impact. Composition The system consists of the following devices: - an electronic control unit; - two (driver and passenger) front air bags with dual stage activation, - a driver's knee bag with single-stage activation as standard, - a driver's knee bag with single-stage activation as an option, - an ECS decentralised supplementary impact detection sensor (Early Crash Sensor), - passenger air bag manual disabling switch, - two sidebags under the fabric on the front seats; - two Window Bag modules for side protection of the occupants (not present on Spider versions); - two side impact sensors in the side pillars; - two electronic pretensioners on the front belt reel. The following indications show the system is working properly: - system fault warning light (red) in the instrument panel: - passenger air bag disabled warning light on the front courtesy light; - front seat belts not fastened warning light (in the front courtesy light until JAN 06 and later on in the instrument panel) - connection via B- CAN with the diagnostic socket - integral with the Body Computer - to test operation via the EXAMINER. 1. Front occupant seat belt unfastened warning light Electronic control unit The following diagram shows the control unit. 1 - Electronic control unit 2 - Indication showing direction of motion The control unit is the central occupant protection processing unit and is fastened rigidly to the vehicle floor pan near the central tunnel. It manages all the containment system detection and activation devices by processing signals from the various sensors distributed throughout the vehicle and internal sensors. The control unit should always be fitted with the arrow, stamped on the adhesive plate, facing the direction of travel of the vehicle. Always check that there are no foreign bodies between the control unit and the bodyshell and tighten the fixing bolts to the recommended torque. If the control unit falls to the ground or is subject to abnormal knocks during handling, it MUST be replaced. Composition The control unit contains an electronic deceleration sensor that enables safety device activation. This sensor consists of two-directional accelerometers that are part of the ECS front sensor and power the operation of the side sensors. Operation Frontal impact: When the impact is of moderate severity, the electronic control unit controls the first airbag activation stage and then, following a significant temperature increase, the second stage so that the energy discharged onto the occupant is not harmful. Conversely, in the case of very severe impact, the control unit activates both stages almost simultaneously to absorb most of the kinetic energy from the occupant's body before it strikes the steering wheel or dashboard. The supplementary ECS sensor also allows the airbag to be activated earlier than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is completed before the occupant's body begins to move toward the steering wheel or dashboard. Side impact: Similarly, when side impact occurs, the control unit is able to recognise direction and intensity and thus activate both airbags present on the side affected by impact. To provide total cover against side impacts, two satellite sensors located in the centre pillars are used. When a side impact takes place, the satellite sensors detect the impact signal directly along the transverse axis of the vehicle and send it to the control unit. When processed by the control unit microprocessor, this signal reveals the severity of the side impact and is thus able to decide whether to operate the sidebags on the affected side, only if the control unit safety sensor enables the activation. The side airbags (window bag and Side Bag) are activated simultaneously and independently of the front safety devices. After each activation of one of the controlled systems (pretensioners, front airbags, sidebags), the control unit stores the activation in its permanent memory and controls activation of the fault warning light on the instrument panel. Before it is replaced, the control unit guarantees activation of individual devices within the following limits: - 3 impacts with activation of front seat belt pretensioners alone; - 3 impacts in total (right or left) with side bag activation; - 1 impact with activation of the pretensioners and front airbags; - any combination of the above cases up to the maximum number. If one of the limits described is not reached, it will be possible to reuse the control unit after carrying out the RESET procedure using the EXAMINER once system operating conditions have been restored. The final activation, corresponding to the maximum number for the limits indicated above, will prevent further reset procedures. Self-diagnosis The control unit carries out continuous self-diagnosis of system operation. More specifically: - it detects and stores faults; - it diagnoses connnections to system components and any type of fault that has occurred; - it indicates the source of these faults by turning on an instrument panel warning light. Faults stored in the control unit may be deleted only after the fault has been repaired by means of the EXAMINER device. If a fault is detected in the passenger airbag disablement switch, the control unit treats is as though it is off for safety reasons. Module operation is therefore inhibited and the instrument panel warning light is turned on. Driver's air bag module 1 - Cover 2 - Containment case 3 - Gas generator 4 - Retaining rings 5 - Bag Specifications The driver's air bag is a passive safety device. It takes the form of a bag that inflates automatically in the case of frontal impact to interpose itself between the driver's body and front passenger compartment structures. The Air Bag module is installed in the middle of the steering wheel. The module cover also acts as a horn control. Composition The module comprises: - a plastic cover that tears at preset points when activated to allow the bag to expand correctly. - a 60 litre bag, made out of nylon thread woven to minimse skin abrasions in the case of contact and folded in such a way as to ensure that inflation is gradual and not directed toward the driver; - two pyrotechnic type gas generators; - a containment case. Operation Bag inflation is determined by a gas generator that offers two intervention stages that can be activated separately according to impact severity. Each gas generator is activated by two electrical resistances that burn propellent inside the generator to allow the bag to expand. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. Bag deflation is immediate, due to two holes present in the lower part of the bag. This holes also soften contact between passenger and bag to avoid the risk of abrasions. The device consists of two plates and is built into the stalk unit via its lower plate. It is secured in place by means of fasteners on the upper plate. Inside the two plates, the leads connecting the module and horn buttons are wound in a coil so that they can follow steering wheel movements. Two of these are used to connect the air bag module (first and second stage) and one to connect the steering wheel electrical functions (horn, radio controls). A ring on the lower plate, steering wheel side, automatically prevents both plate from turning in relation to one another hwen the device is disconnected from the steering wheel. The new clock spring is equipped with a safety key for transport, which must be removed after installation. Operation Inside the two plates, the leads connecting the air bag module and the various electrical functions are wound into a spiral with sufficient coils to follow the steering wheel rotations. The upper plate is turned by fasteners on the inside of the retaining ring that fit into the seat on the steering wheel hub. In a working position, the steering wheel presses on the ring to release it from its fasteners and thus allow both plates to turn freely. When the steering wheel is removed, the spring-loaded ring locks rotation between both plates. This function prevents the upper plate, now no longer secured to the steering wheel, from turning freely and unwinding or winding the coil inside the device and possibly causing it to break. The following must be observed during operations that require removal of the steering wheel and device. - always work with the car's wheels aligned straight ahead; - secure both plates with a band for safety before removing the device from the steering wheel stalk unit. If the upper plate should turn in relation to the lower plate for any reason so that the exact starting position is no longer certain, the clock spring MUST be replaced. Passenger air bag module 1 - Bag 2 - Gas generator 3 - Connector Specifications The passenger airbag module is a passive safety device that protects the front passenger in the event of front impact by means of a bag that interposes itself between the occupant and the vehicle dashboard. Composition The module comprises: - a metal containment mount; - a paper bag protection that opens along predefined tear marks in the event of activation to allow the bag to emerge; - a 120 litre bag in nylon, a fabric that minimises skin abrasions in the event of contact. The bag is folded so that it does not inflate directly towards the occupant. - two pyrotechnic type gas generators; - bag guide brackets; Operation The passenger airbag operates in exactly the same way as the driver's side airbag. Bag inflation opens the flap in the dashboard along predefined cut lines. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. The braids inside the airbag unfold in such a way as to allow inflation to the maximum specified dimensions to prevent collateral damaging effects on passengers. Inflation is immediate due to the presence of vent holes in the end of the bag. Passenger side airbag disablement key switch A key switch at the end of the dashboard on the passenger side (accessible only with the door open) allows the user to deactivate the passenger airbag so that a child seat can be installed without problems. On the front seats, child seats are positioned facing towards the back of the car. Operation A switch operated by means of the emergency key in the TEG allows enablement (ON) and disablement (OFF) of the air bag module on the passenger side. In this case, the control unit cuts out passenger air bag activation but enables normal operation of the pretensioner (only with seat belt fastened) and the side bags. This happens because if a passenger is present but the switch has been left OFF by accident, the air bag will not activate - only the pretensioner. Deactivation is indicated by a warning light on the front courtesy light coming on. 1 - Key-operated switch 2 - OFF position: Passenger air bag disabled 3 - ON position: Passenger air bag enabled 4 - Passenger side disablement warning light Composition The unit consists of a case that houses the switch, a key barrel inserted in the case and held in place by a clip and a plate that indicates the positioned assumed by the switch (ON or OFF). Switch faults are indicated by activation of the air bag system fault warning light. During the normal key on diagnostic procedure (4 seconds), the electronic control unit checks switch status. if the status detected is OFF, it excludes the module from activation, stores the corresponding signal and controls activation of the relevant warning light on the instrument panel. If the recognised status is ON, the warning light flashes for an additional four seconds at the end of the four second diagnostic procedure and then goes off. In the case of switch anomalies or faults, the system reacts as follows: - passenger side module is not activated - air bag system fault warning light comes on - passenger side air bag module disablement warning light comes on - deactivation status is saved. The switch is not operated with the ignition key ON (e.g. using the second key). In this case, the electronic control unit saves an error, indicates it by turning on the air bag system fault warning light and deactivates the module. Knee air bag module 1 - Outer cover 2 - Bag 3 - Gas generator 4 - Generator mount 5 - Mounting plate 6 - Safety plate Specifications Two air bag modules are also fitted in the lower part of the dashboard in front of the passenger's knees and beneath the driver's steering wheel. These modules protect the lower limbs and increase protection for the driver and front passenger, particularly by preventing them from sliding forward, which is a possible cause of injury, particularly to the chest. Composition The knee bag module consists of a metal container that houses the gas generator and a nylon bag. The container is secured to a mounting plate and a safety plate that secures it rigidly to the lower part of the dashboard. Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is triggered that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The expanding gases emerge through openings to inflate the bag. When the bag is inflated, the bag is in an optimum position to perform its role of protecting the occupant. Bag deflation is immediate due to the presence of vent holes in the end of the bag. Side bag module 1 - Outer cover 2 - Fastening 3 - Gas generator 4 - Bag Specifications The front seats contain two side bag modules installed beneath the trim to increase the protection offered by the body in the event of side impact. This device ensures the airbag is always in an optimum position in relation to the occupant, regardless of the angle of the seat or the size of the occupant. The side bag protects the chest and pelvis areas and also - together with the door panels - protects critical areas of the body such as the ribs and abdomen. Its position on the seat always ensures maximum efficacy irrespective of seat position, even if the seat occupant is not seated correctly, because bag opening dynamics minimise the risk of body damage due to impact against the body. Do not cover the front seat backrest with extra covers. Do not wash the seat backrest with water or steam under pressure. Composition The side bag module consists of a metal container that houses the gas generator and a nylon bag with a volume of 12 litres. The plastic container includes a paper bag protetion with preset break points. When the backrest cover is fitted, the exterior of the trim in the area over the bags includes seams designed to yield easily to allow the bag to inflate. The module is connected to the electrical system by means of two leads with yellow sheaths. These are contained, together with the seat earth connection lead, in a protective fabric-lined duct secured to the seat structure. Both leads end in a connector that is secured to the floor beneath the seat. Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is triggered that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The gases expand and emerge through openings to inflate the bag. Bag inflation causes the weak seams in the backrest trim to yield and allow the bag to emerge. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. Bag deflation is immediate due to the presence of vent holes in the end of the bag. it is not possible to carry out operations on seats fitted with air bags, apart from seat removal/refitting. It is strictly forbidden to disassemble seats fitted with airbags. Window bag module (not present on spider versions) 1 - Connector 2 - Gas generator 3 - Fastening plates 4 - Bag retaining clips 5 - Bag 6 - Sealing brace Specifications The window bags are activated together with the sidebags and interpose themselves between the occupant and the vehicle to prevent the head coming into contact with highly intrusive objects such as glass, pillars etc. Because the window bags extend from the front pillar to the luggage compartment, they protect front and rear passengers. The window bag system offers the best performance due to the broad area covered and their ability to be self-supporting even without a backing. Composition The window bag module consists of: - a gas generator secured by mounts to the rear car pillar; - a flexible pipe in permeable cloth secured by a band to the gas generator that diffuses the gas evenly over the entire length of the bag; - a bag of about 30 litres in volume secured to the gas generator together with a flexible pipe. It is made out of permeable nylon and folded inside a containment sleeve. The bag is designed to ensure, once fully inflated, correct absorption of impact energy while maintaining the occupants' heads at a proper distance from the impact area. Once fully inflated, the gas leaves the bag immediately through the porous tissue. - plastic clips that secure the bag to the ceiling rail; - plastic plates to secure the bag onto the vehicle; - a retaining strap secured to the front pillar that holds the bag in position once inflated; Operation The gas generator is electrically activated by means of a signal from the electronic control module. Following this signal, a pyrotechnic activation is triggered that causes the gas in the generator to expand. The expanding gas emerges through special openings and is distributed evenly along the length of the bag through the hose to make the bag inflate. The increase in bag volume causes the fastening container to break, the sleeve seams to yield and the trim to open. Everything is arranged so that the bag emerges correctly downward. The bag is made to inflate correctly by a retaining strap on the front end of the bag. When fully inflated, the bag is in an optimal position to protect the occupant. The bag deflates immediately after being inflated by the gas because the fabric is permeable. Front impact satellite sensor Specifications A supplementary ECS “Early Crash Sensor” on the front beam near the bonnet lock also helps the electronic control unit to operate more quickly than a conventional system so that the airbag activation stage is comleted before the occupant's body begins to move towards the steering wheel or dashboard. Side impact satellite sensors Specifications The side protection system consists of the airbags and also an electronic control circuit that ensures the system operates correctly. Two satellite sensors containing an accelerometer are installed inside the side pillars to measure accelerations resulting from side impact. Operation If the acceleration level detected by the relevant sensor causes a given threshold to be exceeded, the information is compared with a measurement obtained by a safety sensor in the air bag system electronic control unit. If the measured values are consistent, the control unit controls activation of the side bags and window bags on the side affected by impact. Front seat belt pretensioners Specifications The pretensioners - located on the front seat belt reel - are pyrotechnic devices that are activated by a signal from the electronic control unit. Activation of the seat belt pretensioners is controlled by the same strategy as the air bags. The pretensioners are designed to take up slack in the seat belt to ensure it holds the occupant against the backrest from the first moments of impact, thus reducing movement inside the passenger compartment. The seat belts are also fitted with load limiters which decrease the force transmitted by the belts to the chest: the force level at which the limiters act is sufficient to considerably reduce the risk of fracturing shoulder blades and ribs, even in people with brittle bones (e.g. the elderly). Operation The following figure shows the pretensioner mechanism. 1 - Gas generator 2 - Electrical connector 3 - Belt 4 - Reel When the car decelerates to a sufficient extent, as measured by system acceleromters, the electronic sensor in the electronic control unit sends a signal to trigger the gas generator pyrotechnic charges. The combustion of the propellant produces a chemical reaction creating inert gas whose pressure produces a force that thrusts a piston upwards, changing the rotary movement of the reel into the opposite direction of the seat belt, rewinding it by a few centimetres. Once the pretensioners have been activated, the belts are locked and must be replaced. Airbag system warning lights 1 airbag system fault warning light on the instrument panel 2 passenger air bag disabled warning light on the front courtesy light; 3 warning light signalling seat belts not fastened, in the instrument panel (until JAN 06, in the front courtesy light) Air bag system fault warning light With the TEG inserted, the fault warning light (red) comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and then goes off. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the corresponding fault code. If no system faults are detected at key on and no fault conditions are present in the fault memory, the warning light goes off after four seconds of self-diagnosis. Otherwise it stays on. The warning light stays or comes on during normal car operation in the following cases: - the control unit detects a fault in the airbag system; - the control unit detects a crash with system activation; - when a fault is detected in the warning light connection circuit. As a consequence of a crash when the pretensioners or sidebags alone are activated, the warning light stays on until system operating conditions are restored (replacement of affected part or control unit repair using an EXAMINER) If the crash causes the front airbag modules to activate, the warning light stays on permanently because the control unit cannot reset (in this case the control unit must be replaced). If internal operating errors occur during the operational lifetime of the control unit that cannot be repaired by means of the EXAMINER, these are indicated by permanent activation of the warning light. Passenger air bag disabled warning light With the TEG inserted, the yellow passenger side air bag disabled warning light comes on for about four seconds (initial self-diagnosis stage) and flashes for the next 4 seconds. If the control unit detects a fault in the warning light, it saves the fault code, turns on the fault warning light and maintains the passenger side airbag module disabled. System operation is restored by means of an EXAMINER as with the fault warning light. Passenger side module disablement MUST be performed only with the TEG NOT INSERTED IN THE TEG READER: this operation causes an error to be stored in the control unit). Seat belt reminder "FIRST REMINDER CYCLE"; WARNING LIGHT SIGNAL The "seat belts" warning light signals that the (driver's or passenger or rear seat) seat belts are not fastened in accordance with the following strategy: - the warning light comes on in fixed mode, at key-on, if the seat belt has not already been fastened; - the warning light comes on in fixed mode if, with key on, the belt is unfastened (unless the following conditions apply, when the warning light should flash); - if the belt is already fastened, the warning light remains off at key on; - the warning light goes out if, the seat belt is fastened at key on. - the warning light should remain off at key off. The signalling via the warning light on constantly can never be excluded. "WARNING CYCLE": WARNING LIGHT AND HORN SIGNAL The warning cycle is activated for 90 seconds if, with the seat belt not fastened and the key inserted (key on status), at least one of the following conditions is verifed: - time elapsed equal to 30 secs and vehicle speed above 4 km/h - vehicle speed above 25 km/h - distance travelled more than 500 m The warning cycle consists of the warning light coming on in flashing mode (frequency of 2 Hz DC 50%) combined with an acoustic signal. Operation during the 90 second cycle: - if the seat belts are fastened, the warning cycle is interrupted immediately (the warning light goes out and the buzzer stops) and the system is ready for a new signal cycle. - if one of the three events that caused the activation of the warning cycle no longer exists, the cycle continues until the 90 secs have elapsed - if a further warning is required, the warning light indicates the new event by interrupting the current warning cycle (the acoustic signal stops and the seat belt reminder warning light changes from a flashing to a fixed light) and activating the new signal. The system then resumes the warning cycle prior to the new, most recent event. If the seat belt is fastened during the new event warning, the warning cycle ceases. - if the key is turned off, the warning cycle stops immediately. Operation after 90 seconds: if the seat belt unfastened status persists: - the acoustic signalling is deactivated - the warning light flashing cycle stops and the warning light remains on in fixed mode. The warning cycle is only carried out once, if the above mentioned conditions occur: then, at the end of the 90 second period, if the seat belt is still not fastened, it is not repeated. New warning signal: The warning cycle is only repeated when the seat belt not fastened condition is detected again (transition from seat belt fastened to seat belt not fastened) and one of the three conditions described previously is detected. Method for excluding the warning cycle (warning light flashing /horn) The user can deactivate the warning cycle temporarily by means of the following procedure: Within one minute of key-on, proceed as follows: - do up the driver and passenger side seat belts. To make the procedure easier, the seat belts can be fastened before the key on. - keep the belts fastened (simultaneously) for at least 20 s (with the TEG inserted). - unfasten at least one of the seat belts. The warning cycle will be automatically activated again at each new key on operation. The user can deactivate the warning cycle permanently only with the aid of the Technical Service dept. The deactivation procedure must be performed using a diagnostic instrument (Examiner) in communication with the control panel. Noone can deactivate the signal issued by the warning light on the dashboard. This is always present (fixed light) if the seat belt is unfastened.

ALFA ROMEO CODE SYSTEM The vehicles are equipped with an electronic system known as the ALFA CODE to produce the engine immobilizer function. The ALFA CODE system only allows the engine to be started by means of the NCM after a secret code, memorized previously in the NCM, is received. The second generation Code system is incorporated in the Body Computer Node (NBC). The ALFA CODE system comprises 5 basic components (in addition to the Body Computer which acts as a control unit): - CAN line for dialogue between the NBC and the NCM - two-way serial line for recovery (W line); - two TEG devices (electronic key) containing a transponder with a secret code; - an aerial that reads the code contained in the TEGs; - the NCM. 1 - NBC 2 - NCM 3 - Aerial in the TEG Reader 4 - TEG (electronic key) Operation The ALFA CODE allows the start of the engine management by the NCM by means of a coded dialogue between the NBC and NCM during the stage that precedes start up. After key on - i.e. TEG correctly inserted in the TEG Reader - the NCM sends a code request to the NBC, which responds only after it has identified (via its aerial) the presence of a known TEG in the TEG Reader. If the secret code in the answer is valid, the NCM continues with the regular engine management activities, allowing the engine to be started up. The NCM can only memorize the secret code through a special procedure. Operation of the ALFA CODE is guaranteed if any of the other NBC functions are not working properly. After recognizing an enabled transponder, the ALFA CODE switches off any alarm system. Interaction between the alfa code and the electronic key (teg) Every TEG contains a transponder with an IDENTIFICATION CODE and a SECRET CODE. As soon as the TEG is inserted, the transponder sends the identification code to the ALFA CODE which, having recognized it as one of the enabled ones, continues with the cryptographic transponder recognition strategy. If the identification code is not recognized, the procedure is aborted and the engine cannot be started. The cryptographic transponder is recognized by means of a challenge-response algorithm with an encrypted code exchange. The code recognition time is less than 160 ms per attempt. The ALFA CODE attempts transponder acquisition for up to 1 second. Communication between the engine control node and the alfa code Communication between the ALFA CODE (NBC) and NCM takes place via the C-CAN in normal service conditions. Every exchange of information between the ALFA CODE and the NCM is guided by the NCM (ALFA CODE never interrogates the NCM but only responds after receiving a request). After KEY-ON, the flow of code exchange operations between the ALFA CODE and the NCM depends on the status (blank or memorised) of the engine control unit. If the NCM is blank, the procedure involves sending a fix-code request to the NBC: in this way the NCM learns the secret code and stores it in its memory. This procedure is known as CODE RECORDING. If the NCM has already been stored, the procedure involves checking that the fix-code stored in the engine management control unit memory and the one memorized in the NBC correspond: the NCM asks the NBC for the secret code and compares it with its own. This procedure is known as CODE VERIFY. 1 - Key on 2 - NCM initialisation 3 - NCM status memorised/blank 4 - Memorisation successfully completed? 5 - ENABLE ENGINE MANAGEMENT = the software flow continues with engine management 6 - PROHIBIT ENGINE MANAGEMENT = activates a timer that imposes a delay to enable a new procedure only after 0 - 600 s. The +15 supply must be turned off and then on again. If no timer is available (con +30), it will be necessary to wait with key-on for 0 - 600 s. After this, a new procedure can be run, i.e. KEY- OFF and KEY-ON 7 - Is the secret code valid? 8 - SEE POINT 6 9 - SEE POINT 5 A - CODE VERIFY B - CODE RECORDING Code recording The CODE RECORDING procedure is the memorizing of the fix code in the engine control unit. Only after the ALFA CODE has memorized the identification codes, the secret code and the fix code, is it ready to satisfy the request to transmit a code from a blank NCM. After power on, the engine control unit initialises its software and requests a fix code if it is blank. If the ALFA CODE is not blank, it responds by sending the fix code, but only after having recognized an authorized TEG. If the TEG is not authorized (unrecognized) or there is no TEG inserted, the ALFA CODE does not respond. When the ALFA CODE is blank, the aerial contains no transponder and a PER (fix code request) is sent from the NCM to the ALFA CODE, the ALFA CODE does not respond. Code verify This standard procedure is repeated throughout the vehicle lifetime whenever the user inserts the TEG in the Reader (KEY ON): this procedure enables the starting of the engine if the TEG is inserted and enabled. The code verify procedure continues even when the user presses the START/STOP key (CRANKING). After KEY ON (+15), the ALFA CODE detects whether the TEG transponder has been enabled. At the same time as KEY ON, the NCM initializes its software until it verifies whether a fix code has been memorized. If the answer is yes, it sends a fix code request to the ALFA CODE. In response to this request, the ALFA CODE only sends the fix code, encrypted by the Minikrypt, to the engine control unit if the transponder is recognized as enabled. If the ALFA CODE receives further fix code requested, it only needs to re-read the transponder in the aerial before responding to the NCM if visible signs of tampering are present (see later). If the transponder is not recognized (incorrect transponder, no transponder in the aerial, etc.), the ALFA CODE will send the code (incorrect transponder or missing transponder) to the engine control unit. If the ALFA CODE is blank and the NCM sends a fix code request, after having recognized the transponder, the ALFA CODE responds by sending a blank NBC transponder recognized code message encrypted by the Minikrypt. Method of using c-can or recovery line w Communication between the NBC and NCM takes place along the C-CAN line by default: if the C-CAN line is faulty, the recovery strategy is as follows: - C-CAN faulty - the NCM changes to recovery status on the W serial line and requests the code from the NBC: if the outcome is positive, start-up is permitted. - in the event of problems on the W line, the NCM transfers to recovery status by means of the Diagnostic instrument at the end of the retransmission attempts. The recovery strategy is mainly managed by the NCM, which acts as a master unit during communication: the NBC, acting as the slave unit, must always be ready to respond to code requests from the C-CAN network and also from the W serial line. Communication via the c-can Communication via the Body Computer and the NCM takes place via the following two CAN messages: - IMMO CODE REQUEST (immo code request) - IMMO CODE RESPONSE (immo code response). The IMMO CODE REQUEST is sent by the NCM and received by the NBC. The IMMO CODE RESPONSE is sent by the NBC and received by the NCM. Communication via the w line If the system changes to recovery mode due to a malfunction in the CAN network, information must be exchanged between the NCM and NBC via the W serial line. This code exchange is only carried out for the CODE VERIFY procedure: it is not therefore possible to run a CODE RECORDING procedure via the W line. Information must be exchanged via the serial line in exactly the same way as via the C-CAN network: The NCM control unit is the communication master unit while the NBC control unit responds to requests received by the NCM. Both messages - IMMO CODE REQUEST and IMMO CODE RESPONSE - are carried on the serial line. Checking the w line electrical connection Because communication only takes place on the W line in recovery mode, an ERROR status would not not be recognised until the system was used i.e. because the customer would not be able to move the vehicle. A strategy for checking the W serial line has therefore been added so that the line can be diagnosed. Protection codes The ALFA CODE function is performed via the exchange of secret codes between system subunits (TEG, NBC, engine control unit). - UNIVERSAL CODE: this is the code that an unprogrammed ALFA CODE sends to the NCM when it detects the presence of a transponder in the TEG. The ALFA CODE warning light turns on at a frequency of 1.6 Hz and duty cycle of 50%. The warning light flashes to indicate that the system is properly connected but the vehicle is not protected by a code. - IMMO CODE: This is the basic code that provides the secret code and the fix code. An automatically generated immo code is allocated to each vehicle. The IMMO CODE is used to generate all the other secret codes used by the ALFA CODE function. - SECRET CODE: This code is resident in the transponder. It is stored in the transponders contained in the TEG when the transponders are programmed and in the ALFA CODE when the keys are programmed at the end of line. - FIX CODE: This is stored in the ALFA CODE during end of line programming. - ELECTRONIC CODE (PIN): This is obtained from the fix code and printed on the CODE CARD, which is given to the vehicle owner. It takes the form of a 5-figure decimal code (0 is not permitted). It is used to access the NBC memory in protected mode in order to reprogram or program new remote control units (TEGs) and/or perform specific diagnostic functions. It is also used in the accelerator pedal recovery procedure described in the specific section on the engine control unit. - IDENTIFIER: This is resident in the transponder and different for each transponder. It is stored in the ALFA CODE during the programming procedure. The ALFA CODE manages a table of enabled identifiers and another table of disabled identifiers. Alfa code function in the nbc The ALFA CODE is a function of the NBC. The main ALFA CODE functions are: - to detect insertion of the TEG in the TEG Reader (+15); - to place the alarm in a deactivated state after recognizing an enabled TEG; - to emit an electromagnetic field to read the TEG transponder; - to send the random code to the transponder; - to receive the encrypted code transmitted by the TEG; - to store up to 8 identification codes; - to store the secret code; - to manage a list of up to a maximum of 8 enabled identification codes; - to manage a list of 16 permanently disabled identifiers. - to manage the C-CAN line towards the engine control unit; - to control activation of the warning light on the panel via communication with the NQS; - to carry out self-diagnosis. Aerial The aerial in the TEG Reader is powered by the NBC to energise the TEG transponder. Since the aerial needs to be as close as possible to the transponder (on account of electro-magnetic immunity, the limited range of the transponder and small dimensions) it is fastened to the front part of the TEG-Reader. Transponder (in the teg) A cryptographic transponder is located inside the TEG. Operation At the time of Key On (+15), the transponder is energised by the aerial and responds by emitting a rolling, encrypted secret code. The emission into the atmosphere is sufficiently powerful to produce a high immunity to electromagnetic interference and the range is such that it can be received by the aerial in the TEG READER.. If the code is recognized as valid, the ALFA CODE sends the engine control unit, on request, a coded signal allowing the engine to be started. Up to 8 electronic keys (TEGs) can be stored in the ALFA CODE. The TEGs are supplied already memorised by the production plant. All the codes are also stored in a database managed by Parts. When the new vehicle is delivered to the customer, the service network does not need to carry out any memorisation procedure. If the TEGs are lost or extra TEGs are required, order from Parts in accordance with the procedures described below and in the REPAIR PROCEDURES section. Op. 5580E ANTI-THEFT DEVICE Specifications The transponder in the TEG has the following coded in its memory: - SECRET CODE which is the same for each transponder in the same kit; - IDENTIFICATION CODE which is different for each transponder produced; - PROGRAMMING DATE for the secret code; - The identification code differs from transponder to transponder to guarantee that no two transponders have the same identification code even if there is a request for a duplicate in the Network. Programming the teg The memorisation procedure is divided into two stages in sequence: - the transponder in the TEG is stored in the ALFA CODE; - The ALFA CODE manages memorisation of the fix code in the engine control unit. This second stage is implemented automatically when the first is completed successfully after key on. The transponders are sent to the TEG manufacturer programmed with the identifier (different for each transponder). The manufacturer generates an immo code, computes the relevant codes (secret code, fix code) and programmes the secret code and the programming date in the transponders. Once programmed, it prints a bar code on a disposable label that contains the immo code, the TEG identifiers, the programming date, the emergency key mechanical code (door opening) and, if present, the remote control/alarm codes. The secret code in the TEGs is stored in the ALFA CODE during the end of line programming procedure and is used for TEG identification in the cryptographic algorithm. Programming a new body computer If the Body Computer is replaced, the ALFA CODE must be programmed with the secret code and fix code of the vehicle to which it will be installed. The database is accessed using the chassis number to obtain the vehicle immo code. This is used to supply the secret code and fix code, which are programmed in the NBC. For a new NBC, the tables of enabled and disabled identifiers are new. Once the NBC has been installed in the vehicle, the TEG identifiers are stored (see reprogramming). An ALFA CODE programming operation can only be performed with a blank NBC by the ALFA ROMEO parts dept. Reprogramming the teg TEG reprogramming involves storing the TEGs enabled upon vehicle start-up in the NBC. New TEGs to be programmed and TEGs already programmed will be entered in the ignition so that they can be recognised by the ALFA CODE, which stores those presented during the procedure in the enabled identifier table and transfers those not presented from the table to the disabled identifier table. Disabled teg table If an enabled TEG is no longer available (lost, stolen or no longer operational), its operation must be disabled during the subsequent programming procedure (necessary to memorise a new replacement TEG for example). The ALFA CODE manages a table in the EEPROM that can contain data on 16 disabled TEGs: the identifiers of enabled TEGs not presented during the reprogramming procedure are transferred to this table. If the disabled TEG table is full, any new TEG will replace the first entered in the table. This table also allows the traceability of TEGs used on the vehicle. Reprogramming procedure The minimum time required for KEY-ON during the memorisation procedure is 1 second. The TEG reprogramming procedure is performed/guided by the Diagnostic/Inspection Instrument: this procedure is activated by means of access protected by the vehicle PIN. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: - the Diagnostic instrument commands the NBC to initialise the TEG learning procedure; - the operator inserts the first TEG and asks the NBC to learn it: the NBC reads the transponder following key-on, checks whether the secret code is correct and, if so, learns the TEG identifier; - the operator repeats operation 2 for all the TEGs. Once all the TEGs have been learnt, the Diagnostic instrument commands the NBC to store them permanently in its EEPROM via the following procedure: - the NBC compares the learnt identifiesr with those currently in its memory - data on TEGs stored in the EEPROM but not presented during learning are moved to the disabled TEG table. - data on learnt TEGs are stored in the enabled TEG table only if they are not already present in the disabled TEG table. - It is possible to program up to 8 enabled TEGs. Deleting a lost teg from the memory The procedure is similar to that described in the previous paragraph. All the TEGs owned must be presented. Those not presented will be deleted, i.e. transferred to the disabled identifier table. At any time it is possible to delete a lost TEG from the memory using the Diagnostic/Inspection Instrument. The identifier of this TEG is transferred to the disabled identifier table and will no longer be recognised. Code card This card shows: - The emergency code (electronic code) that allows the Service Network to program electronic keys (TEGs) and remote controls using an EXAMINER. - The emergency key mechanical code identifies the mechanical profile of the key and must be specified on the order to receive the key already cut. 1 - Electronic code 2 - Mechanical code Operation The electronic emergency code is also used for system diagnosis and for other operations using Examiner or other diagnostic instruments. Fault diagnosis The ALFA CODE function allows self-diagnosis to be carried out for system components. The NBC is capable of identifying and memorizing the presence of the following malfunctions in its EEPROM: - Transponder: defective or missing transponder or secret code incorrect. deleted/disabled unknown/not memorized - Transponder aerial: electrical connection defective (circuit open, short circuit to earth or to battery) Active diagnosis By means of commands sent from the Diagnostic instrument, it is possible: - To ask whether the ALFA CODE type is: blank (whenever a TEG is inserted) programmed at end of line (whenever a TEG is inserted) spare part (whenever a TEG is inserted) blank/programmed NCM link with NCM OK / KO - Request the number of TEGs programmed. - Read one TEG at once and find out for each TEG: valid transponder whether the TEG is memorised its position in the table whether the secret code is valid the TEG ID - Request the number and identifier of the last TEG used - Request a reading of all enabled TEGs - Request the number of TEGs enabled and the number of TEGs disabled - Perform manual memorisation of TEGs by means of successive acquisitions and the condition of the transponder must be verified at each acquisition It is also possible detect the presence of a transponder in the aerial and whether it is valid or not. - Request current system status identified by: last TEG used and enabled and recognised the NBC has received a code request from the engine control unit the NCM is blank the ALFA CODE is blank the NBC is enabled to send the Minikrypt key the identifier of the last TEG used is present in the enabled TEG table the identifier of the last TEG used is present in the disabled TEG table The ALFA CODE has identified a tampering attempt on the +15 supply - Control activation/deactivation of the CODE warning light at the NQS ALARM SYSTEM The alarm system performs: - perimeter surveillance, - volumetric surveillance (with microwave sensors) - anti-tilt surveillance, - surveillance of supply lead cutting. The NBC Body Computer manages the alarm function: activating the microwave sensors and detecting the status, sending/receiving commands from the external modules via the serial line. The system is turned on/off by means of a remote control interfaced witha receiver in the NBC, the remote control unit and the receiver are radio controlled. The alarm system can also be deactivated by inserting an enabled TEG recognised by the ALFA CODE (emergency deactivation). The doors are locked upon insertion. The microwave volumetric and anti-tilt protection can be excluded by operating a button in the front courtesy light. After one theft attempt, a flashing code emitted by the deterrent warning light indicates the detecting sensor: this warning light also indicates the sending unit battery charge status. DIRECT INPUTS: - Negative signal from NA switch signalling driver's door open - Negative signal from NA switch signalling passenger door open - Negative signal from NA switch signalling boot open - Negative signal from NC switch signalling bonnet open - +15 - Direct serial line from microwave/anti-tilt sensors - Radiofrequencey Receiver - DIRECT OUTPUTS - Serial line with Siren Control unit - Power supply / Enablement for Microwave/Anti-tilt Sensors - Right front direction indicator activation - Right rear direction indicator activation - Right side direction indicator activation - Left front direction indicator activation - Left side direction indicator activation - Left rear direction indicator activation - Emergency warning light LED activation - A-bus serial line Structure The alarm system consists of the following modules: - Body Computer: manages system operation and controls external modules. - Sensors on the doors, boot and bonnet: detect attempts to open the doors, boot and bonnet. - Remote control system (sending unit + receiver included in the NBC) - Siren: emits signal beeps and an acoustic alarm. - Microwave sensors: detect movements inside the passenger compartment. - Anti-tilt sensor: detects a change in vehicle tilt following a lift. - A-bus serial line: connects the Body Computer to the Siren. 1 - NBC 2 - Switches on doors 3 - Siren 4 - Microwave sensors on doors and rear (*) 5 - Anti-tilt sensor 6 - Sensor exclusion button with LED 7 - TEG (*) only present for Great Britain Market. Operation There are eight different possible states for the alarm system: - DEACTIVATED; - REST; - ON; - SURVEILLANCE; - ALARM; - OFF; - PROGRAMMING; - FAULT DIAGNOSIS; Each of these statuses is described in the following paragraphs. Deactivated Deactivated status is the NBC's status whenever the ALFA CODE detects an enabled TEG. This operation effectively turns off the alarm. When the alarm system is deactivated it does not respond to the commands from the receiver (key on). It changes from deactivated to rest status when the TEG is removed. Rest Rest status is the basic alarm system status. It is possible to change from rest status to the following statuses: - fault diagnosis: when a diagnostic session is activated by means of a diagnostic instrument connected to the NBC. - surveillance: when the vehicle is protected by issing an on command and passing through the on stage. - deactivated: when the ALFA CODE detects an enabled TEG. In the rest condition, the NBC continues to acquire the +15 status to stop the system changing to surveillance mode and above all to prevent alarm activation This information distinguishes two fundamental rest modes: vehicle operating (+15 present) or left (+15 absent), which is a prelude to surveillance mode. During rest status, it is possible to cut out volumetric and antitilt protection manually within one minute of KEY OFF. On The on command changes the alarm from rest to surveillance mode This operation is always inhibited in the presence of a +15 signal. The on command is issued by pressing the sending unit key. It is indicated by the turn signals coming on for 2.5 s and the emission of a synchronous beep. When the command is received, the NBC activates the alarm activation procedure as described within 100 ms: - SIGNALLING OF SWITCHING ON IN PROGRESS. Blinkers activated with fixed light for 2.5 s. Deterrent warning light caused to flash at 4 Hz. BEEP command sent to siren. - SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS/VERIFICATION: The control unit diagnoses the following components: - microwave/tilt sensor module; - siren; It verifies sensor status via appropriate commands: - after max. 2.5 the anti-tilt module; - after max. 3 seconds, the siren; - after max. 3.5 secdons the microwave sensor modules. If the responses to the verification commands are not received within the requiered times, the module is declared non-operational. Plausibility of door (2 or 4), bonnet and boot switch statuses is also checked (perimeter protection): If one of the entrances if found not to be closed, this entrance is excluded from surveillance. Door lock status verification: 4 seconds after turning on, door lock status is verified and cases of repulsion are detected (incorrectly performed door lock manoeuvre). DIAGNOSTIC INFORMATION DISPLAY: Faults present when the system is turned on are indicated by: - emission of an alert beep on the siren 4 seconds after turning on; - flashing of the siren anomaly blinkers; - problem type indicated by means of the deterrent warning light. 8 Hz flashing mode for 2.5 s indicates that one or more of the following anomaly causes is present: - one or more doors open - boot open - bonnet open - door not locked (repulsion) - microwave sensors faulty Activation of a fixed warning light for 10 seconds indicates that one or more of the following anomaly causes is present: - siren faulty - tilt sensor faulty. - SENSOR ACTIVATION: Command sent to the volumetric/tilt sensor module. - SIREN ACTIVATION: If the siren operates correctly, a siren activation command is sent and the heart-beat management procedure begins on the serial line. - END OF PROCEDURE: The alarm system is on: the deterrent warning light is commanded to flash at 0.8 Hz. - INTERRUPTION DUE TO OFF REQUEST If an off command is received from the remote control during the turning on stage, the procedure is interrupted and switches to the turning off stage. If a warning light or acoustic signal is in progress, these are suspended to give way to the off indications. Automatic activation Automatic activation allows the alarm system to switch from rest to surveillance mode in automatic, timed manner. Two self-activation modes are provided. FROM KEY-OFF: - KEY OFF is detected; - The self-activation counter begins counting; - If a closed/open transition is detected at any of the driver's doors or the bonnet or the boot then the counter begins from zero;. - The counter reaches the "SELF-ACTIVATION TIME" value. - The NBC checks whether an enabled TEG is inserted; - If an enabled TEG is inserted, self-activation takes place; - If no enabled TEG is present, self-activation does not take place; PASSIVE mode (last door): - KEY OFF is detected; - The self-activation counter begins counting; - If a closed/open transition is detected at the driver's door, on any of the doors or the bonnet or the boot then the counter begins from zero;. - if the counter reaches 2 minutes wihtout any open to closed transition being recorded, self-activation is cancelled; - the counter reaches the "SELF-ACTIVATION TIME" value. - The NBC checks whether an enabled key is inserted; - if an enabled key is inserted, self-activation takes place; - if no enabled TEG is present, self-activation does not take place; Self-activation modes are enabled according to the operating mode (see country map table "PASSIVE SELF-ACTIVATION ENABLEMENT" and "KEY-OFF SELF-ACTIVATION ENABLEMENT"). Surveillance from self-activation is complete for all entrances. The operating modes allow: - activation/deactivation of volumetric surveillance (microwaves). - activation/deactivation of the tilt module. During the self-activation stage system diagnosis takes place in the same way as during the normal activation stage. The central locking is not activated during the self-activation stage. Warning lights/acoustic signals are enabled by the operating mode. The definition of the driver's side door for different specifications (RHD and LHD) is specified during the manufacturer's end of line programming. Reactivation The reactivation operation allows the sytem to move automatically from the REST stage to the SURVEILLANCE stage when, after an authorized deactivation, door/boot/bonnet opening or other consistent actions are not found to have occurred. The procedure for reactivation is as follows: - The alarm system is switched off. - The reactivation counter begins counting. - If a closed/open transition is detected at any of the doors or the bonnet or the boot then reactivation is cancelled;. - The counter reaches the "SELF-ACTIVATION TIME" value. - The alarm is switched on taking into account any system exclusions (volumetric protection, siren,...) made at the last switching on. Surveillance During surveillance status, the NBC performs the following operations: - +15 SIGNAL CHECK The NBC downloads information on the presence of a +15 signal: if it detects the presence of the +15 signal for longer than 100 ms without a previous deactivation command, the NBC interprets this manoeuvre as a theft attempt and controls the changeover to alarm status. - EXCLUSION OF EXTERNAL MODULES DUE TO LOW BATTERY VOLTAGE If the battery voltage is below 8.5 V for longer than 30 mins, the NBC deactivates external modules (microwave sensors, tilt sensor) in order to safeguard the life of the battery and to be able to start up the engine later on. - PERIMETER SURVEILLANCE The NBC monitors the status of the six inputs from the four doors, bonnet and boot: if one of these changes status for longer than 500 ms, the NBC changes to alarm status. - PROTECTION AGAINST FALSE ALARMS DUE TO NBC RESET During the surveillance stage, external interference or a theft attempt could cause the NBC to reset and re-initialise its functions. In this case, the NBC checks whether the alarm was on before the reset so it can re-activate the external modules, except for those excluded at the last activation. - ALARM ACTIVATION During the surveillance stage, the alarm may be activated by the perimeter protection and also by external modules or the siren (due to the wires being cut). When one of the alarm activation signals is received, the NBC immediately changes to alarm status and triggers the cycle specified for the type of alarm received. Alarm If one of the sensors involved in the surveillance identifies an irregular situation (attempted or actual intrusion, interference and/or theft of the vehicle), the alarm sytem moves to ALARM status. Alarm status is characterised by the activation of optical/acoustic signals consisting of activation of the siren and indicators. SIGNALS The signalling consists of a succession of alarm cycles. Operating mode parameters are defined in the operating mode table. The type, numbmer and duration of alarm cycles for each mode are managed by the NBC: the siren may only be turned on (sound emission starts) and off (sound emission ceases). For example, if the operating mode requires the emission of 3 alarm cycles lasting 26s at 6s intervals, the NBC will behave as follows: - Blinker activation and control of siren activation with associated sound configuration parameters. - After 26s of blinker deactivation, the siren is deactivated. - 6s wait. - Repeat points 1, 2 and 3 until the required cycles are completed. STORING THE ALARM CAUSE For diagnostic purposes, a record of the alarm causes recognised by the NBC is kept. The NBC memorizes the last 10 alarm causes, associating the cause and alarm system state at the time the system wash switched on with each of the causes. The following alarm causes can be memorised: - driver's door - passenger door - microwave sensors - anti-tilt sensor - cutting of siren cables - boot - bonnet - +15 - cutting of +30 cable - siren intrusion with incorrect siren deactivation command - incorrect heart-beat For each alarm cause, the system status is memorised, described by: - left door open - right door open - bonnet open - boot open - system activated by self-activation - system activated by remote control - microwave sensor defective - anti-tilt sensor defective - siren defective - serial line not operational The system changes from alarm status to the following statuses: - rest: via a deactivation command or via detection of key on by the immobiliser of an enabled key. - surveillance: when the alarm cycles set off are ended. Deactivation Deactivation may occur in surveillance mode or in alarm mode. This is carried out by pressing the key on the sending unit, which commands the NBC to deactivate the alarm system according to the following procedure: deactivation is indicated by two flashes of the 1 Hz blinkers and two synchronous beeps (indication is enabled/non enabled according to the operating mode). This signal is activated within 100 ms of receiving the deactivation command: - the siren is deactivated. - external modules are deactivated. - the NBC interrupts the perimeter protection and, if present, al the counter-measures activated. The command is activated even with the +15 signal present. After deactivating and at the first key on, the control unit runs the signals for sending unit batteries flat, alarms from volumetric, tilt and perimeter sensors, +15 and +30. Diagnosing external modules The NBC diagnoses the operation of the serial line for connection to the siren and and the serial connection lines to the external modules, checking for short circuits to earth, to the battery and for the presence of open circuits. A diagnostic check is carried out on the serial lines when communication is activated, typically upon activation of the alarm system. The external modules are diagnosed when the system is activated by reading the diagnostic communication protocol from which the following information is obtained. - sensors activated and working - sensors broken No diagnostic checks are required for the perimeter protection switches. The diagnostic information obtained at the time of activation is stored in the EEPROM to ensure the system can be serviced. To carry out fault diagnosis, use the diagnostic equipment provided. Active diagnosis During a diagnostic session, the NBC may be required to carry out a diagnostic check on the external modules: the NBC then sends the appropriate command and communicates the outcome to the diagnostic instrument. If the NBC cannot communicate with the module during this operation, the response to the diagnostic instrument will be: - module not responding. Similarly, a diagnostic check may be requested on the serial lines, with the following possible outcomes. OK or KO. It is also possible to read the alarm cause table stored in the NBC. Recovery If an external module (microwave sensors, tilt) is recognized as not functioning, it is excluded for the entire surveillance cycle. The next time the system is switched on, the diagnostic check is carried out again on the modules which should be reactivated if they are recognized as working. SIREN PIN OUT 1 - Siren power supply 2 - Serial line 3 - Earth 4 - N.C. Microwave / tilt sensors Two microwave sensors for volumetric control are fitted in the passenger compartment on the doors. On the version for the Great Britain market, a third sensor, located at the back in the center of the vehicle, improves the volumetric control further by reducing the remaining uncovered areas. The two/three sensors are similar and comprise a transmitter and a receiver incorporated in a module. The sensor on the driver's door works as the MASTER, the other as the SLAVES: they are connected to one another by means of a dedicated serial line The tilt sensor is fitted in the passenger compartment on the centre tunnel.
