All the sensors may be deactivated (together and not separately) by means of the appropriate button on the courtesy light. 1 - Sensor deactivation LED 2 - Sensor deactivation button Receiver SPECIFICATIONS The remote control/receiver system interfaces with the NBC to activate the following functions: - activate central opening/locking of the doors and, where specified, of the windows and courtesy light activation. - turn the alarm system on and off. The remote control system consists of: - sending unit: this is fitted in the TEG, is radio controlled and sends a rolling code to the receiver. It has two or three function control keys and a LED to verify code transmission and battery charge status. - receiver: radio-controlled, built into the NBC with operating frequency of 433.92 Mhz. The receiver is located in the NBC and equipped with a wire aerial that emerges from the body computer. Receiver module with 433.92 Mhz working frequency, and the following functions: - to receive and decode signals from the sending unit; - store up to 8 transmitters; - generate a door opening and closure command (by exiting blinker control, if required); - turn the alarm system on and off; - generate a timed courtesy light activation command. The remote control and receiver system has two operating modes: - on; - off. ON CONTROL At the on control, the receiver sends a signal to the NBC, which: - implements door locking - controls a change in alarm system status from rest to surveillance if the NBC is designed to do this. The on command is issued by pressing a key on the sending unit: it is indicated by the turn signals coming on for 2.5 s (lthe signal is enabled/disabled via the EEPROM). Activation is permanently inhibited (except during diagnosis) with the +15 key-on signal present. When the key is pressed, the sending unit LED flashing frequency is 3 Hz. The sending unit transmits the full rolling code in response to continuous pressure on the key lasting at least 50 ms. If the key is held down continuously, the sending unit interrupts transmission after 20s. To continue transmitting, release the button on the sending unit and press again. If the receiver detects a continuous transmission (code received always the same), after the first status switch, it excludes the possibility of continuous command switching. ON The receiver acquires the rolling code, compares it with codes stored during the programming stage and identifies it from among them. Once the code has been recognised, the receiver locks the doors and changes the alarm from rest to surveillance mode if the NBC is designed to do this. If the NBC contains an alarm system, if the vehicle has been locked beforehand using a mechanical key, the NBC must implement the door lock/alarm activation as indicated below when the sending unit button is activated: - doors locked with key and alarm off (self-activation time not yet elapsed): no door lock operation and alarm activation; - doors locked with key and alarm on (self-activation time already elapsed): operation of door lock (opening) and alarm deactivation; - doors released and alarm off (self-activation time not yet elapsed): operation of door lock (locking) and alarm activation; - doors released and alarm on (self-activation time already elapsed): no door lock operation and alarm deactivation; DEACTIVATION Once the receiver has received an off command from the sending unit, it sends a message to the NBC which: - controls door release. - controls a change in alarm system status from surveillance to rest if the NBC is designed to do this. The system is turned off by pressing the key on the sending unit: the signal is issued by two flashes of the blinkers at 1 Hz, d.c. 50% (function enabled/disabled via the EEPROM). Deactivation is enabled even with the +15 signal present. The receiver controls release according to the rules described in the activation paragraph (only if lock status is active). Alarm system deactivation is also controlled. For more details on the sending unit. See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING PROGRAMMING THE ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) The electronic key is programmed at end of line together with the ALFA CODE. During the vehicle's lifetime, it is possible to make the TEG Reader (NTR) learn new keys, e.g. if ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) are added or deleted. Upon each new programming procedure, all the Electronic Keys not presented during the above procedure (for the removal of lost keys) are cleared from the memory. All available TEGs must be programed upon each programming. Those not presented will be deleted from the memory and it will not be possible to program them. Procedure for storing an electronic key teg The TEG storage procedure is managed by the Diagnostic instrument (Examiner) and can be activated only by entering the ELECTRONIC CODE (shown on the CODE CARD). The procedure consists of learning the TEG codes and involves secret codes being received by the TEG Reader and then stored. During the procedure, the codes are stored permanently in the TEG Reader EEPROM memory. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: - the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to initialise the TEG learning procedure and confirms this to the operator; - the operator enters the first TEG to be stored; - the TEG Reader receives the secret code and the ID of the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) and learns it; - the Diagnostic instrument confirms that learning has taken place; - the previous stages are repeated for each TEG that must be learned, up to a maximum of 8; - once the TEGs have been learned, the operator asks the Diagnostic instrument to store them: the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to store the TEGs learnt. Only TEGs learned during the procedure are stored in the EEPROM. Any TEGs no longer presented will not be stored. Code system component managment There is a centralized DATA BASE (for all markets) managed by the FIAT PARTS DIVISION for ordering all CODE system components. The production plant transfers all the necessary data into this data base together at the time of vehicle production. FIAT PARTS then uses this data base for ordering components that need replacing by the Dealer Network. The data base contains numerous pieces of information, such as: - vehicle chassis no.; - secret code; - code of each ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG); - emergency key mechanical code; - programming date. If one of the CODE system components needs replacing and is being ordered, follow the procedure described below. Lost teg Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. The codes of the lost TEGs must be cleared from the memory of the TEG Reader: proceed as follows: 1. Connect the Tester to the tester output on the vehicle. 2. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode. 3. Enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader. 4. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory. At the end of the procedure, print a table showing the identification code/s still enabled. If no printer is available, copy the codes from the screen onto the FIAT PARTS system form. Only if the Body Computer already contains 8 ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) send the codes to Fiat Parts to update the DATABASE. Request for a new teg Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to request a new TEG (entering the part number) and specify the quantity. Note that the Body Computer is designed to store up to 8 TEGs. It is not therefore possible to accept orders when the sum of the number of TEGs already available to the customer plus the new TEGs ordered exceed this quantity. Keep a record of the form used to order the TEGs in order to monitor the situation. Programming teg codes into the teg reader memory Once the new TEGs have been received from Fiat Parts, ensure that all the old TEGs in the customer's possession are available. Connect the Tester to the vehicle tester output and run the following procedure. 1. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode. 2. Enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader. 3. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory. 4. Check system operation before returning the vehicle to the customer by starting it up using all the TEGs and opening/closing the doors using the remote control unit. In the case of operating faults, it is possible to order spare parts only, but it is absolutely forbidden to exchange electronic control units between different TEGs because it will not be possible to service the vehicle in the future. Replacing lock barrels and/or emergency mechanical keys This becomes necessary when one or more door lock barrels (driver's door lock or others) are forced. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single electronic key kit complete with dowels (entering the part number) for the vehicle type and specification. It is not possible to order a single barrel by giving a single mechanical code. The mechanical code of the emergency key and the electronic code of the TEG are defined together during initial memorisation on a vehicle at end of line and must not be separated under any circumstances. Replacing the reg reader Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession. They should also prove that they are the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single TEG Reader (entering the part number to identify the version). Once the new programmed TEG Reader has been received from Fiat Parts, proceed as follows: 1. INTRODUCTION The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles behind the vehicle thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision. The information concerning the presence or distance of the obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic and visual signals. - the frequency of the acoustic impulse warnings depends on the distance of the obstacle from the rear bumper. - the display in the instrument panel shows the areas around the vehicle which start flashing if the system detects that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle. The distance measurement only takes place when the system is activated, whilst only the control unit is operational in the inactive state. The parking assistance system comprises the following components: 1 - electronic control unit 2 - ultrasound sensors located in the rear bumper 3 - speaker (buzzer) 4 - instrument panel display OPERATION Activation and deactivation of the system The system is activated if the following conditions are present simultaneously: - Key ON - Reverse gear engaged When the system is activated the buzzer sounds as a warning. The system is deactivated by disengaging reverse gear. Obstacle distance acoustic signals The control unit processes the information supplied by the sensors, operating the buzzer to signal the presence of any obstacles. The sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle. The sound lasts for 75 ms, whilst the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance of the obstacle: impulses in quick succession indicate the presence of an obstacle that is very close. A continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away. The acoustic signal stops immediately if the distance of the obstacle increases. The sound cycle remains constant if the distance measured by the centre sensors remains unchanged, whilst if this situation occurs for the side sensors, the signal is interrupted after 3 seconds (for example, to prevent signals in the case of manoeuvres alongside walls). Obstacle distance visual signals The control unit processes information supplied by sensors, sending the information to the instrument panel for signalling the presence of any obstacles. The instrument panel display with the system activated shows the various areas around the vehicle. The various areas in the different cases are either off, flashing or on constantly in accordance with the following logic (SEE DIAGRAM): example: - obstacle in the right rear area (sectors 1 and 2) - obstacle still far away: sectors 1 and 2 both off - the obstacle is getting closer: sector 2 is flashing, sector 1 remains switched off - the obstacle is getting even closer: sector 1 is on constantly, sector 2 goes out; the situation is similar for the other sectors. In the case of large obstacles (e.g. walls) one and only one sector is lit up at a time. Autodiagnosis and recovery The control unit carries out an autodiagnostic test when it is switched on. The sensors are diagnosed every time they are activated. A fault even in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system which is deactivated. The errors detected by the control unit can be read via the CAN using suitable diagnostic equipment (Examiner). Error signalling Any faults/errors are signalled in the instrument panel by the relevant warning light coming on and the message "PARKING ASSISTANCE NOT AVAILABLE" in the display. The warning signals that the system is not available without any reference to the faulty sensor or the type of fault. COMPONENT SPECIFICATIONS Parking sensor control unit (cpa) The control unit is an electronic component connected to the rear wiring that manages the assistance function by carrying out the following functions: - receiving the button activation/deactivation signals via the CAN and directly - activating the sensors - processing the signals received by the sensors - checking the operation of the sensors - operating the buzzer - managing the fault diagnosis and test functions The electronic control unit has a device that protects against voltage fluctuations and short circuits. It is located in the luggage compartment, on the right rear side panel; it is connected with three connectors (one not used on this version): - CONNECTOR A (rear wiring) control unit power supply and signals from other nodes or vehicle components; - CONNECTOR B (not used); - CONNECTOR C (rear wiring) rear bumper sensors power supply. Ultrasound sensors The sensor is an ultrasound transducer which acts as an intelligent transmitter and receiver of ultrasound impulse packages. Both the frequency and the voltage of the impulses are produced in the transducer. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo which is amplified and converted into a digital signal, sent to the electronic control unit via the same line used for the transmission request. Each sensor can also be operated as a receiver only, in order to be able to take a triangular measurement between two sensors. This technique allows better detection of small obstacles and in situations featuring critical reflection. The sensors all have the same electrical and mechanical properties; the maximum detection distance for each sensor can be adjusted using software according to the location of the actual sensor. The frequency and the volume of the signalling can be controlled by the control unit.

BLUE&ME Nav BLUE&ME based on Windows Mobile is a personal telematic system which allows the use of applications for communication and entertainment, specially designed for use in vehicles. The BLUE&ME system is available in two versions: - standard version, with hands-free function for Bluetooth mobile phones with voice commands, SMS voice player and media player with USB port - BLUE&ME Nav de-luxe version which, in addition to the previous functions, includes a satellite navigation system which uses the USB port, with map pre-loading and shows the navigation information on the control panel reconfigurable multifunction display. The de-luxe BLUE&ME Nav system is described in this section. The standard version is described in: See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES The control unit manages the entire system and is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The entire operation of the system is also managed by voice commands, picked up by the microphone near the front courtesy light. The alphanumerical display used for text messages is the one for the control panel. See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS The control unit is then connected to the controls on the steering wheel (in addition to the radio control buttons, there are 2 specific buttons for this function). "BLUE&ME" HANDS-FREE SYSTEM The BLUE&ME system includes the hands-free function for Bluetooth mobile phones with voice commands, SMS voice player and media player with USB port. Thanks to its complete integration with the voice commands, the controls on the steering wheel and the on-board display information, the Blue&Me system allows Customers who have a mobile phone with Bluetooth to use it even if it is in their jacket pocket or handbag without ever having to take their hands off the steering wheel. In order to use the voice commands the voice recognition system does not require any preparation process. The system is capable of recognizing the voice commands given, irrespective of gender, by the tone of voice and intonation of the person giving the instructions. It is possible to listen to music stored on a USB device, selecting the tracks and play modes using either the controls on the steering wheel or voice commands. An example of a screen for the telephone input function is shown below: Connection with bluetooth telephone The system is connected to a mobile phone with a Bluetooth interface and hands-free profile. The first connection between the mobile phone and the device (pairing procedure) is regulated by a password; the user connects by keying the password into their own mobile phone in the menu for Bluetooth connections. It is possible to memorize up to 5 users who are connected automatically at subsequent key-ons without manual intervention on behalf of the actual user. In each case, only one mobile phone can be connected to the control unit via Bluetooth. The operation of the control unit is linked to the availability of the user's mobile phone for Bluetooth hands-free profiles, in particular: - the Bluetooth system comes on independently at the Key on and starts the search for Bluetooth (mobile) devices to connect with immediately. - the equipment switches off independently at the Key off, releasing any Bluetooth connection that may be activated: there is a delay of 30 seconds (provisional figure) to suppress accidental switching off of the engine (in traffic, at traffic lights, etc.). - if a phone call is in progress, the conversation is kept activated (except for the display in the control panel) even after the car is switched off; the control unit and the radio finally switch off at the end of the conversation. Operating procedures Incoming call: - when the signal for an incoming call reaches the phone: the radio is turned to mute, the ringing of the mobile phone is emitted through the speakers and the number/name of the caller (if available) is shown on the instrument panel display - at this point the user can accept or reject the call - during the conversation the user listens to the other person on the radio audio system and speaks via the microphone - when the conversation is over the radio returns to its status prior to the call (volume, mode, etc.) When a conversation is in progress, the user can carry out the following operations: - alter the volume of the conversation using the radio Vol + and Vol - buttons. The last 2 functions in the list are linked to presence on the GSM network, the user profile and the mobile phone of the necessary specifications and authorizations to manage 2 calls simultaneously. Outgoing call The user can make a call in 4 ways - using their own mobile phone keypad - using the list of recent calls - using their own mobile phone list - dictating the number they wish to call. Media player The Blue&Me multimedia player makes it possible to play digital audio stored on a USB device via the vehicle sound system simply by connecting it to the USB port on the vehicle: The following operations can be carried out using the multimedia player: reproduction of digital audio: it is possible to reproduce all digital audio files (.mp3 - .wma - .wav) or a personalized playlist (in .m3u or .wpl format); selection of audio depending on the category: it is possible to reproduce all digital audio that belongs to a certain category, for example an album, an artist or a musical genre; use the reproduction functions: it is possible, whilst playing tracks, to use certain functions such as Play, Stop, Next track, Previous track, Random and Continuous play. The instructions for reaching the destination are given by means of voice messages and pictograms and the names of roads shown in the instrument panel display. The navigation system makes it possible to: - enter a new destination; - navigate to a point of interest (which can be selected from a list of categories such as, for example, hotels, restaurants, airports, railway stations, etc.); - acquire journey information (arrival time, distance from the destination, vehicle position); - recall one of the last destinations memorized; - set preference for the type of route to be followed such as, for example, motorway, toll roads, ferries; - simulate the route to a prearranged destination in advance. The navigation maps are loaded onto the USB device connected to the USB port on the vehicle. In order to use the voice commands the voice recognition system does not require any preparation process. The system is capable of recognizing the voice commands given, irrespective of gender, by the tone of voice and intonation of the person giving the instructions. OPERATION: GPS reception is difficult under trees, among high buildings, in car parks, in tunnels and in any place where satellite aerial reception may be hindered. The Blue&Me navigation system needs a few minutes to determine the new position of the vehicle if the vehicle is moved with the system switched off (e.g. transported on a ferry). If the vehicle battery is disconnected the GPS needs about 15 minutes to be activated. The system has an autocalibration function which requires about 100 km driving until it becomes operational, from when it first comes into service or when the tyres are changed; during this stage the position calculated could be less accurate. In conditions where wheel grip is continuously bad (e.g. when sliding on ice), the system detects an inaccurate position temporarily. To start using the navigation function proceed as follows: - connect the USB device, with the pre-loaded maps, to the USB port on the vehicle; - make sure that the ignition key is in the MAR position; - press the windows command on the steering wheel and say "Navigation": at this point say "New destination" and then "Address": - the system will ask for the desired country, say the country for your destination; - the system will then ask for the name of the destination town to be entered starting with manual interaction followed by a voice command; - scroll using the up and down buttons for the characters required to compose the name of the town, confirming each one selected by pressing the SRC/OK button; - as soon as a sufficient number of characters has been entered, the system will say the name of the town. It will then be possible to continue by entering the name of the town using the controls on the steering wheel; - continue by entering the name of the destination road, using the same method as previously, - say "Start" to start the navigation immediately. The address can only be entered when the vehicle is stationary, for safety reasons. The manoeuvres to be carried out (turn right, turn left, turn around, straight on or reverse) will be shown, by means of pictograms on the control panel reconfigurable multifunction display. The display will also show the name of the road being driven along and the distance to a manoeuvre; when close to a turn the name shown will be the name of the road where the manoeuvre needs to take place. a - Navigation pictogram b - Distance to the next manoeuvre c - Name of the road The voice instructions given by the system recommend all the manoeuvres to be carried out: in particular, the manoeuvre is announced first and then detailed instructions are given. In order to become familiar with all the navigation system functions and modes, refer to the handbook that comes with the vehicle. Code activation and recognition procedure The Connect (NIT) includes an ANTITHEFT function that prevents it operating in the case of theft. The NIT is installed during production and connected to the CAN network in order to establish communication with the Body Computer and store an antitheft code known as the Exchange Code. At each subsequent Key On (and even if the battery is disconnected), an automatic authentication procedure is repeated: if the Exchange Code check is positive, the system begins to operate. If the codes compared are not the same, a message appears on the display asking the user to enter a manual code (Master Code - 4-figure code from 1111 to 6666) that is shown on the radio code card. The Master Code is pre-programmed in production and different for each NIT. It is also different from the Exchange Code. The manual Master Code input procedure is necessary only if: - the Body Computer is replaced - an NIT is installed that has already been used on another vehicle with a CAN network A new NIT (never installed on other vehicles) may be fitted using an automatic authentication procedure without manual input of the Master Code. Wap mode The term WAP stands for: WIRELESS APPLICATION PROTOCOL. WAP technology makes it possible to access the Internet using a mobile phone when no computer is available. WAP browsing is relatively similar to conventional browsing on a PC but the same performance cannot be expected as with PC Internet access and an ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line: a technique that allows data to be transferred at high speed over normal phone lines using special Modems) because the graphics are very poor with WAP and the information is reduced to the essentials. Because WAP technology is specific, mobile phones cannot be used to access ordinary WEB sites as with a PC. The Internet supports WEB pages produced with language such as HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language: the international language of electronic texts - hypertexts) that are displayed on a PC by means of BROWSERS (Navigators, such as: NETSCAPE NAVIGATOR, INTERNET EXPLORER, etc…). WAP is based on a different language: WML (Wireless Markup Language) with its own Script (another word for Program. This usually indicates a program written in a particular language to perform tasks connected with the operating system), with its own image formats and also requiring its own BROWSER or MICRO- BROWSER to display WEB pages. These BROWSERS are built into the latest WAP mobile phones: if you enter the required settings (indicated below), you are able to access the required WAP sites. For WAP phones, addresses are also in “HTTP:// ”, the format used for the WEB. WAP pages are located on an HTTP Server and their technical operation is as follows: when a WAP address is entered on the display of a mobile phone, the phone forwards an HTTP request for a WML page resident on a WEB Server. The request is received over the GSM network by the WAP GATEWAY that forwards it to the WEB Server by means of a coding/decoding procedure. At this point, the requested page returns to the WAP GATEWAY, which codes/decodes it to route it to the mobile phone that originated the request. This is what happens when the requested content is already in WML format (for mobile phones). The requested pages are often in HTML format (for PC). In this case, the WAP GATEWAY acts as a real time HTML - WML translator. In the case of complex sites with lots of graphics, the result on the mobile display could be illegible. NAVIGATION SYSTEM MODULE Operation The navigation system allows you to reach a destination set by the user, by giving visual and acoustic instructions. The navigation module built into the NIT receives data on progress (forward motion and reverse) and direction changes from information made available on the CAN network by the NBC. It cross-checks this with information received from GPS satellites by means of the GPS aerial on the car roof to calculate the Estimated Car Point (car location). The navigation module does not contain a gyroscope because if no signals are received from the satellites, the Navigation system recognises the car's motion using vehicle motion information received from the CAN. Upon initial activation and each time the battery is disconnected, the GPS takes about 15 minutes to activate. The navigation system takes about 100km to self-adjust accurately from the first system start-up and when the tyres are changed. If the engine is turned off and the vehicle is moved with the system off (e.g. on a pick-up truck), at the next key-on, the GPS system will take a few minutes to determine the car's new position. The navigation CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the Connect system and is the same as used for audio CDs. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation drive simultaneously: the navigation system can, however, work partly even without the navigation CD-ROM inserted. Route guidance The main function of the Navigation module is called Route Guidance. This is responsible for extracting, managing and processing the information required to guide the user to the set destination. These activities are, basically: ROUTE CALCULATION: Calculation of the route between the current position and the destination. Route calculation with multiple destinations. Route recalculation in the case of deviation from the current route. Calculation of an alternative route. TRUE ROUTE GUIDANCE: Identification of the position of the vehicle on the route (and calculation of the distance to the destination); Identification of junctions along the route; Identification of manoeuvres at the junctions along the route (and graphic and voice instructions for the user); Calculation of the distance to the next junction where the user has to make a turn; junction zoom function in built-up areas. DIGITAL MAPS: The official M. MARELLI CD ROM contains a Map Database that is made available to all other system functions. Access to any map data (segments, areas, locations etc.) required by other modules takes place through one of the functions available on this CD ROM. COMPLETE DATA BASE MANAGEMENT: If a map CD-ROM is present, the navigation function uses the entire data base available (map list, points of interest, etc.). USE OF REDUCED DATABASE WHEN CD-ROM NOT PRESENT (LISTENING TO A MUSIC CD): It is possible to listen to an audio CD in the CD player during the navigation process. Simply follow the procedure described. The map CD should be inserted in the CD player for the entire duration of entering the destination and route calculation activities. At the end of this processing, the CD ROM can be removed using the eject button. At this point the system will: 1) automatically load the route calculated into the memory; 2) eject the map CD. The audio CD can now be inserted to start listening. Under these circumstances one part of the map information is available (names of towns and names of roads) relating only to the segments of the route. In any case, the reduced data base in the CONNECT memory allows deviations from the route with automatic recalculations, without the need to reinsert the CD-ROM. However, the efficiency of these recalculations depends very much on the length of the original route. When the route data in the memory is not sufficient to continue the navigation process, there is a request to reinsert the map CD. If the system is switched off during navigation without a CD ROM, the next time it is switched back on, the map CD must be inserted to access the navigation functions. When the TEG is inserted, the Connect and Navigation system module are activated. Address book The CONNECT contains two different address books: one for the phone and the other for the navigation system. The purpose of both is to make it easier to enter data (a phone number or destination) required by the user without going through a long procedure each time. This operation may be carried out once only and the result is saved in CONNECT and associated with a memorable name. Then all you have to do is identify a saved option by selecting from a list or entering the memorable name. Both address books are also stored in a back up memory (flash memory). This means that information stored remains even after the system has been turned on and off. Phonebook The following fields are present in the phone book: name: memorable label for fast access to the list. Phone number: number used by CONNECT for calls. Position: origin of the item in the list. Voice recognition: voice sample for activation via voice recognition. Name and number may be entered by the user during creation of a new address book item. In this case, the origin field indicates that the item is stored permanently in the CONNECT internal address book. Or Name and Number may be present on the SIM Card that the user has inserted in the CONNECT SIM Reader. The System also displays this information as phone book items. After the Card has been inserted, the address book management module reads all the items on the Card and makes a copy by creating new temporary items if the name/number pair is not already present in the CONNECT address book. In this case, the position field indicates that the item comes from the SIM CARD. This item type is deleted from the address book when it is downloaded or the system is turned off. The following phone book functions are available to the user: enter new item delete all items in the phonebook listen to/delete all voice samples recorded by the user select item (open detailed window). Detailed window: send call to the selected number modify an individual item (name, number, listen/modify) delete an individual voice sample: delete an individual item save an individual item in the Frequent Number list. It is also possible to copy all the items from the CONNECT phonebook to the SIM Card and vice versa. It is also possible to copy the contents of the phonebook on the SIM Card inserted to another SIM Card. In any case, the content of the target phonebook will be completely overwritten. The item may be entered in the address book when the destination is entered. It is also possible to associate a voice sample to be used to call up the address by means of the voice recognition function. CONTROLS The controls for the following functions are located on the driver's door panel trim: driver's window opening/closing; passenger window opening/closing exterior rear view mirror joystick. The buttons for opening/closing the passenger window are located on the passenger door panel trim. OPERATION All the functions described here are managed by the two door control units and the luggage compartment control unit (for the rear doors) See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS Door locking / unlocking The simultaneous operation of the two door locks takes place via: the TEG remote control; the locking/unlocking button in the centre console. The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot. See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The fuel flap is locked/unlocked together with the doors. If the remote control fails, insert the metal insert (inside the key) in the lock in the driver's door and turn it. With the central locking on, pulling the interior opening lever for one of the doors causes the closure for all the doors to be released. If there is no electrical power supply the doors can be locked manually The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard. The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice. The LED in the driver's door produces the following signals: Locking the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds; Dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds; Unlocking the locks: the LED goes out. The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN. Possible adjustments It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked. It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again. The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel: - assisted boot unlocking: the rear boot is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes; - independent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors. Electric windows The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only). Automatic operation takes place as follows: if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual: the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. Short drop function When the doors are opened (whether with key-on or key-off status), the door nodes implement the short drop function to prevent interference between the windows and the roof or the hood. The short drop position is set at 10 mm from the window full closure position. In detail: when the door is opened if the window is closing, this takes place until the Short Drop position is reached and NOT until it is completely shut. If the position of one or both of the windows is the same as the Short Drop position, no automatic movement will take place. If the door is open, the windows can be moved manually either downwards or upwards in the space between the "window completely open" and "Short Drop" positions and therefore the window cannot be completely closed. When the door is closed, the windows stopped in the Short Drop position are completely closed automatically. Middle drop function (spider version only) If there is a request to open/close the Hood, the door nodes activate the Middle Drop function: Following the request for the hood opening or closing cycle, the windows are lowered to prevent interference with the movement of the hood; the Middle Drop position is fixed at 50 mm from the position where the windows are completely closed. On the command to open or close the hood using the dedicated button (see DF 7030H) and in key-on conditions, the hood control node sends a signal to start the opening cycle: if the windows are in the "completely closed" position on in an intermediate position between "completely closed" and Middle Drop, the door nodes activate the movement of the windows until they reach the Middle Drop position. When the Middle Drop position is reached, the door nodes send suitable signals allowing the hydraulic movement of the Hood. If the position of one or both of the windows is the same as the Middle Drop position or they are in the position between "completely open" and Middle Drop, no automatic movement takes place. If the window raising controls are pressed during the movement of the hood and the glass is in the Middle Drop position, they are ignored and the Middle Drop position is maintained. If, on the other hand, the window is in a position between "completely open" and Middle Drop it is possible to raise the window until it reaches the Middle Drop position. The windows can always be lowered with the Hood in any position. Behaviour if the hood is faulty. In this situation the door nodes exclude the automatic middle drop function, in other words when the fault appears the glass can move freely in the range between "completely open" and "completely closed" if the door is closed or in the range between "completely open" and "short drop" if the door is open. Window movement interruption The door nodes should interrupt the operation of the window in the following cases: - when automatic movement is in progress and either the up or down control is pressed; - at the top or bottom end of travel in both manual or automatic mode; - when the window is in the process of closing and the Short Drop position has been exceeded and the door is opened at the same time. After the window is placed in the Short Drop position when the door is closed, the window is closed as far as the top end of travel position. Anti-crush safety function Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing: under these circumstances the control unit immediately interrupts the travel of the window and reverses it to the lower end of travel position. If a failure is detected in the system or if the anti-crush safety function is activated 3 times in the space of 1 minute or if there is a failure, the system automatically enters into recovery mode (self-protection). This condition is evident from the window closing by being raised in stages. If this happens the system restoral procedure must be carried out as follows: work with the doors closed and the windows closed, as well as the hood closed - on the Spider version; completely open the driver's door window keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position; completely close the driver's door window keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position; proceed in the same way for the passenger window as well; make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work correctly in automatic mode. Following no power supply to the control units (e.g. battery disconnected) the system must be "initialized" once again following the procedure described above. Rear view mirror adjustment The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis. Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space). In addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver's seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged.

INTRODUCTION The new Spider is equipped with an electrohyraulic system for the automated movement of the hood which ensures that the driver can open and close the hood quickly and safely without leaving their seat. OPERATION The automatic activation of the hood takes place by pressing the dedicated button in the centre console. The button is pressed for the entire duration of the operation. The manoeuvre is reproduced in the control panel display which illustrates the movement of the hood diagramatically. The completion of the manoeuvre is confirmed by a "beep" and by the "HOOD OPENING (OR CLOSING) CYCLE COMPLETED" message which appears in the display. Any error messages notifying the presence of any system malfunctions also appear in the display. These errors may be temporary, involving a break in the operating cycle which can then be restored, or they may be permanent. In this case, the hood system must be repaired at a Service Centre. There is a manual emergency procedure which allows the hood to be closed. Only move the hood with the vehicle stationary because the hood should not be opened/closed whilst the vehicle is moving: if there has been an accidental attempt to activate the hood whilst the vehicle is moving, this manoeuvre will be automatically prevented. If the activation of the hood was started with the vehicle stationary and then the vehicle was driven, the process, once started, can only be completed by stopping the vehicle once again. At the start of the hood opening or closing operation, always check that the windows in the doors are slightly lowered (middle drop) in automatic mode. If this is not the case, release the hood activating button and lower the windows in both doors using the buttons or open the doors slightly. In order not to run the battery down, it is advisable to carry out the hood opening or closing operations with the engine running. SYSTEM COMPONENTS An electronic control unit controls the entire electrohydraulic system which carries out the hood automatic opening/closing cycle. The activation of the hood takes place by pressing the dedicated button located on the centre tunnel. Numerous sensors are located in the hood and hood cover locks and in the hood activating cylinders. Thanks to the information received from the sensors, the control unit controls the locking and unlocking of the hood and hood cover locks by means of dedicated electric motors and it controls the hydraulic system for the cylinders for the hood, the arch and the hood cover. 1. Left front lock 2. Front locks hydraulic cylinder 3. Right front lock 4. Arch 5. Right hood cover lock 6. Right flap motor 7. Right arch movement hydraulic cylinder 8. Right flap 9. Right hood activation hydraulic cylinder 10. Hood cover movement hydraulic cylinder 11. Hood control electrohydraulic assembly 12. Hood cover movement device 13. Hood electronic control unit 14. Hood cover 15. Left arch movement hydraulic cylinder 16. Left hood activation hydraulic cylinder 17. Left hood cover lock 18. Left flap motor 19. Left flap 20. Hood frame Hood The hood comprises a double layer fabric with rubber in between and a (7mm) layer of polyurethane applied to the inside of the cloth which has a sound insulation function. There is padding (A) under the inner lining to protect the head in the case of accidental impact against the frame linkage. The hood is equipped with a (3.15 mm thick) glass heated rear windscreen fastened by the pressing of the polyurethane perimeter seal to produce an optimum seal and finish. The rearscreen cannot be replaced separately from the cloth. The steel frame is made up of linkage securing it to the bodyshell, a front crossmember, a rear arch and three intermediate ribs. The front closure takes place by means of two locks (by the hood) and two strikers (on the windscreen crossmember) activated by an electrohydraulic device capable of detecting the approach of the lock levers to the correct position and activating the closure of the actual levers. 1. Front crossmember 2. Rib 1 3. Rib 2 4. Rib 3 5. Arch 6. Right mounting bracket 7. Heated rear windscreen 8. Left mounting bracket The front, side and rear seals are secured to the frame guaranteeing the correct seal with the windscreen crossmember, the side windows and the hood cover. All the seals have been treated with silicon paint. Hood cover The hood cover features a steel structure with a black PVC finish trim and aluminium mouldings. The hood cover is connected to the vehicle by two gooseneck hinges positioned at the side. Two rubber buffers are fitted at the bottom of the hood cover frame and are compressed on the hood linkage because when it is in the rest position folded in its housing with the hood cover closed in order to limit shaking whilst driving. The opening/closing of the hood cover is controlled by a hydraulic cylinder which acts on the device that operates the lifting lever. GLASS ROOF SLIDING BLIND Introduction The fixed glass sunblind consists of 2 panels sliding lengthways that stow away out of sight in a compartment in the rear part of the roof in an area covered by the roof panel. The sunblind extends so far that it completely obscures the glass bonded on the roof panel and fits to the roof lining. During opening the sunblind panels slide along the side guides until they are positioned in the section box. The sun blind panels are placed in rest position by the inner shape of the box and by two preload springs. Side pads guarantee the absence of noise when the sunblind panels are sliding. The sunblind section system is made up as follows: 1. a frame made up of the following parts: - front crossmember (plastic) - central crossmember (metal) - rear crossmember (plastic) - right/left side guides (aluminium) - section box (plastic) - two springs with comoulded plastic terminals. 2. two coiled metal cables with comoulded plastic terminal (right/left) operated by an electric motor fitted into the aluminium guides making up the frame to move the sun blind panels. 3. a front sunblind panel and two rear sunblind panels with their own slide pads. Operation Control button (A) is located in the front courtesy light unit. The panels are closed and opened by operating the pushbutton. Automatic opening Takes place when the opening button is pushed for T>300 msecs. The sunblind panels move from fully closed position to max opening position when they are positioned inside the section box. This movement takes place in three steps. Automatic closure Takes place when the closure button is pushed for T>300 msecs. From sunblind panels located in the section box move from fully open to closed position to completely obscure the glass part of the roof. This movement takes place in a single step. Anti-crush safey function The sunblind panels may be moved only with the key on and they are also equipped with an antipinch system managed by the electronic control unit and active during the panel closure stage. The function is active during the movement and throughout its travel. When the panel meets an obstacle on the front side of the sunblind panel, the direction of motion is reversed. Initialization procedure When the blind device or motor is removed or if the electrical power is disconnected with the blind moving or during the 10 seconds after it comes to a stop, the sliding blind system must be re-initialised as described below. - Move the sunblind to fully closed position if it is not already in that position. If the antipinch function cuts in continuously, force the panel to closed position by pressing the button in closed position. After 10 seconsds, the roof moves to closed position in jerks (provided the button is held down). When the panel makes contact with the mechanical stop (metallic noise), release the button. - Remove the electronic key for at least 10 seconds and then re-insert it into the TEG Reader. - Press the button to closed position. - Keep the button pressed until you hear the mechanical geared motor stop. - Within 3 seconds, re-press the button in CLOSED position. - Keep the button pressed in the same position. At this point, the roof will perform a full automatic open and close cycle. Keep the button pressed during the cycle. If this does not take place, repeat the operations from the beginning. The initialisation cycle is complete.

Dashboard and interior trim The trim material used for the car interior features contributes significantly to the pleasing sensation enjoyed by the car's passengers. Even the synthetic leathers immediately convey a gratifying sensation of comfort, solidity, luxury and sportiness. The slush moulding tecnique used for the dashboard and interior trim ensures outstanding results. Though this manufacturing process is not new, it has been continually refined through the use of new materials and new processing technologies to create vehicle interior parts that offer high standards of visual and tactile satisfaction. During the production of parts with complex shapes, trim materials may undergo stretching, polishing and loss of surface texture definition. The importance of these features assumes increasing weight when it comes to assessing the qualitative level of a car. On this vehicle, our choice fell on trim materials with a natural feel. The original material used to trim the first style model was a faithful reproduction of real leather with all the characteristic physiological traits of natural hide. After undergoing various processes, this symbol of tradition and innovation is transferred to the nickel shells that give rise to the synthetic leathers that are applied to the car's invisible, functional trim structures. Slush technology allows us to make the most of this feature and convey it more effectively while enhancing it with high tactile performance due to the pleasing nature of the material and its softness or yield, conferred by the presence of a layer of medium-density expanded polyurethane. The "leather" trim production stage is followed by foam application. This involves the positioning firstly of the trim and then of a rigid plastic insert required to give the component its structural properties in a resin mould that is the mirror image of the synthetic leather shell. The polyurethane resin poured into the gap between shell and structure expands to fill the free spaces with soft material. COURTESY LIGHTS The front courtesy light above the windscreen includes three lamps with three control switches: it is possible to switch on the corresponding spot light using the outside buttons (A); the centre button (B) switches the centre light on and off, which is also turned on with a timed delay as described below. The courtesy lights lighting delay is based on a logic managed by the Body Computer whilst the rear courtesy light is operated by the door control units in accordance with a logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN: Courtesy light activation strategy When any of the doors is opened both the courtesy light comes on and there is a timed delay of 3 minutes which is reactivated each time a door is opened. When, on the other hand, the button in the courtesy light is pressed during the timed delay, the courtesy lights are switched off and the timed delay in progress is zeroed. When all the doors are closed at the key-off (TEG extrated), the previous timed delay is zeroed and a 10 second timed delay is activated; (this delay is interrupted in the case of a key-on (insertion of the TEG). When all the doors are closed at key-on (insertion of the TEG) the courtesy light is immediately switched off. - When the TEG is removed, the courtesy light comes on and a 10 second timer is activated. - The courtesy light goes off at the "Door locking" command. - At the "Door unlocking" command, the courtesy light is turned on and a 10 second timer is activated. - If the inertia switch is operated the courtesy light comes on for 15 minutes. Courtesy light control is deactivated on door opening The button on the front courtesy light may also disable the assistance of the courtesy light upon door opening. This is achieved by holding the button down continuously for at least 1.5 seconds (the user is informed of disablement by a confirmation beep). If the courtesy light is on when the key is pressed, it goes off immediately. If the courtesy light is off, it comes on when the key is pressed but goes off again after the confirmation beep. Reactivation of courtesy light assistance To re-enable control by the doors, simply press the key again, even for a short time. Spot-light activation The courtesy light spot lights are activated only by pressing the relevant button and are timed for 15 minutes if on at key off (TEG removed). They are not timed if they are activated at key on (TEG inserted). Spot-light activation/deactivation cannot be dimmed. Dimmer activation In all cases described, the lights are turned on and off gradually (dimmer control) over 2 seconds (the 2 second dimmer time is always added to the times described above during activation and deactivation). The gradual switching on/off (dimmer control) should not be interrupted under any circumstances (not even after another door is opened, key on, etc.).
