Introduction The topics are covered with reference mainly to new technical features. Priority is given to descriptive and operational aspects with minimal coverage of underlying principles, rules and precaution. For information on repair methods and vehicle specifications, see the specific sections on repair procedures. Aerodynamics The styling of the new car is designed to reflect great personality and originality and improves on the attributes of roominess, practicality and sturdiness achieved by previous models. The front, sides, rear and underbody were developed with particular attention to aerodynamics and allow outstanding drag coefficient values. Safety The main aim of car manufacturers is definitely the total safety of the driver and passengers. To adapt the vehicle to highly demanding European and international market regulations, the new vehicle was designed with great attention to detail in order to achieve an optimum response in all situations. Passive safety A vehicle's passive safety is the collection of technical and product solutions designed to protect the occupants of the vehicle in the case of an accident. The search for excellent performance has led to the introduction of design and construction solutions on the new vehicle that represent the state of the art in the field of passive safety. The occupant protection system The occupant protection system is composed of the following features fitted as standard on all trim levels: - the front protection system includes the electronic control unit, dual activation stage front driver and passenger air bags, driver and passenger knee bag, front seat belts with pretensioned buckle and load limiter in the reel, a control unit and safety sensor on the front tunnel, a additional decentralised impact detection sensor in the headlamp carrier crossmember, seat belt unfastened sensors for the front seats, occupant presence sensor on the passenger seat and passenger air bag manual disabling switch. - the chest/pelvic side protection system comprises two side bags in the front seats and two head/window bags along the roof side members - rear seats bolts with 3 attachment points on the two rear seats. For more information on the Air Bag system See descriptions 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM The solutions adopted in the design and manufacture of the seats, the dashboard and the interior panels and fittings increase the degree of passive safety of the vehicle. For more information on these topics, refer to the specific chapters. Resistance to impacts All the features relating to Passive Safety have been developed in order to offer the maximum protection for the occupant in all possible impact situations at high speed: - frontal impact - rear impact - side impact - roll over The behaviour of the bodyshell in crash tests has more than adequately satisfied the international safety standards. Pedestrian protection The style of the front part of the vehicle has been developed taking into account the protection of pedestrians as required by the most recent international legislation. The shapes are smooth and rounded and there are no unsafe projections for the safety of pedestrians. The ample surface area of the bonnet minimizes the risk of contact between pedestrian's heads and the rigid front pillars. The most rigid components are located inside the engine compartment a suitable distance away from the bonnet in order to allow the bonnet skin to absorb the energy forces of the impact with the pedestrian's head. Protection against fire At the end of the 90's with the introduction of new European regulations regarding crash tests and with the introduction of fuel injection systems, the need to seriously redefine the design of the bodyshell and the layout of the various systems on the vehicle. The entire vehicle, from the bodyshell to the various components is therefore subject to the rigorous observance of the most recent and most stringent internal regulations regarding protection against fire. Fuel system and evaporation control system and fps Special care has been taken over the layout to locate potentially critical devices outside of the impact area, also the routing of the various systems, which has been carefully considered from the earliest stages, is very well protected in order to reduce potentially critical situations. - The underbody fuel and evaporation control pipes are arranged parallel to the extremely strong underfloor side member. There is also a specific plastic duct to protect against accidental contact (stone chipping, etc.). In the engine compartment on the right hand side, metal sections of pipe have been used to prevent any fuel leaks in the case of contact during an impact. - The petrol versions have a returnless fuel system which allows the fuel return pipe to the tank to be dispensed with reducing the risk of leaks. - The evaporation control system active charcoal filter is located in the left rear wheel arch, in other words in an area that is not vulnerable and is near the tank. - There is an inertia switch on alll versions (FPS - Fire Prevention System) that immediately switches off the engine a few milliseconds after the start of the impact. - The plastic tank exceeds not only national but also foreign legal requirements. It is located in an area protected in the case of a collision and has the capacity to withstand any deformation without the risk of fuel leaks. Also, being plastic, there is no risk of explosion if the vehicle is on fire. Engine compartment electrical equipment - The positive battery terminal is not facing the direction of travel and the risk of short circuiting in the case of a frontal impact is thereby greatly reduced. - The main section of the high power positive leads is directly on the positive battery pole in a maxi fuse box. This solution prevents the presence of sections of cable not protected by fuses and therefore exposed to accidental short circuiting. There is also a series of automatic sectioning devices operated by the inertia switch (FPS) which, in the initial milliseconds following a serious impact, detach the battery connection to the high power leads averting the risk of a short circuit. - All the main cables are electrically insulated and fitted inside corrugated covers for mechanical protection against the possible risk of abrasion. - The electrical insulation of the starter motor/battery power lead is made from a material with good resistance to abrasion and cutting with the routing using special fastenings and protected by metal brackets. Passenger compartment interior electrical equipment - All the cables are protected by fuses located in the body computer control unit on the left side of the dashboard. - The routing of all the cables has been designed to prevent pinching during fitting or interference during operation and to reduce the potential risk of short circuiting to a minimum. Exhaust pipe - All the components that could suffer from radiated heat (reduced by the presence of a special shield) from the exhaust system have been located a suitable distance away. - Large metal shields on the underbody make it possible to protect the surrounding parts from the heat produced by the exhaust pipe (tank, handbrake cables, flexible supports). The structure of the vehicle The chassis The chassis contains several ets of longitudinal box section structural elements, connected to one another by transverse elements and finished off by dashboard and floor panels. The floor panel box sections are integrated with the bodyshell elements, finishing off a perfectly integrated and solid structure. The absorption of energy from a frontal or rear impact is mainly carried out along the two load lines consisting of the front struts, engine mounting frame, rear struts, underfloor side members and side members. The continuity, for the entire length of the vehicle, of these three parts guarantees gradual defornation in accordance with the severity of the impact. In addition, the connection between the struts and the engine suspension frame contributes in distributing the load towards the deformed obstacle in the optimum way. The high resistance material and differentiated thicknesses of the front and rear side members are designed to support the forces developed by the front and rear crossmembers in the case of impacts at low speed without damage and, at the same time, to allow the absorption of all the impact energy in impacts at high speed without the passenger compartment being deformed. There is a box section crossmember at the front with controlled deformation collapsible struts (crash box), whilst there is a very thick crossmember at the rear with a collapsible open section. Both crossmembers are made from high resistance steel and are bolted onto the floor panel in order to facilitate servicing operations. Above the engine and in front of the H nodes there are a further two struts that intercept the stresses arriving from the top part of the vehicle through their deformation, especially when the vehicle crashes into the back of a lorry. The galvanizing treatment on both sides of all the chassis and bodywork structural elements and the use in some areas of increased galvanizing thickness panels, prevents the risk of rust, both structural and aesthetic and therefore guarantees the maintenance of structural performance for the entire life of the vehicle. Bodyshell strength Torsional rigidity Diagram showing deformation due to torsion Torsional strength figures Bodyshell with windows and bulkhead: Brera: 128000 daNm/rad Spider 56300 daNm/rad Bending strength Diagram showing deformation due to bending. Bending strength figures Bodyshell with windows and bulkhead: Brera: 2200 daN/mm. Spider: 789 daN/mm. Windscreen and rearscreen The fixed windows are a further safety feature. To increase the vehicle safety level, the windscreen is in laminated glass. This solution prevents the glass from shattering if struck by stones or gravel to assure visibility at all times and above all to offer a high level of protection if struck with the head. The windscreen and the rearscreen are bonded to the bodyshell, thereby contributing to increasing the structural strength of the vehicle: the seals flush with the bodywork contribute to reducing the noise due to oncoming air (wind noise). The bumpers They have been designed to provide excellent protection in the case of minor impacts. The rear crossmembers right behind the outer shell of both bumpers and the absorbers (for the rear with collapsible cell inserts) positioned between the bumper shell and the crossmember, limit damage in impacts at up to 4 km/h. The underdashboard crossmember The crossmember made from mangnesium to make it light and integrate with the other sub-systems, is located between the two front pillars underneath the dashboard with the shape reproducing the entire upper dashboard. It guarantees a sturdy connection not only between the pillars but also with the floor to which it is connected by means of two struts. This configuration contributes significantly to ensuring the non-deformability of the entire front area of the passenger compartment during head-on and side impacts. Because it also acts as a support structure for the steering column, it prevents the steering wheel moving back and upwards during all types of frontal impact. The crossmember under the dashboard also has the function of contributing to the release of the pedals; in effect, an appropriate size bracket is securely fastened to the crossmember by the releasable pedal assembly triggers that is positioned in such a way as to release the brake and clutch pedals if they are retracted; this cancels out the thrust of the pedals on the occupants tibia and protects the survival space. The structure of the vehicle - spider version The structure of the Spider version is derived, to a great extent, from the Alfa Brera coupè and has all the safety and resistance features. On account of the special configuration (no roof), special reinforcements that are designed and tested, at length, to confer high rigidity and resistance in all impact conditions and, in particular, in the most critical situations, have been fitted. In detail: first of all the floor panel has been strengthened, at both the bottom and the top Special attention has been paid to the structural design of the two rollbars behind the seats and the reinforcements Another particularly critical area - the windscreen pillars - has been reinforced with suitable high resistance inserts Mainly high resistance material has been used on the Spider version as well for the various bodyshell components in order to withstand the forces developed in the case of low speed impacts and, at the same time, allow the absorption of all the energy during high speed impacts without the passenger compartment being deformed. Possibility of damage and repair of impacts at low speed Special attention has been paid to impacts at low speed to limit damage to the front section of the vehicle, thereby preventing costly repairs to the chassis and cooling module. The chassis structural elements (struts) have been designed in such a way that they are not deformed in this type of impact in spite of the forces exchanged with the parts in front subjected to the impact against the obstacle. There is a strong crossmember behind the front bumper made from a high resistance material that is capable of absorbing all the typical impact energy in a low speed accident thereby preventing damage to the most expensive components inside the engine compartment. The crossmember is bolted to the front side members to facilitate the operations of removing and refitting. During the first stages of the impact the front crossmember starts to deform absorbing a considerable amount of energy and moving backwards parallel to itself without collapse instability that could damage the radiant pack behind; as the situation progresses, the deformation is transmitted to the absorption elements (crash box), in other words the longitudinal box sections that produce controlled high absorption efficiency controlled folding. The cooling module has been located a safe distance from the actual crossmember and from the engine layout so that in the case of low speed impacts there is space for it to move backwards without being involved in the damage. The new feature is that the cooling module is supported by the headlamp carrier crossmember from above and the engine frame crossmember from below by means of releasable fastenings that allow it to move backwards without deforming the attachment feet in the case of an impact, in effect the pressure transmitted by the duct to the strong side parts of the reservoirs in the initial moments is sufficient to release the fastenings. The release can be restored without special operations and does NOT require repair activities. In this way the labour time and therefore cost is considerably lower than conventional solutions. The vehicle is also fitted with a collapsible system for the fastenings securing the front headlamps to the headlamp carrier crossmember. Following an impact the fastenings yield and the entire headlamp casing retracts without any damage to it. To restore the vehicle simply tighten the new fastening tabs to the headlamp casing. The rear part of the vehicle is similar to the front: in this case too there is an extremely strong crossmember made from a ultra resistant material which contains highly efficient impact absorbers near the rear side members. In thise case the absorption elements are the only components to replace in the case of low speed shunts. Sound insulation General specifications To meet EEC standards, the vehicle's exterior noise levels must be lower than 74 decibels. Driving comfort and living conditions inside the passenger compartment have been improved by: - optimising the body through a thorough examination of all parts subject to noise, which have been made stiffer and fastened more securely; - choosing contact materials with great care; - by improving the insulation against noise transmitted from the road surface, from mechanical parts and from the suspension; - by taking great care over parts assembly, aerodynamics and all parts with shapes that affect acoustic comfort, such as door handles, door mirrors, bumpers and other outlines; - by fitting new generation engines with high-tech features designed to improve acoustic/vibrational factors; - by fitting a new barycentric engine mounting. Another area of improvement has been the passenger compartment insulation. The following action has been taken: - highly efficient sound-absorbent materials with optmum thickness and layout on the vehicle; - fitting of a sound-absorbent undershield in the lower part of the engine compartment for acoustic insulation; - elimination of acoustic holes (areas where sound can pass between the engine compartment and passenger compartment) by fitting double-lipped seals, thicker rubber plugs; - by fitting the various sound-insulation parts together more tightly to avoid uncovered areas; - extensive use of sound-absorbent seals; - sound-proofed coating of panels with heat-bonded materials applied before painting; - lining of the bulkhead and front steps to remove the sensation of the engine's presence; - application of heat-expanding materials inside the box sections prior to painting to reduce noise transmission. During body cataphoresis process, the volume of these materials expands ten times to fill the box section effectively. - lining the boot compartment appropriately to reduce rolling noise; - carefully examining the fitting and size of parts liable to squeak such as the facia, heater and seats: the anchorage and fastening points have been reinforced. To maintain the high level of acoustic comfort achieved, the specifications adopted during manufacture must be restored exactly in the event of repair. PROTECTION OF THE BODYSHELL Introduction The vehicle body is designed to withstand for many years any environmental attack to the interior, not visible but potential subject to corrosion, and exterior, particularly subject to damage that may affect the exerior appearance of the vehicle. In order to achieve these objectives specific activities have been carried out during all the development stages of the model including both the design and the production process using the most up to date and innovative methods (FMEA, Robust Design). These instruments have been used to apply the guidelines for special anti-corrosion standards that ensure completely accessibility of the bodyshell to the protection and painting processes (in particular the rust prevention cataphoretic painting process) and the correct shape of each element designed to prevent any possible build up of dampness in the box sections and allow the perfect sealing of all the panel joins. Galvanising The bodyshell basic protection level has been defined in parallel to the design and process criteria: 85% of the bodyshell is made up of panels galvanized on both sides. In particular, all the structural elements of the chassis are 100% galvanized. Out of these, the structures defined as safety structures (suspension mountings, seat belt reinforcements, ect.) are made from high thickness zinc galvanized panels (20 microns compared with 8 for standard galvanized panels). The bodywork is made totally from panels galvanized on both sides for the moving parts (covers and frames) and for all the elements of the fixed outer panels, including those that make up the door stops, visible with the doors open. All the anti-corrosion provision has been subjected to laboratory tests and checked on the vehicle with FOR-LIFE tests which were carried out in special test areas that reproduce the most stringent conditions of the northern European market. The total galvanizing of the outer bodyshell makes it possible, together with the protection package provided by the painting process, to produce the 3 year goal without cosmetic corrosion points. The protection package provided by galvanized panels and cataphoresis for all the structures makes it possible to exceed the 8 year vehicle life without panel perforation in the most harsh climates of northern Europe and to comply with the European legislation regarding safety points (10 years with structural weaknesses). Painting A new painting system has been launched for the production of the vehicle designed and produced using the most recent technological innovations available on the market both as far as the adoption of application systems is concerned and in terms of the choice of products. This innovation involves the introduction, for the entire colour range, of water-based enamels and the use of PUR 2K transparent resin in place of traditional products. This last solution, in addition to resulting in a reduction in the emission of organic compounds into the atmosphere, improves the final aesthetic appearance, allowing the original shiny finish to last better and endowing it with improved resistance to chemical and mechanical attack such as, for example, better resistance to the tiny scratches caused by the action of the brushes in automatic car washes. The vehicle colour type and specifications are shown on the identification plate that shows the following information. A - paint product supplier B - enamel colour and type C - code D - type of product to be used for touching up and painting in the event of service operations Re-apply the wax oil treatment if box section parts are replaced during service. Recycling of materials Main specifications According to EEC ELV (End of Life Vehicles) directives, all metallic and non-metallic parts must be recovered from the vehicle and reused, 80% to produce new material and 5% for recovered energy. Nowadays, some 75% of a vehicle's weight is made up of metal that can easily be recovered by melting when different metals can be separated by heating to their different melting points. All the remaining part of the vehicle, amounting to 25% by weight, must be recovered before this stage. The solution to the problem of recycling plastics is resolved at the design stage: the possibility of re-using the material on future components must be assessed at this time: The aims to be considered at the design stage include: - ease of component disassembly; - choice of noble materials in the recyclable polymer chain (giving priority to parts made up of a single family, e.g. PP). Recycling does not allow the production of a part that is the same as the original part because the material may not be able to guarantee the necessary levels of reliability or it may not be financially viable. Plastics may be recycled in a cascade pattern. For example: - insulating material for the building industry is obtained from seat padding; - the material used to line the wheel arches is obtained from the bumpers and then goes on to produce sound-proofing elements. In the end, it becomes a fuel for energy production. This model has been designed to ensure that all its plastic and elastomer parts (rubbers) weighing over 50 grams are marked with coded symbols to identify the material during recycling and also to ensure that all its components are recyclable. In particular, the impacts that could be exerted on the environment both during the life cycle of the product and during the scrapping stage are already analyzed during the design stage. In some cases the choice of materials has been made using an innovative evaluation system known as L.C.A. (Life Cycle Assessment) which makes it possible to assess the effects on the environment globally, taking into account not only the engineering and industrial specifications of the materials, but also the environmental critical areas during the production of the raw materials during usage and at the end of life. Great emphasis has been placed for this model on improving its recyclability: technological solutions in single materials have been favoured and the polymer families present have been further reduced. The recycling therefore involves three successive generations of vehicles contributing to savings in raw materials. Other materal reuse processes are also being examined outside the motor industry, following the lead taken by the F.A.Re (Fiat Auto Recycling) partnership in the Eighties and Nineties. Another important point to note concerns the use of heavy metals in the motor industry. The metals in question are hexavalent chrome (Cr6), Mercury (Hg), Cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb). These are banned (Cr6) or permitted only in tiny amounts when their use must be indicated by labelling or by including information in the documents supplied with the vehicle. The tables in the chapter "GENERAL INFORMATION AND TECHNICAL DATA - OPERATING DATA" show symbols for and descriptions of recyclable materials present on the vehicle. This is to ensure that the best available products are used to wash the interior, paint plastic parts and carry out repairs, bonding etc. The aim is to avoid the possibility of damage by using incompatible products. Labelling also allows organic materials to be selected on the basis of their chemical composition. During service, it is also advisable to separate materials on the basis of their composition to ensure that they can be recycled more easily. The warning light flashes 2.Move on to step 4 4 OIL PRESSURE SENSOR CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check correct operation of the oil pressure sensor Move on to Step 5 1. Pressure sensor defective 1. Replace pressure sensor Op. 1084A40 ENGINE OIL LEVEL SENSOR - R + R 2. Oil circuit pressure incorrect 2.Restore the correct pressure 3. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, see the Table See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there was a knocking noise from the front. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs End of diagnosis The noise disappears when the brake pedal is operated Restore the correct tightening of the front brake calipers to the steering knuckle Op. 3310A30 FRONT BRAKE CALIPER (ONE) - R.R The noise only occurs during take off and is persistent Move on to Step 2 The noise occurs whilst accelerating or braking with the wheels steered. Move on to Step 6 The noise only occurs during acceleration or braking Move on to Step 1 The noise increases as the engine torque increases Move on to Step 8 The noise is also present in other conditions Move on to Step 1 1 OIL LEAKS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem The check on the shock absorber should only be carried out after driving on a dry road, slight dampness of the stem is considered normal since this is due to evaporation that takes place during the operation of the shock absorber. If there is persistently oil on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated Move on to Step 2 Leaks from other parts that are lubricated Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure Leaks from the shock absorber stem valve guide Replace the shock absorber Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 2 CHECK ON CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT SLIDING All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and rotate the front wheels by hand. Make sure that there are no impediments to the movement or noise during rotation. Move on to Step 3 Constant velocity joint seized Replace the constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT 3 CHECK ON CORRECT TIGHTENING OF DIFFERENTIAL SIDE JOINT FLANGE All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the bolts fixing the differential side joint flange are correctly tightened. Move on to Step 4 Not tightened to torque Restore the correct tightness 4 CHECK ON INTERFERENCE BETWEEN DRIVESHAFTS AND SURROUNDING PARTS All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no interference between the driveshafts and adjacent parts (track control arms, front frame). Move on to Step 5 Interference between the driveshafts and adjacent parts. Restore correct tightening of gearbox side support Op. 1008A42 POWER UNIT RIGID SUPPORT - GEARBOX SIDE - R.R. and engine side support Op. 1008A46 POWER UNIT RIGID SUPPORT - TIMING SIDE - R.R. 5 CHECK ON CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT EFFICIENCY All OK Problems encountered Operation Try and move the driveshaft and check that there is not excessive clearance for the constant velocity joints. Move on to Step 6 Gearbox side constant velocity joint chamber broken. Replace the constant velocity joint Op. 2710A24 DIFFERENTIAL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE) L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVE SHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT Wheel side constant velocity joint chamber broken. Replace the constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT Wheel side joint worn. Replace the constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT 6 WHEEL SIDE BOOTS AND WHEEL BEARINGS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the wheel side boot. If it is not intact, check that there are no leaks or no grease in the actual boot. If everything is okay and the noise was more pronounced whilst steering, check the wheel bearings. Move on to Step 7 Boot broken. Replace the boot Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT Grease leaks/no grease. Renew the correct amount of grease of the appropriate type Wheel bearing faulty. Replace the wheel bearing Op. 4450C28 FRONT WHEEL HUB,LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R WITH WHEEL REMOVED, CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY on the side where the problem occurs, positioning it with the magnetic race towards the steering knuckle ring. 7 DIFFERENTIAL SIDE BOOT CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the differential side boot. If it is not intact, check that there are no leaks or no grease in the actual boot. Move on to Step 8 Boot broken Replace the boot Op. 2710A24 DIFFERENTIAL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE) L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVE SHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT Grease leaks/No grease Renew the correct amount of grease of the appropriate type 8 WHEEL SIDE JOINT TIGHTENING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Remove the left wheel Op. 4450B02 LEFT FRONT WHEEL - R.R and/or the right one Op. 4450B04 RIGHT FRONT WHEEL - R.R Check that the constant velocity joint fastening nut is tightened and that the staking is in place. Move on to Step 9 Nut loosening Replace the nut, restore the torque tightening and stake Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT 9 INTERFERENCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of interference between the suspension elements or between the latter and the bodyshell. Also check that there are no signs of interference between the lower track control arm and the shock absorber fork due to damage/partial removal of the bush. In particular, check that there are no signs of wear on the suspension springs and that they do not show signs of abrasion. If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation. Move on to Step 10 Inteference due to incorrect fitting. Eliminate the interference and restore the correct fastening. If this is not possible, replace the defective components. Abrasions or non conformity of the spring. Replace the spring Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R taking care to fit it correctly Signs of interference between the lower track control arm and the shock absorber fork Replace the lower track control arm. 10 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARMS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is not excessive clearance at the track rod end connected to the steering knuckle. In order to carry out this operation the guard under the engine must be removed Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. and disconnect the bolt connecting it to the front steering knuckle Check for possible contact (abrasion) between the lower arm and the seats in the chassis. Also check the condition of the front bush at the mounting between the chassis and the lower track control arm. Move on to Step 11 There is clearance in the track rod end connected to the steering knuckle. Replace the lower track control arm Op. 4410B40 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM (WITH BALLJOINT) FOR LEFT OR RIGHT FRONT SUSPENSION (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY Presence of abrasion on the lower track control arm. Replace the lower track control arm Op. 4410B40 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM (WITH BALLJOINT) FOR LEFT OR RIGHT FRONT SUSPENSION (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY Front bush not intact. Replace the lower track control arm Op. 4410B40 LOWER TRACK CONTROL ARM (WITH BALLJOINT) FOR LEFT OR RIGHT FRONT SUSPENSION (ONE) - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY 11 TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom. Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check See Test 4410OA CHECKING CORRECT TIGHTENING OF FRONT SUSPENSION the tightening torques of the non-yield point type fixing bolts: - the shock absorber stem fastening to the mounting; - the fastening of shock absorber mounting to the bodyshell; - the fastening of the shock absorber to the fork; - the fastening of lower/upper end of the connecting rod for shock absorber fork anti-roll bar; - the fastening of the shock absorber fork to the lower track control arm; - the fastening of the track control arm to the steering knuckle; - the fastening between steering box rod and the steering knuckle; - the front fastening of the U-bolt securing the anti-roll bar to the engine frame; - the fastening of the vertical bracket to the engine frame and the bodyshell; - the fastening of the upper track control arm to the steering knuckle; - the fastening of brake caliper to the steering knuckle; - the fastening of the brake disc shield; Visually inspect that the yield point type bolts have not loosened, the list is given below: - the fastening of the steering box to the engine frame; - the rear fastening of the U-bolt securing the anti-roll bar to the engine frame; - the front/rear bushes securing the lower track control arm to the engine frame; - the fastening of the upper track control arm to the bodyshell; - the front/centre/rear fastening of the engine frame to the bodyshell; - the fastening of the engine side engine connecting rod to the chassis; - the fastening of the gearbox side engine connecting rod to the chassis. Move on to Step 12 Non-shear bolts not tightened to torque. Restore the correct tightening. Yield point type bolts loosened. Replace the yield point type bolts and restore the correct tightening. 12 ANTI-ROLL BAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check, following the See Test 4410CA CHECKS ON STABILIZER BAR after having disconnected the upper track rod end for the shock absorber fork connecting rod, that the anti-roll bar does not come down quickly. Also check that there is not excessive clearance for the pins connected to the bar and to the shock absorber fork. Move on to Step 13 The anti-roll bar comes down quickly. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4410C10 FRONT SUSPENSION ANTI-ROLL BAR - R+R - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY Excessive clearance for the connecting rod connecting pins. Replace the connecting rod Op. 4410C12 FRONT SUSPENSION ANTI ROLL BAR JOINT (END) (ONE), LH OR RH - R.R 13 UPPER TRACK CONTROL ARMS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance between the track control arm track rod ends and make sure that the boot is intact. The bolt connecting the track control arm to the steering knuckle must be loosened in order to carry out this operation. Also check the condition of the track control arm bushes. Move on to Step 14 There is clearance or the boot or the bushes are not intact. Replace the upper track control arm. 14 SPRING/SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for the presence of and condition of the upper/lower spring shims. Remove the shock absorber Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R checking that the shock absorber reaction to a manual load is correct. Move on to Step 15 Upper/lower spring shims not intact. Replace the spring shims Shock absorber reaction to manual load not correct. Replace the shock absorber Op. 4410A12 FRONT SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMANTLING/REASSEMBLY OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R 15 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists The fault is due to another system (engine, clutch, differential). Search for the cause in one of these systems, following the appropriate diagnostic procedures

Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there are transverse vibrations at the front section. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Carry out the latter first. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there is transverse vibration in the front section. Continue depending on when the vibration is present. End of diagnosis The vibration is noticeable during take off and release. Move on to Step 5 The vibration is accompanied by noise which increases with speed. Move on to Step 2 The vibration is accompanied by noise over unmade roads. Move on to Step 1 1 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check: - that the driveshaft-wheel side joint matching is correct; - that the seal is present. Move on to Step 2 Incorrect matching. Replace the constant velocity joint and the driveshaft Op. 2710A10 DRIVESHAFT WITH JOINTS (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R Sealing ring missing. Replace the constant velocity joint and the driveshaft Op. 2710A10 DRIVESHAFT WITH JOINTS (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R 2 INTERMEDIATE SHAFT BEARING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the condition of the intermediate shaft bearing. Move on to Step 3 Bearing damaged Replace the bearing Op. 2710A35 INTERMEDIATE DRIVESHAFT BEARING SUPPORT - R.R 3 WHEEL SIDE JOINT CLEARANCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the clearance for the wheel side constant velocity joint is not too great. Move on to Step 4 Excessive clearance compared with the opposite wheel side joint. Replace the wheel side constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT and carry out the correct greasing. 4 WHEEL SIDE JOINT SEIZING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Rotate the wheel by hand and check that there is no seizing of the wheel side constant velocity joint. Move on to Step 5 There is seizing of the wheel side joint. Replace the wheel side constant velocity joint Op. 2710A20 WHEEL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE), L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVESHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT and carry out the correct greasing. 5 WHEEL SIDE JOINT TIGHTENING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Remove the left wheel Op. 4450B02 LEFT FRONT WHEEL - R.R and/or the right one Op. 4450B04 RIGHT FRONT WHEEL - R.R Check that the constant velocity joint fastening nut is tightened and that the staking is in place. Move on to Step 6 Nut loosening Replace the nut, restore the torque tightening and stake Op. 4450C28 FRONT WHEEL HUB,LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R WITH WHEEL REMOVED, CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY 6 CLUTCH PLATE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no irregular wear on the surface of the clutch plate. Move on to Step 7 Surface of the clutch plate worn unevenly. Replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R 7 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present. End of diagnosis The fault persists The fault is due to another system (engine, gearbox, differential, suspension). Search for the cause in one of these systems, following the appropriate diagnostic procedures.

With the engine running, there is noise at take off when the various gears are engaged: the noise changes as the speed changes. Test results 1 REDUCTION GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the reduction gear More specifically: - it should not be worn or damaged; - there should not be excessive clearance; - the ring gear fastenings should not be slack. Move on to Step 2 Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear 2 SATELLITE CARRIER PIN CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the wear of the satellite carrier pin or the housing in the differential casing Op. 2110D20 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING, REMOVED - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, CHECK PLANET AND SATELLITE GEARS End of diagnosis Differential casing wear Replace the differential casing Op. 2110D20 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING, REMOVED - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, CHECK PLANET AND SATELLITE GEARS

With the vehicle stationary, the gearbox in neutral and the engine running, there is a high frequency, low intensity noise coming from the area of the gearbox. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Visually inspect whether the problem is accompanied by an oil leak from the gearbox/differential. Press the clutch pedal and check whether the noise increases. Check the gearbox/differential oil level Op. 0010T41 MANUAL GEARBOX OIL CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY Move on to Step 1 Oil leak detected from the gearbox Proceed as instructed in the See table X015 GEARBOX/DIFFERENTIAL OIL LEAKS The noise disappears or decreases considerably with the clutch pedal pressed: the noise comes from inside the gearbox Proceed as instructed in the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Oil level too low. Restore the correct level Op. 0010T41 MANUAL GEARBOX OIL CHECK LEVEL AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY and carry out a road test. If the fault persists, move on to Step 1 1 SPLINED HUB CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for excess grease on the clutch plate hub bushes and the gearbox main shaft Move on to Step 2 Gearbox main shaft hub faulty Replace the gearbox main shaft Op. 2110B MANUAL GEARBOX WITH DIFFERENTIAL GEARS AND SYNCHRONISERS Clutch plate hub bushes faulty. Restore the correct lubrication for the bushes. If necessary, replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R 2 CLUTCH PLATE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check: - Clutch plate wear; - Fouling (oil or grease) of the clutch plate; - That there is no distortion of the clutch plate; - That there is no damage to the pressure plate diaphragm spring. End of diagnosis Clutch plate or pressure plate faulty Replace the clutch plate Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R Presence of oil or grease. Also replace the gearbox input oil seal Op. 2110B34 MANUAL GEARBOX (6 SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH, CHECK COMPONENTS, REPLACE SYNCHRONIZERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS

With the engine running, there is a noise (whistling inside the gearbox) when a specific gear is engaged. This noise decreases or disappears on changing gear Test results 1 SYNCHRONIZER RING CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Overhaul the gearbox Op. 2110B34 MANUAL GEARBOX (6 SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH, CHECK COMPONENTS, REPLACE SYNCHRONIZERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS In particular, check the synchronizer rings of the gear engaged: there should be no wear on the inner surfaces. Move on to Step 2 Seals worn Replace the synchronizers Op. 2110B34 MANUAL GEARBOX (6 SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH, CHECK COMPONENTS, REPLACE SYNCHRONIZERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS 2 GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Overhaul the gearbox Op. 2110B34 MANUAL GEARBOX (6 SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH, CHECK COMPONENTS, REPLACE SYNCHRONIZERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS In particular, check the teeth of the gear engaged: there should be no signs of wear or seizing Move on to Step 3 Gears worn Replace the gears involved Op. 2110B34 MANUAL GEARBOX (6 SPEED) WITH DIFFERENTIAL - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY - WASH, CHECK COMPONENTS, REPLACE SYNCHRONIZERS AND INTERNAL CONTROLS 3 REDUCTION GEAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the reduction gear More specifically: - it should not be worn or damaged; - there should not be excessive clearance End of diagnosis Reduction gear damaged Restore the clearance or, if necessary, replace the reduction gear

Whilst driving round bends (both left and right) there is a noise in the area of the gearbox. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Steer to the right or to the left and check whether the noise increases. Steer fully and then release the steering wheel: check whether the intensity of the increases or not with the steering angle. Move on to Step 1 The noise only varies when steering either to the left or to the right Proceed as instructed in the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING The noise stops in a straight line Proceed as instructed in the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING The noise varies greatly with the steering angle Move on to Step 2 The noise remains constant with the steering angle Move on to Step 1 1 DIFFERENTIAL CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the differential and, in particular, the bearings Op. 2110D MANUAL GEARBOX DIFFERENTIAL End of diagnosis Bearings damaged Replace the bearings Op. 2110D26 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING BEARINGS - REPLACE WITH DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING REMOVED Gears worn or damaged Overhaul or replace the differential casing Op. 2110D20 DIFFERENTIAL INTERNAL CASING, REMOVED - DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, CHECK PLANET AND SATELLITE GEARS 2 CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check the transmission constant velocity joints End of diagnosis Joint damaged Replace the joint Op. 2710A24 DIFFERENTIAL SIDE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT (ONE) L/H OR R/H - R + R WITH DRIVE SHAFT REMOVED - INCLUDES BOOT REPLACEMENT

Noise (creaking) is heard when the clutch pedal is operated Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the engine idling and the gearbox in neutral, press the clutch pedal fully down and see whether the noise disappears. Then, with the engine running and the handbrake on to lock the wheels, engage first gear and release the clutch to see whether the noise disappears. Move on to Step 1 1. The noise disappears with the clutch pressed 1. Proceed as instructed in the See table S001 ENGINE KNOCK 2. The noise disappears with the gear engaged. 2. Proceed as instructed in the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING 1 CHECK THRUST BEARING ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the thrust bearing: it should not be worn Move on to Step 2 Bearing fault. Replace the thrust bearing. Op. 1820B38 HYDRAULIC CLUTCH ACTUATOR WITH COAXIAL CONTROL - R.R WITH GEARBOX REMOVED 2 CLUTCH CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check the condition of the cluch plate and the flexible coupling. End of diagnosis Fault in clutch plate or flexible coupling Replace the clutch assembly Op. 1810A20 CLUTCH - R + R

Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is creaking coming from the rear suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING . Carry out the latter first. If the problem is only on one side, carry out the checks and any operations on the appropriate side only. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING , there was a creaking noise from the rear. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs End of diagnosis The noise only occurs whilst moving Move on to Step 1 1 DUST COVER CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Position the vehicle on a two column lift and raise it. Check that the dust cover is correctly attached and is not rubbing against the spring or the shock absorber casing, by moving it and applying pressure and releasing it above the shock absorber casing Move on to Step 2 It is released. Check the possibility of reattaching the cover, otherwise replace the end of travel buffer. There is rubbing Replace the end of travel buffer 2 CHECKS UNDER THE FLOOR All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no pipes, handbrake cable or heat shields under the floor that are producing noise. Also check that springs on the layout brackets are not a source of noise See Test 4420OA CHECK ON STATE OF CLIPS ON LAYOUT BRACKETS Move on to Step 3 Pipes or heat shields incorrectly fastened Renew the correct fastening Handbrake cable noisy Lubricate the handbrake cable Springs or rubber mountings damaged Replace the faulty components 3 CAMBER ROD BUSHES CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of deterioration (contact/rubbing) on the crossmember, for the camber rod bushes Move on to Step 4 Bushes deteriorated Replace the camber rod checking the correct camber values Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 4 TRANSVERSE PLATE BUSH CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of deterioration (contact/rubbing) on the bush fastening the transverse plate to the crossmember. Move on to Step 5 Bush deteriorated. Replacement of longitudianl arm complete with transverse plate and bodyshell mounting bracket, in accordance with the Op. 4420B10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION WISHBONE (ONE) - R+R checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 5 LONGITUDINAL ARM BUSHES CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no deterioration/rubbing of the bush on the mounting bracket securing the arm to the bodyshell. Check that there is no deterioration/rubbing of the front and rear bushes fastening the longitudinal arm to the steering knuckle. Move on to Step 6 Bush deteriorated. Replacement of longitudinal arm complete with bodyshell mounting bracket, in accordance with the Op. 4420B10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION WISHBONE (ONE) - R+R restoring the correct toe in values Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY Bushes deteriorated Replacement of rear stub axle checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 6 CHECKS ON ANTI-ROLL BAR All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no faults with the anti-roll bar See Test 4420CA CHECKS ON REAR ANTI-ROLL BAR More specifically: - correct positioning of anti-roll bar in relation to the vehicle centre-line; of the bar is centered, check for any signs of mounting/bar sliding; - paint not worn at the points where the bar and the crossmember come into contact; - condition of centre flexible mountings in the contact area with the bar; - presence of grease in the boots for the connecting rod between the bar and the longitudinal arm; - fastenings to torque between bar and crossmember; - fastenings to torque between bar and longitudinal arm connecting rod. Check, after loosening the longitudinal arm, through a rotary movement, that there is no seizing/excessive clearance for both joints for the rod connecting the bar to the longitudinal arm. Move on to Step 7 Torque tightenings not correct. Restore the correct tightening. Incorrect positioning of bar in relation to vehicle centre line. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4420C10 REAR SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR - R+R Paint worn at the contact points (rubbing between anti-roll bar and crossmember). Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4420C10 REAR SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR - R+R Signs of tearing or damage to the flexible mountings. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4420C10 REAR SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR - R+R Signs of seizing /excessive clearance for the connecting rod joints. Replace the connecting rod 7 SPRING/SHOCK ABSORBER ASSEMBLY CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Also check that the positioning and the fitting of the semi-corner assembly (spring-shock absorber assembly) is correct. Check the condition of the spring lower rubber seal and the rubber coating for the upper shim. Check that there are no signs of rubbing on the suspension spring at its supports. Also check that the spring shows no signs of interference. If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation. Move on to Step 8 Semi corner units incorrectly positioned or fitted. Restore the correct fitting/positioning of the components. The correct fitting (of the spring-shock absorber assembly) should be carried out positioning the two cusps (arranged at 180°) of the mounting parallel to the fastening axis of the shock absorber to the longitudinal arm. Signs of tearing on the rubberized shims. Replace the components making sure that they are correctly position (spring in contact with the lower plate projection). Signs of interference on the spring. Replace the shock absorber spring Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R. and the lower seal if damaged. 8 CHECKS ON THE SHOCK ABSORBER BUFFER PLATE All OK Problems encountered Operation Following the Op. 7040B18 LOAD COMPARTMENT LOAD PLATFORM SIDE TRIM ONE LH OR RH - R.R remove the luggage compartment interior lining side panels, check: - that the noise is not caused by the movement of the shock absorber buffer plate; - that the buffer plate is fitted in the correct position See Test 4420AG CHECK ON CORRECT FITTING OF SHOCK ABSORBER BUFFER PLATE End of diagnosis The buffer plate is loose. Tighten the upper nut to torque so that the buffer plate does not move any more. The buffer plate is not fitted correctly. Refit the buffer plate correctly.

Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is a whistling noise coming from the rear suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Carry out the latter first. If the problem is only on one side, carry out the checks and any operations on the appropriate side only. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there was a whistling noise from the back. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs. End of diagnosis The noise increases when cornering. Move on to Step 1. The noise increases in vertical oscillation conditions. Move on to Step 2. 1 CHECKS ON THE WHEEL HUB All OK Problems encountered Operation Visually inspect that the yield point type bolts fixing the bearing to the steering knuckle have not loosened. Also check for the presence of grease on the wheel hub. Move on to Step 2 Yield point type tightenings loosened Replace the shear bolts and restore the correct tightness Presence of grease on the wheel hub. Replace the wheel bearing complete with hub on the side where the noise is loudest Op. 4450C28 FRONT WHEEL HUB,LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R WITH WHEEL REMOVED, CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY This bearing is used by the ABS active sensors to calculate the wheel speed. It should NEVER come into contact with metal shavings because they could alter the gap and prevent a correct reading from the sensor. 2 BRAKE DISC CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check for any distortion to the disc heat shield. Turn the wheel assembly to check for noise due to contact between disc and heat shield. Move on to Step 3 Heat shield deformed. Restore the correct gap/replace the guard Op. 3310B59 REAR BRAKE DISC GUARD (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. Contact between heat shield and disc. Replacement of brake disc Op. 3310B48 REAR BRAKE DISC (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. if the noise persists, replace the wheel bearing complete with hub Op. 4450D10 HUB FOR ONE REAR WHEEL, L/H OR R/H - R+R WITH WHEEL REMOVED - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY 3 SHOCK ABSORBER STEM CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Remove the left and/or right wheel. Check that the noise is not due to irregular friction between the shock absorber stem and the gasket, checking the condition of the stem chrome surface. End of diagnosis There is irregular friction. Lubricate the stem raising the dust cover with a layer of silicon grease. If the noise persists, replace the shock absorber Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R.

Whilst driving, especially on unmade roads, there is knocking coming from the rear suspension. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Carry out the latter first. If the problem is only on one side, carry out the checks and any operations on the appropriate side only. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS All OK Problems encountered Operation Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there was a knocking noise from the back. Continue depending on the circumstances in which the noise occurs. End of diagnosis The noise disappears when the brake pedal is operated. Restore the correct tightening of the rear brake calipers to the stub axle The noise only occurs during acceleration or braking Move on to Step 1 The noise is also present in other conditions Move on to Step 1 1 OIL LEAKS CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem. the check on the shock absorber should only be carried out after driving on a dry road, slight dampness of the stem is considered normal since this is due to evaporation that takes place during the operation of the shock absorber. If there is a persistent oil leak on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated Move on to Step 2 Leaks from other parts that are lubricated Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure Leaks from the shock absorber stem Replace the shock absorber Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R. 2 HANDBRAKE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the handbrake cables or outer casing do not knock against the fuel tank, heat shields or bodywork during oscillations. Move on to Step 3 Inteference between outer casing or cables and other elements Cover the outer casing with foam rubber tape in the area of the interference or lubricate the cable 3 INTERFERENCE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there are no signs of interference between the suspension elements or between the latter and the bodyshell. In particular, check that there are no signs of wear on the suspension springs and that they do not show signs of abrasion. If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation. Move on to Step 4 Inteference due to incorrect fitting. Eliminate the interference and restore the correct fastening. If this is not possible, replace the defective components Abrasions or non conformity of the spring Replace the spring Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R. taking care to fit it correctly 4 TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom. Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check See Test 4420OB CHECK ON CORRECT TIGHTENINGS FOR REAR SUSPENSION the tightening torques of the non-yield point type fixing bolts: - the shock absorber shim; - the lower mounting of the shock absorber to the longitudinal track control arm; - the transverse plate to the longitudinal arm; - the bracket fastening the longitudinal arm to the body; - the fastening for the bush to the longitudinal arm; - the anti-roll bar to the crossmember; - the connecting rod to the bar and to the longitudinal arm; - the camber rod to the steering knuckle; (only for the 2.2 JTS) - the rear fastening of the longitudinal arm to the steering knuckle; (only for the 3.2 V6 engine) - the rear differential fastening to the crossmember; - the brake caliper to steering knuckle; - the brake disc guard to the steering knuckle; - the steering knuckle to the hub. Visually inspect that the yield point type bolts have not loosened, the list is given below: - the shock absorber bracket to the bodyshell; - the camber rod to the crossmember; - the transverse plate to the crossmember; - the longitudinal arm bush to the mounting bracket on the bodyshell; - the front fastening for the longitudinal arm to the steering knuckle; - the crossmember to the bodyshell. Move on to Step 5 Non-shear bolts not tightened to torque Restore the correct tightness Shear bolts loosened Replace the shear bolts and restore the correct tightness 5 CAMBER ROD CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance between the camber rod and the crossmember or between the camber rod and the steering knuckle. Also check the condition of the crossmember bush. Move on to Step 6 There is clearance or the crossmember side fastening bush is not intact Replace the camber rod checking the correct camber values Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 6 TRANSVERSE PLATE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance at the mounting of the plate on the crossmember. Also check the condition of the bush fastened to the crossmember. Move on to Step 7 There is clearance or the bush is not intact. Replacement of longitudinal arm complete with transverse plate and bodyshell mounting bracket, in accordance with the Op. 4420B10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION WISHBONE (ONE) - R+R checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 7 LONGITUDINAL ARM CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check at the longitudinal track control arm that: - there is no clearance between the bush and the mounting bracket on the bodyshell; - there are no glycol leaks (fluid inside the hydraulic bush) at the bush fastened to the bodyshell. Move on to Step 8 There is no clearance between the bush and the mounting bracket on the bodyshell. Replacement of longitudinal arm complete with transverse plate and bodyshell mounting bracket, in accordance with the Op. 4420B10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION WISHBONE (ONE) - R+R checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY Glycol leaks from the bush fastening the longitudinal arm to the bodyshell. Replacement of longitudinal arm complete with transverse plate and bodyshell mounting bracket, in accordance with the Op. 4420B10 L/H OR R/H REAR SUSPENSION WISHBONE (ONE) - R+R checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 8 REAR STUB AXLE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that there is no clearance between the stub axle and the longitudinal arm and between the stub axle and the camber rod. Also check the condition of the stub axle bushes. Move on to Step 9 There is clearance or the bushes are not intact. Replacement of rear stub axle, in accordance with Op. 4450D14 STUB AXLE FOR ONE REAR WHEEL HUB, LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R WITH HUB REMOVED - INCLUDES BUSH REPLACEMENT IF NECESSARY - CHECK WHEEL GEOMETRY SEPARATELY checking the toe-in values are correct Op. 4450A40 REAR WHEEL GEOMETRY - CHECK USING OPTICAL EQUIPMENT, INCLUDES ADJUSTMENT IF NECESSARY 9 ANTI-ROLL BAR CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation After having disconnected the lower track rod end for the rod connected to the longitudinal track control arm, check that the anti-roll bar does not come down quickly. Also check that there are no signs of wear or tears on the connecting rod boots. Move on to Step 10 The anti-roll bar comes down quickly. Replace the anti-roll bar Op. 4420C10 REAR SUSPENSION STABILIZER BAR - R+R Signs of wear or tears on the connecting rod boots. Replace the connecting rod 10 SHOCK ABSORBER PLATE TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK All OK Problems encountered Operation When the luggage compartment interior lining side panels are removed following the Op. 7040B18 LOAD COMPARTMENT LOAD PLATFORM SIDE TRIM ONE LH OR RH - R.R Check the tightening torques for the following bolts: - fastening of the shock absorber buffer plate; Check that the buffer plate is fitted correctly See Test 4420AG CHECK ON CORRECT FITTING OF SHOCK ABSORBER BUFFER PLATE Move on to Step 11 Torque tightenings not correct Restore the correct tightening. Plate not correctly fitted Refit the plate correctly 11 CHECK ON MATCHING OF SHOCK ABSORBER MOUNTING TO ALUMINIUM SUPPORT ON TURRET All OK Problems encountered Operation The left and/or right wheel must be removed to carry out this check then check: - that the mounting and support are correctly matched; - the condition of the shock absorber mounting. Move on to Step 12 Matching between mounting and support not correct Restore the correct matching Rubber detached from the metal parts of the mounting Replace the mounting 12 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION All OK Problems encountered Operation Check that the fault is no longer present End of diagnosis The fault persists The knocking is caused by another system (e.g. the fuel float in the tank). Whilst the steering is operated there is a noise when it reaches the end of travel position. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the level of the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Restore the correct fluid level: if there are leaks, continue follow the instructions in See table X030 POWER ASSISTED STEERING SYSTEM FLUID LEAKS 2. The noise increases towards the end of travel position and with the engine speed (roar) 2. Move on to Step 1 3. The noise remains constant (hissing whilst steering, puffing on release) 3. No intervention is nececssary: the noise is due to the by-pass valve that discharges the excess pressure 1 CHECK ON POWER ASSISTED STEERING FLUID QUALITY ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Make sure that there is no emulsified fluid (fluid that is lighter in colour with bubbles) Move on to Step 2 Emulsified fluid. Eliminate any air infiltration from the power assisted steering system pipes Op. 4130B10 POWER STEERING FLUID RESERVOIR - R.R. 2 POWER ASSISTED STEERING PIPES CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for constrictions in the flexible and rigid system pipes. Move on to Step 3 Pipes faulty. Replace the damaged parts, replacing all the gaskets. See Assembly Op. 4130B POWER STEERING HYDRAULIC SYSTEM 3 CHECK CORRECT OPERATION OF THE POWER STEERING PUMP ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the power assisted steering pump is working properly End of diagnosis Power assisted steering pump malfunction Replace the power assisted steering pump Op. 4130B20 POWER STEERING PUMP - R.R.

After operating the steering numerous times, a noise is heard when the steering wheel is left still Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Visually inspect the level of the power assisted steering fluid in the reservoir. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Connect the climate control system to the special repressurizing equipment and check the system pressures by carrying out the See Test 5040OB AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM OPERATION CHECK (PRESSURE) Check the wear condition and correct belt alignment and tensioning. Run the engine at idle speed with the A/C system off and check whether the noise comes from other auxiliary components (engine fan, water pump, alternator). Increase the rpm and check for vibrations. Move on to Step 2 1. Pressure level incorrect 1. Move on to Step 1 2. Belt alignment/tension incorrect or belt worn. 2. Restore correct alignment/tension or replace the belt. 3. The noise is from other auxiliary components (engine cooling fan, coolant pump, alternator). 3. Continue as indicated in the diagnostic test procedure. 1 CHECK PRESSURE VALUES IN HIGH AND LOW PRESSURE CIRCUIT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Keep the recharging device connected and check the pressure levels in the system high and low pressure circuit with the compressor on and engine running: pressure values low in high and low pressure circuit; pressure values high in high and low pressure circuit; check that the pressure values (high and low) during compressor operation do not pulse and that the circuit does not equalise slowly when the engine is turned off. End of diagnosis 1. Low circuit pressure values (insufficient coolant in circuit) 1. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 2. High circuit pressure values (too much coolant in circuit) 2. Flush the system and restore the correct charge of fluid and gas Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE 3. Pulsing circuit pressure values (compressor discharge valve permanently open) 3. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter. 2 CHECK ON FASTENING OF PIPES AND COMPONENTS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the compressor, the pipes and the system components are correctly fastened. Check the following, in order: bracket fastening to the engine block; fastening of pipes (by bands and spacers) no interference between pipes and other components in the engine compartment; condenser cleanlineness or damage (presence of mud, foreign bodies). Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. Move on to Step 3 1. Fastening of components incorrect 1. Retighten fastenings to torque 2. Interference in the engine compartment 2. Restore the correct layout of the pipes 3. Condenser obstructed or damaged. 3. Clean or replace the condenser Op. 5040A40 AIR CONDITIONING CONDENSER - R+R 4. Also check for cracks in the compressor fastenings to the bracket on the engine block. 4. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3 CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITHOUT THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Checks to be carried out without the compressor on: disconnect the service belt and check for contact between the armature and pulley; with the belt disconnected, check for contact between the pulley and external elements. check the wear of the pulley bearing by rotating the moving plate in both directions of rotation. check whether the compressor magnetic coupling shows signs of overheating. Move on to Step 4 1. Presence of contact between armature and pulley. 1. Replace the compressor electromagnetic coupling with pulley 2. Presence of contact between the pulley and external elements. 2. Remove the contact. 3. Bearing worn 3. Replace the pulley 4. Signs of overheating on the compressor magnetic coupling 4. Replace the pulley If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter. 4 CHECKS TO CARRIED OUT WITH THE COMPRESSOR ON ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION After restoring the correct connection of the service belt, turn the compressor on and off to check: visually if the compressor magnetic coupling plate slips due to oil or grease on the plate; if slippage takes place between the compressor belt and pulley. Move on to Step 5 1. Oil or grease on the plate. 1. Clean the oil or grease off the plate and find the oil leak. 2. Slippage between compressor belt and pulley. 2. Replace the belt 5 CHECK FOR GAS LEAKS ON THE COMPRESSOR SIDE ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION With the engine started and the climate control system at the maximum speed (compressor button ON), place the temperature adjustment knob/button in the maximum cold position, move the probe of the leak detector near the connector to be analyzed and check for any leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Withdraw the pipes from the compressor and ensure that the o-rings on the pipes are correctly positioned. Check the condition of the pipe fastening threads on the compressor. With the engine off and the compressor off, bring the leak detector probe up to the compressor pulley near the shaft stem and rear cylinder head gasket to check for leaks. If there is a leak, repeat the test to make sure that there really is a leak. Also check whether the leak is located in other coolant system components. End of diagnosis 1. Compressor pipe o-rings poorly positioned (pinching). 1. Reposition the compressor pipe o-rings correctly. 2. Pipe fastening threads not intact. 2. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 3. Leak located on shaft stem or compressor rear head. 3. Replace the compressor Op. 5040A20 AIR CONDITIONING COMPRESSOR - R+R - INCLUDES FLUID LEVEL CHECK AND TOP UP IF NECESSARY 4. Leak located in other cooling system components. 4. Remove the leak and restore the circuit to correct operation. If the compressor is replaced due to a mechanical problem, remember to clean the entire circuit and change the drier filter.

Whilst driving there is noise coming from the fan. This diagnosis can only be made after See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING Carry out the latter first. The climate control is working normally but there is excessive noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. Test results 0 PRELIMINARY CHECKS ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Having carried out the road test, during the See table S015 NOISE WHILST DRIVING there was a noise from the front identified as a noise coming from the passenger compartment fan. In particular, check: that the fan and spiral is clean, if there are any foreign bodies, deposits of dust on the vanes and/or leaves remove them/blow through moving the fan from the engine support; that there are no breaks or cracks in the fan; there are no vibrations or noise at low speed (check the operation with the fan detached from the assembly but the electrical connection fitted). "The operation for determining vibrations should be carried out with great care wearing protective goggles to avoid fragments of the fan being expelled into the surrounding area" Move on to Step 2 1.Fan dirty 1.Clean the fan casing and all the ducts. 2.Presence of breaks or cracks in the fan. 2.Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. 3. Electric motor noisy, fan not balanced or blades. 3. Replace the fan. Op. 5040C30 AIR CONDITIONING FAN - R.R. 2 AIR DUCT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check for foreign bodies and damaged components inside the air ducts. Move on to Step 3 Presence of foreign bodies or damaged components inside the air ducts. Eliminate the obstructions from the dashboard ducts. 3 AIR VENT CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the vents are intact and that there are no foreign bodies that could give rise to noise. Move on to Step 4 Vents obstructed. Restore the operation of the vents. 4 POLLEN FILTER CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the pollen filter is not blocked and that the recirculation air intake is not blocked with foreign bodies or parts (e.g. wiring) that are not correctly fitted. Move on to Step 5 1. Filter obstructed. 1. Replace the filter element Op. 5010B09 PURIFYING (POLLEN) FILTER FILTER ELEMENT - REPLACE 2. Air intake blocked by foreign bodies. 2. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation. 5 FAN INTAKE CHECK ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the fan intake in the air intake chamber is not blocked by the presence of foreign bodies. End of diagnosis Presence of foreign bodies in the air intake chamber. Eliminate the obstructions and restore correct operation.

Seal not perfect. 2. Restore the correct operation of the seal. 6 EVAPORATOR REPLACEMENT ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Replacement of the evaporator (check whether it is possible to clean it) "The use of Aircomatic equipment amd Wynn's Airco-clean is recommended for disinfecting the mould on the evaporator and the directions should be followed". The diagnostic equipment signals: Error P0087 (Pressure at pipe) This error is detected if the pressure measured is too low. As a result, the engine is switched off. 0 Preliminary checks ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION The fuel system is highly sensitive. The work must be carried out with the greatest cleanliness and care. Any air in the system could damage the high pressure fuel pump. The vehicle must therefore never be driven with the fuel tank empty. Check that the tank contains the correct type of fuel. The fuel reserve should be more than 5 litres. Check that there are no leaks from the fuel system. Check the hoses and pipes connected to identify any obstructions, damage, etc. Check that the connectors and seals are correctly fitted. Move on to Step 1 1.The tank contains irregular substances (petrol, other fluids) 1.Clean the tank and refill it correctly 2.There are less than 5 litres in the tank 2.Top up the fuel level to more than 5 litres 3.Fuel system leaking or not correctly sealed 3.Renew the seal for the system. If necessary, replace the faulty components 4.Pipes obstructed or damaged 4.Renew the pipes. If necessary, replace the faulty components 1 High pressure check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check that the diesel pressure parameter is correct as described in the test.
