test, that the pressure in the return pipe to the tank is less than 1 bar See Test 1060OA CHECK ON RETURN LOW PRESSURE FUEL CIRCUIT Move on to Step 4 Pressure above the maximum limit: return pipe to the tank obstructed Repair the pipe, if necessary, replace it 4 Low supply pressure check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Check, as described in the test, that the diesel pressure between the filter and the pressure pump is between 2 and 3 bar See Test 1060OB CHECK ON SUPPLY LOW PRESSURE FUEL CIRCUIT Move on to Step 10 Pressure below the minimum limit or above the maximum limit Move on to Step 5 5 Low supply pressure check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Constrict the return pipe, downstream of the valve, and carry out the test again with the pipe constricted checking that the pressure at the filter outlet stays below 2 bar See Test 1060OB CHECK ON SUPPLY LOW PRESSURE FUEL CIRCUIT Move on to Step 6 Pressure rises to 5 bar: pressure regulator valve on filter mounting pump pressure at the filter inlet is more than 2.2 bar Move on to Step 10 Pressure below 2.2 bar Move on to Step 8 8 Low supply pressure check ALL OK PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED ACTION Measure the difference The fuel system is highly sensitive. The work must be carried out with the greatest cleanliness and care. Any air in the system could damage the high pressure fuel pump. The vehicle must therefore never be driven with the fuel tank empty. CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check that the tank contains the correct type of fuel Remove the content and wash the tank 2 The fuel reserve must be greater than 5 litres. Put back a fuel quantity of at least 5 litres 3 Check for leaks in the fuel circuit. Check the hoss and connected pipes to identify any obstructions, damage etc. Check for breaks/scratches on the fuel supply or injection pipes. Check the fuel pipe fittings (quick-fit) Check that the oil pipes are not leaking. Check the condition of the three-way fastening elements. Check the fittings and seals are correctly fitted (use only Fiat Auto approved sealants). Check for blockages, leaks, air or water in the fuel system. Repair or, if necessary, replace the faulty components Op. 1040 FUEL TANK AND PIPES 4 Check the tightening torques for the capscrews: Restore component tightness to the correct values 5 Check the fuel filter Restore the fuel filter to correct working order or replace if necessary Op. 1044B20

Check the seal of the secondary air inlet/turborcharging system hoses. Also check for any obstructions or porosity. Check for leaks in the intercooler. Check that the pipe restriction bands in the air intake/inlet system are correctly fitted. Install fitting 1.870.752.000 between the turbocharging sensor and the intake chamber. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Position the diagnostic equipment in the passenger compartment and make the connections. Select "pressure gauge" on the diagnostic equipment and prepare for the acquisition of data in "intake pressure" mode with a 2000 mmHg full scale deflection and select a time of 10 seconds. Road test the vehicle (observing the speed limits in force) and perform the following test: - On a motorway route, allow the vehicle to reach 2500 rpm in 4th gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar. - On a motorway route with fast-moving traffic, let the vehicle reach 2500 rpm in 3rd gear. - Initiate graphic acquistion by pressing start on the diagnostic equipment and 2 seconds later fully depress the accelerator pedal until the engine speed is 3500 rpm. - Once this speed is reached completely release the accelerator pedal. - Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant section, with the exception of the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 -2080 mbar (1444 -1581 mmHg) corresponding to a supercharging value of 900 -1080 mbar.

Visually inspect that during start-up, the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vanes adjustment device) moves by around 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. Also check the conditions of the wheel rims making sure they are not distorted or broken, replacing them if any faults are found. Carry out the test on an uneven road surface, at a speed of 40 km/h to check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by small imperfections (suspension damping) with the consesquent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment. Check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by large imperfections and the consequent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment, carry out the road test at a speed of 40 km/h over a route that has a series of pot-holes. Check the rapid damping of any pitching produced by the irregularities in the road surface, carrying out the test at a speed of 50 km/h on a straight road with suitably spaced humps and holes. This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the driving comfort of the vehicle in accordance with the enclosed table. Judgement Vote Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 The reference vehicle has a driving comfort default rating of 7.

Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. Before proceeding with the test, check the tyre inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring it to the correct values if it is found to be incorrect. Also check the wheel rim conditions, checking for distortions or breaks, replacing them if they are found to be faulty. Carry out the test on a route where there are left and right hand bends of different degrees, evaluating the laying down speed of the vehicle round the bends, trying to take the bends at a constant speed, avoiding carrying out pull/release manoeuvres. Evaluate the stability of the vehicle by simulating a lane change/overtaking and check that violent vehicle reactions do not appear leading to unsafe driving during this manoeuvre. Then carry out a road test on an unmade road (cobblestones) where there are right/left hand bends of different degrees to evaluate the tendency of the rear of the vehicle to lose grip. This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the behaviour of the vehicle in terms of rolling/pitching in accordance with the enclosed table. Judgement Vote Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 The reference vehicle has a rolling/pitching default rating of 7.

Disconnect the electrical connection for the linear sensor. See K120 LINEAR SENSOR FOR FANS Check that Pin 1 is earthed and Pin 2 is at +5V. Connect a linear potentiometer (end of scale 1 KOhm, previously positioned at around 500 ohm between the centre pin andone of the side ones) to the pins of the linear sensor electrical connector. Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Using a multimeter, check that the voltage between pins 1 and 3 is around 2.5V. Switch on the engine and switch on the air conditioning using the special switch located on the climate control system control unit. The climate control system should come on normally in these circumstances. Alter the potentiometer resistance until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is about 0 V. The air conditioning system should switch off in these conditions because the engine management node receives low circuit pressure information. Alter the potentiometer resistance until the voltage reading on the multimeter between pins 1 and 3 is about 4.6V. The air conditioning system should switch off in these conditions because the engine management node receives high circuit pressure information.

Using an Examiner set to the Voltmeter mode, select a 20 Volt full scale deflection and 5 seconds, connect the black probe to the vehicle earth and the red probe on pin 3 of the mist sensor output signal, turn the key on and press the START button. The signal shown should be a set of PWM impulses with a frequency of 100 Hz and a Duty Cycle that varies between 10 and 90% as indicated in the table below. The first 100 sensor output readings should not be considered (about 1 sec). 1. earth 2. +15 3. not connected 4. signal output PWM% Duty Cycle = T1 / T2 where: T1= duration of impulse T2 = 1/f = 1/100 Hz = Duratation of transmission T2 = 10msec ± 7% PWM of 20% at 70% This is the normal sensor operating range. Within this range, the sensor supplies a PWM signal proportional to the amount of condensation present on the windscreen. PWM = 10% Indicates an internal sensor fault. This fault is defined as follows: the sensor self-diagnosis detected an internal electrical problem. PWM = 80% This condition indicates a sensor limit condition. This is defined as follows: The sensor optics are saturated due to too much direct sunlight. The signal is transmitted as long as the limit condition described above persists. PWM = 90% This condition indicates a sensor limit condition or failure. It is defined as one of the following: The sensor optics are saturated due to too much reflected energy. This may be due to a very high level of condensation or an object between the windscreen surface and the sensor. The internal sensor temperature reached and exceeded 70°C. The internal processor is disabled to avoid damage. A fault signal is transmitted as long as the excess temperature persists. PWM = 0 % and 100% These two conditions will never be transmitted by the sensor. Specific hardware faults may be interpreted by the receiving input stage as PWM signals or 0% or 100% due to the static nature of the signal (microcomputer that does not process or conditions of dc to +12V or GND or open circuits). Messages transmitted by PWM 100% Sensor " off " or fault in communication or d.c. to +12 V 90% Sensor saturated or locked in excess temperature 80% Sensor faulty or subject to direct sunlight 70% Condensation intensity Max to moderate 60% Condensation intensity moderate to slight 50% Condensation intensity light to identifiable 40% Condensation intensity slightly visible 30% Condensation intensity not visible to the human eye 20% Windscreen clean - No condensation 10% Internal sensor fault. 0% Sensor " off " or fault in communication or d.c. to GND

Take the vehicle on the road under safe conditions and respecting the highway code Turn on the CRUISE CONTROL system and set the ON/OFF switch on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk to ON Check the Cruise Control warning light comes on. Drive the vehicle at 50 or 70 km/h in 4th gear (according to the maximum speed limit on the road). Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk towards SET + and release it immediately to store the speed reached. Remove your foot from the accelerator and check the vehicle maintains the set speed. Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk toward the SET+ position and maintain the position to increase the speed to 70 or 90 km/h (according to maximum speed limit on the road). do not operate the accelerator. Release the control wheel and maintain the set speed for a few seconds. Press the BRAKE pedal and release immediately, then wait for the vehicle speed to drop to 50 or 70 km/h do not operate the clutch. Press and release the RESUME key on the end of the stalk and check that the vehicle returns to the last stored speed value (70 or 90 km/h, according to the level set previously). do not operate the accelerator. Press the CLUTCH pedal and release immediately, then wait for the vehicle speed to drop to 50 or 70 km/h do not operate the brake Press and release the RECALL key on the end of the CRUISE CONTROL stalk and check that the vehicle returns to the last stored speed value (70 or 90 km/h, according to the level set previously). do not operate the accelerator. Turn the wheel on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk towards SET- to reduce vehicle speed to 50 or 70 km/h. do not operate the brake, clutch or accelerator pedals. Release the control wheel and maintain the set speed for a few seconds. Turn off the system by setting the ON/OFF switch on the CRUISE CONTROL stalk to OFF and check that the vehicle speed drops. do not operate the brake, clutch or accelerator pedals.

The key remote control is supplied by a CR2032 lithium battery (3 V, 220 mAh), remote control operation is ensured between 2.6 and 3.6 V with a maximum current of 15 mA. At least 9000 activations of 1 s duration and 3000 activations of 5 s duration are guaranteed over a period of two years. The battery voltage is monitored to check the charge level: the threshold is set at 2.6±0.06 V. If the remote control receiver detects that the battery is flat, it is still possible to carry out a total of 100 operations. Operating frequency: 433.92 MHz. CHECK TO BE PERFORMED RESOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Take out the key battery and connect the diagnostic instrument in Voltmeter mode to the key terminals with the correct polarity. Check that the voltage exceeds 2.2 Volts. Replace the battery Note that after replacing the battery, the remote control variable code must be re-synchronised: this operation is carried out by pressing the remote control key twice. Note that if the remote control has been activated more than 255 times, variable code synchrony between the sending unit and the receiver will be lost (the receiver will no longer be able to identify a variable code message correctly). Synchrony should therefore be restored by pressing the remote control unit key twice.

Check the operation of the satellite navigation system Check that the map disc is consistent with the vehicle model. In NAV mode, check that the number of satellites in the last line on the right is at least 3 indicating that the satellite reception is correct. If the reading for the number of satellites is less than 3 then the reception is not good enough to locate the vehicle. It is probably a question of insufficient cover. In this case try and move the vehicle to an area where there is good reception or compare the reception with other cars located in the same place. The satellite reception test should be carried out in an open area. In this case, without a comparison it is impossible to say whether or not the navigator is defective. If, on the other hand, the comparison reveals even worse reception, check the connection of the satellite aerial, the electrical continuity, the correct power supply and, if necessary, test with different equipment that is definitely working properly.

the Connect can be switched on manually, using the left knob or automatically with the key ON signal. If the Connect has been turned off manually (using the left knob), before turning the ignition OFF, it will not come out automatically at the next key ON. STEP CHECK TO BE CARRIED OUT SOLUTION IF THE CHECK IS NOT OK 1 Check power supply (+15) With the ignition ON, check that the correct battery voltage is present between pins 4 and 8 of the 8-way Connect connector and earth. Check the connector is correctly inserted in the other part. Try to move it from its seat by shifting it by a small amount in all directions, holding the connector case in your fingers and the wiring in your hand. The connector should remain in place Apply a moderate pulling force. The connector should remain in place check whether the power supply turns off, turns on and/or vice versa (touching/not touching) subject the cable to a pulling force and check cable stability (no shrinkage): apply repeated pull-push-pull cycles to the cable and check it remains immobile. Examine the crimping: Use a magnifying glass to examine the terminal criming area. The barrels must be turned symmetrically and three-stranded sections should not emerge from the criming area. The area of bare wire beneath the barrel must emerge by approximately 0.5 mm Replace the 7.5A fuse F 49 located in the CPL, after identifying the cause Restore the wiring if defective 2 Check earth Disconnect 8-way connector A and connect an ohmmeter accross pin 8 and earth and check the resistance is lower than 1 ohm Restore the correct earth connection between pin 8 and the earth point in the right dashboard area 3 Check power supply +30 Check that the correct battery voltage is present between pins 7 and 8 of the 8-way Connect connector and earth. Check the wiring continuity Replace the 15A fuse F 23 located in the CVM, after identifying the cause Restore the wiring if defective 4 Check fuse Check the condition of the fuse located at the back of the Connect. If burnt out, search for the cause of the problem and replace it. 5 Check action of protection Disconnect Connector 8-way connector B. Turn the Connect off and on. Check whether one of the components (CD Changer, amplifier, sound boxes, etc.) is causing the radio fuse to blow. Replace defective speakers Replace the defective amplifier Op. 5570T36 AMPLIFIER FOR SPEAKER SYSTEM - R+R Replace the CD Changer Op. 5570T85 CD/AUDIO PLAYER/LOADER - R.R. If none of the above steps has highlighted problems with the signals and the Connect continues not to switch on then it is defective.

Apply a solution of soapy water to the entire perimeter of the glass. From inside the passenger compartment, blow through with compressed air along the entire perimeter, moving the trims to the side and the top, if necessary. Visually inspect for any bubbles of air on the outer surface: this makes it possible to locate any areas where the sealant is not sufficient or damaged. If there is a lack of sealant on the vertical pillars, the pillar trim can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the top section, the roof lining can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is a lack of sealant on the bottom section, the trim at the base of the (front) windscreen or the rear parcel shelf (for the rearscreen) can be moved and rubber type sealant can be injected from the inside. If there is insufficient sealant in widespread areas, the overall seal of the window cannot be guaranteed and therefore it has to be removed and the windscreen or the rearscreen must be completely resealed.

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: The steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

The engine oil level check should be carried out with the vehicle on a flat surface with the engine off a few minutes (5) after the engine has been switched off. - Extract the engine oil dipstick, clean it and then fully reinset it, extract it and check that the level is between the MIN and MAX marks on the actual dipstick. - If the oil level is close to or actually below the MIN mark, introduce the recommended oil through the filler until it reaches the MAX mark. If, after checking, the engine oil level is above the MAX mark, it must be corrected. After topping up the engine oil, before checking the level, let the engine run for a few seconds and wait for a few minutes after it has been switched off. Slowly introduce the recommended fluid into the circuit via the filler on the engine coolant supply reservoir, keeping the level above the MAX reference until fluid comes out of the bleed; then close the bleed screw. When the hood is moved using the electric control and is left in any intermediate position, even with the ignition switched off, the following takes place: - after 12 minutes the electric control no longer allows the hood to be moved normally, but only lets it be closed. - after a further three minutes the electric control allows no further movement. In order to be able to move the hood again normally using the electric control it is necessary to wait for at least 10 minutes, with the ignition off, to let the movement system cool down. To carry out checks, maintenance or repair operations with the hood stopped in any intermediate position, if the operation is expected to take more than 10 minutes, it is advisable to place the hood in the position necessary to carry out the operation, using the electric control, and then discharge the hydraulic system pressure as described below. Fit a pipe of appropriate length to the pipe section on the wate presence sensor on the fuel filter to allow fluid to be drained into a suitable container after bleeding. - Loosen the water presence sensor on the fuel filter. Carry out this action gradually, taking care to check that the amount of fuel expelled is between 75 and 80 cc - Tighten the water sensor on the fuel filter. - Examine the expelled fluid: if it contains water without evident traces of diesel, repeat the bleeding operation. - If traces of diesel appear, repeating the bleeding operation ensures that the fuel filter does not contain any more water. - Turn the ignition key to the OFF position. - Connect the electrical connection to the water presence sensor on the fuel filter. - Check that no more leaks are present in the lower part of the fuel filter after running the engine for one minute. ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working in safety.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle takes place through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated in the TEG, this takes place in entirely the same way as with the traditional remote control incorporated in the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safetly plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. INITIALISIATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode.

Carry out the measurement with all the emission control devices active and at the specified idle speed. - Insert the probe of an exhaust gas analyser into the end of the exhaust pipe for at least 30 cm. If the shape of the exhaust tailpipe will not allow the probe to be fully introduced, add an extension that ensures a seal in the joint area. - Wait for the exhaust gas tester indices to stabilise. - With the engine idling, check that the CO2 level is within specified limits. Carry out the measurement with all the emission control devices active and at the specified idle speed. - Allow the engine to warm up. - Insert the probe of an exhaust gas analyser into the end of the exhaust pipe for at least 30 cm. If the shape of the exhaust tailpipe will not allow the probe to be fully introduced, add an extension that ensures a seal in the joint area. - Wait for the exhaust gas tester indices to stabilise. - With the engine idling, check that the CO2 level is within specified limits. Measurement Value Validity CO2 emisssions (in accordance with directive 1999/100/CE) [g/km] 221 2.2 JTS Measurement Value Validity CO2 emisssions (in accordance with directive 1999/100/CE) [g/km] 270 3.2 JTS

- Start the car and let it warm up until the radiator cooling fan has come on twice. Leave as little time as possible before starting the test once the engine is warm and avoid leaving the engine to idle for long periods. Check that the probe diameter is at least 0.22 times the diameter of the exhaust pipe. Ensure that the exhaust gas intake fittings do not allow leaks. - Position the fume meter measurement probe in the end of the exhaust pipe, ensuring that its end is positioned in a pipe section where the gas flow is evenly distributed. - If necessary, to meet the above requirements, apply an extension to the exhaust pipe so that the coupling to the exhaust pipe is sealed and the end of the probe is positioned in a long straight section towards the engine that is at least six times the tailpipe diameter and at least three times the tailpipe diameter downstream. Check that the probe intake pipe from the tailpipe to the fume meter is on an ascending gradient without any sharply angled joints. Ensure the counterpressure at the probe is as specified and does not exceed 7.5 bars during the test. - With the engine running at idle speed, place the gearbox in neutral and release the clutch pedal. - Position the fume metre so that exhaust gas can be drawn off. - Take the reading shown by the fume meter pointer. - As the engine is idling, operate the accelerator pedal quickly but smoothly until the engine is running at maximum rpm and the regulator cuts in. - Record and note down the maximum fume level indicated by the fume meter during acceleration without taking values during the release stage into account. - Once the maximum rotation speed has been achieved, release the accelerator control until the engine resumes idling. - Check that the fume meter pointer returns to the position measured previously at idle speed. - Repeat the above operations at least six times until the fume readings stabilise. The readings may be considered stable when they are within a band that is 0.25 m-1 wide for four consecutive readings and not in decreasing order. - The fume value to be considered is the arithmetic mean of the four stabilised values. - Check that the fume level meets the required value stamped on the vehicle marking summary plate located in the engine compartment and indicated in the following table. Measurement Value Validity Exhaust fumes 0.51 m-1 2.4 JTD 20V

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow very carefully the warnings given below when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damaging components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed: this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated. ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow very carefully the warnings given below when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damaging components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead hammer if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin hammer for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed: this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated. ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: The steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that it has taken place, carry out the check described below. Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the door and check that the window does not lower during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

If this procedure is carried out after removing-refitting the propeller shaft, make sure that the "alignment shims" which may have been removed during the removal have been refitted. CHECK THE ALIGNMENT BETWEEN THE REAR SECTION AND THE RDA "D" 1. Fit the tool prepared previously with the following components as illustrated: the "base" (1a) marked with the letters "A/D"; the "collar" (1b) marked with the letter "DA" and the "calibrated pin" (1c) marked with the letter "D" fitted in the special opening in the base marked with the letter "D". The spacers available from the Parts Dept. are 2 and 5 mm and should never be used in pairs. After fitting the spacers refit the brackets using the special bolts depending on the shim used. After fitting the spacers, check the propeller shaft angles once again.

Removing Refitting - Position the driveshaft in a vice fitted with protective jaws. 1. Remove the bands securing the protective boot using a suitable tool. If the boot cannot be moved back, cut it using an appropriate tool and remove it. 1. Clean the driveshaft constant velocity joint until the safety ring is accessible. 1. Extend the safety ring using suitable pliers. 2. Extract the wheel side constant velocity joint from the driveshaft. NOTE: On joints without a safety ring, remove the constant velocity joint from the driveshaft by force. 1. Remove the wheel side constant velocity joint safety ring. On joints without a safety ring, the ring is positioned on the driveshaft and must therefore be removed from this position. 1. Remove the protective boot. Place a new safety ring in the housing on the constant velocity joint. Check that the safety ring is correctly fitted. For joints without a safety ring, fit a new safety ring on the driveshaft. - Place the wheel side constant velocity joint in its housing on the driveshaft. Push the constant velocity joint until the safety ring is correctly positioned. - Fill the joint and the boot with the specified grease. Component Type Description Classification Qty. ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: The steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: The steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

ATTENTION All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid personal injury.The engine compartment contains many moving parts, components at high temperatures and live wires. Follow the warnings given below very carefully when working in the engine compartment: turn off the engine and wait for it to cool down, do not smoke, do not use naked flames and ensure a fire extinguisher is available.The use of special tools is required for certain procedures. The use of these tools is vital for working safely.Follow the current workshop safety regulations. Where necessary, the Manual contains specific procedures to be followed to prevent dangerous situations from arising.For the use of chemical products, follow the safety instructions on the card from the supplier to the consumer.The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000 V and above which could be very hazardous to people especially if they are suffering from a heart condition. Therefore take great care when working on these systems or in the vicinity of their components. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob.The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a conventional key.Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. All the operations should be carried out taking great care to avoid damage to components.To release parts that are sticking, tap gently using an aluminium or lead mallet if iron materials are involved; use a wooden or resin mallet for light alloy parts.When dismantling, check that components that should be marked have the appropriate references.When refitting, lubricate the parts, where necessary, to prevent seizing during the initial operating period. When refitting it is vital to respect the adjustment nut tightening torques.Each time they are refitted, replace gaskets, oil seals, flexible washers, safety plates, self-locking nuts, pre-treated screws and all parts that have deteriorated.Use adhesive paper or clean cloths to suitably protect those parts of the engine which, if they remain uncovered after dismantling, will allow dust or foreign bodies to enter.Only genuine spare parts should be used to replace units or components that have been removed. this is the only way of ensuring the interchangeability and perfect operation of the various components. When the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the same condition (released or locked) as previously. Whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected during workshop operations, leave the TEG inserted when disconnecting the battery: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. PRECAUTIONS When the engine is hot the cooling system is pressurized. Wait for a few minutes before working on the cooling system components, making sure that the pressure has been discharged. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALISIATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS Before dismantling the air conditioning system cooling circuit the system must be drained and the refrigerant collected. Op. 0010T84 COOLANT FOR AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM - DEHYDRATE AND REPRESSURIZE If the system components have been disconnected, seal the connectors with suitable plugs to prevent moisture and impurities getting into the system. Replace the O-rings on the connectors before reconnecting the pipes. Use only green coloured seals that are resistant to R134a refrigerant fluid. Lubricate the connector threads with anti-freeze and tighten the connectors to the recommended torque. R134a refrigerant fluid cannot be mixed with the Freon R12 that is used in climate control systems on earlier vehicles; therefore Freon R12 should never be used in air conditioning systems operating on R134a. All the system components have been specifically designed for the use of R134a and are NOT INTERCHANGEABLE with those from earlier vehicles using Freon R12. There is a special draining/collection system for R134a fluid. The anti-freeze for lubricating the compressor is also special and differs from the one used for systems running on Freon R12. Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. PRECAUTIONS The air conditioning system uses environmentally friendly R134a refrigerant fluid. The following safety instructions must be followed meticulously when working on the system: Any R134a fluid that may accidentally escape from the climate control system or the drainage/collection/repressurizing equipment may become toxic if it is very close to a naked flame or in the presence of certain metals (e.g. magnesium or aluminium) in the form of fine particles or powder. It is therefore advisable to work in an area where there are no naked flames, and which is well ventilated with an extraction system working. Avoid prolonged contact between R134a and the skin during evaporation because after expansion it can cause "burns" as a result of the low temperature (-26.5°C). It is therefore advisable to wear leather or thick fabric gloves. It is vital to protect eyes from contact with the refrigerant fluid because the extremely low temperature can cause serious injuries. Draining the fluid in the open air constitutes a danger to the environment. The R134a can only be drained using special equipment. When the engine is hot the cooling system is pressurized. Wait for a few minutes before working on the cooling system components, making sure that the pressure has been discharged. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.
