WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Take care with electrical arcs: Even if the voltage is 12V, the battery can produce high currents if there is a short circuit, creating arcs or sparks that can be dangerous to the mechanic or create a fire hazard; Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed To prevent serious damage to the electrical and electronic components, never try and start the engine with the battery earth lead slack. Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed To prevent serious damage to the electrical and electronic components, never try and start the engine with the battery earth lead slack. Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Take care with electrical arcs: Even if the voltage is 12V, the battery can produce high currents if there is a short circuit, creating arcs or sparks that can be dangerous to the mechanic or create a fire hazard; Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed To prevent serious damage to the electrical and electronic components, never try and start the engine with the battery earth lead slack. Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. - Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Take care with electrical arcs: Even if the voltage is 12V, the battery can produce high currents if there is a short circuit, creating arcs or sparks that can be dangerous to the mechanic or create a fire hazard; Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed To prevent serious damage to the electrical and electronic components, never try and start the engine with the battery earth lead slack. Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Take care with electrical arcs: Even if the voltage is 12V, the battery can produce high currents if there is a short circuit, creating arcs or sparks that can be dangerous to the mechanic or create a fire hazard; Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it, but rather by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. Access to the vehicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated into the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated into the key fob. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. The following documentation often still uses the expressions Key ON, Key OFF, ignition-operated power supply (INT) or key to MAR, key to STOP, key to AVV. These must be interpreted in accordance with the following summary table: Key ON TEG inserted in TEG Reader Key OFF TEG removed from TEG Reader ignition controlled power supply (INT) TEG inserted into TEG Reader key on MAR TEG inserted in TEG Reader key on STOP TEG removed from TEG Reader key on AVV TEG inserted and START/STOP button pressed To prevent serious damage to the electrical and electronic components, never try and start the engine with the battery earth lead slack. Never pull the leads or wiring using force because this would result in the cables being disconnected from the connectors or terminals. Disconnect all the control units and electronic devices when carrying out arc welding operations on the bodyshell. Before replacing a fuse, check that the circuit protected is not faulty. When replacing fuses, make sure that the new fuse is the correct amperage. Do not use fuses that have a higher or lower amperage than required. PRECAUTIONS When working on electrical components, always follow very carefully the precautions described below: Remove rings, wrist watches and other metal objects. Take care with electrical arcs: Even if the voltage is 12V, the battery can produce high currents if there is a short circuit, creating arcs or sparks that can be dangerous to the mechanic or create a fire hazard; Take care over high voltages. The electronic ignition system produces voltages of 20,000V and more, which could be very dangerous. Take great care when working on or near these components. Prevent fire risks. Do not smoke when working close to the battery or components which get hot during use (e.g. halogen bulbs), nor in the area of the engine compartment when the engine is still hot. Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring, etc.) turn the ignition key OFF and DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS TO BE FOLLOWED FOR OPERATIONS ON VEHICLES FITTED WITH AIR BAG SYSTEMS The following instructions MUST BE FOLLOWED during any operation involving vehicles equipped with Air Bags and pretensioners. Preliminary instructions It should be remembered that Air Bag modules should be handled with care. Their use, transportation and storage are regulated by the procedures for handling such components, which are given below. Before carrying out any repair operations to the bodywork, welding or operations that involve removing the Air Bag modules or the control unit: Always disconnect the battery, i.e.: disconnect the two leads from the pole and insulate them taping them carefully. Disconnect the electrical connection for the control unit waiting at least 10 minutes after disconnecting the battery. If the battery is disconnected the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Position the devices with the cover upwards in the lockable metal cupboard. This cupboard, especially designed for this purpose, should not, under any circumstances, be used to store any other types of material, particularly if they are flammable. The cupboard should be designed to store pyrotechnic charges (metal, impact resistant cupboard with grates to allow natural ventilation) and should have the markings required by law (DANGER EXPLOSIVES - NO NAKED FLAMES - NOT TO BE OPENED BY UNAUTHORIZED PERSONNEL). All the connectors used and wired to the Air Bag modules and/or pretensioners contain a short circuit clip. Until the Air Bag modules and/or pretensioners are connected to an appropriate energy source there is no possibility of them being accidentally activated. The continuity of the system components can only be measured after the modules have been replaced with specific dummy resistances. A system component that has not been activated during an accident is considered to still be "active". Therefore unexploded components that have to be removed from the vehicle (on account of defects or the warranty has expired, etc.) should be returned to the special centre following the procedure described below. The safety system components should ONLY be fitted and dismantled by skilled, authorized personnel. Failure to follow the procedures described below could result in the accidental activation of the system, personal injury or repairs to the system that are not necessary. AIR BAG MODULES AND/OR PRETENSIONERS MUST NOT, UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES, BE DISMANTLED.. All the system components have been specifically designed to work on a specific marque and type of vehicle, therefore Air Bags should not be adapted, reused or installed on other vehicles, only the ones for which they have been designed and produced. Any attempt to resue, adapt or install one on a different type of vehicle could result in serious injury or even be fatal for the occupants of the vehicle in the case of an accident. Interventions on system components After every repair to the system it should be checked using the EXAMINER or other diagnostic equipment. Module duration The system pyrotechnic components have different life spans. Therefore they must be replaced at the following intervals: Air bag modules or pretensioners: 14 years Clock spring: 10 years Air bag module replacement (due to defects or expiry of warranty) If an Air Bag module is being replaced because it is defective or the warranty has expired: Remove the detachable part of the adhesive label from the new module and place it in the special folder containing the vehicle details (model, registration date, chassis number) and the serial number of the old module. The file should be kept for future checks. A new adhesive plate is supplied together with the module and it should be stuck on top of the one located either near the driver (door or centre pillar) or in the passenger glove compartment. However, it must be perforated first at the month 14 years after the year in which the module is fitted (e.g. 2019 for 2005). Similarly, if the clock spring or a pretensioner is being replaced, remember that the recommended life of these components is 10 years. Control unit replacement The electronic control unit should ALWAYS be replaced after an impact that results in the entire system being activated (Air Bag and pretensioners). If the control unit is being replaced, the detachable part of the adhesive label must also be removed and placed the special file mentioned above. Replacing the clock spring The clock spring for connecting the driver's Air Bag module is equipped with a device that automatically stops it rotating when the steering wheel is removed. This is designed to prevent the upper plate, now no longer secured to the steering wheel, from turning freely and unwinding or winding the coil inside the device and possibly causing it to break. The device is automatically released when refitting the steering wheel. In the case of replacement, the replacement clock spring is supplied separately from the steering column switch unit and it should be fitted with the wheels straight because this is the corresponding position for the new device. The new device is equipped with a safety tab that keeps it locked. Painting operations There are no special safety regulations to follow for painting and subsequent drying operations in an oven because the modules in particular have been designed in such a way that the outside surfaces of the vehicle are not damaged when they get hot from normal paint drying systems. It is forbidden to use naked flames near the modules. All the electronic control units (including the Air Bag system) are always removed if the ambient temperature could reach or exceed 85°C. Interventions after an accident If any of the safety system components is damaged following an accident it MUST be replaced. Do not attempt to repair the control unit, clock spring or Air Bag modules and/or pretensioners. Accidents with or without system activation Several of the system components should be inspected after an accident whether the system has been activated or whether it has NOT been activated. These components are: Steering column; Steering column supports; Electronic control unit and modules mounting area; Clock spring; Dashboard (the area of the passenger Air Bag module and knee bag). If the component shows signs of distortion, breaks or bends it should be replaced. Accidents with system activation Several of the system components should be replaced if the vehicle is subject to a frontal impact that has fully or partly activated the system. In the case of partial activation (pretensioners, Side Bags or Head Bags), these components are: Pretensioners, Side Bags or Head Bags Electronic control unit (only after the third activation of the pretensioners, Side Bags or Head Bags) In the case of total activation (Air Bags, Side Bags, Head Bags and pretensioners), these components are: Front Air Bag modules Knee Bag modules Pretensioners, Side Bags or Head Bags Electronic control unit As far as the wiring and connectors are concerned, they should be inspected for any signs of burning, melting of the outside insulation or damage from excessive heat. Any signs of damage to the clock spring or in the area where the electronic control unit and Air Bag modules are mounted means that the damaged components should be replaced. Dangers to health The following precautions should be observed when handling activated Air Bag modules and/or pretensioners: - wear polythene protective gloves and safety goggles; - wash your hands and other parts of the body exposed with soap and water after touching exploded Air Bag units. Effects of overexposure There is no potential danger of exposure to the propellants as the system is completely sealed. The propellant mixture is in a solid state therefore it is impossible to inhale it even if the gas generator cartridge is broken. There is no danger to human health if the gas escapes. Contact with the skin should be avoided and the propellant should not be swallowed. In the case of: - Contact with skin: wash immediately with soap and water. - Contact with eyes: wash eyes immediately with running water for at least 15 minutes. - Inhalation: take the affected person into the open air immediately. - Swallowing: induce vomiting if the person is conscious. A doctor should always be called in these situations. SAFETY REGULATIONS WHEN HANDLING MODULES In normal conditions the driver's and passenger Air Bags and/or pretensioners are activated by the electronic command during the impact. The gases that develop in these conditions are not toxic. It is important that the personnel who carry out repairs to devices fitted on the vehicle follow the safety regulations listed below. The personnel working on the devices should be trained and should observe the following precautions: - When removing and replacing open (exploded) Air Bags, only move the modules one at a time and wear protective gloves and goggles for the removal. Always rest the Air Bag module with the opening flap and the pre-breaking splining facing upwards. Never place anything on top of this flap. - Do not hold pretensioners by the rod when handling. - At the end of the operations wash your hands thoroughly with soap and, if there is any contact with the residual powder and your eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of running water. - On all versions with Air Bags it is forbidden to work from the front seats before having rendered the system inoperative by disconnecting the two battery leads and waiting at least 10 minutes. - The metal Air Bag components are very hot just after it has exploded. Avoid touching these components for 20 minutes after the Air Bag has been activated. - Never carry out repair operations on Air Bag modules or pretensioners. Send all defective modules to the supplier. - Never heat the Air Bag module (e.g. through welding, striking, drilling, mechanical machining, etc.); - Never fit Air Bag units and/or pretensioners that have been dropped or show signs of any type of damage. The storage of Air Bag modules together with flammable or combustible materials is prohibited. Gas generators should not come into contact with acid, grease or heavy metal: contact with these substances could cause the formation of gases that are poisonous or harmful or explosive compounds. Replacement parts should be stored in their original packaging and the same procedures as for Air Bag modules that have not been activated and have been removed from the vehicle should be followed for their temporary storage, i.e. in a specially designed, locked, metal cupboard (impact resistant metal cupboard with grates for natural ventilation) The cupboard should have special warning signs (DANGER: EXPLOSIVES - NO NAKED FLAMES - NOT TO BE OPENDED BY UNAUTHORIZED PERSONNEL). SCRAPPING AIR BAG MODULES OR PRETENSIONERS The Air Bag modules and/or pretensioners fitted on the vehicle should not be scrapped with the actual vehicle, but removed first. The Air Bag units and/or pretensioners cannot be scrapped unless they have been activated first. If the Air Bag module and/or pretensioners has not been activated during an accident it should be considered as still charged. All unexploded material SHOULD NOT BE ACTIVATED, but should be sent to a specialist centre with the following written on the accompanying docket: "AIR BAG CONTAINING PYROTECHNIC CHARGE TO BE DEACTIVATED". The local laws in force must be observed. The devices must be sent in the packaging that replacement components are received in and, if it is not available, the packaging only can be ordered from the PARTS DEPT. Obviously, if Air Bags and/or pretensioners are being replaced, the original packaging should be kept intact for dispatching devices not activated. Not following the procedures described here can cause the accidental activation of Air Bag units and/or pretensioners and result in personal injury. Air Bag units that have NOT been activated should be disposed of through normal methods. Air Bag units and/or pretensioners that have not bee activated contain substances that are dangerous to health and can cause personal injury if the sealed container is damaged during disposal. The disposal of Air Bag units and/or pretensioners not carried out in accordance with this procedure may be in violation of regulations in force on this subject. ORDERING METHODS If necessary, the devices can be ordered, as and when required, from the Aftersales Parts Department - Volvera through the V.O.R. procedure since the Network should not keep these parts in stock. In any case, a record should be kept of internal movements by recording the module identification numbers and vehicle details (chassis number, registration date, model, etc.).

PROGRAMMING THE ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) The electronic key is programmed at end of line together with the ALFA CODE. During the vehicle's lifetime, it is possible to make the TEG Reader (NTR) learn new keys, e.g. if ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) are added or deleted. Upon each new programming procedure, all the Electronic Keys not presented during the above procedure (for the removal of lost keys) are cleared from the memory. Upon each new programming procedure, all the Electronic Keys not presented during the above procedure (for the removal of lost keys) are cleared from the memory. Procedure for storing an electronic key teg The TEG storage procedure is managed by the Diagnostic instrument (Examiner) and can be activated only by entering the ELECTRONIC CODE (shown on the CODE CARD). The procedure consists of learning the TEG codes and involves secret codes being received by the TEG Reader and then stored. During the procedure, the codes are stored permanently in the TEG Reader EEPROM memory. Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to initialise the TEG learning procedure and confirms this to the operator; the operator enters the first TEG to be stored; the TEG Reader receives the secret code and the ID of the ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG) and learns it; the Diagnostic instrument confirms that learning has taken place; the previous stages are repeated for each TEG that must be learned, up to a maximum of 8; once the TEGs have been learned, the operator asks the Diagnostic instrument to store them: the Diagnostic instrument commands the TEG Reader to store the TEGs learnt. Only TEGs learned during the procedure are stored in the EEPROM. Any TEGs no longer presented will not be stored. CODE SYSTEM COMPONENT MANAGMENT There is a centralized DATA BASE (for all markets) managed by the FIAT PARTS DIVISION for ordering all CODE system components. The production plant transfers all the necessary data into this data base together at the time of vehicle production. FIAT PARTS then uses this data base for ordering components that need replacing by the Dealer Network. The data base contains numerous pieces of information, such as: vehicle chassis no.; secret code; code of each ELECTRONIC KEY (TEG); emergency key mechanical code; Programming data If one of the CODE system components needs replacing and is being ordered, follow the procedure described below. Lost teg Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. The codes of the lost TEGs must be cleared from the memory of the TEG Reader: proceed as follows: Connect the Tester to the tester output on the vehicle. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode. enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory. At the end of the procedure, print a table showing the identification code/s still enabled. If no printer is available, transcribe the codes from the screen to the FIAT PARTS system form. Only if the Body Computer already contains 8 ELECTRONIC KEYS (TEGs) send the codes to Fiat Parts to update the DATABASE. Request for a new teg Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to request a new TEG (entering the part number) and specify the quantity. Note that the Body Computer is designed to store up to 8 TEGs. It is not therefore possible to accept orders when the sum of the number of TEGs already available to the customer plus the new TEGs ordered exceed this quantity. Keep a record of the form used to order the TEGs in order to monitor the situation. Programming teg codes into the teg reader memory Once the new TEGs have been received from Fiat Parts, ensure that all the old TEGs in the customer's possession are available. Connect the Tester to the vehicle tester output and run the following procedure. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode. enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader. end PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory. Check system operation before returning the vehicle to the customer by starting it up using all the TEGs and opening/closing the doors using the remote control unit. In the case of operating faults, it is possible to order spare parts only, but it is absolutely forbidden to exchange electronic control units between different TEGs because it will not be possible to service the vehicle in the future. Replacing lock barrels and/or emergency mechanical keys This becomes necessary when one or more door lock barrels (driver's door lock or others) are forced. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single electronic key kit complete with dowels (entering the part number) for the vehicle type and specification. It is not possible to order a single barrel by giving a single mechanical code. The mechanical code of the emergency key and the electronic code of the TEG are defined together during initial memorisation on a vehicle at end of line and must not be separated under any circumstances. Replacing the reg reader Ask the Customer for all the remaining TEGs in their possession. They should also prove that they are the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single TEG Reader (entering the part number to identify the version). Once the new programmed TEG Reader has been received from Fiat Parts, proceed as follows: Check the serial number stamped on the plate applied to the order form corresponds to that shown on the TEG Reader. Check the vehicle chassis no. printed on the plate applied to the order form corresponds to the vehice chassis no. If all codes correspond, install the TEG Reader on the vehicle instead of the malfunctioning unit. Connect the Tester to the tester output on the vehicle. Set the TEG Reader to PROGRAMMING mode. enter the TEGs still in the driver's possession into the TEG Reader. End PROGRAMMING mode; the IDs of any TEGs not presented will be cleared from the TEG Reader memory (NTR). Check system operation before returning the vehicle to the customer by starting it up using all the TEGs and opening/closing the doors using the remote control unit. Replacing the engine management control unit This is required if the engine malfunctions. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the personal computer provided to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the part number of the Engine Control Unit to be replaced. Once the Engine Control Unit has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow self-programming. Press the START/STOP button with the clutch or brake depressed to start the vehicle and check the engine is operating correctly. Replacing the electric steering lock This is required if the electric steering lock malfunctions. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the personal computer provided to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the part number of the Electric Steering Lock to be replaced. Once the Electric Steering Lock has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow self-programming. After 10s, remove the TEG from the TEG Reader and wait for the steering to lock mechanically (this will take place after approx 5s). Check that the steering is locked. Replacing the body computer This is required if the Body Computer malfunctions. The Customer must prove that he or she is the owner of the vehicle by producing the registration document and identification data. Use the Personal Computer supplied to log onto Fiat Parts. Enter the chassis no. of the customer's car, the model code and set up a VOR order to order a single Body Computer (entering the part number to identify the version). Once the Body Computer has been received from Fiat Parts, install it on the vehicle and insert the TEG in the TEG Reader to allow alignment of the Secret Codes. Press the START/STOP button with the clutch or brake depressed to start the vehicle and check the vehicle electrics are operating correctly.

WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS Follow these precautions when working on the tailgate assembly: When working on the hinges, take care not to damage the paintwork. Following an adjustment operation that required the hinges to be moved, the tailgate must be removed and the hinge area repainted. Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

Removing Refitting - Remove the rear parcel shelf. Op. 7015A05 TAILGATE LOWER INTERIOR PANEL-R R 1. Release the retaining buttons using the special tool. Tool Description Function Validity 1823015000 Knife Retainer removal 2. Undo the rear parcel shelf mounting pins. 3. Undo the bolts. 4. Release the inner retainers using the special tool. Tool Description Function Validity 1823015000 Knife Retainer removal 5. Keep the panel. Refitting Removing - Check that the panel is not damaged. - Position the panel and engage the inner retainers. - Tighten the bolts. - Tighten the rear parcel shelf mounting pins. - Attach the retaining buttons. Disconnect the control cable (3a) from lever retainers (3b). 4. Keep the lever. Refitting - Check that the lever is not damaged. Removing - Connect the control cable to the lever retainers. - Position the lever and tighten the bolts. - Check the operation of the bonnet lid opening mechanism.

Removing Refitting Op. 7025A24 BONNET LID OPENING LEVER - R+R Op. 7055B54 UNDER ENGINE PROTECTION/GUARD - R.R. Op. 7210E10 R.R. Fit a sensor to the end (2a) of the transmission cable (1b), then extract the transmission cable (2b), leaving the sensor in its place (to be used for reinserting the cable when refitting). Refitting Removing - Check that the control cable is not damaged. - Use the probe to reinsert the transmission cable in its seat. Avoid bending the bowden cable or kinking it so that it could become deformed. - Secure the bowden cable correctly to its retainers. Removing Refitting - Open the bonnet. 1. Undo the upper bolts fixing the front bumper. 1. Undo the lock retaining nuts. 2. Move lock (2a) slightly aside and disconnect retainers (2b) and (2c) from operating cable (2d). 3. Detach the electrical connection. Description Connector 3 BONNET OPEN SWITCH See I010 BONNET RELEASE SWITCH 4. Recover catch (2a) by moving the upper edge (4a) of the bumper slightly. Refitting Removing - Check that the lock is not damaged. - Slightly move the upper edge of the bumper and position the lock. - Connect the control cable to the lock retainers. - Screw in the lock nuts without tightening them. - Tighten the upper bolts fixing the front bumper. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity FRONT BUMPER Bolt M6x22 0.7 ÷ 1.1 1. Adjust the position of the lock. The arrows indicate the possible movements. - Tighten the lock nuts to the recommended torque. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity BONNET LID LOCK Nut M6 0.7 ÷ 1.1 - Check that the bonnet opens and closes properly.

Removing Refitting - Open the bonnet. 1. Release the retaining buttons using the special tool. Tool Description Function Validity 1823015000 Knife Retainer removal 2. Keep the weather strip. Refitting Removing - Check that the weather strip is not damaged. - Position the weather strip and do up the retaining studs. - Close the bonnet.

Removing Refitting - Open the bonnet. 1. Release the seal starting at one end. Refitting Removing - Check that the seal is intact and there are no signs of damage. - Position the seal and fit it in its housing starting at one end. - Check that the contact between the seal and the bonnet is correct.

Removing Refitting - Open the bonnet and support it appropriately. 1. Using a screwdriver, release the retaining springs from both ends of the telescopic strut (without removing them). 2. Remove the telescopic strut. 3. Undo the ball pins, if necessary. Refitting Removing - Check that the telescopic strut is not damaged. - If removed, retighten the ball pins. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity TELESCOPIC STRUT BALL JOINT 2.2 ÷ 2.6 - Refit the telescopic strut, press fitting the ends in the ball pins. - Fit the retaining springs. - Check the operation of the telescopic strut and ensure the boot lid is correctly supported.

- Open the boot lid. 1. Check that the self-adjusting buffers are working properly. Replace them if necessary. Op. 7025B12 BOOT LID BUFFERS/MOUNTINGS - R.R. AND ADJUST 2. Check that the boot lid housing seal along the entire perimeter is working properly. 3. If necessary, adjust the position of the lock striker. Op. 7040B22 LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT/LOAD PLATFORM MOULDING - R+R Op. 7025B58 BOOT LID LOCK STRIKER - R+R - If the adjustments indicated in the previous points are insufficient, adjust the position of the boot lid hinges as described below. Support the boot lid if necessary. 1. Working from both sides of the vehicle, loosen the boot lid bolts and adjust the boot lid position using the slotted holes in the hinges. The arrows indicate the possible movements 2. After adjustment, tighten the bolts to the specified torque. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity BOOT LID Bolt - 0.7 ÷ 0.8 - If necessary, adjust the lock striker position as described below. - If the adjustment of the fastening between boot lid and hinges is insufficient, proceed as follows. 3. Working from both sides of the vehicle, loosen the bolts (3a) fixing the tailgate hinges (3b) to the body and adjust the hinge position using the slotted holes. The arrows indicate the possible movements. 4. After adjustment, tighten the bolts to the specified torque. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity BOOT LID HINGES Bolt - 0.7 ÷ 0.8 - If necessary, adjust the lock striker position as described below.

Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Undo the end of travel buffers ring nut. 2. Remove the buffers from the housings for the boot lid using a screwdriver for leverage and raising the support plane. The buffers removed cannot be reused. Refitting Removing - Check that the new buffers are not damaged. 1. Fit the new buffers (1a) in place, without rotating the ring nut (1b) in relation to the base (1c). Place the mounting base (1c) in contact with the panel. There is only one mounting fitting position. - Close the boot lid twice, checking that it closes correctly and completely. During this stage the end of travel buffers adjust themselves by means of a movement inside their moving casing. - Reopen the boot lid. 2. Rotate the ring nut (1c) clockwise through around 340° until it is aligned with the references (2a and 2b) on the ring nut and on the base. - Close the boot lid again and check that it shuts properly and the profile is correct.

Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Undo the bolt and remove the retainer. 2. Release the retaining buttons using the special tool. Tool Description Function Validity 1823015000 Knife Retainer removal 3. Keep the trim. Refitting Removing - Check that the trim is not damaged. - Position the cover and fasten it using the retaining buttons. - Position the retainer and tighten the bolt. - Close the boot lid.

Removing Refitting Op. 7025B26 L/H OR R/H BOOT LID LIFT DEVICE (ONE) - R+R 1. Undo the boot lid hinge bolts. 2. Remove the hinges. Refitting Removing - Check that the hinge is not damaged. - Restore the sealant between the hinge and the body, then position the hinge. - Screw in the bolts without tightening (for alignment) Op. 7025B26 L/H OR R/H BOOT LID LIFT DEVICE (ONE) - R+R Op. 7025B10 BOOT LID - ALIGNMENT

Removing Refitting 1. Open the boot lid and support in a stable manner. 2. Using a screwdriver, release the retaining springs from both ends of the lift device (without removing them). 3. Remove the lifting device. 4. Undo the ball pins, if necessary. Refitting Removing - Check that the lifting device is not damaged. - If removed, retighten the ball pins. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity TELESCOPIC STRUT BALL JOINT 2.2 ÷ 2.6 - Refit the lifting device press-fitting the ends in the ball pins. - Fit the retaining springs. - Check the operation of the telescopic strut and ensure the boot lid is correctly supported.

Refitting Removing - Check that the control cable is not damaged. - Place the control cable in position. - Attach the front end of the control cable to the housing. - Tighten the trim fixing bolts. Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Release the retaining buttons (1a) using the special tool. Tool Description Function Validity 1823015000 Knife Retainer removal 2. Undo the bolts (2a) and move the lock (2b) after having moved the edge (2c) of the trim slightly. 1. Disconnect the electrical connection (1a) after having released the protection (1b). Move the striker (2a) and disconnect the emergency opening rod (2b) releasing it from the retainers (2c) and (2d). 3. Keep the striker. Refitting Removing - Check that the striker is not damaged. - Connect the emergency opening rod to the striker retainers. 1.
