Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Remove the perimeter seal releasing it from the housing. Refitting Removing - Check that the seal is intact and there are no signs of damage. 1. Place the seal in position so that the join (1a) is in line with the lock striker (1b). - Check that the contact between the seal and the boot lid is correct.

Removing Refitting Op. 7025B38 BOOT LID LOCK - R+R 1. Undo the bolts. 2. Remove the lock (2a) from the motor (2b). 3. If necessary, undo the bolts (3a) and separate the bracket (3b) from the motor (2b); lastly, disconnect the electrical connection (3c) from the motor. Refitting Removing - Check that the motor is not damaged. - If removed, connect the electrical connection to the motor, then position the wiring and the bracket and tighten the bolts. - Position the motor on the lock. - Tighten the bolts. Op. 7025B38 BOOT LID LOCK - R+R

Removing Refitting Op. 7040L75 GLOVE COMPARTMENT ON REAR TUNNEL TRIM R. R. 1. Undo the bolt. 2. Extract the switch and bridge (2a) and disconnect the electrical connection (2b). Description Component CENTRAL BOOT OPENING CONTROL SWITCH See H033 BOOT CENTRAL OPENING SWITCH 3. Keep the switch and wiring. Refitting Removing - Check that the switch is not damaged. - Connect the electrical connection. - Place the switch and wiring in position. - Tighten the bolt. Op. 7040L75 GLOVE COMPARTMENT ON REAR TUNNEL TRIM R. R.

Removing Refitting - Position the vehicle on a lift. - Raise the vehicle. 1. Undo the rear bolts fixing the right rear wheel arch liner. 2. Undo the nuts fixing the wheel arch. 3. Move the rear section of the wheel arch slightly after having released it from the housing. 1. Open the fuel filler cap access flap. 2. Working via the wheel arch housing, undo the inner flap fixing nuts. 3. Disconnect the retainer. 4. Remove the flap. Refitting Removing - Check that the flap is not damaged. - Position the flap. - Connect the retainer. - Working via the wheel arch housing, screw in the inner flap fixing nuts without tightening them. - Adjust the position of the flap in relation to the bodywork, then tighten the nuts. - Place the wheel arch in position. - Tighten the nuts and the bolts. - Remove the vehicle from the lift.

Removing Refitting - Open the tailgate. 1. Release the retainers (1a) and remove the right rear light cluster access cover (1b). 2. Extract the fuel filler emergency opening control cord (2a). Fit a sensor in the end (2b) of the cord (to be used for reinserting the cord during the refitting stage). - Open the fuel filler cap access flap. 1. Undo the motor fixing bolts. 2. Undo the fuel filler cap. 3. Gently extract the motor support. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. 1. Disconnect the emergency control cord (1a) from the motor retainer (1b). 2. Extract the actual cord leaving the sensor in its place. Refitting Removing - Check that the emergency control cord is not damaged. - Connect the emergency control cord to the motor retainer. 1. Using the sensor, place the cord (1a) in the right rear light cluster access compartment (1b). - Undo the fuel filler cap. - Place the support and motor in position and secure them using the bolts. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. - Close the fuel filler cap access flap. - Working from the luggage compartment, check that the cord is working. - Place the right rear light cluster access cover in position and secure it using the retainers. - Close the tailgate. Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Rotate the retainer (1a) and release it, then remove the access cover (1b) for the right rear light cluster, releasing the retainer (1c). 2. Extract the fuel filler emergency opening control cord (2a). Fit a sensor in the end (2b) of the cord (to be used for reinserting the cord during the refitting stage). - Open the fuel filler cap access flap. 1. Undo the motor fixing bolts. 2. Undo the fuel filler cap. 3. Gently extract the motor support. 4. Retighten the fuel filler cap. 1. Disconnect the emergency control cord (1a) from the motor retainer (1b). 2. Extract the actual cord leaving the sensor in its place. Refitting Removing - Check that the emergency control cord is not damaged. - Connect the emergency control cord to the motor retainer. 1. Using the sensor, place the cord (1a) in the right rear light cluster access compartment (1b). - Undo the fuel filler cap. - Place the motor and support in position. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. - Tighten the bolts fixing the motor. - Close the fuel filler cap access flap. - Working from the luggage compartment, check that the cord is working. - Place the right rear light cluster access cover in position and secure it using the retainers. - Close the boot lid.

Removing Refitting - Open the tailgate. 1. Release the retainers (1a) and remove the right rear light cluster access cover (1b). 2. Extract the fuel filler emergency opening control cord (2a). Fit a sensor in the end (2b) of the cord (to be used for reinserting the cord during the refitting stage). - Open the fuel filler cap access flap. 1. Undo the motor fixing bolts. 2. Undo the fuel filler. 3. Gently extract the motor support. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. 1. Disconnect the electrical connection. Description Component FUEL FLAP LOCK GEARED MOTOR See N058 FUEL FILLER FLAP LOCK GEARED MOTOR 2. Keep the motor and support (2a) and extract the emergency control cord (2b) leaving the sensor in its place. 1. Undo the bolts. 2. Separate the motor (2a) from the support (2b). Refitting Removing - Check that the motor is not damaged. - Position the motor on the support and tighten the bolts. - Connect the electrical connection. 1. Using the sensor, place the cord (1a) in the right rear light cluster access compartment (1b). - Undo the fuel filler cap. - Place the motor and support in position. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. - Tighten the bolts fixing the motor and support. - Close the fuel filler cap access flap. - Working from the luggage compartment, check that the cord is working. - Place the right rear light cluster access cover in position and secure it using the retainers. - Close the tailgate. Removing Refitting - Open the boot lid. 1. Rotate and release retainer (1a), then remove right rear light cluster access cover (1b) by removing retainer (1c). 2. Extract fuel filler emergency opening control cord (2a). Fit a sensor in the end (2b) of the cord (to be used for reinserting the cord during the refitting stage). - Open the fuel filler cap access flap. 1. Undo the motor fixing bolts. 2. Undo the fuel filler cap. 3. Gently extract the motor mount. 4. Retighten the fuel filler cap. 1. Detach the electrical connection. Description Component FUEL FLAP LOCK GEARED MOTOR See N058 FUEL FILLER FLAP LOCK GEARED MOTOR 2. Keep motor and mount (2a) and extract emergency control cord (2b), leaving the sensor in its place. 1. Undo the bolts. 2. Separate motor (2a) from mount (2b). Refitting Removing - Check that the motor is not damaged. - Position the motor on the mount and tighten the bolts. - Attach the electrical connection. 1. Using the sensor, place cord (1a) in right rear light cluster access opening (1b). - Undo the fuel filler cap. - Place the motor and mount in position. - Retighten the fuel filler cap. - Tighten the bolts fixing the motor and mount. - Close the fuel filler cap access flap. - Working from the luggage compartment, check that the cord is working. - Position the right rear light cluster access cover and secure it using the retainers. - Close the boot lid.

- Prepare the hood for the operation. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE - Open the hood housing cover using the electric control. 1. Open the boot lid using the emergency control (1a) after having activated the retainer (1b) and opened the cover (1c) behind the left seat. 1. The arrows (3b) indicate the possible movements 4. After adjustment, tighten the nuts. Component Fastening dia Value (daNm) Validity HOOD HOUSING COVER HINGES Nut - 0.7 ÷ 0.8 - Refit the left and right strikers. Op. 7025D26 HOOD HOUSING COMPARTMENT COVER LOCK STRIKER (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. If it is still necessary: Op. 7040C12 HOOD HOUSING COMPARTMENT FRONT TRIM - R.R. 1. Working on both sides of the vehicle, undo the bolts (1a) for the supports (1b) for the locks and adjust the position of the locks using the slotted openings in the supports. the arrows indicate the possible movements. - If necessary, adjust the position of the lock strikers. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the operation. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE Op. 7025D12 HOOD HOUSING COMPARTMENT COVER INNER LINING - R.R. 1. Undo the bolts securing the trim. 2. Undo the trim retaining nuts. 3. Lower the side covers manually after having removed the adhesive tape. 4. Lower the hood housing cover (4a) using the electric control and leave the 5th arc (4b) raised. 1. Apply adhesive body tape along the perimeter of the outer trim to protect the paintwork. 2. Raise one end (2a) of the outer trim slightly and, using a cutter (2b), cut the sealant (2c) along the entire perimeter of the outer trim. 3. Remove the outer trim. Refitting Removing - Check that the outer trim is not damaged. 1. If the outer trim that has been removed is being reused, remove the sealant remaining on the trim using solvent. 1. Remove the sealant that remains on the hood housing cover using solvent. 2. Remove the adhesive tape 3. Apply new sealant, CC80/SPAF100/HR, following the instructions on the product packaging. - Position the outer trim centering it on the cover, then press it along the entire outer perimeter to make the sealant stick. - Raise the hood housing cover using the electric control and leave the 5th arc raised. 1. Working on both side covers (1a), rotate the release retainer (1b) in the direction of the arrow (1c) until it is in the unlocked position (1d). 2. Rotate the side covers (1a) upwards until they are in position (2a), then secure them using adhesive bodywork tape. 1. Check that the outer trim (1a) is in the correct position, then tighten the fixing nuts (1b). 2 Tighten the outer trim fixing bolts. Op. 7025D12 HOOD HOUSING COMPARTMENT COVER INNER LINING - R.R. - If discharged, restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. Op. 7030H03 HOOD MANUAL OPENING FOLLOWING DEACTIVATION OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - CARRY OUT PROCEDURE - Check that the hood is working correctly.

Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the operation. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE 1. Using the electric control, place the 5th arc (1a) in the raised position (as illustrated), the hood housing cover (1b) in the fully raised position and the side covers (flaps) (1c) in a lowered position (as illustrated). 1. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the operation. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE - Open the boot lid. 1. Undo the bolts (1a) and the nuts (1b) and remove the hinge (1c) for the hood housing compartment cover. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the operation. Using a screwdriver, release the retaining clips from both ends of the telescopic strut (without removing them). 3. Remove the telescopic strut by disengaging it from the ball joints. Refitting Removing - Check that the telescopic strut is not damaged. If necessary, replace both the left and right telescopic struts in order to maintain uniform operation of the actual telescopic struts. - Engage the telescopic strut with the ball joints and fit the retaining clips. - If discharged, restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. Take care to avoid any damage to the body paintwork. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: therefore during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

If necessary (in emergency, during workshop repairs, etc.) the hood can be closed manually following the instructions below. - Open the oddments compartment behind the right seat. 1. Pull the hydraulic system pressure release valve operating cable (1a) until it is in the end of travel position. If necessary, use the screwdriver (1b). 1. Open the boot using the electric control. If this is not possible, open it pulling the emergency control (1a) after having opened the oddments compartment behind the left seat. 1. Working at the front of the boot, pull the handle (1a) and open the flap (1b). 1. Take the spanner (1a) and the screwdriver (1b) that are supplied. 2. Insert the spanner (1a) in the hexagonal socket located inside the opening (1c) then, with the help of the screwdriver (1b), turn the spanner (1a) clockwise until it is in the end of travel position (about 90°) to open the hood housing compartment cover locks. - Close the boot lid completely. This operation must be carried out first in order to be able to open the hood housing cover. 1. Carefully open the hood housing cover (1a) manually until it is in the end of travel (vertical) position. This operation should be carried out slowly to allow the oil for the hydraulic control piston to drain. In addition, during the initial opening stage for the hood housing cover (1a), take care that the lower middle section (1b) is not resting on the middle section (1c) of the boot lid; if necessary, press the boot lid in that area (1c) with your hand. 1. Raise the hood (1a) and pull it slowly until it is near the front windscreen. 1. Check that the hooks (1a) for the locks are open (as illustrated). 2. Rest the front section (2a) of the hood on the windscreen crossmember (2b). 1. Working in the centre of the crossmember above the windscreen, remove the cover (1a). 2. Use the spanner and the screwdriver supplied, employed for opening the hood housing cover. Insert the spanner (1b) in the square socket located inside the opening (1c) then, with the help of the screwdriver, turn the spanner (1b) anti-clockwise until it is in the end of travel position (about 90°) to close the hood front locks. 1. Working on the hood housing cover, rotate the side covers (1a) downwards after having turned the leers (1b) releasing the attachment tooth. 1. Raise the hood 5th arc slowly until it is in the end of travel, vertical position. 2. Lower the hood housing cover slowly until it is in the end of travel position taking care to ensure that the side covers do not interfere with other parts. 1. Lower the hood 5th arc (1a) until it is resting on the cover (1b). 1. Open the boot lid by pulling the emergency control (1a) after having opened the oddments compartment behind the left seat. Use the spanner and screwdriver supplied that have been used previously. 1. Insert the spanner (1a) in the hexagonal socket located inside the opening (1c) then, with the help of the screwdriver (1b), turn the spanner (1a) anti-clockwise until it is in the end of travel position (about 90°) to close the hood housing compartment cover locks. 1. Completely lower the hood housing cover 5th arc, applying manual pressure, from the bottom upwards, by the side references (1a) on the hood inner fabric (this operation allows the inner levers to go past the dead lock and lower the 5th arc completely). - The hood is closed. If necessary, it is possible to move the vehicle. The hydraulic system pressure must be restored to reopen the hood. Raise the hood 5th arc (1a) slowly until it is in the end of travel, vertical position. 1. Open the boot lid by pulling the emergency control (1a) after having opened the oddments compartment behind the left seat. 1. Working at the front of the boot, pull the handle (1a) and open the flap (1b). 1. Take the spanner (1a) and the screwdriver (1b) that are supplied. 2. Insert the spanner (1a) in the hexagonal socket located inside the opening (1c) then, with the help of the screwdriver (1b), turn the spanner (1a) clockwise until it is in the end of travel position (about 90°) to open the hood housing compartment cover locks. - Close the boot lid completely. This operation must be carried out first in order to be able to open the hood housing cover. 1. Carefully open the hood housing cover (1a) manually until it is in the end of travel (vertical) position. This operation should be carried out slowly to allow the oil for the hydraulic control piston to drain. In addition, during the initial opening stage for the hood housing cover (1a), take care that the lower middle section (1b) is not resting on the middle section (1c) of the boot lid; if necessary, press the boot lid in that area (1c) with your hand. 1. Rotate the hood housing compartment floor covering (1b) retainers (1a), then release them. 2. Remove the trim (1b) releasing the retainers (2b). 1. Remove the hydraulic control unit sound insulation cover. 1. Reactivate the release valve by manually rotating the lever (1a) from position (1b) to the end of travel position (1c) forcing it gently into this position. 1. Reposition the hydraulic control unit sound insulation cover. 1. Position the hood housing compartment floor covering (1a) attaching the retainers (1b). 2. Rotate the covering retainers and attach them. - If the hood opening/closing system is not faulty, complete the hood opening or closing cycle using the electric control. - If the hood opening/closing system is faulty, proceed with the fault diagnosis using the Examiner.

Release flexible rod (3b) from loop (4a). - Raise the front part of the hood manually. - Cover vehicle bodywork and upholstery with protective cloth. 1. Disconnect front part (1a) of the interior lining from internal retainers (1b). 1. Extract links (3a) through loops (3b), releasing retainers (3c). 1. Bring perforated ends (1a) of the links into line with holes (1b) in the hoop and bring holes (1c) in the interior lining into line with holes (1b) and (1d) on the hoop, then secure the parts with rivets (1e). 1. Attach front part (1a) of the interior lining to internal retainers (1b). 1. Fit flexible rod (1a) in loop (1b). 2. If removed, position flexible rod (1a) on mounting (2a) and fit rivet (2b). 3. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the operation. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE 1. Electrically open the hood until it is possible to work on the front panel (1a). 2. Release the front part (2a) of the hood interior lining from the internal retainers (2b). 3. Remove the inner lining expansion retainers (3a), after unscrewing their expansion bolts. 4. Move the side seal edges. 5. Remove the front panel (1a) releasing the side retainers (5a). Refitting Removing - Check that the front panel is not damaged. - Move the side seal edges then position the front panel and engage the side retainers. - Position the side seal edges. - Apply the expansion retainers to the front panel and then tighten the expansion bolts. - Secure the front part of the hood interior lining to the internal retainers. - If discharged, restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. Op. 7030H03 HOOD MANUAL OPENING FOLLOWING DEACTIVATION OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - CARRY OUT PROCEDURE - Check that the hood is working correctly.

Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the procedure. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE - Place the front part of the hood in a half open position using the electric control. - Remove both seats. Op. 7045A10 FRONT SEAT (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. - Place protective cloths on the vehicle fittings and bodywork. 1. Disconnect front part (1a) of the interior lining from internal retainers (1b). 2. Working on both sides of the hood, drill out rivets (2a) securing links (2b) (keep the parts of the rivets). 3. Release links (2b) from retaining rings (3a). 1. Drill out rivets (1a) securing the hood interior lining, then release ends (1b) of the links (keep the parts of the rivets). 2. Let interior lining (2a) lower itself. 3. Extract links (3a) through loops (3b) by releasing retainers (3c). - Raise the rear part of the hood using the electric controls 1. Working from both sides of the hood, drill out rivets (1a) (keep the parts of the rivets). Take care not to damage the hydraulic pipes and wiring at the back. 2. Move interior lining edges (2a) and undo bolts (2b). 3. Detach side links (3a) from terminal fastenings (3b) and from loops (3c). 1. Release frame (1a) for the hood inner lining from retainers (1b) for upper profile (1c) of heated rear windscreen (1d). 1. Manually raise the upper part of heated rear windscreen (1a) and uncover hoop (1b) 2. Drill out rivets (2a) (keep the parts of the rivets). 3. Keep the hood interior lining. - Remove any residues left from the removed rivets, from the inside of the hood tensioning hoops, working as follows: - Using a jet of compressed air, blow down one open end of the ribs and retrieve any residues left by the removed rivets from the other open end of the ribs. Refitting Removing 1. Check that hood interior lining (1a) is not damaged. In particular check that links (1b) are intact. - Restore the surface protection to the metal parts, which may have been damaged when the rivets were removed, etc. 1. Position hood interior lining edge (1a) on rib (1b) and secure it with rivets (1c). 2. Manually lower the upper part of heated rear windscreen (2a), disengaging it from rib (1b). 1. Check the integrity of retainers (1a). Attach frame (1b) to retainers (1a) along the upper part of the heated rear windscreen. 1. Working on both sides of the hood, insert side links (1a) into loops (1b) and position terminal fastenings (1c) in their housings. 2. Position side brackets (2a) and screw in bolts (2b). 3. Position side links (3a) and secure them with rivets (3b). - Lower the rear part of the hood using the electric controls. 1. Working on the front side of the hood, insert links (1a) into loops (1b) and engage retainers (1c). 1. Bring perforated ends (1a) of the links into line with holes (1b) in the hoop and bring holes (1c) in the interior lining into line with holes (1b) and (1d) on the hoop, then secure the parts with rivets (1e). 1. Working on both sides of the hood, insert links (1a) into retaining rings (1b), then secure their ends (1c) in place with rivets (1d). 2. Connect front part (2a) of the interior lining to internal retainers (2b). - Check that the hood opens/closes correctly, by moving it manually. - Restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. Op. 7030H03 HOOD MANUAL OPENING FOLLOWING DEACTIVATION OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - CARRY OUT PROCEDURE - Later on, check that the hood opengs/closes properly using the electric control. Op. 7045A10 FRONT SEAT (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R.

Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the procedure. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE - Raise the rear part of the hood using the electric controls. 1. Working on the side of the telescopic strut to be removed, drill out rivet (1a) (keep the parts of the rivet). Take care not to damage the hydraulic pipes and wiring at the back. 2. Move interior lining edge (2a) and undo bolts (2b). 3. Disconnect side link (3a) from terminal fastening (3b). - Completely lower the rear part of the hood using the electric controls. 1. Using a screwdriver, prise up the retaining clips from both ends of the telescopic strut (without removing them). 2. Remove the telescopic strut by disengaging it from the ball joints. Do not attempt to remove the telescopic strut with the hood in any other position; removing the telescopic strut when it is compressed could be dangerous. Refitting Removing - Check that the telescopic strut is not damaged. If the telescopic strut needs to be replaced, in order to maintain uniform tensioning, both the left-hand and right-hand telescopic struts should be replaced. 1. With the rear part of the hood completely lowered, engage telescopic strut (1a) onto the ball joints and fit retaining clips (1b). 1. Place side link (1b) terminal fastening (1a) in position. 2. Position side bracket (2a) and screw in bolts (2b). 3. Position side link (3a) and secure it with rivet (3b). - If discharged, restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. Op. 7030H03 HOOD MANUAL OPENING FOLLOWING DEACTIVATION OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - CARRY OUT PROCEDURE - Check that the hood is working correctly.

Move interior lining edge (2a) and undo bolts (2b). 3. Disconnect side link (3a) from terminal fastening (3b). - Completely lower the rear part of the hood using the electric controls. 1. Do not attempt to remove the telescopic strut with the hood in any other position; removing the telescopic strut when it is compressed could be dangerous. Refitting Removing - Check that the telescopic strut is not damaged. If the telescopic strut needs to be replaced, in order to maintain uniform tensioning, both the left-hand and right-hand telescopic struts should be replaced. 1. With the rear part of the hood completely lowered, engage telescopic strut (1a) with the ball joints and fit retaining clips (1b). 1. Place side link (1b) terminal fastening (1a) in position. 2. Position side bracket (2a) and screw in bolts (2b). 3. Position side link (3a) and secure it with rivet (3b). - If discharged, restore the hood hydraulic system pressure. Op. 7030H03 HOOD MANUAL OPENING FOLLOWING DEACTIVATION OF HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - CARRY OUT PROCEDURE - Check that the hood is working correctly.

Refitting Removing - Check that the bracket is not damaged. - Position the spacer and the buffer, if removed and then tighten the nuts. - Place the bracket in position and tighten the rear fixing nuts. Using the electric control, place the 5th arc (1a) in a raised position (as illustrated), the hood housing cover (1b) in a completely raised position and the side covers (flaps) (1c) in a lowered position (as illustrated). 1. Tighten the bolts (1a) securing the front backet (1b). Op. 7040C11 HOOD HOUSING COMPARTMENT FLOOR TRIM - R.R. - Check that the hood is working correctly.

Position central drip channel (4a) and the plastic washers, then screw in bolts (4b) without tightening them (for later adjustment on the door windows). In particular, check the seal fitted on drip channel (4a) is correctly positioned when the door windows are in the closed position; if necessary remove the seal (op. 7030H37) and loosen bolts (4b) then adjust the position of drip channel (4a); the possible position changes are indicated by the arrows. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the procedure. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE 1. Removing Refitting - Prepare the hood for the procedure. Op. 0010T79 HOOD HYDRAULIC SYSTEM - DISCHARGE AND RESTORE PRESSURE - Open the front part of the hood, until the spring pad is accessible. 1. Gently move the edge of the inner hood lining. 2. Remove the rubber protection from the nut. 3. Undo the nut. 4. Remove the spring pad. Do not let the spring pack escape from the pad stem. 1. WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. Use the specialist equipment for removing the window glasses, working very carefully to avoid damaging the glass and the bodyshell. During the operations illustrated below always use either the piano wire or the vibrating blade to cut the sealant. The two tools can usually be used interchangeably. Follow the manufacturer's recommendations for sealants meticulously, as far as the instructions for usage and times are concerned. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated. Use the specialist equipment for removing the window glasses, working very carefully to avoid personal injury. Always move the glass with the help of an assistant.

PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. After fitting a cover, mould it carefully onto the upholstery. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. The seats are fitted with side Air Bags and pretensioners: follow the specific safety instructions Op. 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

Align the two guides (1a) and (4a), proceeding as follows: lift up seat sliding control lever (1c) and keep it raised, then manually slide the two guides (1a) and (4a) until they are in the rear end of travel position, in order to align them; lastly, release the sliding control lever and attach the retainers for the guides to the attachment teeth. Removing Refitting FOLLOW ALL THE RECOMMENDED SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS See descriptions 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM Op. 7045A25 FRONT SEAT BACKREST LUMBAR ADJUSTMENT KNOB (ONE), LEFT OR RIGHT - R.R. 1. Move backrest tilt lever (1a) and undo bolt (1b). 2. Remove the panel. 1. Disconnect the backrest trim rear retainers. 2. Disconnect the lower two ends of the backrest cover attached to one another. 3. Along the rear sections (3a), disconnect ends (3b) attached to one another. 4. Release the front end of the backrest trim from the cushion. 5. Raise the backrest trim as far as possible. 1. Insert hands under padding (1a) and release head restraint retainers (1b), then with the help of a second operator extract backrest trim with padding and head restraint (1c). - If necessary, separate the backrest trim from the padding as described below. 1. Prise up the trim and release from the padding border. 2. Use cutters to cut all the front backrest trim retainers. 3. Separate trim (3a) from padding (3b). Refitting Removing - Observe the following precautions. Never repair the trim. Only use new trims. It is strictly prohibited to use any type of backrest trim that is not designed for this particular kind of seat. - Check that the airbag backrest trim identification mark is on the same side as the sidebag module. - If a new backrest trim is being fitted, position the labels as described below. - Remove the removable part of the adhesive label from the new backrest trim. Place a copy of label (1b) in a special folder containing the vehicle details (model, registration date, chassis number) and the serial number of the old backrest trim. The file should be kept for future checks. - Fit the detachable part of the original label on the lower part of the seat, where similar labels for the seat and the sidebag module and the airbag wiring can already be found. - If removed, position the backrest trim on the padding and crimp the retainers using special pliers. Ensure the trim retains its shape on the padding during the various refitting stages. - Fit the trim on the upper padding area. - Position the padding on the seat frame and attach the head restraint pins to the appropriate bushes. - Fully fit the backrest trim onto the padding. - Connect the rear and lower ends of the backrest trim. - Connect the backrest trim rear retainers. - Move the backrest tilt lever and position the panel, then tighten the bolts. PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: therefore during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected: the steering will thereby remain unlocked and free to turn. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (BRERA) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

WARNINGS Work carefully on the fittings and use the recommended tools correctly to prevent damage. Take care to avoid any damage to the body paintwork. When working on the seat belt pretensioners, refer to the warnings for the Air Bags Op. 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM PRECAUTIONS Before working on the electrical system (connectors, electrical components, wiring etc.), always DISCONNECT THE BATTERY. If the battery is disconnected, the Steering Lock Node remains in the condition (unlocked or locked) that it is in: during workshop operations and repairs, whenever it is necessary to turn the steering wheel with the battery disconnected, leave the TEG inserted when the battery is disconnected. The steering will therefore remain released and free to turn. When working on the seat belt pretensioners, refer to the precautions for the Air Bags Op. 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM In particular, with regard to the pretensioners: - Pretensioners are made from pyrotechnic materials and therefore must be moved, handled and stored correctly in order to avoid damage or cracks. - In normal conditions, pretensioners are only activated on the action of the electric ignition control during a collision. During activation small quantities of gas develop. This gas is mostly made up of nitrogen; this is a non-toxic gas. - Pretensioner surfaces must be protected from exposure for over 6 hours to temperatures above 100° C, as well as from sparks and from naked flames. - With temperatures above 180° C the auto-ignition of the gas generator can be checked. - Pretensioners should be protected from the stress of collisions or falls. - Pretensioners that have undergone a fall of over 1 metre onto concrete or similar materials, must no longer be used and should be sent back to the supplier, with details of the fault. - Gas generators must not come into contact with acids, water, grease or heavy metals; contact with these substances can cause the formation of toxic, poisonous gases or explosive compounds. - Unburnt gas generator fuel is slightly flammable, therefore components should never be dismantled, damaged, sawed or interfered with. Pretensioners have a validity of 14 years : they therefore need to be replaced after this time. It is forbidden to store pretensioners with: - flammable materials - combustible materials It is strictly forbidden to dismantle pretensioners into their component parts. - When being shipped in on-road vehicles, they must be stored in the luggage compartment. The device cannot be shipped in the passenger compartment. - Buckles with pretensioners should be kept in dry places and protected from dampness. - Buckles with pretensioners must only be kept in cupboards or compartments that can be locked; these must be ventilated and far away from naked flames and heat sources. - During breaks or at the end of a job, buckles with pretensioners must be kept under lock and key. When working on a vehicle (installation, removal) the following points must be respected: - Do not subject pretensioners to heat, for example during welding, brasing, knocks, drilling, mechanical processes, painting with temperatures over 100° C, etc. When carrying out such processes, the pretensioner must be removed from the vehicle. - If heavy knocks are expected to be made in the area of the electronic control unit, disconnect the battery terminals, carefully isolate them and wait 1 minute - Do not carry out repairs on pretensioners. - Primed pretensioners that are not installed on the vehicle and are to be scrapped, must first be activated. - Primed pretensioners fitted in the vehicle must not be demolished with the vehicle but removed beforehand. - If a pretensioner fails to activate during an accident, the device should be considered still primed. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) Following a power supply failure to the control units (for example, battery disconnection) the system must be initialized once again, following the instructions below and working with the ignition key ON (TEG inserted) and the doors and windows closed. - completely open the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (lower) end of travel position - completely close the driver's door window, keeping the operating button pressed for at least 3 seconds after the (upper) end of travel position - carry out the same operations for the passenger window - make sure that the initialization is correct by checking that the windows work properly in automatic mode. Each time the battery is disconnected the vehicle loses some electrical parameters; therefore when the battery is reconnected the vehicle electrical system initialization procedure should be carried out following the instructions below. INITIALIZATION PROCEDURE FOR DOOR NODES (SPIDER) - Connect the battery. - Close the boot lid. - Insert the TEG. - Close the hood using the electric control (if not available, use the emergency system). - Get into the vehicle and close the doors. - Close the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Open the windows in the doors, using the buttons and keep the buttons pressed for at least 3 seconds after the end of travel open position has been reached. Release the buttons. - Close the windows in the doors until the end of travel closed position has been reached. Release the buttons. - The initialization procedure is over; to check that the initialization has taken place, carry out the check described below. - Place the window for one of the doors in an intermediate open position; open the same door and check that the window does not descend during the initial opening. If the window does lower then the vehicle has not been initialized and the process must be carried out/repeated.

Vehicle towing points The vehicle is equipped with two threaded seats one at the front and one at the rear for the installation of the tow hook present in the housing inside the spare wheel, located in the boot under the carpet. When towing the vehicle, it is compulsory to resepct specific highway code regulations relating to the tow hook and procedures for towing on the road. Clean the threaded seat carefully before tightening the hook. Before towing, make sure that the tow hook is fully tightened. Ensure that the electronic key is inserted in the TEG Reader If the key is extracted the steering lock will come on automatically and it will be impossible to steer the wheels. If it is necessary to disconnect the battery, carry out the operation only with the electronic key inserted in the TEG Reader. This avoids the need to engage the steering lock. With the engine switched off the brake servo and the power steering are not working so greater effort is required on both the brake pedal and the steering wheel. General safety instructions The activities connected with the bodywork repair operations involve the use of specialist equipment as well as handling chemical products which must be done in accordance with the supplier's recommendations. Special attention should therefore be paid to: The correct use of materials, instruments and equipment: before carrying out any operation, read the instruction manual very carefully and and follow the directions and recommended safety regulations. Specially designated work areas must be equipped with a ventilation system that meets standards as far as air exchange, the filtration of harmful substances (solvents) and keeping down dust levels are concerned. Dangerous substances that have to be used must be handled following the supplier's instructions and recommendations. *-The collection and disposal of waste must be carried out in accordance with current legislation. Whilst working with and handling dangerous substances, the appropriate accident prevention measures must be taken (wearing protective clothing, masks, gloves, goggles, etc.). Vehicle repair operating cycles The vehicle repair operating cycles usually consist of the following stages: checking vehicle measurements; cutting/removing damaged elements and preparing the bodyshell for welding; welding replacement parts; preparation for painting; painting; restoring anti-corrosion conditions, sound insulation, sealants. Check and restore specified bodyshell measurements This is the first stage of the repair operation during which the distortion suffered by the bodyshell is measured and evaluated and the elements involved are identified. The first actual repair operation is also carried out during this stage: pulling the bodyshell to restore the distances before cutting and removing the damaged elements. Stretching the body Pulling the bodyshell, to restore the distances, is carried out on the alignment benches where it is possible to secure the bodyshell using vices and mountings to be fitted in accordance with the specific instructions for each vehicle that come with the bench. Templates, positioned in the recommended places, are used to check the bodyshell measurements either using the measurements given by the manufacturer of the template for each model or, alternatively, those for the vehicle given in the "Description and Operation" section. Example of a possible alignment bench configuration. General repair instructions The battery leads must be disconnected before carrying out any operation on the vehicle. For safety reasons and for a better quality repair, IT IS FORBIDDEN TO: replace the structural parts of the bodyshell without using a repair bench. The use of the bench makes it possible to guarantee the restructuring of the vehicle with the original manufacturing measurements, ensuring the correct positioning of the components that make up the forecarriage and the rear part of the vehicle. heat the structural parts of the bodyshell to straighten them. cut and weld, any bodywork element and reinforcement, edge to edge, on the same line. Remove the damaged components cutting them by the join elements following the cutting lines given in the Service Manual. Correctly carried out, this operation involves a gap of several centimetres between the two cutting lines in order to distribute the meltable spots created by the welding. Before carrying out any operation, read the instruction manual carefully and the safety instructions and warnings given by the manufacturer together with the equipment and follow all safety precautions most stringently. The use of the following is required for removing damaged panels: alternating power saws; circular saws; power chisels (only if necessary); plasma cutting systems; electric drills; milling machines; grinders; hammers and dolly blocks; disc grinders; air extractor fans. Alternating power saw This type of saw makes it possible to make fast, precision cuts with the possibility of regulating the speed of the blade so that it can be adpated to suit different conditions. Example of the use of an alternating power saw Vibrating circular saw A circular saw is used in cases which require high precision cutting; for example, the panel in a box section to replaced superimposed on the panel that should not be damaged. By adjusting the speed and the number of oscillations it is possible to achieved the required precision according to the usage conditions. The high safety level for this instrument means that it is advisable to use it as an alternative to other types of saws. Example of a circular saw Power chisel Power chisels are used to deatch parts of panels and are recommended: *- when it is not possible to use the air saw, chamfering machine or drill, e.g. when another panel lies behind the panel to be cut that must not be damaged. *- when it is not possible to separate the welded panel directly by inserting the chisel tip between the two panels along the join, in order not to leave edges to be removed at a later stage. The different fittings that it comes with increase its versatility. Example of the use of a power chisel. Plasma cutting system This cutting system, produced through the combined effect of an electric arc and gas or a gas mixture, is used if very large panels have to be removed. Depending on the thickness of the panel and the depth of the cut, the value of the current and flow of gas can be adjusted in accordance with the instruction manual supplied by the Manufacturer. The use of plasma cutting systems requires use of an extraction system to remove the harmful gases and fumes. The weld spot should be marked using a drift, in order to provide support for the centering point thereby preventing the cutter from slipping and damaging the surrounding area; the cutter should then be pushed until it reaches slightly deeper than the thickness of the panel to be removed (see diagram below). Milling machine A milling machine for removing spot welds is used after the panel to be replaced has been cut to allow the removal of the metall offcuts remaining on the edges of the bodyshell. The milling machine works on the panel cutting it as far as the panel underneath and insulating the spot weld. After removing all the spot welds the piece cut off can be removed using pliers. Hammer and dolly block These instruments are used when panels have to be straightened in order to have a reaction point supporting the panel. The dolly blocks are designed so that they can be adapted to suit the different shapes of the panel and, when the work area permits, they can replace the hammer. The levers have the same usage instructions as the dolly blocks, however they are designed so that they can be introduced through openings and into restricted spaces into areas that are difficult to reach. Dolly blocks and levers are also used to remove distortions from the edge of panels that are not removed thereby allowing them to be matched with replaced panels preventing the structure from being weakened. The bodywork components can be welded using different methods: Spot welding; Seam welding (MIG):; Brazing. Equipment The following equipment is used for these operations: welding gun; seam welder (MIG); oxyacetylene torch (brazing). General information on electric spot welding During spot welding the heat required to melt the metal is provided by the resistance to the flow of current which the metal opposes. Spot welding is carried out on panels where the join edges are overlapping and takes place through localized fusion of the metal that makes up the panel so no filler metal is required for this type of welding. In areas where three or more panels are overlapping, the spot welding must be repeated a second time. The type of join that is produced is the discontinuous type; the weld spots must be correctly spaced in order to confer good mechanical resistance following precise instructions (see the tables below). Spot welding In the case of spot welding, check: that the arms are correctly aligned; that the diameter of the ends of the electrodes is correct; the planarity and correct matching of the edges of the weld; the correct welding sequence. Before welding, apply electro-galvanizing protective to the edges of the join to protect the box sections from corrosion. If welds are made on this type of surface it produces a concentration of tension that causes it to break. Example of correct spot welding at corners. A. Area where welding should not be carried out. Seam welding (mig) MIG welding should be used for parts where spot welding cannot be used. When seam (MIG) welding, check: the speed of the wire the correct execution of the seam welding beads (alternation of welding sections) In this welding system the electrode (an automatic advance continuous wire) is protected by an atmosphere of inert gases (where the initials MIG come from - Metal Inert Gas). - The continuous advance of the wire (which constitutes both the electrode and the filler metal), allows long welds to be made with no interruptions. The flow of inert gases sent to the welding area eliminates the air surrounding the fusion bath preventing the oxidation of the metal and also carries out the function of a protective coating for coated electrode welding. For these reasons, MIG welding differs from welding carried out with a coated electrode through the absence of slag on the welding seam and there is also no porousness which can occur with normal arc welding. The use of MIG welding systems requires use of an extraction system to remove the harmful gases and fumes. Operating methods In order to weld two panels correctly using a MIG welder: grind or pickle the panel thoroughly, position the equipment so that whilst carrying out the welding the torch outer casing does not become twisted or folded in such a way that could obstruct the advance of the wire, wear protective clothing and a suitable mask with a non-actinic visor (standard no. 8 glass for currents of 40-60A and no. 9 for currents of 80-200A). Regulate the flow of gas in accordance with the instructions from the Manufacturer of the equipment. Make two spot welds at the ends of the join line and one in the middle, then make welds in between the two sections defined in this way. The spot welds should be 25 - 30 mm apart. The diagram below shows how to carry out the welding correctly (1). the correct gap is about 1 mm. Carrying out welding (2) using an inert gas electrode (MIG) to join adjacent panels. It is not advisable to carry out a seam weld initially because, in addition to being difficult in practical terms, it may cause the panel to become distorted as a result of the build of heat involved. The difficulties in carrying out a single seam weld lie in the need to move the torch fairly slowly to produce good penetration of the weld but sufficiently quickly so as not to run the risk of "burning" the panel. Moving the torch too quickly also leads to a poor seal of the weld seam because, after the operation of grinding the seam, an insufficient layer of filler material remains to guarantee the resistance of the join. After initially spot welding the panel, a disc grinder must be used to until the weld spots are level with the panel. At this point the alignment of the panels must be checked and, if necessary, corrected using a hammer and dolly block. Then proceed with filling the gaps between the various spot welds through alternating welding sections, keeping the torch at an angle of about 60' (see previous diagram). 1. Tack welding the join. The advantage of the welding operation is confirmed by the appearance of the rear of the weld seam which should show a series of spherical caps side by side for the entire length of the join. The MIG welder can also be used for joining overlapping panels where only one side is accessible. To carry out spot welding, the panels must adhere perfectly and the torch must be perpendicular to the surface. In this way the action of the electrode initially melts the first panel, then the second where a crater is produced that is filled by the advance of the electrode. In order to carry out this operation correctly, the welding machine must be regulated to current values that are suitable for the thickness of the panels being worked on with the torch resting on its supports and pressure on the surface to facilitate the panels being brought close together. Air filtration and purification systems When carrying out work that produces fumes, gas and powder that is dangerous to the mechanic, air filtration and purification systems must be used. These systems are designed for the various requirements to handle different volumes of air that require purification. The operation of these systems is usually based on the combined action of mechanical and electro-static filtration and purification using active charcoal. Filtration takes place in two stages: mechanical elimination, using gauze filters, of the largest particles of powder and then subjecting the air flow to ionization which statically charges the particles of powder which are then eliminated from the flow through an electrostatic process. The flow of air is then purified by passing through active charcoal filters. In these systems, in addition to the specific efficiency, the ease of handling and noise levels have been improved and are never troublesome. The diagram below illustrates a possible conformation. PAINTING Introduction Painting the bodyshell has two fundamental objectives: protecting the surfaces of the panels from the elements and an aesthetic function of providing colour and shine. The larger number of chemical products used in painting operations means that special care must be taken over their handling and usage. These painting operations involve the emission of paint fumes and solvent vapours which, if breathed in by the operator, could constitute a serious danger to health and should therefore only be carried out in spray booths. The operator should always wear a mask and protective clothing. These masks should be the filtration type for operations that do not take very long and the total protection pressurized type for longer operations. Equipment The following equipment is used during painting operations: filtration masks and protective clothing, masking and taping machines; spray booths and drying ovens; spray guns; infrared lamps; polishing machines; Protective clothing When carrying out painting operations suitable protective clothing must be worn to protect the operator from contact with harmful agents. It is also advisable to use a barrier cream on any exposed areas (face, hands, arms) which should be removed at the end of the painting operations. Filtration mask This type of mask only protects the operator's respiratory system and protective goggles and headgear should be also worn at the same time. Its use is recommended for small retouching operations. Example of a filtration mask. Pressurized mask This type of mask guarantees protection of the face and hair and is supplied with pure air from the compressed air system used for the spray gun. The air is purified further with a degree of separation close to 100% by an active charcoal filter fitted to the operator's belt. The slight excess pressure created inside the helmet prevents the penetration of paint vapours. The use of this mask is advisable for long painting operations. Example of a pressurized mask Spray booth Spray booths are used for painting operations and baking prepared parts. If the extent of the damage repaired is medium or large, it would be helpful to have a special spray booth and a hot air circulation oven for drying the paint. The area should be equipped with an air conditioning system and filtered by purifiers, mainly comprising active charcoal filters. The optimum painting conditions that should be maintained in the booth during the painting stage are as follows: constant temperature of between 22 and 25° C constant humidity of between 75 and 80% The area in question could be: a combined painting and drying booth; a separate type painting booth and drying oven. Spray guns Developments in the study of ergonomics and spray painting techniques have led to the definition of a new type of high volume air and low atomization pressure spray gun that allows a considerable reduction in the paint mist. This type of spray gun has been designed to be lighter with a grip that reduces tiredness and eliminates cramp and with controls that require far less effort than conventional spray guns. The handling of the spray gun is also made easier by the even weight distribution and by the improved design that makes it easier to operate. The most interesting aspect of this spray gun is the supply system that allows painting in any direction, even with the cup facing downwards, also improving the cleaning procedures with considerable savings in terms of time and materials. The possibility of painting from the top or the bottom, in addition to preventing the formation of areas that are too wet or too dry, also facilitates access to areas of the bodywork that are difficult to reach. Special care has been taken over the ease of adjustment which requires minimal, simple movements. This spray gun is extremely efficient combining a very fine atomization capacity for any product, even water soluble, used by bodyworkers at a pressure of 0.7g (10 PSI) or below. Thanks to these capacities for using paint materials, it has been possible to achieve a considerable saving in economic terms and an improvement in working conditions. The diagram below illustrates some possible uses of the spray gun. Use of the spray gun. A - Method of normal usage B - Use from the bottom to the top C - Use from the top to the bottom Infrared portable lamps If the operation is restricted to small retouches, then the use of an oven is not practical. In these cases the paint can be dried using special infrared lamps fitted on parabolic mirrors. The use of one or more lamps positioned so that the surface that has been retouched is subject to an even temperature allows the paint film to bake and the result is comparable to that achieved in an oven. This type of lamp greatly reduces drying times, thereby also reducing energy consumption. The lamp should only be used when the paint has already dried to an extent that it is "out of the powder" stage. Drying a retouch using a portable infrared lamp. Polishing machines The paint should only be polished after the enamel has been baked and after it has cooled down to ambient temperature. Polishing is also necessary if there are defects in the paintwork such as dust, paint fumes, drips, orange peel or small scratches. There are a large number of products that can be applied, either manually or mechanically using a polishing machine, to remedy these defects. The tool should be paralle to the surface to be polished and should not be at an angle to prevent the paint from overheating and producing circular concentric grooves. General safety instructions The activities related to the bodywork repair operations involve the use of specialist equipment as well as the handling of chemical products, which must be done in accordance with the supplier's recommendations. Special attention should therefore be paid to: The correct use of materials, instruments and equipment: before carrying out any operation, read the instruction manuals very carefully and follow the directions and recommended accident-prevention regulations scrupulously. Specially designated work areas must be equipped with a ventilation system that meets standards as far as air exchange, the filtration of harmful substances (solvents) and keeping down dust levels are concerned. Dangerous substances that have to be used must be handled following the supplier's instructions and recommendations. *-The collection and disposal of waste must be carried out in accordance with current legislation. Whilst working with and handling dangerous substances, the appropriate accident prevention measures must be taken (wearing protective clothing, masks, gloves, goggles, etc.). Vehicle repair operating cycles The vehicle repair operating cycles usually consist of the following stages: checking vehicle measurements; cutting/removing damaged elements and preparing the bodyshell for welding; welding replacement parts; preparation for painting; painting; restoring anti-corrosion conditions, sound insulation, sealants. Check and restore specified bodyshell measurements This is the first stage of the repair operation during which the distortion suffered by the body is measured and evaluated and the elements involved are identified. The first actual repair operation is also carried out during this stage: stretching the body to restore the correct dimensions before cutting and removing the damaged elements. Stretching the body Stretching the body to restore the distances is carried out on the alignment benches, where it is possible to secure the body using vices and mountings to be fitted in accordance with the specific instructions for each vehicle, which come with the bench. Templates, positioned in the recommended places, are used to check the bodyshell measurements either using the measurements given by the manufacturer of the template for each model or, alternatively, those for the vehicle given in the "Description and Operation" section. For safety reasons and for a better quality repair, IT IS FORBIDDEN TO: replace the structural parts of the body without using a repair bench. The use of the bench makes it possible to guarantee the restructuring of the vehicle with the original manufacturing measurements, ensuring the correct positioning of the components that make up the forecarriage and the rear part of the vehicle. heat the structural parts of the bodyshell to straighten them. cut and weld, any bodywork element and reinforcement, edge to edge, on the same line. Remove the damaged components by cutting them along the joints, following the cutting lines given in the Service Manual. The use of the following is required for removing damaged panels: alternating power saws; circular saws; power chisels (only if necessary); plasma cutting systems; electric drills; milling machines; grinders; hammers and dolly blocks; disc grinders; air extractor fans. Alternating power saw This type of saw makes it possible to make fast, precision cuts with the possibility of regulating the speed of the blade so that it can be adapted to suit different conditions. By adjusting the speed and the number of oscillations it is possible to achieve the precision required, according to the usage conditions. The high safety level for this instrument means that it is advisable to use it as an alternative to other types of saws. Example of a circular saw Power chisel Power chisels are used to detach parts of panels and are recommended: *- when it is not possible to use the air saw, chamfering machine or drill, e.g. when another panel lies behind the panel to be cut that must not be damaged. *- when it is not possible to separate the welded panel directly by inserting the chisel tip between the two panels along the join, in order not to leave edges to be removed at a later stage. The different fittings that it comes with increase its versatility. Example of the use of a power chisel. General information on electric spot welding During spot welding the heat required to melt the metal is provided by the resistance to the flow of current which the metal opposes. Spot welding is carried out on panels where the join edges are overlapping and takes place through localized fusion of the metal that makes up the panel so no filler metal is required for this type of welding. In areas where three or more panels are overlapping, the spot welding must be repeated a second time. The type of join that is produced is the discontinuous type; the weld spots must be correctly spaced in order to confer good mechanical resistance, in accordance with the precise instructions (see the tables below). Spot welding In the case of spot welding, check: that the arms are correctly aligned; that the diameter of the ends of the electrodes is correct; the planarity and correct matching of the edges of the weld; the correct welding sequence. Before welding, apply electro-galvanizing protective to the edges of the join to protect the box sections from corrosion. Seam welding (mig) MIG welding should be used for parts where spot welding cannot be used. When seam (MIG) welding, check: the speed of the wire the correct execution of the seam welding beads (alternation of welding sections) In this welding system the electrode (an automatic advance continuous wire) is protected by an atmosphere of inert gases (this is where the initials MIG come from - Metal Inert Gas). - The continuous advance of the wire (which constitutes both the electrode and the filler metal), allows long welds to be made with no interruptions. The flow of inert gases sent to the welding area eliminates the air surrounding the fusion bath, preventing the oxidation of the metal. It also carries out the function of a protective coating for coated electrode welding. For these reasons, MIG welding differs from welding carried out with a coated electrode due to the absence of deposits on the welding seam. Neither is it affected by the porosity that may occur with normal arc welding. The use of MIG welding systems requires use of an extraction system to remove the harmful gases and fumes. Operating methods In order to weld two panels correctly using a MIG welder: grind or pickle the panel thoroughly, position the equipment so that whilst carrying out the welding the torch outer casing does not become twisted or folded in such a way that could obstruct the advance of the wire, wear protective clothing and a suitable mask with a non-actinic visor (standard no. 8 glass for currents of 40-60A and no. 9 for currents of 80-200A). Regulate the flow of gas in accordance with the instructions from the equipment's Manufacturer. Make two spot welds at the ends of the join line and one in the middle, then make welds in between the two sections defined in this way. The spot welds should be 25 - 30 mm apart. It is not advisable to seam weld initially because, in addition to being difficult in practical terms, it may cause the panel to become distorted as a result of the buildup of heat involved. The difficulties in carrying out a single seam weld lie in the need to move the torch fairly slowly to produce good penetration of the weld but sufficiently quickly so as not to run the risk of "burning" the panel. Moving the torch too quickly also leads to a poor seal of the weld seam because, after the operation of grinding the seam, an insufficient layer of filler material remains to guarantee the resistance of the join. After initially spot welding the panel, a disc grinder must be used until the weld spots are level with the panel. At this point the alignment of the panels must be checked and, if necessary, corrected using a hammer and dolly block. Air filtration and purification systems When carrying out work that produces fumes, gas and powder which are dangerous to the mechanic, air filtration and purification systems must be used. These systems are designed for the various requirements to handle different volumes of air that require purification. The operation of these systems is usually based on the combined action of mechanical and electro-static filtration and purification using active charcoal. Filtration takes place in two stages: mechanical elimination, using mesh filters, of the largest particles of powder and then subjecting the air flow to ionisation, which statically charges the particles of powder. These are then eliminated from the flow through an electrostatic process. The flow of air is then purified by passing through active charcoal filters. In these systems, in addition to the specific efficiency, the ease of handling and noise levels have been improved and are never troublesome. The diagram below illustrates a possible conformation.
