PAINTING Introduction Painting the body has two basic objectives: protecting the surfaces of the panels from the elements and an aesthetic function of providing colour and shine. The large number of chemical products used in painting operations means that special care must be taken over their handling and usage. These painting operations involve the emission of paint fumes and solvent vapours which, if inhaled by the operator, could constitute a serious danger to health. These operations should therefore only be carried out in spray booths. The operator should always wear a mask and protective clothing. These masks should be the filtration type for operations that do not take very long; for longer operations the masks must be the total protection pressurised type. Equipment The following equipment is used during painting operations: filtration masks and protective clothing, masking and taping machines; spray booths and drying ovens; spray guns; infrared lamps; polishing machines; Protective clothing When carrying out painting operations, suitable protective clothing must be worn to protect the operator from contact with harmful substances. It is also advisable to use a barrier cream on any exposed areas (face, hands, arms) which should be removed at the end of the painting operations. Filtration mask This type of mask only protects the operator's respiratory system and protective goggles and headgear should be also worn at the same time. Its use is recommended for small retouching operations. Example of a filtration mask. Pressurized mask This type of mask guarantees protection of the face and hair and is supplied with pure air from the compressed air system used for the spray gun. The air is purified further with a degree of separation close to 100%, by an active charcoal filter fitted to the operator's belt. The slight excess pressure created inside the helmet prevents the penetration of paint vapours. The use of this mask is advisable for long painting operations. Example of a pressurized mask Spray booth Spray booths are used for painting operations and baking prepared parts. If the extent of the damage repaired is medium or large, it would be helpful to have a special spray booth and a hot air circulation oven for drying the paint. The area should be equipped with an air conditioning system and filtered by purifiers, mainly comprising active charcoal filters. The optimum painting conditions that should be maintained in the booth during the painting stage are as follows: constant temperature of between 22 and 25° C constant humidity of between 75 and 80% The area in question could be: a combined painting and drying booth; a separate type painting booth and drying oven. Spray guns Developments in the study of ergonomics and spray painting techniques have led to a new type of high volume air and low atomisation pressure spray gun that allows a considerable reduction in paint mist. This type of spray gun has been designed to be lighter with a grip that reduces tiredness and eliminates cramp and with controls that require far less effort than conventional spray guns. The handling of the spray gun is also made easier by the even weight distribution and by the improved design that makes it easier to operate. The most interesting aspect of this spray gun is the supply system that allows painting in any direction, even with the cup facing downwards, also improving the cleaning procedures with considerable savings in terms of time and materials. The possibility of painting from the top or the bottom, in addition to preventing the formation of areas that are too wet or too dry, also facilitates access to areas of the bodywork that are difficult to reach. Special care has been taken over the ease of adjustment. This requires minimal, simple movements. This spray gun is extremely efficient combining a very fine atomization capacity for any product, even water soluble, used by bodyworkers at a pressure of 0.7g (10 PSI) or below. Thanks to these capacities for using paint materials, it has been possible to achieve a considerable economic saving and improved working conditions. Renewing anti-corrosion/sound insulation/sealant treatments The treatments carried out on the body in order to produce the necessary corrosion resistance, sound insulation and sealant properties may be damaged or destroyed during the repair operations. DESCRIPTION The electrical system is designed to increase the car's safety level and prevent the possibility of fires and other consequences of electrical malfunctions. State-of-the-art connectors have been introduced to rule out the possibility of many connection defects. Power is distributed via the junction units and/ or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum wiring complexity. All wiring looms have been made modular (sub-assembly composition) by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints. The main safety solutions adopted are as follows: - power supplies protected by maxi fuses to cut off the electrical system in the event of a short circuit (see detail below); - the only cables not fitted with maxi fuses (starter motor and alternator) are armoured and located in protected areas. In the event of an emergency - operation of the inertia switch - these cables are disconnected by an automatic device located in the battery fuse box See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING - the layout of the whole system is optimised to reduce the risk of damage in the event of faults or accidents; - wiring installation has been optimised to reduced incorrect positioning and noise due to vibrations - all wires offer high resistance to abrasion; - the wires in the engine are specially designed to be resistant to high temperatures and are protected by outer casings or piping; - the wires in the passenger compartment are protected by corrugated pipes and napped tape to reduce noise levels; - the main connections come with secondary lock terminals and lever locks or "CPA" to prevent terminal deformation. All systems and electrical equipment are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12V. The battery is recharged by the alternator during engine operation See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main power supply lines are protected by MAXI FUSES housed in the engine compartment junction unit; other shunt fuses are located outside it. This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Some circuits are continuously supplied, even with the car at a standstill and the TEG extracted, because they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied with the TEG inserted in the TEG Reader: the distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT and 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the "steering lock node", and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key. The lines that distribute power to the various appliances are represented by wiring diagrams for the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all the lines as they leave the battery and maxi fuse boxes. Refer to specific diagrams for more details.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION All electrical systems and circuits are supplied by battery A1. The main power supply lines are protected by maxi fuses in the maxi fuse box on the battery B99, in particular: - CVM: engine compartment junction unit B1 power supply - connector X; - CPL: junction unit under the dashboard B2 power supply - to pin A of connector C; - CPR : heater plugs control unit power supply See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT The B99 fuse box includes the automatic battery disconnection device which, in emergencies, cuts off the power supply to the engine starting/ recharging cable. See descriptions 5530 CURRENT GENERATION There is an additional fuse box B98, next to the maxi fuse box on the battery on one side of the actual battery, with two MIDI maxi fuses which supply the additional heater. See E6015 ADDITIONAL HEATER The following, amongst others, are supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B1: - the steering lock node M89 (which "replaces" the ignition switch), fuse F3; - the junction unit under the dashboard B2 and the one in the luggage compartment B45 fuse 1. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT ignition-operated, 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the steering lock control unit, and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key. The power supply for the M89 control unit reaches pin C1 of M89 from the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 whilst pin A4 of M89 is earthed. The TEG inserted status is sent by the TEG Reader H3 via the CAN - pins 3 and 8. The same signal is sent, redundantly, to the steering lock node M89, from pin 2 and the latter, in turn, forwards it via the CAN. With the TEG inserted, numerous ignition-operated circuits and services are supplied (lines INT and 15/54): lines leaving pins A1 and B1 of M89. With the TEG inserted, without starting up (INT/A line): other circuits and services are supplied: from pins B3 and C8 of M89.

All wiring looms have been made modular (sub-assembly composition) by changing the way functions are distributed inside the connectors and replacing welds with short-circuiting joints. The main safety solutions adopted are as follows: - power supplies protected by maxi fuses to cut off the electrical system in the event of a short circuit (see detail below); - the only cables not fitted with maxi fuses (starter motor and alternator) are armoured and located in protected areas. In the event of an emergency - operation of the inertia switch - these cables are disconnected by an automatic device located in the battery fuse box See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING - the layout of the whole system is optimised to reduce the risk of damage in the event of faults or accidents; - wiring installation has been optimised to reduced incorrect positioning and noise due to vibrations - all wires offer high resistance to abrasion; - the wires in the engine are specially designed to be resistant to high temperatures and are protected by outer casings or piping; - the wires in the passenger compartment are protected by corrugated pipes and napped tape to reduce noise levels; - the main connections come with secondary lock terminals and lever locks or "CPA" to prevent terminal deformation. All systems and electrical equipment are supplied by the battery at a voltage of 12V. The battery is recharged by the alternator during engine operation See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The main power supply lines are protected by MAXI FUSES housed in the engine compartment junction unit; other shunt fuses are located outside it. This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Some circuits are continuously supplied, even with the car at a standstill and the TEG extracted, because they are connected directly to the battery. Other circuits are supplied with the TEG inserted in the TEG Reader: the distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT and 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the "steering lock node", and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key. The lines that distribute power to the various appliances are represented by wiring diagrams for the various functions and systems. This general diagram shows all the lines as they leave the battery and maxi fuse boxes. Refer to specific diagrams for more details.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION All electrical systems and circuits are supplied by battery A1. The main power supply lines are protected by maxi fuses in the maxi fuse box on the battery B99, in particular: - CVM: engine compartment junction unit B1 power supply - connector X; - CPL: junction unit under the dashboard B2 power supply - to pin A of connector C; The B99 fuse box includes the automatic battery disconnection device which, in emergencies, cuts off the power supply to the engine starting/ recharging cable. See descriptions 5530 CURRENT GENERATION The following, amongst others, are supplied by the engine compartment junction unit B1: - the steering lock node M89 (which "replaces" the ignition switch), fuse F3; - the junction unit under the dashboard B2 and the one in the luggage compartment B45 fuse 1. The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (INT ignition-operated, 15/54, INT/A, "AVV", etc.) is managed by the steering lock control unit, and takes place in exactly the same way as on models with a traditional key. The power supply for the M89 control unit reaches pin C1 of M89 from the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 whilst pin A4 of M89 is earthed. The TEG inserted status is sent by the TEG Reader H3 via the CAN - pins 3 and 8. The same signal is sent, redundantly, to the steering lock node M89, from pin 2 and the latter, in turn, forwards it via the CAN. With the TEG inserted, numerous ignition-operated circuits and services are supplied (lines INT and 15/54): lines leaving pins A1 and B1 of M89. With the TEG inserted, without starting up (INT/A line): other circuits and services are supplied: from pins B3 and C8 of M89.

DESCRIPTION This vehicle is equipped with a CAN (Controller Area Network) system of electrical connections: it involves a software and hardware solution which is designed to efficiently manage the resources on the vehicle, allowing: - the sharing of information between the various electronic units; - the integration of several electronic units through one network; - a high network information exchange speed; - advantages in economic terms because there is a considerable reduction in the wiring/connectors inside the vehicle; - higher standards in terms of quality and reliability. The advantage of using a CAN system stems from the fact that communication takes place between numerous control units and consequently the number of signals to be managed is very high. For this reason the signals travel on a CAN type serial Bus where one wire is high level (H) and the other low level (L); these signals on the CAN Bus are differential, i.e. the value assigned to the bit is represented by the difference between the CAN-H and CAN-L voltage levels. The different electronic units which make up the system, known as network nodes, are connected to the CAN by means of communication interfaces known as transreceivers; these connection interfaces, integrated in the electronic units, constitute the gate for sending/reading the information at the CAN or at the serial lines. The exchange of information at CAN type serial lines is only possible using a transmission protocol which is the collection of rules that allow communication between two or more nodes by means of the exchange of information or data packages. The main element of the network is the Body Computer. The Body Computer node is entrusted with "waking up the network" when a "known" TEG is inserted in the TEG Reader (if there is a problem with the Body Computer this task is entrusted to the instrument panel). The Body Computer also carries out the network checking functions which make it possible to provide information on: - the network activity status; - the functional failure status of the individual electronic units (nodes); - a possible CAN fault. The various electronic units process the various signals coming from the corresponding sensors both for their own management and for other control units to which they are sent via the CAN. The specific structure adopted for this vehicle consists of two CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to two different areas: - C-CAN for dynamic vehicle control (high speed): bus CAN-H and CAN-L; - B-CAN for the management of standard body functions (low speed): bus CAN-A and CAN-B; the two CAN communication networks are connected to one another by a gateway for transferring joint information, located in the Body Computer Node. The fault diagnosis of the nodes connected to the B-CAN network is carried out via the CAN network, whilst for those connected to the C-CAN this is carried out by means of the specific K lines. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR There is also the W line, ISO 5 serial for recovery of the Code system See E7010 CODE and the A-BUS serial line ISO 5 for the alarm, wiping functions, lighting, tyre pressure monitoring system. See E1060 A-BUS SERIAL LINE Power is distributed via the junction units and/ or fuses boxes. These are connected to control elements (relays and static actuators) to ensure maximum electrical protection and minimum wiring complexity. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The Body Computer M1 is supplied directly from the battery via line protected by maxifuse F1 of engine compartment control unit B1 at pin 18 of connector F that interfaces with underfacia control unit B2 . The Body Computer M1 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) at pin 9 of connector F of the interface with the junction unit under the dashboard B2 : this signal is used, amongst other things, to "wake up the network". Pins 8 and 9 of connector I of M1 are earthed. The nodes connected to Body Computer M1 - from pins 36 and 37 of connector B - via the high speed C-CAN network are: - engine management control unit M10; - ABS/VDC control unit M50 ; - steering angle sensor K58; - yaw sensor K74. The following nodes are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the B-CAN low speed network: - underfacia junction unit B2 ; - instrument panel E50; - driver's side door control unit M66 , passenger side door M67 ; - parking sensor control unit M84 ; - seat control unit H66 and H67; - hood control unit M187 (Spider only); - Air Bag control unit M60 . - climate control sytem control unit M70; - controls on the steering wheel (via the clock spring D47); - built-in radio-telephone-navigator P20; - Bluetooth control unit M162; - steering lock control unit M89 ; - TEG Reader H3.

DESCRIPTION This vehicle is equipped with a CAN (Controller Area Network) system of electrical connections. The different electronic units that make up the system, known as network "Nodes" are connected to the CAN; the main element of the network is the Body Computer. The various electronic units process the various signals coming from the corresponding sensors both for their own management and for other control units to which they are sent via the CAN. The structure consists of two CAN communication networks which connect nodes belonging to two different areas: - C-CAN for dynamic vehicle control (high speed): bus CAN-H and CAN-L; - B-CAN for the management of standard body functions (low speed): bus CAN-A and CAN-B; the two CAN communication networks are connected to one another by a gateway for transferring joint information, located in the Body Computer Node. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES A special A-BUS ISO 5 serial line manages the connection with the following functions: -alarm (siren); - automatic wiping (rain senosr); - automatic lighting (dusk sensor).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The Body Computer M1 is supplied directly from the battery via line protected by maxifuse F1 of engine compartment control unit B1 at pin 18 of connector F that interfaces with underfacia control unit B2 . The Body Computer M1 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) at pin 9 of connector F of the interface with the junction unit under the dashboard B2 : this signal is used, amongst other things, to "wake up the network". Pins 8 and 9 of connector I of M1 are earthed. The A-BUS serial line is connected from pin 25 of connector B of the Body Computer M1 with the alarm sensor P90 - pin 2 - and with th steering column switch unit H5 - pin 2 of connector A; the latter manages the signal from the rain sensor. Serial A-BUS line is connected from pin 7 of connector D of body computer M1 to the rain and dusk sensors built ino the electrochrome interior rear view mirror P65, pin 3.

DESCRIPTION The side lights are switched on at the first turn of the ring nut on the left steering column switch unit lever. The turning on of the side lights is managed by the Body Computer. The side lights control function is activated through the TEG on enablement signals (INT) and the command from the steering column switch unit: the four side lights are supplied in this way. The number plate light and numerous other interior lights for lighting the passenger compartment, instruments and controls are activated together with the side lights (these are described and explained in the wiring diagrams for the relevant components). Activation/deactivation information is sent via the CAN network: in this way, the side lights warning light in the instrument panel is also activated. The instrument panel also activates the nightime lighting. The side lights can be activated automatically by means of the dusk sensor if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that operates at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons. The "parking lights" function is turned on - only with the TEG extracted - by pressing the button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel: a roger beep signals engagement. If the steering column switch unit left lever is turned (in the same way as for activating the direction indicators) it is possible to choose whether to turn on the side lights on both sides of the vehicle (lever in middle position) or only those on one side (lever downwards to select the left side, lever upwards to select the right side). The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The side lights warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on. It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the length of time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds, up to a maximum of 210 seconds. Inserting the TEG or keeping the flasher lever pulled for more than 2 seconds eliminates the function. The correct operation of the lights is checked by the side lights and no. plate lights check function: the following is checked for each of the circuits: - circuit open or bulb missing - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt) When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display. For safe driving, if there is a fault with one of the rear bulbs, with the side lights on the brake light bulb on the corresponding side comes on dimly to simulate the brightness of the side light. The system also detects any faults in the dusk sensor. if a fault is detected, the "general failure" warning light is turned on and the information is shown simultaneously on the display.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Two signals (earth) are sent from the steering wheel stalk unit H5 to the Body Computer M1 that manages both side lights and low beams in manual or AUTO mode (automatic dusk sensor activation). The "Light 1" signal - is sent to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 7 of connector C. The "Light 2" signal - is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unig H5, pin 8 of connector C. The side lights are turned on manually when the "Light 1" signal is missing and the "Light 2" signal is present. The side lights are activated in AUTO mode when the Light 1 signal is not present and the Light 2 signal is not present. If both signals are present, the lights are permanently off. The side lights are automatically activated by the dusk sensor housed in the mirror P65 (signal via the A-BUS line to pin 7 of connector D of M1); the dusk sensor in P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2. The lights are also activated by the parking lights button located in the left switch unit H90 which sends an earth signal to pin 17 of connector H of M1. The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the front side lights F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 40 and 30 of connector B, for the rear side lights F30 (left) and F31 (right) and the number plate lights F50 and F51 from pins 5, 6, 9 of connector D and 38 of connector E. Via the CAN line, the Body Computer M1 is connected to instrument panel E50 to manage the side lights on warning light and, if faults are detected in the circuit or in the bulbs, the lights failure warning light; in the vent of a fault with the dusk sensor there is a specific signal.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with two dipped headlamps in the lights. The headlamps are switched on by the steering column switch unit by turning the ring nut to the position after the side lights. A special relay, located in the junciton unit under the dashboard, controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps via two lines protected by special fuses. The relay for engaging the dipped headlamps is managed by the Body Computer. relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit. With the dipped headlamps on, the simultaneous presence of the main beam and fog lights commands disables the dipped headlamps. The subsequent deactivation of one of these two commands, with the dipped headlamps control still on, involves the dipped headlamps being turned back on. The dipped headlamps can be automatically activated by means of the dusk sensor, if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that works at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons. The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The "dipped headlamps" warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on. It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the length of time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds, up to a maximum of 210 seconds. Inserting the TEG or keeping the flasher lever pulled for more than 2 seconds eliminates the function.

The "Light 2" signal is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 8 of connector C. DESCRIPTION The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. The electronics built into each of the two headlamps switch them on and off according to the times defined by the software and, in accordance with international regulations, the gas discharge bulbs too. The system comprises an igniter located in the base of the bulb and a ballast located in the bottom part of the lamp. The left lamp is the master control unit, whilst the right one performs a slave role. The master lamp acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles. Depending on the inputs, it directly controls the switching on of the left front headlamp (dipped headlamps) and controls the right one in a similar way via the serial line. The dipped beams are activated by turning a wheel on the stalk switch to the next position after the side light setting. A relay in the underfacia control unit controls activation of the low beams via two lines protected by specific fuses. The low beam activation relay is controlled by the Body Computer relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit. With the dipped headlamps on, the switching to main beams causes the shutter in gas discharge bulb to be raised with a switch to main beams. The dipped headlamps can be automatically activated by means of the dusk sensor, if the AUTO function is set on the steering column switch unit. The dusk sensor is an infrared device that works at different sensitivity settings: when the dusk sensor is activated a message is shown on the instrument panel display indicating the sensitivity setting (from 1 to 3): this setting can be adjusted using the "Mode +" and "Mode -" buttons. The "Follow me home" function allows the dipped headlamps and the side lights to remain on even after the engine has been switched off (TEG extracted) for a period of 30 seconds or multiples thereof. The "dipped headlamps" warning light in the instrument panel signals that the lights have remained on. It is turned on using the lever in the same way as for activating the flasher within 2 minutes of the TEG being extracted: each time the lever is operated the length of time the lights remain on is increased by 30 seconds, up to a maximum of 210 seconds. Inserting the TEG or keeping the flasher lever pulled for more than 2 seconds eliminates the function.

The "Light 1" signal is sent from pin 28 of connector G of Body Computer M1 from stalk unit H5, pin 7 of connector C. The "Light 2" signal is sent to pin 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5, pin 8 of connector C. The dipped headlamps are switched on manually when the "Light 1" is absent and when the "Light 2" signal is also missing. The dipped headlamps are activated in AUTO mode when the Light 1 signal is present and the Light 2 signal is not present. If both signals are present, the lights are constantly off. The dipped headlamps are automatically activated by the dusk sensor housed in the mirror P65 (signal via the A-BUS line at pin 7 of connector D of M1); the dusk sensor in P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2. The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: this supplies the dipped headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit B2 : F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line of junction unit B2 protected by fuse F37. Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the junction unit located in headlamp F10. Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "dipped headlamps on" warning light and, if there are problems detected in the circuit, the specific warning light.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with two high beams in the headlamps. The main beams are switched on by the steering column switch unit: - with the dipped beams on, by pushing the lever towards the dashboard (stable mode) - in flashing mode, by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel (unstable mode) The low beam activation relay is controlled by the Body Computer relay energizing is activated by enablement signals with the TEG inserted (INT) and from the specific signal from the steering column switch unit. DESCRIPTION The left and right direction indicators are switched on by raising or lowering the special lever on the left of the steering column switch unit; the function is activated with the TEG inserted (ON). The hazard warning lights (left and right direction indicators operated simultaneously) are activated via a button in the centre console next to the gear lever and activates all the direction indicators simultaneously. An LED at the back of the control button also comes on synchronized with the flashing of the exterior lights. This function is always activated for safety reasons. The engagement of the direction indicators / hazard warning lights is managed by the Body Computer which also controls the flashing frequency which is sent to the other nodes via the CAN serial network. In this way the two direction indicator warning lights in the instrument panel are also switched on; in addition, the system provides a low frequency acoustic signal in conjunction with the activation of the lights. The direction indicators check function checks that the lights are working properly: the following are checked for each of the two circuit (right side branch and vehicle left side): - circuit open or bulb missing - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt) When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: in the instrument panel: a special failure warning light comes on and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display only at the key on. In addition, at the same time as a failure warning light comes on, the flashing frequency of the visual indication in the display and the acoustic signal increases; the flashing frequency of the exterior lights and the LED in the emergency button, on the other hand, remains unchanged. the direction indicators are also used to signal that the commands sent by the remote control have been received and/or to signal a manoeuvre not carried out by the "passenger compartment access" control system. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The direction indicator (earth) activation signals are sent to pins 7 of connector I and 30 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5. The hazard light activation signal (earth) reaches pin 34 of connector G of M1 from control button H20. The Body Computer M1 receives a specific direct power supply for the hazard warning lights via the line for fuse F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B; as a result it controls the side direction indicators F20 (left) and F21 (right) from pins 2 of connector A and 22 of connector B, the sid direction indicators F10 (left) and F11 (right) from pins 38 and 39 of connector B and the rear direction indicators F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 12 and 3 of connector D. A (positive) signal is sent from pin 29 of connector G of M1 to lightup the LED in the control button H20 with the power supply arriving from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of junciton unit B2. The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "direction indicator" warning lights, the buzzer and, if there is a problem in the circuit, the "lights failure" warning light.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights (by means of a red double filament bulb together with the side light) and in the special centre third brake light. They are operated each time the brake pedal is pressed via the special switch on the actual pedal. the switch fitted on the pedals consists of two contacts which supply two signals: the first is the N.A. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal if it is not in the rest postion, i.e. the pedal is pressed; the second is the N.C. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal in the rest position. The lights are turned on by the N.A. contact (pedal pressed). Information from the N.A. switch is sent in particular to the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit, VDC function. See E7022 VDC The control function is activated by the TEG inserted enablement signals (INT) and the command from the switch contact. The brake light check function monitors that the side lights are operating correctly: the following are checked: - open circuit (bulb missing or wiring interrupted) - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt) The continuity of the fuse protecting the switch on the brake pedal is also checked. When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display by means of the specific symbol. the central brake light is controlled directly by the switch on the pedal and is not subject to checking.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The switch I30 receives an ignition-controlled supply (INT) from the fuse line F37 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2: when the brake pedal is pressed, the N.A. switch closes and sends a signal which "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and reaches the Body Computer M1, pin 2 of connector F. The Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the brake lights located in the light clusters F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 32 and 22 of connector E. The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the lights failure warning light and the brake lights check signal if problems are detected in the circuit or in the fuse. The switch I30 controls central brake light F40 directly without any control rules, via the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 5 of connector D.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle brake lights are located at the rear in the side lights (by means of a red double filament bulb together with the side light) and in the special centre third brake light. They are operated each time the brake pedal is pressed via the special switch on the actual pedal. the switch fitted on the pedals consists of two contacts which supply two signals: the first is the N.A. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal if it is not in the rest postion, i.e. the pedal is pressed; the second is the N.C. type and recognizes the position of the brake pedal in the rest position. The lights are turned on by the N.A. contact (pedal pressed). Information from the N.A. switch is sent in particular to the engine management control unit and the ABS control unit, VDC function. See E7022 VDC The control function is activated by the TEG inserted enablement signals (INT) and the command from the switch contact. The brake light check function monitors that the side lights are operating correctly: the following are checked: - open circuit (bulb missing or wiring interrupted) - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt) The continuity of the fuse protecting the switch on the brake pedal is also checked. When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display by means of the specific symbol. the central brake light is controlled directly by the switch on the pedal and is not subject to checking.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The switch I30 receives an ignition-controlled supply (INT) from the fuse line F37 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2: when the brake pedal is pressed, the N.A. switch closes and sends a signal which "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and reaches the Body Computer M1, pin 2 of connector F. The Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the brake lights located in the light clusters F30 (left) and F31 (right) from pins 32 and 22 of connector E. The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the lights failure warning light and the brake lights check signal if problems are detected in the circuit or in the fuse. The switch I30 controls central brake light F40 directly without any control rules, via the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 5 of connector D.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a white reversing light located in the passenger side rear light cluster. It is activated each time reverse gear is engaged: this information arrives via the special switch located on the outside of the gearbox casing. The reversing lights circuit is supplied with the TEG inserted (INT) and protected by a special fuse in the under-dashboard control unit. The signal that reverse gear has been engaged is managed by the Body Computer which forwards this information to the steering wheel interface for the automatic operation of the rearscreen wiper and, via the CAN, to the other nodes, for example to the parking sensors control unit. See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE See E3032 DOOR MIRROR ADJUSTMENT

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The switch for reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of under-dashboard control unit B2. When reverse gear is engaged, the switch closes and sends a power supply to the reversing light in right rear light cluster F31 (left rear light cluster F30 on right hand drive versions), directly via control unit B2 from pin 7 of connector D. The activation signal for the reversing light is also sent to Body Computer M1 - pin 3 of connector F - and from there to steering wheel interface H5, for the automatic engagement of the rearscreen wiper. See E3021 REAR WINDOW WASH/WIPE

It is activated each time reverse gear is engaged: this information arrives from the automatic transmission, or the robotized gearbox, control unit. The circuit for the reversing lights is supplied with the TEG inserted (INT) and is protected by a special fuse in the under-dashboard control unit. The signal that reverse gear has been engaged is managed by the Body Computer which forwards this information to the steering wheel interface for the automatic operation of the rearscreen wiper and, via the CAN, to the other nodes, for example to the parking sensors control unit. FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Versions with automatic transmission: when reverse gear is engaged, automatic transmission control unit M55 sends the reverse gear engaged signal from pin 13 of connector A to relay T20 in engine compartment control unit B1, which receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply from the line for fuse F35 of under-dashboard control unit B2 and sends a power supply to the reversing light in the right rear light cluster - moving section - F36, directly via control unit B2, from pin 7 of connector D. DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with two additional fog lights, located in the front bumper. The fog lights are activated via the special button in the controls to the left of the steering wheel; when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. A relay located in the engine bay control unit controls fog lamp activation via a line protected by a fuse. The relay is managed by the Body Computer; the energizing of the relay is activated by: - the TEG inserted enablement signal (INT); - a control signal coming from the switch; - the side lights on signal. If the side lights are turned off, the fog lamps are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed. When the side lights are switched on again, the fog lights do not come on automatically, but only when the button is pressed again. If the TEG is switched off (OFF position) and then switched back on (MAR), the button must be activated again to turn on the fog lights.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The (earth) activation signal for the fog lights reaches pin 1 of connector I of M1 from the control button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel H90. The side lights activation signal is sent to pin 28 of connector G and 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS The Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the fog lights sending an earth signal to the relay T14: of the engine compartment junction unit B1 - from pin 8 of connector A of M1 - which energizes relay T14: this supplies the fog lights F15 (left) and F16 (right). The circuit is protected by fuse F30 of junction unit B2. The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the "fog lights on" warning light.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with extra-bright red rear fog lamp located in the driver's side rear light cluster. The rear fog lamp is activated via the special button in the controls to the left of the steering wheel; when the lights are on, the warning light in the instrument panel comes on. The switching on of the rear fog lamp is managed by the Body Computer; it is activated by: - the TEG inserted enablement signal (INT); - a control signal coming from the switch - dipped headlamps or fog lights on signal. If the dipped headlamps lights or the fog lights are turned off, the rear fog lamps are deactivated even if the operating button is still pressed. When the side lights are switched on again, the rear fog lamps do not come on automatically, but only when the button is pressed again. If the TEG is switched off (OFF position) and then switched back on (MAR), the button must be activated again to turn on the fog lights. The rear fog lamp check function checks that the light is working properly: the following are checked: - circuit open or bulb missing - short-circuit to earth (bulb s.c. or wiring s.c. to earth) - short circuit to battery voltage (wiring short circuited to Vbatt) When one of the situations described above is ascertained, the Body Computer makes the failure status available to the CAN: a special "lights failure" warning light comes on in the instrument panel and, at the same time, the information is shown in the display.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The (earth) activation signal for the rear fog lamps reaches pin 35 of connector G of M1 from the control button in the panel to the left of the steering wheel H90. The side lights and dipped hedlamps activation signal is sent to pin 28 of connector G and 2 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5. See E2010 SIDE LIGHTS / NO. PLATE LIGHTS See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS the fog lights activation signal reaches pin 1 of connector I of the Body Computer M1 See E2030 FOG LIGHTS On the basis of these signals, Body Computer M1 controls the power supply for the rear fog lamp in the light cluster F30 (right rear light cluster F31 on right hand drive versions) from pin 31 of connector E of M1.

DESCRIPTION The front courtesy light includes three lamps with three control switches: it is possible to switch on the corresponding spot light using the outside buttons; the centre button switches the centre light on and off, which is also turned on with a timed delay as described below. The courtesy light operation is timed according to a strategy managed by the body computer: - When any of the doors is opened, the courtesy lights comes on and there is a timed delay of 3 minutes which is reactivated each time a door is opened. - When, on the other hand, the button on the courtesy light is pressed during the timed delay, the courtesy lights are switched off and the timed delay in progress is zeroed. - When all the doors are closed at the key-off (TEG extrated), the previous timed delay is zeroed and a 10 second timed delay is activated; (this delay is interrupted in the case of a key-on (insertion of the TEG). - When all the doors are closed at the key-on (insertion of the TEG) the courtesy lights are immediately switched off. - when the key is removed, the courtesy light comes on and a 10 second timer is activated. - all the courtesy lights are turned off at the door lock control; - at the door release command, the courtesy light is turned on and a 10 second timer is activated. - If the inertia switch is operated the courtesy light comes on for 15 minutes. The switching on or off takes place gradually (dimmer) with the cycle lasting 2 seconds. If one or more doors are open, this is shown on the instrument panel display; the warning light remain on until all the vehicle doors and boot lid are properly shut. If a given speed limit is exceeded, this is also signalled by means of a buzzer.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The Body Computer M1 receives door open input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door) and 25 of connector E (passenger side door). Front courtesy light G10 is operated from a direct line protected by fuse F39 of under-dashboard control unit B2. The front courtesy light G10 is controlled by the Body Computer M1 : the analogue control signal from the three courtesy light buttons reaches pin 28 of connector E of M1 : the Body Computer M1 consequently supplies the courtesy lights G10, providing a timed earth signal from pins 21, 30 and 37. The Body Computer M1 is connected, via the CAN line, to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "inertia switch operated" signal that lights up the courtesy lights and to which a signal that lights up the "doors open" warning light, when necessary, is sent.

DESCRIPTION When the boot is opened the light in the luggage compartment comes on and goes out when the boot is closed. The light inside the glove compartment comes on when it is opened and goes out when it is closed. The lights located beneath each of the sun blinds are turned on by a switch on the lights. The Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal to compare it with a limit figure (SBMT function): if the battery voltage measured is below the level, it intervenes via the CAN sending a signal to disable a series of loads: these include the glove compartment light, the boot light and the sun visor lights; the function is activated after the key-off (TEG extracted).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION On the basis of the battery voltage (SBMT) described previously, the Body Computer M1 supplies the boot light G40 from pin 23 of connector E and the driver's sun visor light G31 and the passenger sun visor light G32 from pin 33 of connector E; the glove compartment light G30 is supplied in a similar manner from pin 16 connector H. The boot opening switch is located in the lock N47 and sends an earth signal with the boot open to light up the relevant courtesy light G40; the same signal is sent to the Body Computer M1 - pin 36 of connector E "boot open" signal; the same signal is used by the alarm system, when fitted. See E7015 ALARM the glove compartment light G30 is switched on automatcially when the switch I30 closes when the compartment is opened. The lights in the visors G31 and G32 are switched on by an earth signal from the switch on the actual lights.

DESCRIPTION When the boot is opened the light in the luggage compartment comes on; it goes out when the boot is closed. The light inside the glove compartment comes on when it is opened and goes out when it is closed. The Body Computer continuously acquires the battery voltage signal to compare it with a limit figure (SBMT function): if the battery voltage measured is below the level, it intervenes via the CAN sending a signal to disable a series of loads: these include the glove compartment light, the boot light; the function is activated after the key-off (TEG extracted).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION On the basis of the battery voltage control unit ("SBMT") described previously, the Body Computer M1 sends a power supply from pin 23 of connector E to the boot courtesy light G40 and from pin 16 of connector H sends a power supply to the glove compartment light G30. The boot opening switch is located in the lock N47, it sends an earth signal when the boot is open to light up the relevant courtesy light G40; the same signal is sent to the Body Computer M1 - pin 36 of connector E "boot open" signal; the same signal is used by the alarm system, when fitted. See E7015 ALARM the glove compartment light G30 is switched on automatcially - when the switch I30 closes - as the compartment is opened.

DESCRIPTION There are two lights for lighting up the ground ("puddle lights") in the front front doors. The two door control units detect the status of the doors, notify the Body Computer and directly control the switching on of the bulb in the door. The opening of one of the front doors causes the relevant light to come on for a maximum of 3 minutes; when this time has expired the light can only be switched back on again after the door has been reopened. The closing of the driver's door causes the two lights to go out immediately.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The Body Computer M1 receives door open input signals at pin 8 of connector D (driver's front door) and 25 of connector E (passenger side door). The puddle lights G51 and G52 are operated by the driver's door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67 connected by the CAN line to the Body Computer M1. The control units M66 and M67 receive a power supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; on the basis of the logic described previously, each control unit supplies the relevant puddle light G51 and G52, from pins 17 and 18 of connector B.

DESCRIPTION The car is equipped with numerous light sources for optimal lighting of interior instruments and controls. Some of these are lit with the ignition ON (INT), others with the side lights on, others are dimmable in accordance with a rheostat-controlled adjustment strategy managed by the Body Computer. The Body Computer manages the lighting - with the side lights on - of: - cigar lighter; - controls on the front courtesy light - radio phone preparation The Body Computer manages (directly and via the door and boot node control units) the dimmed lighting of: - instrument panel and display; - auxiliary instrument - switches in the doors; - climate control system controls; - built-in radio-telephone-navigator unit; All the other controls are lit up when the ignition is on (INT), i.e. with the TEG inserted. A brightness sensor for the automatic adjustment (day/night) of the brightness of the instrument panel is built-in; it has the task of measuring the ambient light conditions and sending this information (daytime or nightime) to the Body Computer which, on comparing this information with the state of the side lights, selects the appropriate lighting configuration for the vehicle interior (daytime or nightime mode). With this information available, the behaviour of the instrument is as follows: - In "daytime" mode the display can be adjusted to 8 settings, the graphics are switched off, the index lighting is 100% and cannot be adjusted. - In "nightime" mode the display, the graphics and the indexes can be adjusted to 8 settings and the level set will be transmitted to the components that regulate the brightness (climate control display, radio display). This adjustment is made using the "MODE", "MODE +" and "MODE -" buttons located on the steering column switch unit; there are 8 different possible settings. (fom 30% to 100% of the maximum intensity). The level set by pressing the buttons is shown on the instrument panel display; the setting is also memorized and used later on.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The "MODE" "+" and "-" controls, located on the left steering column switch unit lever +15, send an analogue signal to the instrument panel E50 at pin 5 of connector A. The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves pin 5 of connector C of E50 (pin 2 of connector C provides the reference earth). The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 from which it receives the "brightness adjustment" signal which is transmitted to the radio node and to the climate control system control unit See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The power supply with the side lights on is sent from the Body Computer M1 - pin 40 of connector E to the cigar lighter light P50 as well as to the controls on the front courtesy light G10. When the side lights are on, the same power supply is sent - pin 18 of connector H of M1 - to radio telephone wiring D75. The lighting of the front door controls H44 and H50 is managed by the driver side door control unit M66 and passenger side door control unit M67 , supplied at pin 11 of connector D by a line protected by fuse F32 of the underfacia control unit B2 , and connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 . The ignition-controlled power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the switch unit on the tunnel H35. The ignition-operated power supply line (INT), protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, provides the lighting for the hazard warning lights control H20, the control panel to the left of the dashboard H90, the radio controls on the steering wheel D47, the boot opening control unit H33 and those on the seats I65 and I66.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a horn system consisting of two horns with different tones: one high tone and one low tone: the two horns come on simultaneously. The horns are operated by pressing the sides of the steering wheel cover (around the Air Bag). The horn circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by a relay located in the engine compartment junction unit. For safety reasons, the horns can be operated at any time even with the TEG switched off.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The system for the horns receives a power supply via the horn relay T3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 from the line directly from the battery via fuse F10 in junction unit B1. The relay coil is energized by an earth signal produced by the closing of one of the switches on the steering wheel, connected via the wiring through the clock spring D47. The relay thereby supplies the horns P05.

DESCRIPTION The windscreen wash/wipe system is activated by the lever located on the right of the steering wheel, with the following functions: there are five possible positions for the lever, turning it upwards, corresponding to: - windscreen wiper off (stationary); - intermittent/automatic operation; - continuous slow operation; - continuous fast operation; - "antipanic" temporary fast operation (unstable position, turning the lever downwards). In the intermittent/automatic operation position three different positions can be selected by turning the ring nut: - on the "LOW" version the different intermittent speeds are switched on (from the slowest to the fastest; - on the "HIGH" version with the rain sensor: the different sensor settings are switched on: the activation of the rain sensor involves a windscreen wiper arm stroke as feedback to confirm that it has been switched on. The frequency of the windscreen wiper strokes is automatically adjusted depending on the amount of water on the windscreen detected by the sensor: the frequency varies continuously from nil (no stroke - windscreen dry) to wiping at the second continuous speed (heavy rain). The windscreen washer function can be activated by pulling the lever toward the steering wheel: this activates the windscreen washer pump: keeping the lever pulled also switched on the windscreen wiper in accordance with a specific control logic: the windscreen wiper is activated at the first speed: when the windscreen washer control is no longer present, an additional stroke is carried out. The screen washer fluid reservoir has a sensor that signals a decrease in the level by means of a special warning light in the instrument panel. The control of the functions described above is carried out by an electronic device inside the steering column switch unit which produces the intermittent function and controls the operation of the windscreen wiper motor and the windscreen washer electric pump. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A). The correct operation of the rain sensor is controlled by the check function. If the rain sensor is not working properly, the windscreen wiper will operate intermittently whilst the instrument panel display will show the sensor failure.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed. According to the function selected, stalk unit H5 (connector A) sends the following control signals to the wiper motor N15: - from pin 8 for fast operation; - from pin 9 for slow and/or intermittent operation, - pin 6, on the other hand, receives the earth signal coming from the motor end of travel cam which stops operation. The windscreen wiper motor N15 is then earthed. The steering column switch unit H5 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N22 which turns sending the detergent liquid to the windscreen wiper. The rain sensor housed in the mirror P65 receives a supply from the INT line protected by fuse F49 of the junction unit B2 and sends the automatic operating signal to pin 2 of connector A of H5 via the A-BUS serial line of the Body Computer M1 pin 7 of connector D and pin 25 of connector B. The Body Computer M1 is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 to manage the failure signal if there are problems with the rain sensor. The screen washer fluid level sensor k27 sends an earth signal to the instrument panel E50 - pin 12 of connector D - which lights up the warning light directly.

DESCRIPTION The rear wiper control is activated by turning the three-position wheel anticlockwise: - stable central position, equivalent to OFF; - 2 unstable positions: rear wiper activation and rear washer activation. The rear wiper is controlled by the stalk intermittently with an interval of 5 seconds between the end of one stroke and the beginning of the next. The motor is activated throughout the duration of the command and until the brush is reparked. With the windscreen wipers working, if reverse gear is engaged, the rearscreen wiper is automatically activated: this function is managed by the Body Computer, which receives information from the reversing switch See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS Pushing the right steering column switch unit lever activates the rear washing. Keeping the lever pushed for more than 0.5 secs automatically activates the rearscreen wiper at the continuous speed. The windscreen wash/wipe circuit is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay (INT/A) located in the junction unit under the dashboard. The windscreen wiper and the windscreen washer can be activated with the TEG inserted and after starting (INT/A).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5 and the controls on the right lever receive a power supply at pin 11 of connector A from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F43, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Pin 7 of connector A and 9 of connector C of H5 are earthed. The electronic device inside the steering column switch unit H5, which controls the rear wiper receive a power supply at pin 12 of connector C from the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) of relay T12 protected by fuse F52, both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2. Steering wheel stalk unit H5 sends a command to rear wiper motor N16 from pin 1 of connector B while pin 2 receives an earth signal from the motor end stop cam, which stops operation. Pin 3 of connector A of H5 receives the reverse engaged signal for automatic rear wiper operation. The steering column switch unit H5 windscreen washer switch, once activated, sends two signals from pins 10 and 12 of connector A which operate the windscreen washer pump N22 which turns sending the washer fluid to the windscreen wiper.

DESCRIPTION The headlamp washer cleans the headlamp lenses as the windscreen is being cleaned. The headlamp washer function is managed by the Body Computer which automatically activates the headlamp washer, with the dipped headlamps on, when the windscreen washers are activated through the lever on the right of the steering wheel. The headlamp washer consists of a pump that sends detergent to two nozzles located in the bumpers which spray a powerful jet onto the headlamps. A timer activates the headlamp washer pump by means of a series of pulses lasting about half a second. The headlamp washer circuit is protected by a fuse and governed by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The relay T17 in the engine compartment junction unit B1 receives a power supply from the line for fuse F9, from the engine compartment junction unit B1, whilst the energizing takes place through the ignition-operated line (INT/A) from fuse F31 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. The relay operates the headlamp washer pump N25 directly when an earth signal arrives from the Body Computer M1; this signal - from pin 14 of connector A - is sent on the basis of the positive windscreen washer request signal coming from the steering column switch unit H5 - pin 5 of connector A and in the presence of the dipped headlamps on enablement (pin 2 of connector I and pin 28 of connector G of M1). See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS

DESCRIPTION In the event of poor visibility it is possible to activate the demisting of the rearscreen, the exterior rear view mirrors and the lower part of the windscreen. The heating coils for these components absorb a considerable amount of energy and are therefore controlled and possibly deactivated after they have been working for a certain length of time: the demisting is subject to a delay timer, managed by the Body Computer, according to the following logic: - TEG inserted, starting excluded (INT/A); - engagement signal coming from the special button in the climate control system control panel. Under these circumstances the heating coils remain supplied for a maximum of 20 minutes, then the supply is cut off. The supply is cut off in the following conditions: - TEG extracted (key-off); - disengagement signal from the button; - battery voltage below 8.5 V; - after the first 15 minutes of operation if the engine speed is below 960 rpm. With the demisting on, the warning light in the climate control system controls also comes on. The activation timer (20 minutes) is set again each time the button is operated. The climate control system control unit logic also intervenes with the "MAX-DEF" command in accordance with the logic described previously. The "MAX-DEF" function lasts for 3 minutes starting from when the engine temperature exceeds a certain limit. Deactivation of the MAX-DEF control only causes the switching off of the heated rear windscreen if the command to switch it on came from the MAX-DEF button; if, on the other hand, the command was given via the heated rearscreen button, it remains on. The rearscreen demisting circuit is controlled by the heated rearscreen relay and is protected by a specific fuse, located in the under-dashboard control unit. This circuit is controlled by the logic described above directly by the Body Computer. The demisting circuit for the door mirrors, on the other hand, is protected by another fuse in the under-dashboard control unit and is controlled by the door control units, in accordance with the logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN. The windscreen demisting circuit is operated by a special relay located in the engine compartment junction unit and protected by a specific fuse also in that junction unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Heated rearscreen relay T11, located in under-dashboard control unit B2, controls the engagement of heated rearscreen P55 demisting heating coils via the line protected by fuse F40 of control unit B2. Similarly, the engagement of the demisting heating coils for windscreen P56 is operated via the line protected by fuse F41 of control unit B2 and relay T19 and fuse F20, located in engine compartment junction unit B1. The coil for relay T11 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT/A) and is energized by an earth signal coming from the Body Computer M1 - pin 6 of connector F; this signal is sent on the basis of the previously illustrated control logic and in the presence of the heated rear windscreen engagement command or through the MAX-DEF function coming via the CAN from the climate control system control unit M70. The engagement of the demisting heating coils for the door mirrors P60 and P61 is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66 and passenger door M67 connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1. Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of under-dashboard control unit B2. On the basis of the complex control logic illustrated previously, the engagement command for the demisting is sent via the CAN to the two door control units as well; these control the heating coils located in mirrors P60 and P61; the signal comes from pins 7 and 9 of connector E of M66 and M67.

DESCRIPTION The door mirrors can be electrically adjusted in two directions using a joystick control located in the door controls on the driver's side: a selection cursor makes it possible to choose either the left or the right mirror. The button controls two electrical motors located in each of the two mirrors: one motor allows the rotation of the mirror on the horizontal axis, another on the vertical axis. Another button controls the folding back of the mirrors if required (for example when trying to get through a narrow space). On the HIGH version, in addition to moving the door mirrors manually, it is possible to memorize and later on recall 3 positions defined in relation to the position of the driver's seat; the passenger side rear view mirror is also positioned automatically when reverse gear is engaged. This entire complex logic is managed by the driver's seat control unit which converses with the Body Computer via the CAN See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS The interior rear view mirror is electrochrome type: i.e. it contains an electronic device which controls the automatic anti-glare function. The automatic antiglare function is disabled when reverse is engaged. The circuit is protected by a fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard and is operated by the door control units in accordance with the control logic transmitted by the Body Computer via the CAN. The interior rear view mirror power supply circuit is protected by a fuse in the under-dashboard control unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The motors for the exterior rear view mirrors in P60 and P61 are operated by the driver's door control unit M66 and the passenger door control unit M67, connected to one another via the CAN line and to the Body Computer M1 and to the driver's seat movement and memory control unit H66. See E3076 ELECTRICALLY-ADJUSTABLE SEATS The two mirrors contain a potentiometer for each motor which detects the position and sends a feedback signal to the control unit to pins 10 and 11 of connector E of M66 and M67. (pins 15 and 17 of connector E provide a power supply and earth for the potentiometers). Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 . The controls on the driver's door H44 include the joystick and control switch for the exterior rear view mirrors: - selection of the right/left mirror: signal to pin 30 of connector A of M66, - vertical movement: signal to pin 28 of connector A of M66, - horizontal movement: signal to pin 29 of connector A of M66, - mirror folding: signal to pin 20 of connector B of M66. On the basis of the requests set whilst driving or on the basis of values memorized, the control units M66 and M67 control the motors for mirrors P60 and P61 from pin 4 of connector E (joint) and pins 3 and 5 (horizontal and vertical movement respectively). The folding motors are controlled from pins 1 and 8 of connector E of M66 and M67. Electrochrome mirror P65 supplies an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) - from pin 23 of connector D - from a line protected by fuse F32 of under-dashboard control unit B2. The switch for the reversing lights I20 receives a supply controlled by the ignition (INT) from the fuse line F35 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. When reverse is engaged, the switch closes to send a control signal to mirror P65 through control unit B2 - from pin 8 of connector D.

DESCRIPTION The simultaneous operation of the door locks takes place via: - TEG the remote control; - the locking/unlocking button in the centre console. The TEG remote has 3 buttons which allow the operation of the central locking system: a button for unlocking the doors, one for locking the vehicle and one for releasing the boot See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING The door unlocking/locking management strategy is carried out by the door control unit which controls the effective state of the locks through the signals arriving from the switches in the actual locks and the emergency key pawl (driver's door only) in this way the "locking" command is only carried out with all the doors properly shut and the locks unlocked; conversely, the "unlocking" command is only carried out with the locks locked. The fuel flap is also locked/unlocked at the same time as the doors, controlled by the same driver's door logic. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING The locks have an additional motor that carries out the dead lock function which allows the interior door opening handles to be mechanically disconnected so that it is no longer possible to open the door from the inside (for example, after having broken the glass in a theft attempt); the dead lock function also inhibits the operation of the door locking/unlocking buttons in the dashboard. The dead lock function is switched on at the time the doors are locked or by pressing the remote control twice. An LED next to the two above mentioned controls makes the following signals: - locking of the locks: the LED lights up for 3 seconds. If some of the doors or the boot are not properly shut at the time when the locks are locked, the LED flashes at 3 Hz for 3 seconds; - dead lock activation: the LED flashes twice for 0.5 seconds; - unlocking the locks: the LED goes out. The instrument panel acquires the door status signal via the CAN and lights up the "doors open" warning light and, at the same time, the information is shown on the display; in addition, if one of the doors or the boot or the bonnet is open and the speed of the vehicle exceeds around 4 km/h, an acoustic warning is also emitted. It is possible, using the special setup in the instrument panel, to select whether to unlock all the doors or only the driver's front door, whilst all the other doors and the boot remain locked. It is possible to enable/disable the locking of the doors above a certain speed threshold (20 km/h) using the special setup in the instrument panel: in this case the Body Computer implements the locking of the doors when this threshold is exceeded. When the speed returns below this level, the doors and the boot remain locked; later on, when one of the doors is opened, the function is re-enabled and, if the threshold is exceeded, the doors are locked once again. The boot unlocking operating mode can be selected still using the special setup in the instrument panel: - assisted boot unlocking: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes; - indepedent boot unlocking: the boot is locked when the doors are locked, whilst it can be unlocked independently of the unlocking of the doors. See E3045 BOOT AND FUEL FLAP OPENING The doors are automatically unlocked if the inertia switch is operated: the instrument panel receives a signal from the switch, lights up the appropriate warning light and notifies the Body Computer via the CAN. The central locking circuit is protected by two specific fuses - one for the front doors and one for the rear doors - located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The door locking/unlocking function is controlled by the control units for the driver's door M66, passenger side M67, all connected via the CAN line to one another and to the Body Computer M1. Control units M66 and M67 receive a supply - at pin 11 of connector D - from the line protected by fuse F32 of underfacia control unit B2 . Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and of M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 receive the following input: - the "locking" signals from the knobs, at pin 23 of connector B of M66 and M67; - door open signals at pin 35 of connector A of M66 and M67; - the locking/unlocking signals from the emergency key pawl, at pins 24 and 25 of connector B of M66; - the negative signal from the locking/unlocking button, located in the controls on the tunnel H35, at pin 34 of connector A of M66. According to the control logic illustrated, the control units M66 and M67 control the geared motors for the front door locks: the joint power supply for the motors is sent from pin 6 of connector D; the locking/unlocking motors (B/S) are operated from pin 4 of connector D; the dead lock motors (DL) for locks N50 and N51 are operated from pin 3 of connector D. The signalling LED E40 is lit up by a signal from pin 8 of connector C of M66, whilst a reference earth is sent from pin 6. The activation of the inertia switch I50 is indicated at pin 17 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 : this signal, as described previously, causes the opening of the doors.
