DESCRIPTION The boot opening geared motor is operated by: - the special button in the central console; - the remote control (TEG). Operation through the remote control takes place in two ways. - indepedently of the doors: there is a special button on the remote control that allows the boot only to be "unlocked": the boot is released and lifts up slightly. The operation is signalled by the direction indicators flashing twice; when it is closed again the boot returns to the state prior to opening. - together and at the same time as the unlocking of the doors: the tailgate is considered as a fifth door to all intents and purposes: for the control logic. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING One of the two modes described above can be selected using a special setup in the instrument panel. The boot opening function via the button in the courtesy light is disabled (the boot does not open) if the speed of the vehicle is above 10 km/h. The fuel flap is managed directly by the driver's door node and is therefore connected to the locked/unlocked status of the driver's door. The boot opening circuit is protected by a specific fuse, located in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The "boot open" signal is sent by the switch H33 to pin 35 of connector E of the Body Computer M1. According to the control logic illustrated, the Body Computer M1 implements the boot release positive control function from pin 11 of connector F - via the line supplied by fuse F38 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2, pin 18 of connector D - controlling the operation of the boot lock geared motor N57. The boot unlocking function, inside the Body Computer M1 pin 1 of connector F also has a dedicated earth connection: pin 20 of connector F. The "boot not properly shut" signal is sent from the switch located in N57 to pin 24 of connector E. the contact in question signals the "boot not properly shut" condition; the switch is fitted with another contact that signals the "boot open" condition, a contact used by the boot light function See E2520 GLOVE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - LUGGAGE COMPARTMENT LIGHT - SUN VISOR LIGHT The fuel flap opening motor N58 is operated by the same control logic as the driver's front door lock, from pins 1 and 2 of connector D of M66. See E3040 CENTRAL LOCKING Control unit M66 is supplied at pin 11 of connector D - by a line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2 . Pin 7 of connector D of M086 is earthed.

DESCRIPTION The electric windows for the front doors are operated through the switches on the driver's door (both windows) and the passenger side (passenger side only). The control units in the door control the operation of the driver's and passenger side electric window motors which are operated both manually and automatically depending on the version. Automatic operation takes place as follows: - if the button is pressed is between 60 and 300 milliseconds, operation is manual: the glass goes up/down only with the key pressed; - f the key is pressed for longer than 300 milliseconds, operation is automatic: even if the button is released, the glass continues to move up/down until the end of travel position is reached or until the intervention of the anti-crush safety system (if fitted); - pressing the button again whilst the window is moving stops it in the position it is in; - if the button is pressed for less than 60 milliseconds, this is ignored (it is treated as an accidental knock). When the doors are opened (whether with key-on or key-off status), the door nodes implement the short drop function to prevent interference between windows and roof. The short drop position is set at 10 mm from the window full closure position. In detail: if the glass is rising when the door is opened, the window opens to the short drop position and not to the full closure position. If the position of one or both of the window glasses is already at the level of the short drop position, no automatic movement takes place. Each control unit in the door also manages the anti-crush safety function: it acquires information concerning the possible presence of an obstacle whilst the glass is closing: two Hall effect sensors are built into the motor: under these circumstances the control unit immediately intercepts the travel of the glass and reverses it until it is in the bottom end of travel position. The correct operation of the anti-crush sensor is controlled by the control unit check function: in the case of a failure this information is sent via the CAN to the instrument panel to show the information on the display. In addition, if a fault is detected, the control unit inhibits the automatic raising operation only allowing it in steps of 500 ms each time the button is pressed. In this case the system must be initialized once again following the instructions in See descriptions 7005 PASSENGER COMPARTMENT FRONT SIDE DOORS The windows are automatically opened or closed through the special prolonged (more than 2 seconds) command sent by the TEG remote control button. The circuit is protected by two special fuses in the boot control unit. The driver's door control unit acquires both the driver's front door and passenger side front door commands; it manages the movement of the driver's window directly and sends the relevant movement commands for the passenger side window via the CAN to the passenger door control unit which manages the passenger side window directly.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The two control units for driver side door M66 and passenger side door M67 are supplied - by the window function - at pin 8 of connector D via two lines protected by fuses F78 and F80 of the boot compartment fuse box B45. Pin 19 connector B and 7 of connector D of M66 and M67 are earthed. Control units M66 and M67 are connected via a CAN line to one another and to Body Computer M1. Unit H44 contains the driver and passenger side window controls:: dedicated analogue signals are sent to pins 31 and 32 of connector A of M66 (pin 33 supplies a reference earth).. Similarly, the control at the passenger front door H50 sends a special analogue signal to the control unit M67 pin 32 (pin 33 provides the reference earth). Control unit M66 operates the motor N60 (driver's side) directly - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - and via control unit M67 - pins 9 and 10 of connector D - motor N61 (passenger side). Pins 2 and 5 of connector C of M66 and M67 receive signals from the anticrush sensors located in motor N60 or N61; pins 11 and 10 of connector B of M66 and M67 supply a power supply and reference earth to the sensors. The two control units are connected to the instrument panel E50 via the CAN line to manage the signal if there is a failure in the anti-crush safety sensors.

DESCRIPTION The fixed glass sunblind consists of 2 panels sliding lengthways that stow away out of sight in a compartment in the rear part of the roof in an area covered by the roof panel. The sunblind extends so far that it completely obscures the glass bonded on the roof panel and fits to the roof lining. The control button is located in the front courtesy light unit. The panels are closed and opened by operating the pushbutton. The sunblind panels may be moved only with the key on and they are also equipped with an antipinch system managed by the electronic control unit and active during the panel closure stage. The function is active during the movement and throughout its travel. When the panel meets an obstacle on the front side of the sunblind panel, the direction of motion is reversed. The circuit is controlled by the services relay and protected by a specific fuse, both located in the junction unit under the dashboard: there is a power supply both with the TEG inserted (ON) and not inserted (OFF); during the starting stage this relay is temporarily deactivated whilst with the TEG not inserted (OFF) the Body Computer keeps the relay activated for 3 minutes but deactivates it 30 seconds after one of the doors is opened.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The services relay T13, located in the junction unit under the dashboard B2, supplies the sun roof control motor M185 - pin 3 - via the line protected by fuse F46 of B2 by means of the strategy described above and controlled by the Body Computer M1. Pin 6 of M185 receives an ignition-operated power supply (INT) from a line protected by fuse F49 in under-dashboard control unit B2. Pins 1 and 2 of M185 are earthed, while pins 5 and 10 receive opening and closure signals from switches on courtesy light G10.

DESCRIPTION There is a standard type current socket on the tunnel console next to the handbrake which can be used for the cigar lighter or for connecting instruments or equipment operating on 12 V. The cigar lighter heater coil can be located in the front socket in the console; simply press the knob to operate it: after a few seconds it will come out automatically, ready for use. The ring around the socket lights up when the side lights are on. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS The socket is equipped with a thermal protection device: this protection cuts off the power supply if devices that absorb a lot of energy are connected. The circuit for the two current sockets in the console is protected by a specific fuse and controlled by the ignition-operated exclusion relay located in the junction unit under the dashboard. To prevent the battery from being run down, these sockets are ignition-operated (INT/A).
FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The current socket / cigar lighter P050 receives an ignition-operated supply from relay T12 protected by fuse F44 both housed in the junction unit under the dashboard B2.

DESCRIPTION The front seats are available, on request, with a special heating system (comprising two heating elements located in the cushion and the backrest): this allows the seat to be heated to overcome the discomfort of cold passenger compartments in very harsh climates, e.g. when the car is left in the open for long periods in winter. The heating device located in each seat consists of two resistors activated by a controls located on the outside of each seat: there is a ring nut through which the function is switched on/off and the heating is adjusted to 3 different settings (0 = seat heating switched off). Once a certain temperature has been reached the heating stops automatically thanks to a thermal contact inside the actual device. A special LED in the actual switches indicates that the resistances are switched on. The seat heating can only be activated with the ignition on (INT/A). The seat heating circuit is controlled by a special relay and protected by two specific fuses located in the fuse box in the boot.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The seat heating power supply arrives via the relay T21 located in the fuse box in the boot B45; this is energized by the ignition-controlled line (INT/A) which arrives directly from the steering lock node M89; fuses F57 and F67, located in B45, protect the supply circuit for the two seats: the power supply for the two heaters O40 and O41 takes place via the control units M170 and M110 which receive commands from the switches I65 and I66. The switches are lit up with the ignition on (INT) by the line for fuse F49 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats. A multifunction control on each seat includes: - adjustment of the backrest angle; - lengthwise adjustment of the seat; - front and rear height adjustment of the seat (rocker). The system also makes it possible to memorize and recall three different positions for the driver's seat (and the door mirrors): after the position of the seat and the door mirrors has been adjusted, pressing one of the buttons ("1", "2" or "3") for a few seconds memorizes the position; this can only take place with the TEG inserted (ON). To recall a previously memorized position briefly press the relevant button. When a new seat position is memorized any previously memorized settings on this button are automatically cancelled The seats are also equipped with the easy entry function which facilitates access to the rear seats when the backrest is tilted forwards: a special switch detects the operation of the lever that folds the backrest over and controls the automatic movement of the seat forwards until it is in the front end of travel position. Once the backrest is released, the seat return to its previous position. The device is also fitted with an anti-panic function which interrupts the automatic movement described above if one of the seat control buttons is activated. The device also has an anti-crush safety function. whilst the seat is returning into position moving backwards, if an obstacle is detected in the seat's path, the movement stops and the seat is moved about 5 cm forwards to release the obstacle. Seat position memorization does not include heating start up See E3075 HEATED SEATS The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors. The seat movement can only be activated with the ignition on (INT). The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The driver's seat H66 and passenger seat H67 control units control the entire system. The control knobs and buttons for the various functions are built into the control units themselves. The power supply to H66 and H67 - to pin 9 of connector A - passes through fuses F56 and F60, located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45. Pin 5 of connector A and 8 of connector B of H66 and H67 are earthed. Pins 5 and 6 of connector B of H66 and H67 are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN. The two control units N66 and H67 control the various motors that move the seats in accordance with the logic described above: - adjustment of the backrest angle: motor N132 or N135 controlled; - lengthwise adjustment (sliding) of the seat: motor N127 or N130 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - front section: motor N125 or N128 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - rear section (rocker): motor N126 or N129 controlled; - easy entry function activated after the intervention of switch I106 or I107.

DESCRIPTION The LOW trim level of the vehicle is fitted with manually adjusted front seats, with the exception of the backrest angle adjustment which is electrical. A special switch, located on the actual seat. adjusts the "raising" and "lowering" of the backrest if operated in the two different positions. The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors. The seat movement can only be activated with the ignition on (INT). The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box. A relay on each seat controls the motors.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The driver's seat control switch H66 and the passenger seat control switch H67 control the angle of the backrest by means of two relays J139 and J140. The power supply for the two relays J139 and J140 arrives via fuses F56 and F60 located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45. The coils for relays J139 and J140 receive a power supply from the ignition-operated line (INT) protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2 When the switches H66 and H67 are operated in both directions they send a power supply and earth alternately to the two motors M132 and N135 which rotate in two opposite directions adjusting the angle of the seat.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle can be fitted with electrically adjustable front seats. A multifunction control on each seat includes: - adjustment of the backrest angle; - lengthwise adjustment of the seat; - front and rear height adjustment of the seat (rocker). The system also makes it possible to memorize and recall three different positions for the driver's seat (and the door mirrors): after the position of the seat and the door mirrors has been adjusted, pressing one of the buttons ("1", "2" or "3") for a few seconds memorizes the position; this can only take place with the TEG inserted (ON). To recall a previously memorized position briefly press the relevant button. When a new seat position is memorized any previously memorized settings on this button are automatically cancelled The seats are also equipped with the easy entry function which facilitates access to the rear seats when the backrest is tilted forwards: a special switch detects the operation of the lever that folds the backrest over and controls the automatic movement of the seat forwards until it is in the front end of travel position. Once the backrest is released, the seat return to its previous position. The device is also fitted with an anti-panic function which interrupts the automatic movement described above if one of the seat control buttons is activated. The device also has an anti-crush safety function. whilst the seat is returning into position moving backwards, if an obstacle is detected in the seat's path, the movement stops and the seat is moved about 5 cm forwards to release the obstacle. Seat position memorization does not include heating start up See E3075 HEATED SEATS The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors. The seat movement can only be activated with the ignition on (INT). The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The driver's seat H66 and passenger seat H67 control units control the entire system. The control knobs and buttons for the various functions are built into the control units themselves. The power supply to H66 and H67 - to pin 9 of connector A - passes through fuses F56 and F60, located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45. Pin 5 of connector A and 8 of connector B of H66 and H67 are earthed. Pins 5 and 6 of connector B of H66 and H67 are connected to the Body Computer M1 via the CAN. The two control units N66 and H67 control the various motors that move the seats in accordance with the logic described above: - adjustment of the backrest angle: motor N132 or N135 controlled; - lengthwise adjustment (sliding) of the seat: motor N127 or N130 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - front section: motor N125 or N128 controlled; - height adjustment of the cushion - rear section (rocker): motor N126 or N129 controlled; - easy entry function activated after the intervention of switch I106 or I107.

DESCRIPTION The LOW trim level of the vehicle is fitted with manually adjusted front seats, with the exception of the backrest angle adjustment which is electrical. A special switch, located on the actual seat. adjusts the "raising" and "lowering" of the backrest if operated in the two different positions. The seat is also equipped with a lumbar adjustment knob that makes it possible to improve comfort by altering the backrest support: this adjustment is always mechanical and not controlled by electric motors. The seat movement can only be activated with the ignition on (INT). The seat moving circuit is protected by two specific fuses located in the luggage compartment fuse box. A relay on each seat controls the motors.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The driver's seat control switch H66 and the passenger seat control switch H67 control the angle of the backrest by means of two relays J139 and J140. The power supply for the two relays J139 and J140 arrives via fuses F56 and F60 located in the luggage compartment fuse box B45. The coils for relays J139 and J140 receive a power supply from the ignition-operated line (INT) protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2 When the switches H66 and H67 are operated in both directions they send a power supply and earth alternately to the two motors M132 and N135 which rotate in two opposite directions adjusting the angle of the seat.

DESCRIPTION The adjustment of the headlamp light beam according to the load is carried out by means of a special device (located inside the front light cluster) which tilts it appropriately, lowering the light beam if the vehicle is heavily laden and raising it if the load lessens. A special wheel, located in the controls to the left of the steering wheel, allows the adjustment of the headlamps in 4 vertical positions from 0 to 3: - position 0: one or two persons in the front seats, full fuel tank, fully equipped (vehicle in running order); - position 1: five persons; - position 2: five persons with full luggage compartment (about 50 kg); - position 3: driver and 300 kg load, all stowed in the luggage compartment (full load); The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The relay which controls the engagement of the dipped headlamps also supplies the adjustment motors inside the headlamps; this relay for switching the dipped headlamps on is managed by the Body Computer: the relay energizing is activated by TEG inserted (INT) enablement signals and by the steering column switch unit dipped headlamps control.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The dipped headlamps activation (earth) signal - and any AUTO function - is sent to pin 2 of connector I and to pin 28 of connector G of the Body Computer M1 from the steering column switch unit H5 See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to the relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: the latter supplies the dipped headlamps - pin 2 for the lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right); at the same time it provides the enablement for the adjustment motors - pin 6 for lamps F10 (left) and F11 (right); Each circuit is protected by a fuse for the junction unit B2: F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. The control for the headlamp adjustment, located in the unit to the left of the steering wheel H90, also receives the enablement supply - pin 5 of connector A, whilst a control signal produced by the adjustment potentiometer - pin 15 of connector B is sent; this control signal "passes through" the junction unit under the dashboard B and activates the adjustment motors built into the headlamps - pin 7 for the (left) lamps F10 and F11 (right).

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is fitted with two GAS DISCHARGE headlamps. The electronics in each of the two headlamps switches the gas discharge bulbs on and off at the times defined by the software and in accordance with international legislation. The system for each lamp comprises an igniter located at the base of the bulb and a ballast located in the lower part of the lamp. The left lamp is the master control unit whilst the right one carries out a slave role. The master acquires the command for the dipped headlamps, the vehicle speed and from the potentiometers located on the wheel axles. Depending on the inputs, the control unit controls the relevant adjustment motor, located in the headlamps, directly and tilts it as appropriate. For more details See descriptions 5540 EXTERIOR LIGHTING on versions with gas discharge headlamps, the light beam is adjusted automatically and there is no activation of the selector in the panel on the left side. The device is enabled only with the dipped beams on. The electronics for the two headlamps receive a supply from a fuse which protects other ignition-controlled power supplies.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Both electronic systems inside the headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right) are supplied - pin 9 - from the INT line protected by fuse F37 of the junction unit B2. Pins 12 of the two control units are connected to one another by means of a special serial line, whilst the speedometer signal from the Body Computer M1 (pin 28 of connector B) reaches pin 10 of the control unit located in the headlamp F10. Pins 11 of the two headlamps are connected to the diagnostic K line See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR The Body Computer M1 controls the supply for the dipped headlamps sending an earth signal to the relay T1 in the junction unit under the dashboard B2 from pin 8 of connector F of M1 which energizes relay T1: this supplies the low beams of headlamps F10 (left) and F11 (right). Each circuit is protected by a fuse for the junction unit B2: F13 for the left headlamp and F12 for the right. The headlamp alignment function, managed by the connection F10B, is incorporated in the headlamp F10: the two sensors (potentiometers) that measure the geometry at the front K1 and at the rear K2 are connected; on the basis of these signals, the headlamp electronics automatically adjust the light beam by means of a special motor (the motor for the left headlamp is regulated directly, whilst the one for the right headlamp is adjusted via the serial line between F10 and F11).

DESCRIPTION The "Parking Assistance" system supplies the driver with information on distance when approaching obstacles behind the vehicle thereby providing help with parking manoeuvres and identifying obstacles that are outside the field of vision. The information concerning the presence or distance of the obstacle is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic and visual signals: - the frequency of the acoustic impulse warnings depends on the distance of the obstacle from the bumper. - the display in the instrument panel shows the areas around the vehicle which start flashing if the system detects that the vehicle is getting close to an obstacle. The system is activated if the following conditions are present simultaneously: - Key ON (TEG inserted) - reverse gear engaged. When the system is activated the buzzer sounds as a warning. The system is deactivated by disengaging reverse gear. The distance measurement only takes place when the system is activated, whilst only the control unit is operational in the inactive state. An electronic control unit activates and controls the operation of the sensors located in the rear bumper, processes the signals received and operates the buzzer, located under the centre console. The sensors use ultrasound technology and act as intelligent transmitters/receivers with triangulation technology: allowing improved detection in critical situations or in the presence of small obstacles. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer receives an echo which is converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit. The signalling of the distance of the obstacle is achieved through sound and visual signals: - the sound from the buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle: the pause between the sounds is directly proportional to the distance from the obstacle, whilst a continuous sound indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away; - the instrument panel display with the system activated shows the various areas around the vehicle. The various areas are, in the various cases, either off, flashing or on constantly. For more details and information on the operation of the system, See descriptions 5580H PARKING OBSTACLE DETECTION DEVICE The control unit is equipped with an autodiagnostic function: when switched on the control unit carries out an initial test on the sensors which are then continuously subject to fault diagnosis during the operation of the system. A fault in only one sensor inhibits the operation of the entire system which is deactivated. Any faults/errors are signalled in the instrument panel by the relevant warning light coming on and the message in the display. The system is supplied by the circuit protected by a specific fuse in the junction unit under the dashboard.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The parking sensor control unit M84 receives a supply at pin 1 of connector A from the ignition-controlled INT line protected by fuse F49 of junction unit B2; pin 8 of connector A is earthed. The control unit is connected, via pins 7 and 4 of connector A and the CAN, to all the other nodes in the same network, for example receiving the information that reverse gear is engaged. The commands for the display are sent to the instrument panel via the CAN. The buzzer P44 is connected to pins 2 and 10 of connector A. The four front parking sensors K97 are connected to connector C of the control unit M84: pin 1 provides the reference earth, pin 6 the power supply, pins 5, 3, 2 and 4 are connected to sensors K97E, K97F, K97G and K97H, respectively.

DESCRIPTION The Spider version is equipped with an electrohyraulic system for the automated movement of the hood which ensures that the driver can open and close the hood quickly and safely without leaving their seat. The activation of the hood takes place by pressing the dedicated button located on the centre tunnel. The hood opening/closing cycle takes around 25 seconds. The manoeuvre is reproduced in the control panel display which illustrates the movement of the hood diagramatically. The completion of the manoeuvre is siganlled by a buzzer and a message appearing in the display. See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS An electronic control unit controls the entire electrohydraulic system which carries out the hood automatic opening/closing cycle. Numerous sensors are located in the hood and hood cover locks and in the hood activating cylinders. Thanks to the information received from the sensors, the control unit controls the hydraulic system for the cylinders for the hood, the arch, the front locks and the hood cover unlocking/locking the locks for the hood and the hood cover. The "Boot Hood Node" control unit is located in the passenger compartment on the left side under the mat in the hood compartment and it converses through the vehicle CAN with the other network nodes. The "Boot Hood Node (NVB-C)" supervises the following functions: input from the hodd activating button; hydraulic movement control (Hall effect sensors); flap movement control; alarm conditions check (e.g. vehicle speed, system internal errors, etc.) providing a warning via the special warning light and messages in the instrument panel interaction with other control units for the optimum management of the system: door nodes (middle drop), climate control node (heated rear windscreen), Body Computer, BOSE system (hood open or closed); auto-diagnostic functions. The control unit also detects possible errors, that may be temporary (which involve a break in the operating cycle, which can then be restored) or permanent (which require a repair operation to the hood system). There is a manual emergency procedure which allows the hood to be closed. Only move the hood with the vehicle stationary because the hood should not be opened/closed whilst the vehicle is moving: if there has been an accidental attempt to activate the hood whilst the vehicle is moving, this manoeuvre will be automatically prevented. For more details: See descriptions 7030H AUTOMATICALLY OPERATED HOOD The hood activating circuit is protected by two special fuses in the boot control unit.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The hood control unit M187 receives a power supply - at pins 2 and 4 of connector B - via two lines protected by fuses F62 and F63 located in the fuse box in the boot B45. Pins 1 and 3 of connector B of M187 are earthed. The hood control unit M187 is connected via the CAN line to the Body Computer M1 and to the other network nodes - pins 1 and 9 of the connector It is connected, in particular, to the instrument panel E50, signalling alarm conditions and errors or faults detected by means of the dedicated warning light The hood control unit M187 receives signals from different sensors thereby keeping the movements of the hood and the hood cover under control. The hood opening/closing control H130 sends two earth signals to pins 11 and 3 of connector A of M187 to indicate the hood opening and closing request respectively. The Hall effect sensors in the hood closing lock K197 right side and K198 left side, send two signals to indicate the hood "resting" (end of movement travel), pins 12-14 of connector a of M187 and the correct closure of the hood, pins 4-6 of connector A of M187. Pin 13 of connector A provides a power supply for the Hall effect sensors. The hood arch position Hall effect sensor K199, receiving a power supply from the control unit from pin 15 of connector D of M187, sends three signals to indicat that the arch is raised, in the intermediate position or lowered to pins 7, 1 and 3 respectively of connector D of M187. The hood folded Hall effect sensor K200, receiving a power supply from the control unit from pin 15 of connector D of M187, sends a signal to pin 9 of connector D of M187. The hood cover position Hall effect sensor K203, receiving a power supply from the control unit from pin 16 of connector D of M187, sends two signals to indicate the hood cover reasing - to pin 11 of connector C of M187 - and the hood cover raised - to pin 8 of connector D of M18. The Hall effect sensors in the two hood cover locks K201 left and K202 right, receive a power supply form the control unit from pin 14 of connector D of M187 and send two signals to pins 4 and 2 respectively of connector D of M187. The control unit M187 controls the opening of the hood flaps via two motors N190 left and N191 right, controlled by pins 2-13 and 1-12 of connector C of M187; a potentiometer "returns" the position of the flaps to the control unit, to pins 17 and 6 respectively of connector C of M187, whilst a power supply and reference earth are sent from pins 5-18 and 7-16. Lastly, the control unit M187 controls the electrohydraulic unit N192 which moves the hood via three solenoid valves, whilst a pump provides the necessary pressure for the hydraulic circuit: the pump is controlled by pins 1 and 2 of connector E of M187, the valves by pins 2-8, 3-9 and 4-10 of connector F of M187. An NTC sensor is connected to pins 1-7 of connector F of M187 which controls the temperature of the hydraulic pump. The control unit M187 is also connected - from pin 16 of connector A - to the BOSE amplifier P70, pin 24, which modifies the frequency response to compensate for losses that occur when the hood is open. For more details See E3510 RADIO

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with a radio system comprising: - radio; - front speakers (woofers in the doors and tweeters in the dashboard); - rear speakers located in the side panels; - cables connecting the radio with the speakers; - the aerial system: On the Brera version, the aerial system comprises an AM and FM amplifier where the AM signal arrives from the screen-printing in the right rear side window via a unipolar cable whilst the FM signal arrives from the heated rear windscreen filaments via a coaxial cable with its shield earthed at the tailgate right near the connection to the screen-printing. The cable that carries the signal to the radio module comes from the AM/FM amplifier. On the Spider version, the AM/FM stylus aerial is located behind the left wing. A sophisticated HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier can also be fitted. The radio is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The radio is equipped with an anti-theft system through the connection of the radio at the CAN with the Body Computer; it also manages the volume control linked to the vehicle speed: the volume increases and decreases in relation to the speed of the vehicle: this information reaches the radio node via the CAN. Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these make it possible to replicate some of the commands which are acquired in the same way by the actual radio. It is also possible to fit a multi-polar cable connecting the radio to a CD player located in the boot, on the right hand side. See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (4 of connector A) from the battery via the line of fuse F23 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 . Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which radio P20 is connected to Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. Radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via clock spring D47. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The following cables with signals for the speakers leave connector B of P20: - pins 5 and 6 to left front speakers P35 and P45 (P36 for right hand drive versions); - pins 3 and 4 to right front speakers P36 and P46 (P35 for right hand drive versions); - pins 7 and 8 to left rear speaker P30; - pins 1 and 2 to right rear speaker P31; Aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75. This cable is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

DESCRIPTION A sophisticated HIFI system with special HIFI speakers and an outside amplifier is available on request. The system has been developed ad hoc for the vehicle: the acoustic properties of the passenger compartment have been carefully studied so that the amplifier and the speakers are ideally suited to the vehicle: optimum listening is available in any part of the passenger compartment. Unlike the system fitted as standard, this system offers: - special speakers at front and rear, which are midwoofers with separate tweeters; - rear subwoofer speaker located in the luggage compartment; - high power amplifier located in the luggage compartment. The other components (radio, aerial, etc.) are the same as for the standard system. For more details See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 4 and 2 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F23 of engine compartment junction unit B1. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which radio P20 is connected to Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. Radio P20 is connected, via the CAN, to the radio controls on the steering wheel, via clock spring D47. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES Amplifier P70 receives a direct supply from the battery - at pin 1 - via the line for fuse F54 of the fuse box casing in boot B45; pin 2 of amplifier P70 is earthed. Pin 6 of P70 is connected via a line to radio P20 - pin 6 of connector C - which supplies a positive signal to enable the amplifier to be switched on. The cables with signals for the speakers leave from connector B of P20; these signals are sent to the BOSE amplifier P70 which controls the actual speakers: - pins 5 and 6 of P20 to pins 7 and 19 of P70 and to the left front speakers P35 (P36 for right hand drive versions) and P45 - pins 31 and 32 of P70; - pins 3 and 4 of P20 to pins 8 and 20 of P70 and to the right front speakers P36 (P35 for right hand drive versions) and P46 - pins 26 and 27 of P70; - pins 7 and 8 of P20 to pins 9 and 21 of P70 and to left rear speaker P30 - pins 4 and 16 of P70; - pins 1 and 2 of P20 to pins 10 and 22 of P70 and to right rear speaker P31 - pins 5 and 37 of P70. The other signals leaving the BOSE amplifier P70 control the specific speakers: - centerfill P32 - pins 3 and 15 of P70; - subwoofer P49 - pins 11, 12 and 25 of P70; the subwoofer P49 is also supplied via the line for fuse F61 of the fuse box casing in the boot B45. Aerial P25 is connected to the radio by means of the special coaxial cable. A connection lead runs from connector E of P20 to CD player P75. This cable is divided into two sections: one under the dashboard and one under the passenger compartment lining (coupling D96).

DESCRIPTION In the specification with built in CONNECT NAV + radio-phone-navigation system, the phone (GSM module and SIM-CARD reader) is built into the system. The system includes: - GSM module and SIM-CARD reader integrated in the radio-phone-navigation system; - hands free function via the radio speakers; - microphone located in the front courtesy light; - external GSM aerial. The integrated radio-telephone-navigation system is a node in the CAN network, via which it exchanges information with the Body Computer and the other electronic control units. The controls are shown on the integrated radio-telephone-navigation system display. Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these are used to send out radio and also phone commands. Other control buttons are located in the front courtesy light. The stylus aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: this aerial has two functions (GSM/GPS); as far as the telephone is concerned it is a GSM dual band reception aerial (GSM-ETACS at 900Hz and D.C.S. at 1800 Hz). On the Spider version, the GMS/GPS aerial is located on the inside of the hood cover. For more details on phone operation See descriptions 5580P CONNECT PANEL

DESCRIPTION The Blue&Me system allows mobile phones to be used safely inside the vehicle. Includes: - Bluetooth receiver; - voice recognition integrated unit including microphone - integral Text to Speech unit. - USB interface for Media Player. The control unit is also connected to radio controls on the steering wheel (two special keys for this function are provided in addition to the radio control keys). The entire operation of the system is also managed by voice commands, picked up by the microphone near the front courtesy light The alphanumeric display used is that of the control panel. See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS For more details on system operation See descriptions 5570 ACCESSORIES

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Bluetooth control unit M162 is supplied directly (pin 16 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of the under-dashboard control unit B2. Bluetooth control unit M162 receives an ignition-operated supply (INT) (pin 32 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 (F51 as of 04/07) of the under-dashboard control unit B2. Pin 15 of connector A of M162 is earthed. The CAN line through which Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to radio P20, to the controls on the steering wheel - via clock spring D47 - to Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes, reaches pins 14 and 30 of connector A. On the version without a USB Media Player interface, the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected directly to radio P20 - connector D - from pins 7, 23 and 25 of connector A, sending audio+. audio - and MUTE signals respectively, thus using the radio speakers for voice messages and hands-free communication. In the version with Media Player USB interface, the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to radio P20 - connector C - from pins 5, 22 and 21 of connector A with AUX left, AUX right and AUX earth signals. The Media Player USB socket P143 is connected to the Bluetooth control unit M162, to pins 3, 4, 19, 20 and 31 respectively, with signals: signal D+, reference earth, signal D-, 5V power supply and screening. The hands-free microphone located in the courtesy light G10 is connected to pins 8 and 24 of connector A of M162.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is available, on request, not equipped with a CONNECT NAV + system - it can be supplied with wiring for installing a mobile phone. The system includes: - connection for a mobile phone; - hands free function via the radio speakers; - external GSM aerial; - microphone located in the front courtesy light. The connection for the telephone, located at the base of the centre console, includes all the power supplies and signals needed for the operation of the telephone. The stylus aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: this is a dual band GSM aerial (GSM-ETACS at 900 Hz and DCS at 1800 Hz). The radio receives input audio signals from the telephone connection; the sound of the telephone always arrives at a fixed volume which can, however, be adjusted in the radio menu function. The operation of the telephone switches off the radio temporarily (MUTE function). The connection for the telephone has two power supplies - one direct one and one with the ignition key to MAR: the above two lines are protected by two fuses in the under-dashboard control unit; there is also a power supply with the side lights on to light up the telephone. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Connection D75 receives the direct supply - pin 9 - from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of under-dashboard control unit B2 (this power supply "passes through" Body Computer M1, pin 26 of connector H). It receives an ignition-controlled power supply (INT) - pin 7 - via the line for fuse F49 (F51 as of 04/07) of control unit B2. The power supply with the side lights on reaches pin 8 coming from the Body Computer M1, pin 18 of connector H: the telephone, if fitted, is lit up like the other controls See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS Pin 10 of connection D75 is earthed. Pins 4 and 3 of D75 provide the audio signal (+ and - respectively) for the radio P20 - pins 7 and 8 of connector D, which then controls the speakers. See E3510 RADIO Pin 1 of D75 is also connected to the radio P20, pin 9 of connector D (MUTE function). The hands free microphone located in the front courtesy light G10 - connector D - is connected to pins 5 and 6 of D75.

DESCRIPTION The instruments currently on board the vehicle in question are composed of the main control panel located inside the steering wheel and a central instrument console in the middle of the dashboard. The main panel contains a large reconfigurable matrix LCD. There is also a buzzer and a brightness sensor inside the instrument panel for the automatic adjustment (daytime/nightime) of the brightness of the instrument panel lights. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS The centre instrument console consists of: - fuel level gauge with reserve warning light - engine coolant temperature gauge with overheating warning light - engine oil temperature gauge with overheating warning light The instrument panel is a CAN node through which information is exchanged with the Body Computer and with the other electronic units. The centre module containing the three sets of instruments is not a B-CAN node, but is connected by means of a special serial line to the instrument panel node which sends the module all the signals necessary for the display of the required information. - Speedometer: the function of the speedometer includes displaying the vehicle speed in the instrument panel: this information comes from the ABS control unit, via the Body Computer. - Engine rpm: this function involves the display on the instrument panel of the engine rotation speed by means of the message sent via the CAN from the engine management control unit. - Milometer: the milometer function includes the display and memorizing of the total and trip mileage: the journey information is processed by the Body Computer by means of a counter; the special button in the panel to the side of the steering wheel zeroes the trip meter. - Fuel level: the Body Computer receives the signal from the sensor integrated in the pump assembly inside the fuel tank and processes it to guarantee suitable filtering/damping for the panel gauge, also managing the reserve warning light. - Engine oil level: the function signals the status of the engine oil level at starting (for about 3 seconds) in the display. The actual instrument panel operates a hot wire oil level sensor. If the oil level is below the minimum value, the message "minimum oil level" is also sent. - Engine coolant temperature gauge: is operated - via the instrument panel - by the special sensor on the engine. The maximum temperature warning light is controlled by a microprocessor when the value measured exceeds a certain limit. - Brake pad wear state: this function involves the specific warning light coming on: the Body Computer detects the brake pad wear status when braking (signal from the brake pedal) in a prolonged manner (occasional signals are ignored). - Handbrake applied: the warning light for the handbrake status is controlled by a specific switch; in addition, if a given speed level is exceeded in conjunction with this signal, a warning signal is activated: the signal is sent, via the CAN, from the Body Computer. - Insufficient brake fluid: this function involves the "insufficient brake fluid level" warning light in the instrument panel coming on with the signal sent by the Body Computer via the CAN. For more details See descriptions 5560 INSTRUMENTS The operation of the warning lights which do not come under any other functions is illustrated below: the other warning lights and displays are described and illustrated in the diagrams for the components to which they refer.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The ignition-operated power supply (INT) for the instrument panel E50 reaches pin 1 of connector A via the line for fuse F37 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; the direct power supply reaches pin 2 of connector A via the fuse line F53 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2; pin 7 of connector A is earthed (earth controlled by the Body Computer M1). The instrument panel E50 is connected from pins 3 and 4 of connector A with the Body Computer M1 and via the latter to the entire CAN: the signal reaches the electronic speedometer (from the ABS control unit M50) via the CAN: the same signal is replicated by pin 16 of M50 at pin 7 of connector A of the Body Computer M1. The electronic rev counter receives the engine rpm signal received from the engine management control unit M10 via the CAN. The km reset button for the trip meter, located in the left panel H90, sends an earth signal to pin 7 of connector C of E50. The fuel level gauge is controlled by means of signals coming from the level gauge located in the fuel pump assembly N40 - at pins 4 and 15 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 and from there via the CAN to the instrument panel E50. The brake pad wear warning light is controlled on the basis of the signal that reaches pin 23 of connector B of the Body Computer M1 from the sensors for K20 and K21. The insufficient brake fluid level/handbrake warning light is lit up by a signal from the handbrake switch I40 that reaches pin 14 of connector D of the Body Computer M1 or from the signal from the brake fluid level sensor K25 that reaches pin 18 of connector A of M1. All these signals are transferred via the CAN to the instrument panel E50. The engine oil level sensor, incorporated in the temperature and level sensor K52, receives a power supply from the panel E50 from pin 17 of connector B and relays the signal to pin 18. The engine oil temperature, incorporated in the temperature and level sensor K52 receives the reference earth from the panel E50 - pin 17 of connector D - and relays the signal to pin 18. The centre module E20 is connected by means of a special serial line - from pin 1 - to the instrument panel node E50 pin 1 of connector C; the protected power supply reaches pin 3 of E20, whilst the reference earth reaches pin 2. The dimmed power supply for the auxiliary instruments E20 leaves from pin 5 of connector C of E50. See E2535 CONTROL LIGHTS

DESCRIPTION The Blue&Me system, alongside the Bluetooth technology for using a mobile phone in the vehicle, is also available with a navigation system for reaching a destination speedily and safely. The driver is guided to the destination by voice messages and instructions on the instrument panel display. The navigator makes it possible to: - enter a new destination - navigate to a point of interest (which can be selected from a list of categories such as, for example, hotels, restaurants, airports, railway stations, etc.) - acquire journey information (arrival time, distance from the destination, vehicle position) - recover the last destinations memorized - set preference for the type of route to be followed such as, for example, motorway, toll roads, - simulate the route to a prearranged destination in advance. The GPS consists of an aerial that allows the vehicle to be GPS satellite-located: the aerial is connected to a receiver located in the integrated unit by means of a special shielded cable. The GSM aerial is connected to the GSM unit inside the control unit used for the connection of GPRS data for real time traffic services, navigation, etc. The stylus aerial is fitted at the rear of the roof: this aerial has two functions (GSM/GPS); as far as the telephone is concerned it is a GSM dual band reception aerial (GSM-ETACS at 900Hz and D.C.S. at 1800 Hz). On the Spider version, the GMS/GPS aerial is located on the inside of the hood cover. Vehicle position is identified by analysing GPS data together with speedometer and reverse gear signals received from the vehicle. The navigation maps are loaded onto the USB device connected to the USB port on the vehicle. The control unit that manages the entire system is a CAN node via which information is exchanged with the Body Computer, the instrument panel and the other electronic units (e.g. the navigation system downloads mileometer information, reverse engagement signal information etc. ). The control unit is also connected to radio controls on the steering wheel (two special keys for this function are provided in addition to the radio control keys). The entire operation of the system is also managed by voice commands, picked up by the microphone near the front courtesy light. There are three additional control buttons in the panel in front of the centre courtesy light: - NAV: launch of the Navigation Menu - display of incoming information with navigation activated - SOS: access to Roadside Assistance Services - Info: access to infomobility services For more details on system operation See descriptions 5580M ON-BOARD NAVIGATOR

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Bluetooth control unit M162 is supplied directly at pin 16 of connector A from the battery via the line for fuse F39 of under-dashboard control unit B2. Bluetooth control unit M162 receives an ignition-controlled power supply at pin 32 via the line for fuse F51 of under-dashboard control unit B2. Pin 15 of M162 is earthed. The CAN line through which the Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to the radio P20, the controls on the steering wheel - via the clock spring D47 - the Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes, reaches pins 14 and 30 of connector A. The Bluetooth control unit M162 is connected to the radio P20 - connector C - from pins 5, 22 and 21 with the AUX left, AUX right and AUX earth signals. The USB port P143 is connected to the Bluetooth control unit M162, to pins 3, 4, 19, 20 and 31 respectively, with signals: signal D+, reference earth, signal D-, 5V power supply and shielding. The hands-free microphone located in the courtesy light G10 - connector D - is connected to pins 8 and 24 of connector A of M162. The navigation controls, located next to the front courtesy light G10 - connector G - receive an ignition-controlled supply at pin 5 via the line for fuse F49 of under-dashboard control unit B2; pin 6 is earthed. The reference earth reaches pin 3 from control unit M162 - pin 11, whilst the analogue signal for the buttons pressed leaves pin 4 for pin 28 of M162.

DESCRIPTION A road map navigation system reveals the vehicle's position on a map (showing town streets and main roads/motorways) at every moment and pinpoints it on the CONNECT display. In this way the driver is guided step-by-step to the required destination, by means of voice messages and visual information. The system also provides additional information for reaching general services, namely: hotels, car parks, restaurants, chemists, service stations, hospitals, ALFA ROMEO service outlets, railway stations, airports etc. The navigation system uses GPS (Global Positioning System) satellite localisation technology and is fitted, when ordered, in the integrated radio-phone-navigation system known as CONNECT NAV +. The navigation CD-ROM drive is located in the unit. The aerial has two functions (GSM/GPS) for the operation of the telephone and for the operation of the navigator and it is installed on the roof or, on versions without a telephone, it only has a GPS function and is concealed in the roof trim. On the Spider version, the GMS/GPS aerial is located on the inside of the hood cover. Vehicle position is identified by analysing GPS data together with speedometer and reverse gear signals received from the vehicle. Some versions are equipped with a series of buttons on the steering wheel: these are used to send out radio and also phone commands. Other control buttons are located in the front courtesy light. For more details on phone operation See descriptions 5580P CONNECT PANEL

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Radio P20 is supplied directly (pin 7 of connector A) from the battery via the line for fuse F23 of engine compartment control unit B1. Radio P20 receives an ignition-operated (INT) power supply (pin 4 of connector A) via the line for fuse F49 (F51 as of 04/07) of under-dashboard control unit B2. Pin 8 of connector A is earthed. Pins 1 and 3 of connector A receive the CAN line by which radio P20 is connected to Body Computer M1 and the other system nodes. The control buttons located on the front courtesy light G10 - connector G - are connected to pins 10 and 12 of connector D of P20.

DESCRIPTION The ignition and recharging circuit comprises the battery, starter motor and alternator. The starter motor consists of a d.c. motor supplied by the battery and an excitation electromagnet. This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key, whereby the traditional ignition key has been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G.", (Transmitter for Entry and Go), combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. The vehicle is not started by inserting the key and turning it in the ignition switch (which is not present), but by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and operating the START/STOP button. See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING Pressing the START button supplies the motor windings producing electromagnetic forces that rotate the actual motor pinion. This simultaneously activates the electromagnet that operates the mechanism, which causes the pinion to mesh with the flywheel ring gear and thus turn the crankshaft. The alternator recharges the battery during normal engine rotation. The alternator shaft (rotor) is turned by the crankshaft via a belt. When supplied by an excitation current, the rotor generates a magnetic field that sets up an alternating current in the fixed winding (stator). A diode rectifier bridge at the back of the alternator allows the alternating current to be transformed into a direct current that is sent to recharge the battery. A voltage governor, also built into the alternator, maintains the power supply at a constant voltage (14 V) throughout all load variation and engine speed ranges. The efficiency of the recharging system is controlled by the Body Computer which measures the D+ signal coming from the alternator with the engine moving (revs above 700 rpm). If the voltage measured is insufficient, the warning light in the instrument panel is switched on as well as the display of a message. The fuse box on the battery includes an automatic battery disconnection device that, in emergencies, cuts off the supply to the engine starting/recharging lead. This interruption is controlled by the inertia switch in the same way as for the fuel pump. See descriptions 5505 INSTRUMENT/GAUGE ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The START/STOP button H2 receives a power supply - pins 3 and 5 - from the steering lock control unit M89, which "relays" the direct power supply coming - at pin C1 of M89 - from the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1. The lighting for the button is guaranteed by the ignition-controlled line (INT) protected by fuse F49 (F51 from 04/07) of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. When the button is pressed, "AVV" signals are sent from pins 4 and 6 of H2 to M89 - pins B6 and B7; tha latter supplies the electromagnet winding - from pin B8 - pin 50 of the starter motor A20 - connector B. The supply and control signals for button H2 are "redundant" (two identical duplicate signals) for safety reasons, the wish of the user is recognized by means of the presence of only one of the two signals. The steering lock control unit M89 provides this power supply after a series of controls and checks. See E7065 ELECTRIC STEERING LOCK In particular, the TEG inserted status is sent by the TEG Reader H3 via the CAN - pins 3 and 8. The same signal is sent in a redundant manner to the steering lock node M89, form pin 2, and the latter, in turn, forwards it via the CAN. The starting go ahead only takes place if the clutch or the brake pedal is pressed: the control unit M89 receives the signal coming from the clutch switch I31 at pin A5 and the two brake pedal signals I30; the N.A. contact (pedal pressed) at pin C4 of M89 and the N.C. contact (pedal released) at pin C7 of M89. Pin 30 of A20 - connector A - i.e. the actual motor, receives a power supply with the voltage coming directly from the battery A1. The continuous current produced by the alternator A10 (pin B+) - connector B - is sent to the battery A1, passing through the motor A20. These two lines are always supplied and not protected by fuses; they are however controlled by the automatic "battery disconnection" device located in the fuse box on the battery B99: if the inertia switch I50 intervenes, a signal is sent to connector F of B99 which "opens" the device, thereby removing the power supply from the motor A20 and the alternator A10. When the alternator does not turn and therefore does not recharge the battery, an earth signal is sent from pin D+ - connector A - of A10 to the Body Computer M1 - pin 19 of connector A: this is connected via the CAN line to the instrument panel E50 and manages the switching on of the recharging warning light in the instrument panel as described above.

DESCRIPTION The radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of an electric fan operated at two different speeds: - the first speed is activated at a first engine coolant temperature level and a certain air conditioning refrigerant fluid pressure; - the second speed comes on at a higher temperature or pressure. The fan is operated by means of two specific relays located near the engine compartment junction unit. The supply line for the fan is protected by two special fuses, located in the engine compartment junction unit. The fan only comes on with the ignition on (15/54).

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Relays T6 and T7 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 manage the switching on of the two speed fan N11: the coils are supplied by the ignition-operated line (15/54) whilst the power lines are protected by fuses F6 and F7, in the engine compartment junction unit B1. Both are energized by an earth control signal coming from the engine management control unit M10. If the engine coolant reaches an initial temperature level, or the linear sensor K120 signals to the control unit M10 - pin 38 of connector A - that a certain pressure level has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends a signal - from pin 89 of connector A - which energizes the 1st speed fan relay T6 which sends the power supply to the fan N11 via the additional resistance O10: the fan turns at the first speed (slow). The linear sensor K120 receives a power supply and reference earth from the engine management control unit M10, pin 83 and 16 of connector A. If the engine coolant reaches a higher temperature level, or the linear sensor K120 signals to the control unit M10 - pin 38 of connector A - that a higher pressure level has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends a signal - from pin 70 of connector A - which energizes the 2nd speed fan relay T7 which sends the power supply directly to the fan N11: the fan turns at the maximum speed.

DESCRIPTION The radiator and air conditioner condenser cooling system consists of two electric fans operated at two different speeds: - the first speed is activated at a first engine coolant temperature level and a certain air conditioning refrigerant fluid pressure; - the second speed comes on at a higher temperature or pressure. The activation of the fans is achieved by means of two specific relays located in the engine compartment junction unit and a third relay located on the duct for the actual fans. The supply line for the fans is protected by two special fuses, located in the engine compartment junction unit. The fans only come on with the ignition on (15/54). An additional fan increases the cooling in the area of the alternator preventing it from overheating. The supply line for this fan is protected by a dedicated shunt fuse located on the duct.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The relay J30, located on the fan duct, manages the engagement of the fans N11 and N12 at the first speed: the coil and the power line are supplied by the line protected by fuse F6 of the engine compartment junction unit B1. If the engine coolant reaches an initial temperature level, or the linear sensor K120 signals to the control unit M10 - pin 38 of connector A - that a certain pressure level has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends a signal - from pin 89 of connector A - which energizes the relay J30, which sends the power supply to the fans N11 and N12 via the additional resistances O10 and O12: the two fans turn together at the first speed (slow). The linear sensor K120 receives a power supply and reference earth from the engine management control unit M10, pin 83 and 16 of connector A. Relays T6 and T7 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 manage the switching on of fans N11 and N12 at the second speed: the coils are supplied by the ignition-operated line (15/54) whilst the power lines are protected by fuses F6 and F7, in the engine compartment junction unit B1. If the engine coolant reaches a higher temperature level, or the linear sensor K120 signals to the control unit M10 - pin 38 of connector A - that a higher pressure level has been reached, then the control unit M10 sends a signal - from pin 70 of connector A - which energizes the two relays T6 and T7 which send the power supply directly to the fans N11 and N12 which turn together at the maximum speed. The engagement of the cooling fan N194 in the area of the alternator takes place at the same time as the two cooling fans at the first speed, via relay J30. The line is also protected by the dedicated fuse B110, located on the duct.

DESCRIPTION The JTS engine features a fuel supply system with a high pressure pump for direct injection. An electronic control system supervises and governs all engine parameters to optimise performance and fuel consumption by means of a real-time response to different service conditions. The system is managed by a BOSCH MED7.6.1 control unit with a motorized throttle that controls both the ignition and the phased, sequential injection. Depending on the signals received from numerous sensors, the control unit controls the injectors connected to it, managing the following systems: - fuel supply; - high pressure fuel pump control; - air supply; - accelerator pedal - engine cooling; - exhaust with catalytic converters controlled by four Lambda sensors; - fuel vapour recirculation. The control unit of this JTS engine manages the operation of the high pressure fuel pump by controlling an electric pressure regulator and an associated pressure sensor. The throttle body is also controlled electronically by the control unit: throttle opening is calculated in accordance with specific software mapped inside the engine control unit. This system does away with the need for a mechanical link between accelerator pedal and throttle body. The control unit controls the engine timing by means of a pair of electrohydraulic variable valve timing systems - one on the inlet shaft and one on the exhaust shaft; this solution makes it possible to ensure optimum timing by managing the inlet and the exhaust separately; two timing sensors allow the continuous control of the solution set. Thanks to the electronic management described above, this engine conforms to the most recent emission control regulations (EURO 4). For more details See descriptions 1056 PETROL INJECTION SYSTEM The system is also controlled by dedicated relays in the engine compartment control unit. Lines supplying the control unit and various system components (sensors and actuators) are protected by dedicated fuses that are also located inside the engine compartment.

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION Engine management control unit M10 controls and governs the entire electronic ignition and injection system. The control unit M10 receives a direct supply from the battery at pin 92 of connector A via the line protected by fuse F18 of junction unit B1. The ignition-operated power supply (15/54) arrives via a line protected by fuse F16 of the engine compartment junction unit B1 at pin 67 of connector A of M10 . Main injection relay T9 of B1 controls the entire system: it is energized by an earth signal from pin 25 of connector A of control unit M10 and then forwards a power supply: - to pins 3, 5 and 6 of connector A of the actual control unit, via the line protected by fuse F22 of B1; - to air flow meter K41, to fuel vapour recovery solenoid valve L10, to variable valve timing systems N92 and N93 and to Lambda sensors K15, K16, K17 and K18 and lastly to high pressure pump N77; (all these lines are protected by fuse F11 of B1); - to the coils A30, via the line protected by fuse F17 of B1. The fuel pump relay T10 of B1 is supplied by the line for fuse F21 of B1. It is energized by a control signal coming from pin 8 of connector A of control unit M10 and provides the power supply for the electric fuel pump N40 which is earthed via the inertia switch I50, which interrupts the circuit in the event of an impact and stops the dangerous supply of fuel. The engine management control unit M10 receives signals from the various sensors, thereby keeping all the engine operating parameters under control. The rpm sensor K46 provides information, via a frequency signal sent to pins 40 and 55 of connector B of control unit M10, about the engine speed. Intake side timing sensor K106 receives a power supply from pin 24 of connector B of control unit M10 and a reference earth from pin 7 of connector B and sends a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 41 of connector B of the actual control unit. Exhaust side timing sensor K107 receives a power supply from pin 24 of connector B of control unit M10 and a reference earth from pin 7 of connector B and sends a frequency signal corresponding to the timing to pin 56 of connector B of the actual control unit. Fuel pressure sensor K83 receives a power supply from pin 24 of connector B of control unit M10 and a reference earth from pin 27 of connector B and sends a frequency signal corresponding to the fuel pressure to pin 8 of connector B of the control unit. The engine temperature sender unit K36 receives a reference earth from pin 7 of connector B of the control unit M10 and provides a signal proportional to the temperature of the engine coolant at pin 22 of connector B of the control unit. The four Lambda sensors K15, K16, K17 and K18 provide control unit M10 with information about the correct composition of the air/fuel mixture in different exhaust positions: two linear sensor are located upstream of the preconverters while two flat sensors are located downstream of the preconverters. Linear sensor K15 sends the signals to pins 55, 56, 77 and 78 of connector A of M10, whilst it is heated by a heater coil to ensure correct operation even when cold. The heater coil is supplied by fuse F11 of B1 and receives an earth signal from pin 73 of connector A of control unit M10. Linear sensor K16 sends the signals to pins 57, 58, 79 and 80 of connector A of M10, whilst it is heated by a heater coil to ensure correct operation even when cold. The heater coil is supplied by fuse F11 of B1 and receives an earth signal from pin 51 of connector A of control unit M10. Flat sensor K17 sends signals to pins 74 and 75 of connector A of M10, whilst it is heated by a heater coil supplied by fuse F11 of B1, and receives an earth signal from pin 50 of connector A of control unit M10. Flat sensor K18 sends the signal to pins 52 and 53 of connector A of M10 whilst it is heated by a heater coil supplied by fuse F11 of B1 and receives an earth signal from pin 94 of connector A of control unit M10. Detonation sensor K50 makes it possible to have information about detonation conditions by means of a frequency signal sent to pin 44 of connector B of control unit M10: it receives a reference earth from pin 59 of connector B. The detonation sensor K51 makes it possible to have information about detonation conditions by means of a frequency signal sent to pin 58 of connector B of control unit M10: it receives a reference earth from pin 43 of connector B. The air flow meter K41 (supplied by fuse F11 of B1) is connected to pins 11, 12, 26 and 27 of connector B of control unit M10. Accelerator pedal K55 has two built-in potentiometers (a main one and a safety one). The first receives the power supply and earth respectively from pins 83 and 81 of connector A of M10 and sends the corresponding signal to pin 82 of 59 and 61 of connector A of M10 and sends the signal to pin 60 of the same connector. Control unit M10 receives the minimum engine oil pressure sensor K30 signal at pin 28 of connector B. Pin 14 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from the brake lights switch I30 - N.O. contact - with an ignition-controlled supply (INT) from fuse F37 of control unit B2; it receives the signal - N.C. contact - coming from the brake lights switch I30 at pin 20 of connector A of M10 with an ignition-controlled supply (INT) from fuse F35 of control unit B2. Pin 32 of connector A of M10 receives the signal coming from clutch switch I31. The control unit M10 controls the opening of the individual injectors N70, through the special signals sent from pins 49 and 50 (cyl. 1), 47 and 48 (cyl. 2), 32 and 33 (cyl. 3) and 34 and 35 (cyl. 4) of connector B of M10. The fuel pressure regulator N77 is operated by the control unit M10 from pin 2 of connector B. The control unit M10 also controls the coil A30 (supplied by fuse F17 of B1) via the (earth) control signals for the coil primary windings, whilst the secondary winding sends the impulse to the spark plugs: from pins 16, 1, 31 and 46 of connector B of M10 for cylinders 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively. The throttle body actuator N75 has two built-in potentiometers connected in parallel: this controls the throttle opening by means of a step motor. The motor receives a power supply from pins 15 and 30 of connector B of M10. Pin 24 of connector B sends the power supply to the two potentiometers, pin 9 provides the earth signal for them, whilst pins 10 and 25 of the same connector receive signals that arrive from the throttle body actuator N75. The fuel vapour recovery solenoid L10 allows the flow of fuel vapours to the engine intake, where they are added to the mixture entering the combustion chamber. The valve L10 is opened by the control unit when the engine is under load, by means of a duty cycle signal from pin 18 of connector B of M10. The inlet side variable valve timing system N92 mechanically controls the timing advance at the intake: it is controlled by pin 4 of connector B of the control unit. The exhaust side variable valve timing system N93 mechanically controls the timing advance at the exhaust: it is controlled by pin 19 of connector B of the control unit. The control unit M10 is then connected via the CAN to the Body Computer M1 and to the other network nodes: information on the following is sent through this connection - system autodiagnosis, that can be used by connecting to connector C of M1: signals arrive from pin 87 of connector A from the control unit M10 via the special diagnostic line; - engine coolant temperature, which is sent to the instrument panel E50 which manages the gauge and the warning light; - engine rpm, which is sent to the instrument panel E50 rev counter; - minimum engine oil pressure, which is sent to the instrument panel E50 which manages the warning light; It receives the speedometer signal, via the CAN, produced by the ABS control unit M50. The autodiagnostic system for the control unit M10 also produces a signal - which leaves pin 68 of connector A - which is connected directly to the EOBD warning light in the instrument panel E50.
