The vehicle is equipped with automatic transmission which regulates and controls the automatic engagement of the gears. The 6 speed gearbox, in addition to being compact and light, features a control unit integrated with the transmission. It has been designed with special attention paid to limiting consumption. An electronic control unit manages a complex operating logic that allows the use of the gearbox in both sequential conditions, in which the driver manages the engagement of the gears using the lever and, in automatic mode, where the management of the gear changes is delegated to the electronic system. The presence of the transmission control unit makes available the following set of operating modes and specific operational functions: - basic operating mode; - capacity to adapt to operating conditions; - functions designed to improve comfort and fuel consumption. In manual operating mode, the driver can select the gears by pushing the gear lever on the right; at this point a impulse upwards (towards "+") makes it possible to shift to a higher gear whilst an impulse downwards (towards "-") produces a shift to the previous gear. Its ability to adapt to operational conditions allows the vehicle to adapt to the driver's driving conditions and/or road conditions. The most important are as follows: - up & down slope: this function allows the vehicle to recognise road slopes (upward and downward) and modify gear shift points to achieve the best possible compromise at all times between the driver's needs, the road conditions and the vehicle situation (speed and engine speed). - Fast off: automatic transmissions normally shift from one gear to the next when the driver raises his/her foot from the accelerator. This function inhibits this gear shift when the foot is raised quickly from the accelerator, limiting the number of gear shifts and increasing driver comfort. - Cornering: this function inhibits gear shifts when the vehicle is cornering in order not to jeopardise vehicle safety. - Neutral control: after the vehicle has been parked with the gear shift lever in position D for a few seconds (e.g. waiting at a green traffic light), this function is activated. It releases the hydraulic clutch inside the transmission to reduce the resistant torque in the torque converter and thus save fuel while reducing the vehicle's vibration level when idling. - Self-learning to minimise the pulses perceptible to the driver during gear selector operation with the car parked (i.e. shifts from N-R and N-D), it is possible to apply the self-learning procedure to set the band and clutch activation pressures to ensure smoother operation; - Braking assist: this function is activated when the driver brakes and is designed to increase the deceleration of the vehicle by downshifting; - Poor grip: in order to prevent the wheels slipping, during take off in poor grip conditions the gear changes automatically from first to a higher gear. The control unit has its own diagnostic signal used for the continuous monitoring of the entire device. See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

The automatic transmission control unit M55 controls and regulates the entire gearbox management system. The direct power supply reaches engine compartment junction unit B1 at pin 11 of connector A of automatic transmission control unit M55 and at pin 1 of gear selector control unit M53 via a line protected by fuse F18. The ignition controlled supply (15/54) for steering lock control unit M89 reaches pin 1 of connector A of M55 and pin 2 of gear selector control unit M53 via the line protected by fuse F24 of engine compartment junction unit B1. Pin 9 of connector A of M55 is earthed. Gear selector control unit M53, via pins 7-8 and 9-10 and automatic transmission control unit M55, via pins 8-14 and 7-6, communicate via the C-CAN and interface with pins 36 and 37 of connector B of Body Computer control unit M1. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The Body Computer also transmits signals related to the operating status of the transmission to the display on instrument panel E050, via the B-CAN. The reverse gear engaged signal leaves pin 13 of connector A of the automatic transmission control unit M55. See E2022 REVERSING LIGHTS Pin 5 of connector A of the automatic transmission control unit M55 is connected directly to pin B4 of the steering lock control unit M89. If the gear lever is in park/neutral, the signal sent ensures that starting is allowed. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The gear controls on the steering wheel are connected via the clock spring D47 to the gear selector control unit M53, pins 11 and 12. The pins for connector B of automatic transmission control unit M55 have a pin-to-pin connection at the pins for automatic transmission solenoid unit L50. The autodiagnostic system for control unit M55 is achieved by connecting to connector C of Body Computer M1 - pin 7: it receives signals from pin 4 of connector A of control unit M55 via the special diagnostic line (K LINE). See E8010 DIAGNOSTIC MULTIPLE CONNECTOR

DESCRIPTION This vehicle is equipped with a starting system known as Smart-Key where there is no longer a traditional ignition key having been replaced with an electronic key "T.E.G." (Transmitter for Entry and go) combined with an electronic key reader and TEG-Reader radio frequency receiver. Access to the vheicle through radiofrequency recognition of the remote control incorporated in the TEG is entirely the same as what takes place with the traditional remote control incorporated in the key fob. The vehicle is not switched on/started up by inserting the key in the ignition switch (which is no longer present) and turning it but by inserting the TEG in the TEG Reader and activating the START/STOP button. See E5010 STARTING AND RECHARING The distribution of the power supply to the vehicle (ignition-controlled INT, INT/A, AVV, etc.) is managed by the steering lock node and takes place in entirely the same way as for models equipped with a traditional key. See E1010 POWER SUPPLY As there is no longer a mechanical key, the steering lock function is produced electrically via the steering lock electronic control unit, connected to the CAN. The release of the steering by the steering lock node takes place when the ignition-controlled INT is activated. The steering is locked by the steering lock node when the TEG is extracted from the TEG Reader. For more details See descriptions 5520 ENGINE STARTING

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The electric steering lock control unit M89 controls and regulates the entire electrically operated steering column lock system and also manages the vehicle access and starting system. The power supply for the control unit M89 comes, at pin C1 of M89, from the line protected by fuse F3 of the engine compartment junction unit B1, whilst pin A4 of M89 is earthed. The TEG inserted status is sent by the TEG Reader H3 via the CAN - pins 3 and 8. The same signal is sent, redundantly, to the steering lock node M89, from pin 2 and the latter, in turn, forwards it via the CAN. The TEG Reader H3 also receives a power supply - pin 6 - from the line protected by fuse F32 of the junction unit under the dashboard B2. pin 7 of H3 is earthed. The Smart Key system controls several warning lights and/or sends message signals to the instrument panel: the control unit M89 is connected via the CAN line ot the instrument panel E50 and manages the switching on of the steering lock warning light and a series of warning and failure messages shown in the instrument panel display.

DESCRIPTION The vehicle is equipped with numerous electronic control units with an autodiagnostic function. When a diagnostic tester (Examiner or other device) is connected to these control units, self-diagnosis data can be read (parameters, errors) or the available active diagnostic tests can be carried out. All the diagnostic lines flow into the EOBD connector (European On Board Diagnosis) which conforms with Directive 98/69/CE (EURO 3) - ISO standard J1962 in the Body Computer connector C of M1. The same connector is responsible for the fault diagnosis of the nodes (control units) connected to the low transmission speed B-CAN, while the fault diganosis of the dynamic control high transmission speed C-CAN is carried out by means of a specific K line. The following are checked via the B-CAN line: - junction unit under the dashboard; - instrument panel; - door control units; - seat control units; - steering wheel controls; - radio/navigator unit; - Bluetooth control unit; - climate control sytem control unit; - Air Bag control unit; - parking sensor control unit; - steering lock control unit - TEG Reader For more details See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES The following are monitored via individual diagnostic K lines: - engine management control unit; - ABS control unit; - automatic transmission control unit (only on versions with Automatic Transmission); - robotized gearbox control unit (only on versions with Robotized Gearbox); - xenon headlamps control units (if fitted)

FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION The EOBD central tester output is built into Body Computer M1 connector C. It is supplied directly by the battery at pin 16 of the line protected by fuse F39 of underfacia junction unit B2 ; pins 4 and 5 are earthed. Pin 1 is connected to the K line at ABS control unit M50 (pin 6) See E7022 VDC Pin 7 is connected, via the K line, to the engine management control unit M10 See E5030 PETROL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT Pin 7 is also connected through the K line to the automatic transmission control unit M55 (only on versions with Automatic Transmission) See E7050 AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION or with the robotized gearbox control unit M54 (only on the Robotized Gearbox version) See E7051 ROBOTIZED GEARBOX Pin 12 is connected by the K line to the management control units for the xenon headlamps F10 and F11. See E3080 HEADLAMP AGLINMENT CORRECTOR The remaining outlets for other possible K lines are not used on this version. Pins 6 and 14 are connected to the B-CAN: this network controls and "diagnoses" the junction unit under the dashboard B2, the instrument panel E50, the driver's door control unit M66, the passenger door control unit M67, the controls for the seats H66 and H67, the TEG Reader H3, the steering lock control unit M89, the radio or the built-in radio-telephone-navigator P20, the Bluetooth control unit M162 and the controls on the steering wheel D47, the climate control system control unit M70, the Air Bag control unit M60 and the parking sensors control unit M84. See E1050 CAN CONNECTION LINES
